question: How does the World Health Organization (WHO) define reproductive health?

options.A: The biological ability to produce healthy offspring without medical intervention
options.B: A state of complete physical, mental, and social well-being in all reproductive matters
options.C: The total absence of any sexually transmitted infections in a community
options.D: Having regular access to affordable maternity hospitals and clinics

explanation: Think beyond just the physical body! The WHO looks at the whole picture—physical, mental, and social well-being—when it comes to reproductive health. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T1#GNS216_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why does reproductive health cover mental and social well-being alongside physical health?

options.A: Mental health is legally required to be assessed before any family planning service
options.B: Emotional stress can directly alter a person's hormonal balance and fertility rates
options.C: Psychological counseling is the primary treatment for most reproductive tract infections
options.D: Reproductive choices and experiences deeply affect a person's emotional life and social standing

explanation: You know how personal family and reproductive matters are. Because they touch our deepest emotions and community standing, mental and social health are just as vital as physical health! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T1#GNS216_U1_T1_h1)

question: What is a key principle of modern reproductive rights?

options.A: The right to decide freely the number and spacing of children
options.B: The guarantee of automatic financial support for large families
options.C: The right to free private healthcare delivery anywhere in the world
options.D: The legal obligation to have at least two children per family

explanation: Spot on! Modern rights put the power back in the individual's hands to choose if, when, and how many children they want to have. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T1#GNS216_U1_T1_h2)

question: How were early population control programs different from modern reproductive rights?

options.A: Early programs focused exclusively on treating infertility rather than contraception
options.B: Modern frameworks rely on government-mandated family sizes to reduce poverty
options.C: Modern frameworks ignore maternal health in favor of economic development
options.D: Early programs prioritized national demographic targets over individual bodily autonomy

explanation: In the past, programs often focused on hitting government population numbers. Today, we focus on respecting each person's individual rights and personal choices. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T1#GNS216_U1_T1_h2)

question: Which major international conference linked population policy directly with human rights?

options.A: The Geneva Convention on the Treatment of Patients
options.B: The Alma-Ata Declaration on Primary Health Care
options.C: The 1994 International Conference on Population and Development in Cairo
options.D: The 1995 World Conference on Women held in Beijing

explanation: It's the 1994 Cairo Conference! This was a massive turning point that shifted global health focus toward empowering individuals and protecting their rights. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T1#GNS216_U1_T1_h3)

question: Why do international agreements like the Cairo Programme of Action matter for local Nigerian nursing practice?

options.A: They allow nurses to bypass local hospital rules during emergency obstetric procedures
options.B: They eliminate the need for patient consent in family planning clinics
options.C: They legally require international organizations to fund all local nursing salaries
options.D: They provide a standard framework that governments use to shape national health policies and clinic guidelines

explanation: Big global agreements help shape our national laws and clinic guidelines, which directly guide the safe and effective care you will provide to your patients. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T1#GNS216_U1_T1_h3)

question: What is a major reason for high maternal mortality rates in many rural Nigerian communities?

options.A: Limited access to skilled birth attendants and emergency obstetric care
options.B: Universal free access to advanced reproductive technology
options.C: Mandatory hospital deliveries for all pregnant women
options.D: An overabundance of licensed gynecologists in primary health centers

explanation: When clinics are far away and transport is hard to find, delays in getting emergency care during childbirth sadly put many mothers at high risk. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T1#GNS216_U1_T1_h4)

question: As a community health nurse in a rural Nigerian village, what should be your top priority to reduce maternal complications?

options.A: Building multi-story tertiary specialist hospitals in every village
options.B: Training and building referral linkages with local traditional birth attendants
options.C: Closing down all local markets to force women to stay home
options.D: Importing expensive fertility treatments from overseas pharmaceutical companies

explanation: Since many women first consult traditional birth attendants in the village, building a friendly working relationship and training them to spot danger signs early saves precious lives! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T1#GNS216_U1_T1_h4)

question: Which social factor is consistently proven to help young girls delay marriage and early childbearing?

options.A: Traditional community ceremonies
options.B: Living in an urban city center
options.C: Access to formal education
options.D: Employment in the agricultural sector

explanation: Education is a powerful tool! When girls stay in school, they gain knowledge, open up better life opportunities, and naturally delay marriage and childbearing. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T1#GNS216_U1_T1_h5)

question: How does poverty negatively affect the reproductive health of women in resource-limited settings?

options.A: It legally bars them from entering public health facilities
options.B: It guarantees that they will receive substandard care from international doctors
options.C: It prevents them from paying for transport, diagnostics, and essential medications
options.D: It automatically increases their biological fertility rate beyond normal levels

explanation: Out-of-pocket costs for transport, tests, and drugs are tough barriers that often force struggling women to miss out on the vital care they need. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T1#GNS216_U1_T1_h5)

question: What does 'patient autonomy' mean in reproductive healthcare?

options.A: The requirement that family elders approve all medical procedures
options.B: The right of the individual to make self-determining choices about their body
options.C: The legal authority of the healthcare provider to choose the best treatment
options.D: The financial independence of the hospital from government oversight

explanation: Autonomy simply means it is the patient's body and their choice. Every individual has the right to decide what happens to their own medical care. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T1#GNS216_U1_T1_h6)

question: Why is true informed consent sometimes difficult to achieve in strongly patriarchal settings?

options.A: Contraceptive drugs have secret side effects that cannot be explained
options.B: Medical terminology is naturally too complex for any patient to understand
options.C: Nurses are legally required to make treatment choices for female patients
options.D: Patients may be pressured by family members to follow decisions made on their behalf

explanation: In some cultures, family or spousal approval is expected for everything. This can make it tricky to ensure a patient's personal choice is truly respected and free from pressure. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T1#GNS216_U1_T1_h6)

question: What is one of the main ways nurses advocate for reproductive rights in everyday practice?

options.A: Financially sponsoring family planning clinics out of their own salaries
options.B: Providing non-judgmental, confidential care and education to all patients
options.C: Refusing to treat patients who disagree with hospital policies
options.D: Changing national health laws through Supreme Court litigation

explanation: As a bedside nurse, your best advocacy tool is treating every patient with respect, keeping their secrets safe, and educating them without any personal bias. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T1#GNS216_U1_T1_h7)

question: An unmarried young girl comes to the clinic asking about family planning, and another nurse loudly criticizes her morals. What is the best way for you to handle this?

options.A: Ignore the situation because nurse-to-nurse conflicts are discouraged
options.B: Gently intervene, take over the client's care, and provide confidential, non-judgmental education
options.C: Agree with the colleague so the young girl learns a lesson about societal expectations
options.D: Report the girl to hospital security for seeking family planning services

explanation: You've got this! Patient dignity and privacy come first. Step in warmly, protect your patient from stigma, and make sure she gets safe, supportive, and confidential care. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T1#GNS216_U1_T1_h7)

question: According to health standards, what does reproductive health truly cover?

options.A: Complete physical, mental, and social well-being
options.B: The prevention of genetic disorders in newborns
options.C: Only the absence of sexually transmitted infections
options.D: Biological fitness solely for childbearing purposes

explanation: You got this! Reproductive health is much more than just a healthy body or the absence of disease—it embraces your total physical, mental, and social wellness. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T2#GNS216_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why do nurses look at reproductive health as a lifelong journey rather than just a passing phase?

options.A: Because reproductive needs change and persist from birth to old age
options.B: Because healthcare funding is tied to lifelong patient monitoring
options.C: Because reproductive organs never undergo natural degeneration
options.D: Because patients only seek care during their childbearing years

explanation: Spot on! Reproductive health matters at every single stage of life, meaning our care and guidance as nurses never truly stop. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T2#GNS216_U1_T2_h1)

question: Which hormone is the main driver of male reproductive development?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Estrogen
options.C: Testosterone
options.D: Progesterone

explanation: Great job! Testosterone is the key male sex hormone made in the testes that shapes male physical traits and reproductive function. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T2#GNS216_U1_T2_h2)

question: What is the main job of the fallopian tubes in the female body?

options.A: To serve as the usual site for fertilization of the egg
options.B: To provide a muscular environment for fetal development
options.C: To secrete large amounts of protective progesterone
options.D: To produce the monthly supply of mature oocytes

explanation: You nailed it! The fallopian tubes catch the released egg and act as the meeting place where sperm usually fertilize it before it moves to the uterus. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T2#GNS216_U1_T2_h2)

question: What is the medical term for a young girl's very first menstrual period?

options.A: Menopause
options.B: Menarche
options.C: Mittelschmerz
options.D: Dysmenorrhea

explanation: Well done! Menarche is simply the medical word for that first major milestone of monthly bleeding during puberty. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T2#GNS216_U1_T2_h3)

question: Why is emotional and psychological support just as crucial as physical checks during teenage puberty?

options.A: Mental health counseling replaces the need for nutritional guidance
options.B: Rapid bodily changes often cause anxiety, confusion, and body image issues
options.C: Teenagers refuse physical examinations unless given psychological counseling
options.D: Hormonal surges permanently impair the adolescent's cognitive abilities

explanation: Exactly right! Teens go through a whirlwind of physical and emotional shifts, so offering a listening ear is a big part of good nursing care. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T2#GNS216_U1_T2_h3)

question: As women grow older, which health screenings become most important?

options.A: Ovulation tracking and fertility windows
options.B: Congenital anomaly prevention counseling
options.C: Cervical and breast cancer screenings
options.D: Testicular self-examination techniques

explanation: Spot on! Regular checks for cervical changes and breast health are vital preventative steps as women age. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T2#GNS216_U1_T2_h4)

question: A 52-year-old woman comes to the clinic reporting hot flashes and irregular periods. What stage is she likely going through?

options.A: Pubescent transition
options.B: Gestational maturity
options.C: Perimenopause
options.D: Menarche

explanation: You got it! Those sudden hot flashes and wonky cycles are classic signs of perimenopause, the transition phase leading up to menopause. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T2#GNS216_U1_T2_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a major public health challenge for reproductive health in Nigeria?

options.A: Limited access to modern contraceptive methods
options.B: Universal excess availability of fertility treatments
options.C: High maternal mortality ratios in rural areas
options.D: High burden of sexually transmitted infections

explanation: Correct! Too many fertility treatments are definitely not the problem here—rather, it's struggling with basic maternal care access and preventable complications. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T2#GNS216_U1_T2_h5)

question: How do poverty and cultural barriers team up to worsen pregnancy outcomes in tough settings?

options.A: They cause immediate cessation of all hormonal activities
options.B: They automatically increase the biological rate of twin pregnancies
options.C: They eliminate the need for community health nursing outreaches
options.D: They delay timely care-seeking and restrict access to skilled birth attendants

explanation: Spot on. When money is tight or cultural beliefs hold sway, women often reach the hospital too late, leading to avoidable emergencies. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T2#GNS216_U1_T2_h5)

question: What is the heart of reproductive rights?

options.A: The mandatory requirement for every adult to have children
options.B: Free cosmetic surgeries for all citizens reaching adulthood
options.C: Bodily autonomy and freedom from coercion in health decisions
options.D: Government control over family size and birth intervals

explanation: You nailed it! Reproductive rights mean every person has the right to make their own free choices about their body and family planning. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T2#GNS216_U1_T2_h6)

question: Why do modern healthcare programs make sure to involve male partners in reproductive health?

options.A: Men are the only family members who suffer from reproductive infections
options.B: Men often influence household health decisions and resource allocation
options.C: Male involvement completely removes the need for female health education
options.D: Women are legally prohibited from visiting clinics alone

explanation: Great reasoning! Since men often hold the purse strings and make major home decisions in many communities, getting them on board is key to success. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T2#GNS216_U1_T2_h6)

question: What is a core day-to-day nursing duty when it comes to reproductive health care?

options.A: Passing national laws regarding reproductive rights
options.B: Performing major obstetric surgical operations independently
options.C: Providing family planning counseling and education
options.D: Manufacturing pharmaceutical contraceptives for hospitals

explanation: Exactly right! Nurses spend a lot of time guiding clients through family planning choices and teaching healthy habits. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T2#GNS216_U1_T2_h7)

question: Why is keeping strict privacy and confidentiality so important when teenagers come in for reproductive health services?

options.A: It removes the need to document clinical findings in health records
options.B: It is a legal requirement only for adult patients, not minors
options.C: It builds trust and encourages teens to seek necessary medical advice early
options.D: It prevents parents from ever knowing their child is growing up

explanation: You got it! Teens are often scared of being judged. Promising confidentiality helps them feel safe enough to get help before small issues turn big. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T2#GNS216_U1_T2_h7)

question: What does reproductive health truly mean according to the World Health Organization (WHO)?

options.A: A woman's physical capability to carry a pregnancy to full term safely
options.B: The total absence of any bacteria or viruses in the pelvic organs
options.C: The biological ability to conceive and bear children without medical help
options.D: A state of complete physical, mental, and social well-being in all reproductive matters

explanation: Think of reproductive health as more than just working body parts. The WHO looks at the whole person—physical, mental, and social well-being together! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T3#GNS216_U1_T3_h1)

question: As a nurse, why shouldn't you focus *only* on physical symptoms when caring for a client's reproductive health?

options.A: Because physical symptoms are rarely accurate indicators of reproductive disease
options.B: Because reproductive health includes mental, social, and bodily autonomy aspects
options.C: Because hospital policies strictly prohibit treating only physical complaints
options.D: Because laboratory tests cannot detect most reproductive system infections

explanation: You are caring for a human being, not just a body! Since reproductive health covers mental and social wellness too, great nurses look at the big picture. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T3#GNS216_U1_T3_h1)

question: What is the main reason pregnant women are encouraged to attend routine antenatal care (ANC) visits?

options.A: To provide the mother with high doses of broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.B: To permanently prevent any potential complications during the postpartum period
options.C: To schedule the exact date and time when labor will officially begin
options.D: To monitor fetal growth and screen for conditions like anemia and high blood pressure

explanation: ANC is like a check-point for safety! It helps midwives and nurses catch small issues like low blood levels or high BP early before they become emergencies. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T3#GNS216_U1_T3_h2)

question: A mother just gave birth six hours ago in the maternity ward. Which immediate postpartum emergency should you watch out for most closely?

options.A: Gestational diabetes
options.B: Postpartum hemorrhage
options.C: Ectopic pregnancy
options.D: Chronic pelvic pain

explanation: Postpartum hemorrhage (heavy bleeding) is a major postpartum risk, especially in the first few hours after delivery. Always keep a close eye on your patient's lochia and vitals! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T3#GNS216_U1_T3_h2)

question: How do common hormonal contraceptives (like pills and injectables) mainly prevent pregnancy?

options.A: By suppressing ovulation and thickening cervical mucus
options.B: By killing the ovum before fertilization can take place
options.C: By permanently closing the fallopian tubes with scar tissue
options.D: By physically destroying sperm inside the vaginal canal

explanation: Hormones trick the body into holding back the egg (no ovulation) and make the cervical mucus too thick for swimming sperm to get through. Clever, right? [learn more](GNS216_U1_T3#GNS216_U1_T3_h3)

question: Which family planning method category also helps protect against Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs)?

options.A: Hormonal pills
options.B: Barrier methods
options.C: Permanent surgeries
options.D: Intrauterine devices

explanation: Only barrier methods like condoms physically block fluids, which stops both unwanted pregnancy AND pesky STIs. Pills and IUDs do not protect against infections! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T3#GNS216_U1_T3_h3)

question: What makes controlling Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs) so tricky in communities?

options.A: STIs cannot be transmitted if the infected person takes vitamins
options.B: Laboratory tests are completely unavailable in most health clinics
options.C: Many infections present with mild or silent symptoms
options.D: Antibiotics can cure viral infections just as easily as bacterial ones

explanation: Many STIs show zero signs at first! People feel totally fine, so they unknowingly spread the infection before realizing they need treatment. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T3#GNS216_U1_T3_h4)

question: Why is partner notification and treatment a must when managing STIs?

options.A: To punish individuals who engage in unprotected sexual intercourse
options.B: To determine which partner originally contracted the infection first
options.C: To prevent reinfection and break the ongoing cycle of transmission
options.D: To fulfill mandatory insurance reporting requirements for hospitals

explanation: If you treat only one partner, they will just catch the infection right back the next time they have sex. Both partners must be treated together to truly heal! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T3#GNS216_U1_T3_h4)

question: What is one of the biggest roadblocks stopping teenagers from seeking reproductive health care at clinics?

options.A: Judgmental healthcare attitudes and cultural taboos
options.B: A complete lack of biological changes during puberty
options.C: Immunity to all forms of sexually transmitted infections
options.D: Strict laws requiring parental consent for all general check-ups

explanation: Too often, young people stay away from clinics because they are scared health workers will scold, judge, or gossip about them. As nurses, we must be welcoming! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T3#GNS216_U1_T3_h5)

question: What makes a clinic truly "youth-friendly" when it comes to reproductive health?

options.A: Programs that focus solely on treating severe physical trauma injuries
options.B: Medical facilities that treat only patients under twelve years of age
options.C: Clinics that operate exclusively during late night hours on weekends
options.D: Services that offer confidential, non-judgmental care tailored to teenagers

explanation: Youth-friendly clinics win teens' trust by keeping their business private, listening without scolding, and treating them with absolute respect. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T3#GNS216_U1_T3_h5)

question: After how many months of trying to conceive without success do doctors officially define infertility?

options.A: At least five full years
options.B: Exactly six weeks
options.C: Twelve months or more
options.D: Three months or less

explanation: Doctors generally look at a full year (12 months) of regular, unprotected sex before starting infertility investigations. Don't panic too early! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T3#GNS216_U1_T3_h6)

question: Which of these is a very common female-related cause of infertility?

options.A: Permanent enlargement of the prostate gland
options.B: Hyperactive sperm motility within the uterus
options.C: Complete absence of the pituitary hormone testosterone
options.D: Tubal blockages from previous pelvic infections

explanation: Past untreated infections (like PID) can leave scars or blockages in the fallopian tubes, stopping the egg and sperm from meeting. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T3#GNS216_U1_T3_h6)

question: Which common virus is most strongly linked to the development of cervical cancer?

options.A: Human immunodeficiency virus
options.B: Herpes simplex virus
options.C: Human papillomavirus
options.D: Hepatitis B virus

explanation: High-risk strains of Human Papillomavirus (HPV) are the leading cause of changes in the cervix that can lead to cancer over time. Thankfully, we have vaccines now! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T3#GNS216_U1_T3_h7)

question: What is the primary goal of routine screening tests like the Pap smear?

options.A: To permanently cure active bacterial infections in the pelvis
options.B: To detect abnormal cellular changes before cancer develops
options.C: To prevent the initial transmission of sexually transmitted germs
options.D: To measure hormone levels during the normal menstrual cycle

explanation: Pap smears catch weird cellular changes early—long before they turn into cancer—making treatment quick and easy. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T3#GNS216_U1_T3_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT considered a harmful traditional practice?

options.A: Female genital mutilation performed without anesthesia
options.B: Forced physical practices during early puberty rites
options.C: Routine childhood immunizations against measles
options.D: Child marriage involving underage adolescents

explanation: Immunizations save children's lives from deadly diseases! They are a standard, safe medical intervention, unlike harmful cultural practices. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T3#GNS216_U1_T3_h8)

question: What should be your very first priority when nursing a survivor of gender-based violence?

options.A: Demanding that the survivor immediately file a police report before treatment
options.B: Providing compassionate medical care, physical safety, and emotional support
options.C: Telling the patient to forget the incident and focus on daily chores
options.D: Refusing to document physical injuries to protect the hospital from lawsuits

explanation: A survivor's safety, physical healing, and gentle emotional support always come first in clinical nursing. Make them feel safe and heard! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T3#GNS216_U1_T3_h8)

question: According to public health standards, what does reproductive health truly focus on?

options.A: Eliminating all infectious diseases affecting only adult women
options.B: Physical, mental, and social well-being in all matters of the reproductive system
options.C: Controlling population growth through strict laws
options.D: Ensuring every family has at least four children

explanation: Think of reproductive health as a total package! It's not just about avoiding disease or planning family size—it's about a person's overall physical, mental, and social well-being regarding their reproductive system. You've got this! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T4#GNS216_U1_T4_h1)

question: Why are primary healthcare facilities so important for reproductive health in Nigeria?

options.A: They exclusively handle complex surgical procedures
options.B: They are where most rural Nigerians seek initial medical care
options.C: They are fully funded by international donors without local input
options.D: They provide free medications for all chronic illnesses

explanation: Primary healthcare centers are right at the grassroots level. They are usually the very first place everyday people in rural areas go when they need medical help, making them lifesavers! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T4#GNS216_U1_T4_h1)

question: Which of these is a major direct cause of maternal mortality in Nigeria?

options.A: Severe bleeding after childbirth
options.B: Untreated childhood measles
options.C: Chronic adult asthma
options.D: Seasonal malaria outbreaks in men

explanation: Severe bleeding after delivery (known as postpartum hemorrhage) is one of the leading direct causes of maternal death. As a future nurse, knowing this helps you spot why rapid postpartum care is so vital. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T4#GNS216_U1_T4_h2)

question: A pregnant woman in a remote village starts bleeding heavily during labor. What is the most critical factor that decides if she survives?

options.A: The weather forecast for the upcoming week
options.B: Whether she ate a balanced diet during her first trimester
options.C: Her family's ability to buy infant clothing ahead of time
options.D: Quick transport to a facility with emergency obstetric care

explanation: In emergencies like severe bleeding, every minute counts! Getting the mother quickly to a hospital that can handle obstetric emergencies is often the difference between life and death. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T4#GNS216_U1_T4_h2)

question: What is the primary physical cause of obstetric fistula in young mothers?

options.A: Severe malnutrition during early childhood
options.B: A hereditary genetic blood disorder
options.C: Exposure to industrial chemical toxins
options.D: Prolonged and obstructed labor without timely surgical care

explanation: Obstetric fistula happens when labor gets stuck for too long without medical help. The constant pressure creates a tear or opening between the birth canal and the bladder or rectum. Timely medical care prevents this tragic injury. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T4#GNS216_U1_T4_h3)

question: Why does obstetric fistula often cause women to face social isolation in their communities?

options.A: Patients lose their ability to speak after the injury
options.B: Continuous incontinence leads to severe social stigma and shame
options.C: Government laws require isolation of all surgical patients
options.D: Traditional healers forbid them from leaving their homes

explanation: Because of constant leaking of urine or stool, affected women often face heartbreaking stigma and misunderstanding from their communities. As nurses, our empathy and care are crucial in supporting and healing them. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T4#GNS216_U1_T4_h3)

question: What does the term 'unmet need for family planning' actually mean?

options.A: Doctors refusing to prescribe medicines to married couples
options.B: The total absence of hospitals in a given region
options.C: Willingness to avoid pregnancy without using modern contraception
options.D: A complete ban on all contraceptive drugs by the government

explanation: An 'unmet need' simply describes women who want to delay or stop having children, but aren't currently using any modern birth control method—often due to lack of access or information. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T4#GNS216_U1_T4_h4)

question: Which of these commonly stops Nigerian women from using contraceptives?

options.A: Mandatory counseling sessions required weekly
options.B: Laws that punish women for having children
options.C: Fear of side effects and partner disapproval
options.D: An excess supply of free medications in local markets

explanation: Myths about side effects and lack of support from partners or family members are major hurdles. Gentle, accurate counseling from nurses helps clear up these fears! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T4#GNS216_U1_T4_h4)

question: What is a major problem when clinics are not youth-friendly?

options.A: High rates of untreated sexually transmitted infections among teens
options.B: Mandatory health insurance for all teenagers
options.C: Decreased interest in secondary school education
options.D: An immediate surplus of qualified midwives

explanation: If young people feel judged or scared when visiting a clinic, they simply stay away. This means infections and health issues go untreated. Making our clinics welcoming changes everything! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T4#GNS216_U1_T4_h5)

question: A 16-year-old girl visits your clinic for family planning advice but is terrified her parents will find out. How should you respond as a nurse?

options.A: Scold her for engaging in premarital relationships
options.B: Refuse service and call her parents immediately
options.C: Assure her of confidentiality and provide age-appropriate counseling
options.D: Report her to local law enforcement authorities

explanation: Trust is everything in nursing! By assuring her of confidentiality, you make her feel safe enough to get the right health education and protection instead of hiding risky situations. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T4#GNS216_U1_T4_h5)

question: How do patriarchal family structures often impact women's reproductive health in Nigeria?

options.A: They eliminate all cultural barriers to hospital delivery
options.B: They require husbands to attend all antenatal checkups
options.C: They often restrict women's autonomy in making healthcare decisions
options.D: They automatically grant women full control over household finances

explanation: In homes where men hold all the decision-making power, a woman may need her husband's permission or money just to visit a clinic, which can dangerously delay her care. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T4#GNS216_U1_T4_h6)

question: Why is it so effective to partner with traditional and religious leaders when promoting reproductive health?

options.A: They distribute free contraceptives directly to hospitals
options.B: They are licensed medical doctors trained in midwifery
options.C: They hold significant influence over community beliefs and health practices
options.D: They manage the national budget for health infrastructure

explanation: Local leaders are deeply respected by the community. When they support health initiatives, community members are much more likely to listen and adopt healthy practices. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T4#GNS216_U1_T4_h6)

question: What is one of the main goals of state-level health insurance schemes in Nigeria?

options.A: Increasing taxes on imported medical equipment
options.B: Eliminating all private pharmacies in urban centers
options.C: Reducing out-of-pocket spending on medical care for poor families
options.D: Providing free international travel for nurses

explanation: Health insurance helps protect vulnerable families from paying heavy cash bills right at the hospital door, making it easier for everyone to get the care they need. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T4#GNS216_U1_T4_h7)

question: What is a major hurdle when trying to make national health policies work successfully in Nigeria?

options.A: Strict international bans on local medicine production
options.B: A total lack of written guidelines in government offices
options.C: Implementation gaps caused by funding and resource distribution issues
options.D: The absence of any trained healthcare workers in the entire country

explanation: Nigeria often has great written policies, but turning those plans into actual working services on the ground is tricky due to funding shortages and logistical challenges. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T4#GNS216_U1_T4_h7)

question: Which group forms the backbone of direct healthcare delivery in Nigerian primary clinics?

options.A: International policy makers
options.B: Hospital accountants
options.C: Nurses and midwives
options.D: Pharmaceutical manufacturers

explanation: That's you! Nurses and midwives provide the vast majority of direct maternal and child health care across our communities. You are truly the heartbeat of healthcare delivery. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T4#GNS216_U1_T4_h8)

question: A community health nurse notices that pregnant women in her area always arrive late with severe complications. What is the best proactive step to take?

options.A: Wait until the government builds a new tertiary hospital nearby
options.B: Report the patients to local traditional rulers for punishment
options.C: Refuse to treat patients who arrive after their expected due date
options.D: Conduct community education on pregnancy danger signs and early clinic attendance

explanation: Proactive education is key! Teaching women about danger signs before complications arise helps them recognize trouble early and come to the clinic on time. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T4#GNS216_U1_T4_h8)

question: What is the main goal of Nigeria's National Reproductive Health Policy and Strategic Framework?

options.A: To reduce high rates of maternal and child mortality
options.B: To replace traditional birth attendants with medical doctors
options.C: To privatize all primary health care centers in the country
options.D: To increase the importation of foreign pharmaceutical drugs

explanation: You've got this! The core aim of this framework is to tackle the heavy burden of maternal and child deaths through coordinated health actions. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h1)

question: Why should student nurses care about the national reproductive health framework?

options.A: It allows them to practice independently without a supervising physician
options.B: It exempts them from clinical documentation requirements
options.C: It guarantees automatic promotion within the civil service
options.D: It ensures their local community nursing actions match national health goals

explanation: Spot on! Aligning everyday nursing care with national policies helps us all work together effectively to solve health challenges in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h1)

question: Which of these is a key focus during Antenatal Care (ANC) visits in Nigerian clinics?

options.A: Treating chronic adult diabetes mellitus
options.B: Scheduling permanent surgical sterilization
options.C: Conducting forensic examinations for survivors of abuse
options.D: Screening for conditions like gestational hypertension

explanation: Great thinking! ANC visits give nurses a wonderful chance to monitor blood pressure and catch dangerous pregnancy complications early. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h2)

question: A 30-week pregnant woman comes to the clinic complaining of a severe headache and blurred vision. What is your very first nursing action?

options.A: Discharge her home with instructions to eat more salt
options.B: Assess her blood pressure for signs of dangerous hypertension
options.C: Schedule her for routine tetanus vaccination next month
options.D: Encourage her to walk around the ward to improve circulation

explanation: Well done! Severe headaches and vision changes are classic danger signs of preeclampsia. Checking her blood pressure right away is a life-saving priority. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h2)

question: Which of the following is an example of a long-acting reversible contraceptive (LARC) method?

options.A: Combined oral contraceptive pills
options.B: Subdermal contraceptive implants
options.C: Male latex barrier condoms
options.D: Spermicidal foaming vaginal tablets

explanation: Exactly! Implants and IUDs offer long-term protection against pregnancy, but can be easily removed whenever the client is ready. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h3)

question: Why is pre-contraception counseling so important in family planning clinics?

options.A: It is legally required before a patient can purchase over-the-counter condoms
options.B: It permanently prevents users from ever changing their chosen method
options.C: It helps clients choose a method that suits their lifestyle while addressing fears or myths
options.D: It replaces the need for any physical health assessment by a doctor

explanation: You nailed it! Good counseling clears up rumors about side effects and helps clients find the contraceptive method that best fits their personal life. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h3)

question: What is the primary goal of Adolescent and Youth-Friendly Health Services?

options.A: Focusing exclusively on the treatment of geriatric illnesses
options.B: Banning teenagers from visiting local community pharmacies
options.C: Providing confidential and accessible care without judgment
options.D: Requiring parental consent for every routine consultation

explanation: That's right! Youth-friendly centers remove barriers like judgmental attitudes and lack of privacy so young people feel safe seeking help. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h4)

question: Why do many teenagers shy away from standard healthcare clinics for reproductive health needs?

options.A: They fear harsh judgment, stigma, and a lack of confidentiality from staff
options.B: They prefer to use complex surgical procedures at home
options.C: They are completely unaware that health facilities exist in their towns
options.D: They are legally forbidden from entering government hospitals

explanation: Spot on. Fear of being scolded or having their privacy broken stops many young people from getting the care they need early on. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h4)

question: In Nigerian reproductive health programs, what does the acronym PMTCT stand for?

options.A: Primary Medical Treatment for Chronic Tumors
options.B: Prevention of Mother-To-Child Transmission
options.C: Public Midwifery Training and Community Testing
options.D: Postnatal Management of Teenage Children and Teens

explanation: You got it! PMTCT programs focus on stopping HIV from passing from an infected mother to her baby during pregnancy, birth, or breastfeeding. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h5)

question: Why do busy primary health centers often use syndromic management for sexually transmitted infections?

options.A: It guarantees that laboratory scientists are no longer needed in hospitals
options.B: It allows nurses to treat common symptoms immediately using flowcharts before lab results return
options.C: It completely replaces the need for any physical examination of the patient
options.D: It is the only method approved by international pharmaceutical companies

explanation: Brilliant! Syndromic management uses clear symptom guides so nurses can start treatment right away, which is a lifesaver when lab results take too long. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h5)

question: What is a core day-to-day duty of nurses and midwives in Nigerian reproductive health care?

options.A: Providing direct clinical care, health education, and community outreach
options.B: Writing national health insurance laws in the federal legislature
options.C: Manufacturing contraceptive implants in national laboratories
options.D: Importing specialized surgical instruments from overseas

explanation: Exactly! Nurses and midwives are on the frontline, delivering care at the bedside and educating communities on healthy living. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h6)

question: A community midwife in a remote village is treating a woman with severe bleeding after childbirth who needs a blood transfusion. What should she do first?

options.A: Stabilize the patient with available fluids and arrange an immediate emergency referral
options.B: Ask the family members to perform minor surgery in the clinic ward
options.C: Wait until morning before telling anyone about the excessive bleeding
options.D: Discharge the patient immediately to free up the hospital bed

explanation: You've got this! When an emergency is beyond the clinic's capacity, stabilize the patient with what you have and arrange a swift transfer to a higher center. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a major challenge facing reproductive health programs in Nigeria?

options.A: Excessive availability of surplus modern hospitals in every village
options.B: Shortages of trained healthcare staff in rural community clinics
options.C: Cultural or religious resistance to certain family planning methods
options.D: Financial barriers caused by out-of-pocket health spending

explanation: Spot on! Rural areas actually struggle with a lack of enough hospitals and clinics, making the idea of 'surplus hospitals in every village' completely false. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h7)

question: Why is it helpful to involve traditional and religious leaders in community health strategies?

options.A: They hold strong influence over community attitudes and can help promote health-seeking behaviors
options.B: They can write legal prescriptions for controlled narcotic medications
options.C: They control the central government budget for foreign medical equipment
options.D: They are legally trained to replace licensed medical doctors in emergency surgery

explanation: Brilliant! Local leaders are deeply respected; partnering with them helps clear up cultural myths and encourages community members to embrace healthcare. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h7)

question: What is the official definition of reproductive health according to the broader health context?

options.A: The total absence of sexually transmitted infections in an adult population
options.B: A government program aimed at controlling population growth rates
options.C: A state of complete physical, mental, and social well-being in all matters of the reproductive system
options.D: The biological ability to conceive and bear children without medical help

explanation: Reproductive health covers total physical, mental, and social wellness regarding the reproductive system, rather than just lacking disease. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T6#GNS216_U1_T6_h1)

question: Why do nurses need to look beyond the hospital walls when caring for patients?

options.A: Clinical treatments alone are completely useless without government approval
options.B: Patients expect nurses to solve their personal family conflicts
options.C: Hospital regulations require documentation of a patient's financial status
options.D: External economic, social, and cultural forces deeply shape a person's health outcomes

explanation: You've got this! Remember that health doesn't start and stop at the hospital doors. A patient's daily life, money, and community heavily influence their healing. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T6#GNS216_U1_T6_h1)

question: What is a direct financial barrier to emergency obstetric care in poor communities?

options.A: Mandatory taxes on all pregnant women
options.B: Free distribution of essential obstetric medications
options.C: High transportation costs to reach the nearest health facility
options.D: Excessive availability of free community health centers

explanation: Lack of funds for transport often delays getting to the hospital during an obstetric emergency, worsening outcomes. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T6#GNS216_U1_T6_h2)

question: A pregnant woman misses her antenatal visits because she cannot afford transport or clinic fees. Which factor is mainly affecting her health?

options.A: Political party affiliation
options.B: Socio-economic factors
options.C: Cultural taboos
options.D: Genetic factors

explanation: Spot on! Financial struggles and poverty are classic examples of socio-economic factors that make it hard for patients to access care. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T6#GNS216_U1_T6_h2)

question: What is a common result of low health literacy when it comes to family planning?

options.A: Immediate adoption of modern birth control methods
options.B: Increased funding for community health education
options.C: Spread of myths and misconceptions about contraception
options.D: Better understanding of pregnancy danger signs

explanation: When health information is scarce or hard to understand, false stories and rumors easily take over. This is why our patient education role is so vital! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T6#GNS216_U1_T6_h3)

question: How does educating girls and women directly improve maternal health in a community?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for hospitals and clinics
options.B: It empowers women to recognize pregnancy danger signs and seek prompt medical care
options.C: It guarantees that every woman will become a qualified midwife
options.D: It prevents women from ever getting pregnant

explanation: Education is powerful! When women understand health risks, they can spot danger early and make smart choices for themselves and their babies. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T6#GNS216_U1_T6_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a harmful traditional practice affecting reproductive health?

options.A: Female genital mutilation
options.B: Exclusive breastfeeding for infants
options.C: Taboos against sex education
options.D: Child marriage

explanation: Exclusive breastfeeding is a globally recommended health practice, unlike mutilation or child marriage which cause harm. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T6#GNS216_U1_T6_h4)

question: Why can a strong family preference for male children negatively impact a mother's health?

options.A: It forces women into continuous pregnancies until a son is born, straining their bodies
options.B: It reduces the financial income of the father drastically
options.C: It causes hospitals to refuse treatment to female newborns
options.D: It encourages the use of modern contraceptives

explanation: Constant, closely spaced pregnancies driven by the pressure to have a son really wear down a mother's body and deplete her nutrients. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T6#GNS216_U1_T6_h4)

question: What is the main job of government policies in healthcare?

options.A: Deciding which patients get admitted to private rooms
options.B: Manufacturing all pharmaceutical drugs locally
options.C: Personally training every nurse and doctor in the country
options.D: Determining service prioritization, funding, and accessibility

explanation: Government policies set the rules for how money is shared and whether health services actually reach the people who need them. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T6#GNS216_U1_T6_h5)

question: How does political corruption directly hurt maternal and child health programs?

options.A: By building more primary healthcare centers
options.B: By diverting essential medical supplies and funds meant for public clinics
options.C: By lowering the cost of prescription drugs for pregnant women
options.D: By increasing the number of trained midwives in rural villages

explanation: Corruption steals resources meant for the sick, leaving public clinics without basic drugs, working equipment, or safe spaces for mothers. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T6#GNS216_U1_T6_h5)

question: Why should Nigerian nurses do health education in the community alongside bedside care?

options.A: To fulfill strict legal requirements set by international bodies
options.B: To help demystify cultural myths and educate people on safe reproductive practices
options.C: To replace doctors during hospital strikes and emergencies
options.D: To generate extra revenue for the hospital administration

explanation: Great nurses know healing happens outside the ward too! Community talks help clear up dangerous myths and guide people toward safe practices. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T6#GNS216_U1_T6_h6)

question: A nurse notices women in a village prefer risky home births due to tradition. What is the best first step?

options.A: Report all pregnant women in the village to the local police
options.B: Provide culturally sensitive education and build trust regarding hospital delivery benefits
options.C: Refuse to treat any woman who has previously given birth at home
options.D: Ignore the practice since culture cannot be influenced by health workers

explanation: Yarn true! Respecting people's culture while gently building trust is the best way to help them see the safety of hospital deliveries. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T6#GNS216_U1_T6_h6)

question: What does reproductive health cover according to standard health definitions?

options.A: Only the ability to bear children without medical complications
options.B: The prevention of sexually transmitted diseases in teenagers
options.C: The total absence of any infection in the pelvic organs
options.D: Complete physical, mental, and social well-being in all reproductive matters

explanation: Reproductive health is a broad state of complete well-being, not merely the absence of disease or infirmity in reproductive organs. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h1)

question: Why is the nurse considered a vital link in community reproductive health?

options.A: Nurses perform all surgical procedures related to reproductive organs
options.B: Nurses have the sole authority to distribute contraceptive drugs
options.C: Nurses connect community members to formal health institutions and provide primary care
options.D: Nurses write the national policies governing family planning services

explanation: Nurses work directly within communities and clinics, making them the primary bridge for education, prevention, and basic care delivery. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h1)

question: What is the main goal of preventive reproductive health services?

options.A: To treat infertility using modern assisted reproductive technology
options.B: To cure advanced stages of reproductive tract cancers
options.C: To stop health problems before they start through screening and education
options.D: To manage high-risk surgical emergencies in labor wards

explanation: Preventive services aim to intercept diseases early or stop them entirely using vaccines, screenings, and education. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h2)

question: Which nursing action best describes a promotive reproductive health service?

options.A: Suturing a perineal tear following a normal vaginal delivery
options.B: Performing a manual vacuum aspiration for an incomplete miscarriage
options.C: Leading a community health talk on proper menstrual hygiene
options.D: Prescribing antibiotics for a confirmed pelvic inflammatory disease

explanation: Promotive services involve general health education and encouraging positive wellness practices rather than treating active disease. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h2)

question: What is the primary objective of family planning counseling?

options.A: To eliminate population growth in developing nations completely
options.B: To force every woman of childbearing age to use hormonal contraception
options.C: To promote permanent surgical sterilization for all young couples
options.D: To help clients make informed choices about child spacing and family size

explanation: Family planning empowers clients with information to choose their preferred method safely and voluntarily. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h3)

question: A client expresses fear that an injectable contraceptive will cause permanent infertility. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: Agree that hormonal drugs permanently damage the womb and suggest avoiding them
options.B: Insist she takes the injection anyway because healthcare workers know best
options.C: Explain that fertility generally returns after the drug wears off, though it may take a few months
options.D: Tell the client that her fears are unfounded and scold her for listening to myths

explanation: Nurses must address client fears respectfully with accurate medical facts rather than dismissing or forcing them. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h3)

question: What is the main tool used by nurses during labor to track progress and detect complications early?

options.A: Glucometer
options.B: Partograph
options.C: Otoscope
options.D: Sphygmomanometer

explanation: The partograph is a graphic record of labor used to monitor maternal and fetal well-being and flag prolonged labor. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h4)

question: A woman who delivered a healthy baby six hours ago starts bleeding heavily, and her uterus feels soft and boggy. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Wait for two hours to see if the bleeding stops on its own
options.B: Leave the ward to call the senior consultant doctor immediately
options.C: Encourage the mother to stand up and walk around the room
options.D: Massage the uterus gently to stimulate contraction and expel clots

explanation: A soft, boggy uterus after delivery indicates uterine atony, which requires immediate fundal massage to stimulate contraction and reduce bleeding. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h4)

question: What is syndromic management of sexually transmitted infections?

options.A: Treating infections based on recognized groups of symptoms when lab tests are unavailable
options.B: Isolating infected patients in private hospital wards for weeks
options.C: Waiting for definitive blood culture results before starting any medication
options.D: Treating only the male partner in cases of recurrent vaginal discharge

explanation: Syndromic management allows prompt treatment of common STI symptoms during the initial clinic visit using standardized flowcharts. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h5)

question: Why is partner notification and treatment critical when managing a patient with an STI?

options.A: To prevent reinfection and break the ongoing cycle of transmission in the community
options.B: To ensure the hospital can collect double consultation fees from both clients
options.C: To punish the partner for bringing the infection into the relationship
options.D: To force both individuals to undergo permanent surgical sterilization

explanation: Treating only one partner leads to rapid reinfection when sexual contact resumes, making joint treatment necessary. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h5)

question: Which feature is most essential for a successful adolescent reproductive health clinic?

options.A: Charging high fees to discourage casual visits by teenagers
options.B: Youth-friendly services with strict privacy and non-judgmental staff
options.C: Mandatory reporting of all adolescent clinic visitors to their parents
options.D: Locating the clinic inside high school classrooms during lessons

explanation: Adolescents avoid health facilities if they fear moral judgment or lack of confidentiality from staff. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h6)

question: What is a major consequence when health workers judge teenagers seeking reproductive advice?

options.A: Adolescents immediately change their behavior and practice strict abstinence
options.B: Young people report the healthcare workers to international health bodies
options.C: Teenagers stop seeking professional help and turn to unsafe alternatives
options.D: Parents take over the health education role completely at home

explanation: Stigma and judgmental attitudes drive vulnerable youths away from clinics, leading to hidden risks like unsafe abortions. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h6)

question: What does informed consent require before a nurse or doctor performs a reproductive health procedure?

options.A: The hospital management approves the procedure during a board meeting
options.B: The client understands the risks, benefits, and alternatives and agrees voluntarily
options.C: The head of the family gives written permission on behalf of the client
options.D: The local community leader signs a clearance certificate

explanation: Informed consent is an ethical requirement ensuring the patient is fully aware and willing without coercion. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h7)

question: Which of the following actions represents a breach of nursing ethics in reproductive health?

options.A: Discussing a patient's private HIV test result with coworkers in the cafeteria
options.B: Providing confidential contraceptive counseling to an unmarried adult woman
options.C: Reporting a case of child abuse to the appropriate hospital social worker
options.D: Refusing to perform female genital mutilation because it is harmful

explanation: Sharing private patient information outside the direct care team violates confidentiality and patient rights. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h7)

question: What is the main difference between laws and ethics in nursing practice?

options.A: Laws set the minimum legal boundaries while ethics guide moral excellence
options.B: Ethics carry prison sentences while laws only result in job loss
options.C: Ethics are written by parliament while laws are created by hospitals
options.D: Laws apply only to doctors while ethics apply only to nurses

explanation: Laws establish mandatory rules with legal penalties, whereas ethics provide a moral framework for striving toward fair and compassionate care. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h1)

question: Why do nurses need to understand both the law and professional ethics?

options.A: To bypass the need for patient consent during emergencies
options.B: To avoid breaking the law while giving kind, respectful care
options.C: To ensure hospitals never face financial audits
options.D: To successfully prosecute patients who break hospital rules

explanation: Knowing both legal rules and ethical principles protects you from trouble while making sure your patients always feel respected and cared for! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h1)

question: Which ethical principle is all about actively doing good and helping your patient?

options.A: Beneficence
options.B: Autonomy
options.C: Veracity
options.D: Justice

explanation: Think of Beneficence as your active duty to do good and boost the health and well-being of everyone in your care. You've got this! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h2)

question: A pregnant patient decides to refuse a treatment you recommended. You respect her choice. Which principle are you showing?

options.A: Non-maleficence
options.B: Autonomy
options.C: Paternalism
options.D: Justice

explanation: Autonomy is all about respecting a patient's right to make their own informed choices about their body. Their health, their say! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h2)

question: Which two major legal codes deal with criminal law across Nigeria?

options.A: Constitution and Tax Act
options.B: Civil Code and Labour Code
options.C: Family Law and Sharia Supreme Act
options.D: Criminal Code and Penal Code

explanation: In Nigeria, the Criminal Code is used in the southern states while the Penal Code covers the northern states. Both handle serious legal offenses! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h3)

question: Why might health policies and laws look a bit different depending on which Nigerian state you are working in?

options.A: Due to regional differences in laws, culture, and state-level guidelines
options.B: Because nurses are only permitted to follow international laws
options.C: Because the federal government has no ministries dedicated to health
options.D: Due to a complete lack of any written healthcare policies in the country

explanation: Nigeria's federal system means local cultures and state laws can influence how national health guidelines are put into practice. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h3)

question: What are the three core ingredients needed for valid informed consent?

options.A: Payment of all hospital bills in advance
options.B: Written signature from the village head and husband
options.C: Voluntary agreement, full information, and mental capacity
options.D: Verbal agreement witnessed by two police officers

explanation: For consent to be valid, the patient must agree freely, understand the risks and benefits, and be mentally capable of making the choice. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h4)

question: An adult female patient refuses a procedure, but her husband insists you must do it anyway. What should you do?

options.A: Discharge the patient immediately without explanation
options.B: Obey the husband because he is the head of the household
options.C: Respect the patient's autonomous refusal and maintain her confidentiality
options.D: Perform the procedure secretly without the patient knowing

explanation: Every competent adult has the final say over her own body. A patient's right to refuse always overrides outside family demands. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h4)

question: Under most Nigerian laws, what is the main legal exception that allows for an abortion?

options.A: If the family cannot afford a child
options.B: When requested by the husband
options.C: If the pregnancy occurs during school term
options.D: To save the life of the pregnant woman

explanation: Nigerian law is very strict regarding abortion, but saving the mother's life is recognized as a legal exception. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h5)

question: A patient comes to the emergency ward bleeding heavily from an unsafe abortion. What is your immediate priority?

options.A: Provide immediate lifesaving emergency care to stabilize the patient
options.B: Report the patient to the police before offering any medical treatment
options.C: Wait for a court order before administering intravenous fluids
options.D: Refuse care based on personal moral objections to abortion

explanation: Saving a life always comes first! As a nurse, your duty is to stabilize and treat your patient in an emergency, no matter the circumstances. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h5)

question: What is a major ethical debate surrounding Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART) like IVF?

options.A: Guaranteed elimination of all genetic diseases at birth
options.B: Compulsory fertility treatment for all citizens
options.C: Fair access and what to do with unused embryos
options.D: Total absence of any legal regulations worldwide

explanation: ART often raises tough questions about fairness in who can afford it and how leftover embryos should be handled ethically. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h6)

question: Why is clear, informed consent so important before a couple starts IVF treatment?

options.A: Because nurses are legally required to adopt any resulting children
options.B: Because it prevents patients from ever experiencing natural conception again
options.C: Because decisions must be made early about storing or donating leftover embryos
options.D: Because IVF is completely illegal under all Nigerian federal statutes

explanation: Since IVF creates extra embryos, couples must agree in advance on what will happen to them to avoid future legal and emotional conflicts. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h6)

question: What usually stops teenagers from visiting clinics for reproductive health issues?

options.A: Mandatory free distribution of supplies in schools
options.B: A complete absence of hospitals in urban centers
options.C: Fear of being judged and a lack of privacy from staff
options.D: Strict laws requiring adolescent doctors for teenage patients

explanation: Teens often avoid seeking help because they are scared healthcare workers will gossip, judge them, or break their trust. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h7)

question: How does promising strict privacy change how teenagers use reproductive health services?

options.A: It guarantees that teenagers will never experience health complications
options.B: It completely replaces the need for parental guidance at home
options.C: It encourages teens to seek early advice, testing, and care
options.D: It legally forces parents to abandon their teenage children

explanation: When teens know their visit is confidential, they feel safe enough to get timely checkups, contraception, or treatment when they need it. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h7)

question: What do we call a nurse's ability to understand and respect a patient's cultural beliefs while giving great care?

options.A: Cultural competence
options.B: Clinical detachment
options.C: Legal negligence
options.D: Medical paternalism

explanation: Cultural competence helps you bridge cultural and religious gaps so you can care for your patients safely and respectfully. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h8)

question: Which of these is NOT something a nurse should do when dealing with harmful traditional practices?

options.A: Performing the harmful traditional practice to please community elders
options.B: Offering supportive counseling to women resisting the practice
options.C: Providing respectful health education on the dangers involved
options.D: Reporting illegal procedures or child abuse to the right authorities

explanation: As a nurse, your first loyalty is to your patient's safety. You should never take part in harmful traditional practices, no matter the local pressure! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h8)

question: What is one of the main goals of a nurse acting as a patient advocate in reproductive health?

options.A: Prosecuting doctors who violate hospital budgets
options.B: Writing new national criminal codes in parliament
options.C: Protecting patient rights and pushing for fair access to safe care
options.D: Setting insurance premiums for fertility clinics

explanation: As an advocate, you stand up for your patients' rights, fight against unfair treatment, and help them access the care they deserve. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h9)

question: You notice low-income women at the antenatal clinic aren't getting family planning info. What is the best advocacy action?

options.A: Working with the team to set up clear education sessions for all patients
options.B: Telling the affected patients to find a different hospital on their own
options.C: Ignoring the issue because it's not bedside nursing work
options.D: Reporting the patients to hospital management for asking questions

explanation: Good advocacy means speaking up and working with your team to make sure every single patient gets equal access to health information. Great job! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h9)

question: What is the primary function of the external female reproductive organs?

options.A: Protect internal organs from infection
options.B: Produce major female sex hormones
options.C: Produce mature eggs every month
options.D: Nourish a growing baby during pregnancy

explanation: The external genitalia act as a physical barrier to shield delicate internal reproductive tracts from pathogens and trauma. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h1)

question: Why is it important for you as a nurse to understand female reproductive anatomy?

options.A: To prescribe hormonal contraceptives without a doctor
options.B: To diagnose sexually transmitted infections by sight alone
options.C: To accurately assess health problems and provide patient care
options.D: To perform surgical procedures independently in the clinic

explanation: Spot on! Knowing your anatomy helps you spot when something isn't quite right, chat easily with your patients, and guide them through different stages of life with confidence. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h1)

question: Which external structure is a small, highly sensitive erectile organ?

options.A: Labia majora
options.B: Mons pubis
options.C: Clitoris
options.D: Bartholin gland

explanation: The clitoris sits at the top of the labia minora and contains many nerve endings for sexual sensation. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h2)

question: What is the main function of the Bartholin glands?

options.A: Release hormones that trigger puberty
options.B: Protect the pubic bone from physical shock
options.C: Secrete lubricating mucus into the vestibule
options.D: Produce eggs during the monthly cycle

explanation: Bartholin glands sit beside the vaginal opening and produce mucus to keep the mucosal surface moist. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h2)

question: What are the folds inside the vaginal wall that allow for stretching called?

options.A: Fimbriae
options.B: Villi
options.C: Cilia
options.D: Rugae

explanation: Rugae are ridges of muscle and mucous membrane that let the vaginal canal expand greatly during birth and intercourse. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h3)

question: Why is the normal acidic environment of the vagina important?

options.A: It softens the hymen before puberty
options.B: It prevents harmful bacteria from growing
options.C: It speeds up the movement of sperm cells
options.D: It helps the cervix open during labor

explanation: Normal vaginal acidity creates a hostile home for bad bacteria and yeast, protecting the reproductive tract from infections. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h3)

question: Which layer of the uterus is shed monthly during menstruation?

options.A: Epimetrium
options.B: Perimetrium
options.C: Myometrium
options.D: Endometrium

explanation: The endometrium is the inner lining that builds up with blood and nutrients, then sheds if pregnancy does not occur. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h4)

question: A woman in labor is having strong contractions. Which part of her uterine wall is doing all that hard work?

options.A: Perimetrium
options.B: Endometrium
options.C: Myometrium
options.D: Cervical os

explanation: Spot on! The myometrium is made of tough, powerful smooth muscle designed to push the baby safely into the world. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h4)

question: Where does fertilization of the egg by a sperm cell usually take place?

options.A: Within the lower cervical canal
options.B: Inside the main cavity of the uterus
options.C: On the outer surface of the ovary
options.D: Ampulla of the fallopian tube

explanation: The wider ampulla section of the fallopian tube provides the right space and environment for the sperm to meet and fertilize the egg. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h5)

question: What is the role of the fimbriae at the end of the fallopian tubes?

options.A: Catch the released egg from the ovary
options.B: Produce estrogen and progesterone
options.C: Secrete mucus to block foreign bacteria
options.D: Anchor the uterus to the pelvic wall

explanation: Fimbriae are fringe-like fingers that wave over the ovary at ovulation to sweep the egg inside the fallopian tube. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h5)

question: What are the two primary functions of the ovaries?

options.A: Digest nutrients and absorb water
options.B: Filter waste and produce urine
options.C: Pump blood through the pelvic floor
options.D: Produce eggs and secrete sex hormones

explanation: Ovaries serve as both glands that make hormones (estrogen and progesterone) and storage sites for female eggs. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h6)

question: Which part of the ovary holds the developing egg follicles?

options.A: Medulla
options.B: Cortex
options.C: Fimbria
options.D: Fundus

explanation: The outer layer, or cortex, contains ovarian follicles in different stages of growth and maturation. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h6)

question: Which main artery supplies blood directly to the uterus?

options.A: Brachial artery
options.B: Uterine artery
options.C: Renal artery
options.D: Femoral artery

explanation: The uterine artery, branching from the internal iliac artery, brings oxygen-rich blood directly to the uterine walls. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h7)

question: Why do you need to understand how the lymphatic system drains the reproductive organs?

options.A: It explains how menstrual cramps travel down to the legs
options.B: It shows how vaginal pH changes during a bacterial infection
options.C: It dictates the correct dosage for oral contraceptive pills
options.D: It helps track how pelvic cancers can spread through the body

explanation: Exactly! Cancer cells can hitch a ride through lymph vessels to nearby lymph nodes, so knowing these pathways is super important for staging and treatment. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h7)

question: A patient tells you she feels a heavy dragging sensation in her pelvis after having three children. What structures are likely stretched or weakened?

options.A: The Bartholin glands located near the vaginal opening
options.B: Ligaments and pelvic floor muscles supporting the uterus
options.C: The fimbriae at the ends of the fallopian tubes
options.D: The fallopian tubes where fertilization usually occurs

explanation: You're doing great! When pelvic floor muscles and support ligaments get stretched over time, they can lead to uterine prolapse, causing that heavy, dragging feeling. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h8)

question: Which of these is NOT something a nurse would typically do regarding female reproductive health?

options.A: Surgically repairing damaged uterine tissue during a caesarean section
options.B: Educating patients on normal menstrual cycles and warning signs
options.C: Recognizing signs of infection or inflammation in the vaginal canal
options.D: Assisting physicians or midwives during a routine pelvic physical exam

explanation: Spot on! Performing surgery is for doctors and surgeons—your core nursing superpowers include assessing, educating, and supporting patients every step of the way. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h8)

question: What is the primary function of the male reproductive system?

options.A: Filter waste products from the blood
options.B: Produce, sustain, and transport sperm
options.C: Digest complex dietary proteins
options.D: Regulate total body water balance

explanation: The primary role of the male reproductive system is the creation and delivery of sperm cells for reproduction alongside hormone production. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T2#GNS216_U2_T2_h1)

question: Which set of organs belongs to the internal structures of the male reproductive system?

options.A: Prepuce and glans penis
options.B: Scrotal skin and dartos muscle
options.C: Testes and accessory glands
options.D: Scrotum and penile shaft

explanation: Internal structures include the testes, duct system, and accessory glands, while the scrotum and penis are external. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T2#GNS216_U2_T2_h1)

question: Where does spermatogenesis take place inside the testes?

options.A: Seminiferous tubules
options.B: Tunica albuginea
options.C: Prostatic urethra
options.D: Bulbourethral glands

explanation: The tiny coiled seminiferous tubules inside the testicular lobules are the exact sites where sperm cells are produced. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T2#GNS216_U2_T2_h2)

question: Why is the scrotum located outside the pelvic cavity?

options.A: To allow easier access for lymphatic drainage
options.B: To protect the bladder from direct physical trauma
options.C: To shorten the pathway of the ejaculatory duct
options.D: To keep the testes cooler than core body temperature

explanation: Normal sperm production requires a temperature a few degrees lower than standard internal body temperature, which the hanging scrotum provides. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T2#GNS216_U2_T2_h2)

question: What is the main function of the epididymis?

options.A: Neutralize acidic urine in the urethra
options.B: Allow sperm to mature and gain motility
options.C: Secrete the majority of seminal fluid
options.D: Produce primary male sex hormones

explanation: Sperm entering the epididymis are not yet able to swim; they store there while maturing and acquiring motility. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T2#GNS216_U2_T2_h3)

question: A patient asks what happens to sperm immediately after they are created in the seminiferous tubules. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: They travel to the epididymis to mature.
options.B: They enter the prostate gland for activation.
options.C: They mix with urine in the urinary bladder.
options.D: They travel directly out through the penile skin.

explanation: After leaving the seminiferous tubules, sperm move into the duct system and head directly into the epididymis. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T2#GNS216_U2_T2_h3)

question: Which structure travels inside the spermatic cord along with nerves and blood vessels?

options.A: Seminal vesicle
options.B: Bulbourethral duct
options.C: Prostatic utricle
options.D: Vas deferens

explanation: The vas deferens is a primary component of the spermatic cord as it ascends from the scrotum into the pelvic cavity. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T2#GNS216_U2_T2_h4)

question: A male patient is diagnosed with an indirect inguinal hernia. Which nearby anatomical structure is most at risk of compression within the inguinal canal?

options.A: Spermatic cord contents
options.B: Corporis cavernosa
options.C: Urinary bladder neck
options.D: Bulbourethral glands

explanation: Because the spermatic cord passes directly through the inguinal canal, a hernia in this area can compress the vessels and nerves within the cord. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T2#GNS216_U2_T2_h4)

question: Which accessory gland produces a clear mucus to neutralize acidic urine in the urethra before ejaculation?

options.A: Seminal vesicle
options.B: Bulbourethral gland
options.C: Testicular lobule
options.D: Prostate gland

explanation: The bulbourethral glands secrete a pre-ejaculatory fluid that cleans and neutralizes the urethral pathway. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T2#GNS216_U2_T2_h5)

question: What is the primary contribution of the seminal vesicles to semen?

options.A: Acidic waste products for disposal
