options.B: Perform the rectal temperature quickly and gently with lots of lubrication
options.C: Ask the patient to insert the thermometer herself to avoid causing pain
options.D: Explain that rectal temperatures are contraindicated to protect the surgical repair

explanation: Any instrument placed in the rectum can damage the fresh surgical repair site and cause the surgery to fail. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h8)

question: What is a common potential complication following rectovaginal fistula repair?

options.A: Sudden hair loss
options.B: Fistula recurrence
options.C: Permanent total blindness
options.D: Enlargement of the liver

explanation: Due to tension, infection, or poor tissue healing, the fistula can sometimes reopen, requiring further medical evaluation. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h9)

question: What is the purpose of recommending pelvic floor exercises in the long-term recovery phase?

options.A: To help restore and strengthen anal sphincter tone
options.B: To speed up the healing of abdominal skin scars
options.C: To increase the production of digestive enzymes
options.D: To prevent the development of high blood pressure

explanation: Strengthening the pelvic floor muscles improves overall continence and pelvic support after surgery. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h9)

question: What is cervicitis?

options.A: Infection of the uterine lining
options.B: Inflammation of the cervix
options.C: Overgrowth of normal vaginal flora
options.D: Scarring of the fallopian tubes

explanation: Cervicitis refers specifically to the inflammation of the mucosal and epithelial tissues of the cervix. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T14#GNS216_U5_T14_h1)

question: How does chronic cervicitis mainly differ from acute cervicitis?

options.A: It involves long-standing immune cell changes in the tissue.
options.B: It presents with sudden, severe pus-like discharge.
options.C: It never requires any medical or nursing intervention.
options.D: It is always caused by viral agents rather than bacteria.

explanation: Think of acute as sudden and angry with quick pus, while chronic is a longer-lasting, low-grade immune response in the tissue. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T14#GNS216_U5_T14_h1)

question: Which common bacterium that lives inside cells is frequently responsible for cervicitis?

options.A: Staphylococcus aureus
options.B: Escherichia coli
options.C: Pseudomonas aeruginosa
options.D: Chlamydia trachomatis

explanation: Chlamydia trachomatis is a well-known bug that loves to hide inside cervical cells and cause inflammation. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T14#GNS216_U5_T14_h2)

question: What is a common non-infectious cause of cervical inflammation?

options.A: Increased dietary intake of refined sugars
options.B: Chemical spermicides and barrier devices
options.C: Normal fluctuations in monthly estrogen levels
options.D: Inadequate daily fluid consumption

explanation: Not all inflammation comes from germs! Things like chemical spermicides or barrier devices can irritate the delicate cervical tissue. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T14#GNS216_U5_T14_h2)

question: What is the name of the vulnerable zone where columnar and squamous epithelium meet on the cervix?

options.A: Peritoneal cavity
options.B: Transformation zone
options.C: Vaginal fornix
options.D: Endometrial cavity

explanation: The transformation zone is the specific anatomical junction where different types of cervical cells meet, making it highly susceptible to infections and inflammation. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T14#GNS216_U5_T14_h3)

question: Why does an inflamed cervix tend to bleed easily during an examination?

options.A: Complete destruction of the underlying muscle layer
options.B: Fragile tissues and tiny blood vessels opening up from inflammation
options.C: Rapid overproduction of red blood cells by the cervix
options.D: Severe blood clotting disorders throughout the body

explanation: When tissue is inflamed, blood rushes to the area and the vessels become delicate, meaning even a gentle touch can cause spotting. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T14#GNS216_U5_T14_h3)

question: Which symptom is a classic presentation of cervical friability in cervicitis?

options.A: Complete cessation of menses
options.B: Inability to control urination
options.C: Postcoital bleeding
options.D: Severe lower back stiffness

explanation: Because inflamed cervical tissue is very fragile, contact during sexual intercourse frequently causes postcoital spotting or bleeding. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T14#GNS216_U5_T14_h4)

question: A female client reports a thick vaginal discharge and spotting after intercourse. Which condition should you suspect first as a nurse?

options.A: Ovarian cysts
options.B: Uterine fibroids
options.C: Cervicitis
options.D: Cystitis

explanation: Unusual discharge paired with bleeding after sex are classic clues pointing right to cervical inflammation. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T14#GNS216_U5_T14_h4)

question: What is the best and most accurate lab test used to confirm chlamydia and gonorrhea infections of the cervix?

options.A: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate
options.B: Basic metabolic serum panel
options.C: Nucleic acid amplification test (NAAT)
options.D: Complete blood count with differential

explanation: NAAT is the gold-standard test because it is super sensitive at picking up bacterial DNA from a simple swab or urine sample. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T14#GNS216_U5_T14_h5)

question: What key visual finding does a clinician look for on the cervix during a speculum exam for acute cervicitis?

options.A: Pus-like discharge and tissue that bleeds easily
options.B: Complete closure of the internal cervical opening
options.C: Large fluid-filled cysts across the surface
options.D: Pale, dry, and glistening epithelial layers

explanation: During an exam, an angry, infected cervix often shows pus draining out and tissue that is fragile and bleeds at a touch. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T14#GNS216_U5_T14_h5)

question: Why are antibiotics often started right away before lab results are even back?

options.A: To reduce the financial cost of laboratory diagnostic supplies
options.B: To completely eliminate the need for any follow-up testing
options.C: To cure viral infections like herpes simplex immediately
options.D: To stop the infection from spreading upward into the reproductive tract

explanation: Starting treatment fast prevents the infection from traveling up into the uterus and fallopian tubes, avoiding bigger problems later. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T14#GNS216_U5_T14_h6)

question: What essential instruction must be given about sexual partners when treating infectious cervicitis?

options.A: Partners can continue unprotected intercourse during the treatment week.
options.B: Partners only need treatment if they develop severe abdominal pain.
options.C: Only partners with visible symptoms need prescription medication.
options.D: Sexual partners must be checked and treated at the same time.

explanation: Treating partners together is the only way to stop the annoying ping-pong game of passing the infection back and forth! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T14#GNS216_U5_T14_h6)

question: What major upper reproductive tract condition can happen if cervicitis is left untreated?

options.A: Benign prostatic hyperplasia
options.B: Polycystic ovary syndrome
options.C: Endometriosis of the bowel
options.D: Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID)

explanation: If lower tract infections aren't cleared, they can creep upward and turn into pelvic inflammatory disease (PID). [learn more](GNS216_U5_T14#GNS216_U5_T14_h7)

question: How does untreated cervicitis affect a patient's risk of contracting HIV?

options.A: It grants temporary immunity against sexually transmitted viruses.
options.B: It decreases the risk because white blood cells destroy the virus.
options.C: It increases the risk because the mucosal tissue is broken and immune cells are rushed to the area.
options.D: It has no measurable impact on viral transmission rates.

explanation: Inflamed, fragile tissue plus a gathering of immune cells gives viruses like HIV an easier pathway into the body. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T14#GNS216_U5_T14_h7)

question: What is the most important piece of advice to give a patient taking a 7-day course of antibiotics for cervicitis?

options.A: Share the remaining pills with your partner to save money.
options.B: Double the next dose if you forget to take one pill.
options.C: Stop taking the pills immediately if mild stomach upset occurs.
options.D: Finish all the medication even if you start feeling better early.

explanation: Always remind patients to complete their full dose! Stopping early can cause the infection to bounce back stronger. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T14#GNS216_U5_T14_h8)

question: Which of these is NOT something a nurse should tell a patient being treated for infectious cervicitis?

options.A: Use barrier methods consistently to help prevent reinfection.
options.B: Make sure your sexual partner is treated at the same time.
options.C: Stop taking your medicine as soon as the discharge lessens.
options.D: Avoid having sex until your treatment is fully completed.

explanation: Never advise stopping meds early just because symptoms fade. They must finish the entire course! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T14#GNS216_U5_T14_h8)

question: What actually are cervical polyps?

options.A: Congenital malformations
options.B: Infectious cysts of the vagina
options.C: Benign growths on the cervix
options.D: Malignant tumors of the uterus

explanation: Don't worry, these are non-cancerous growths! They just form on the cervical tissue, meaning they are benign. You've got this! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T15#GNS216_U5_T15_h1)

question: Why do doctors still check cervical polyps even though they are usually harmless?

options.A: To stop chronic pelvic pain
options.B: To prevent permanent infertility
options.C: To rule out potential malignancy
options.D: To cure underlying bacterial infections

explanation: Even though most polyps are completely harmless, doctors always check them just to be 100% sure there are no hidden cancer cells. Better safe than sorry! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T15#GNS216_U5_T15_h1)

question: Which hormone is mostly linked to the growth of cervical polyps?

options.A: Insulin
options.B: Thyroxine
options.C: Estrogen
options.D: Cortisol

explanation: Estrogen is the main driver here! Higher levels can stimulate the cervical lining to overgrow and form a polyp. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T15#GNS216_U5_T15_h2)

question: How can chronic (long-term) inflammation lead to a cervical polyp?

options.A: It destroys local nerve endings
options.B: It directly causes malignant cell transformation
options.C: It triggers abnormal tissue proliferation over time
options.D: It blocks the production of estrogen

explanation: Think of it like skin getting a callus from constant friction. Ongoing irritation makes the cervical tissue grow extra cells, forming a polyp over time. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T15#GNS216_U5_T15_h2)

question: What is a very common sign that someone might have a cervical polyp?

options.A: High fever and chills
options.B: Postcoital bleeding
options.C: Inability to control urination
options.D: Severe lower abdominal pain

explanation: Polyps are quite delicate. When friction happens during sex, they easily get irritated and can cause a little bit of light bleeding. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T15#GNS216_U5_T15_h3)

question: A patient comes in complaining of light spotting between her periods and after sex. Which condition is most likely?

options.A: Uterine fibroid
options.B: Pelvic inflammatory disease
options.C: Ovarian cyst
options.D: Cervical polyp

explanation: Spotting between periods or right after intercourse is a classic giveaway for fragile cervical polyps! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T15#GNS216_U5_T15_h3)

question: Which simple tool does a healthcare provider use to actually see a cervical polyp?

options.A: Stethoscope
options.B: Otoscope
options.C: Speculum
options.D: Sphygmomanometer

explanation: A speculum gently opens the vaginal canal so the doctor can get a clear, direct look at the cervix. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T15#GNS216_U5_T15_h4)

question: Why do doctors send the tissue from a removed cervical polyp to the lab?

options.A: To measure hormone receptor levels
options.B: To determine the patient's blood type
options.C: To confirm it is benign and rule out cancer
options.D: To check for viral resistance to antibiotics

explanation: Sending it to the lab is just a routine way to double-check under a microscope that everything is truly non-cancerous. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T15#GNS216_U5_T15_h4)

question: What is the minor procedure called when a doctor removes a cervical polyp?

options.A: Polypectomy
options.B: Salpingectomy
options.C: Hysterectomy
options.D: Oophorectomy

explanation: Easy to remember: 'polyp' + 'ectomy' (meaning removal) gives you polypectomy! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T15#GNS216_U5_T15_h5)

question: Why would a doctor remove a small cervical polyp even if it isn't causing any symptoms?

options.A: To restore normal ovarian function
options.B: To stop potential future bleeding and permit testing
options.C: To prevent the spread of severe bacterial infection
options.D: To enlarge the cervical opening for childbirth

explanation: Taking it out stops random spotting before it starts and lets the lab test the tissue just to be completely safe. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T15#GNS216_U5_T15_h5)

question: What is the best advice for a nurse to give a patient who just had a cervical polypectomy?

options.A: Expect heavy bleeding equivalent to a heavy period
options.B: Avoid sexual intercourse and tampons for a short time
options.C: Douching daily is required to prevent local infection
options.D: Remain on complete bed rest for one full week

explanation: Giving the cervix a little break from anything inserted vaginally lets the small surgical site heal up nicely and safely. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T15#GNS216_U5_T15_h6)

question: A patient calls three days after her polypectomy reporting mild lower belly cramps and very light pink spotting. What should the nurse say?

options.A: Schedule an emergency surgical re-exploration
options.B: Advise her to start taking oral antibiotics right away
options.C: Instruct her to report immediately to the emergency room
options.D: Reassure her that this is a normal, expected finding

explanation: A little bit of cramping and light spotting is totally normal after the cervix has been touched or treated. Just reassure and comfort her! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T15#GNS216_U5_T15_h6)

question: Which part of the female reproductive system is the cervix?

options.A: The lower part of the uterus connecting to the vagina
options.B: The muscular wall of the main uterine body
options.C: The inner lining where a fertilized egg implants
options.D: The coiled tubes that transport eggs to the uterus

explanation: Spot on! The cervix forms the lower, cylindrical neck of the uterus that opens right into the vaginal canal. You've got this! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T16#GNS216_U5_T16_h1)

question: Why do nurses care about catching cervical irritation early?

options.A: It prevents simple discomfort from progressing to chronic or ascending infections.
options.B: It immediately normalizes hormonal fluctuations during the menstrual cycle.
options.C: It guarantees that surgical intervention will never be required.
options.D: It completely eliminates the future risk of all pelvic inflammatory diseases.

explanation: Exactly! Catching inflammation early stops it from traveling up into the upper reproductive tract where it can cause bigger problems. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T16#GNS216_U5_T16_h1)

question: What is the meeting point between the ectocervix and the endocervical canal called?

options.A: The myometrial junction
options.B: The fundal attachment
options.C: The transformation zone
options.D: The pelvic floor arch

explanation: Spot on! It's called the transformation zone—a busy area where different types of cells meet and undergo active changes. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T16#GNS216_U5_T16_h2)

question: Why is the transformation zone easily prone to irritation?

options.A: It has a very thick layer of hard skin cells that easily trap heat.
options.B: It experiences constant muscular contractions during the menstrual period.
options.C: It features active cell transitions that make it vulnerable to external factors.
options.D: It lacks any protective mucus layer to shield it from normal bacteria.

explanation: Correct! Because cells are actively changing and meeting right there, this zone is extra sensitive to infections and friction. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T16#GNS216_U5_T16_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a common cause of cervical irritation?

options.A: Chemical exposure from scented douches
options.B: Mechanical friction during intercourse
options.C: Infectious microorganisms like chlamydia
options.D: Eating high-sodium processed foods

explanation: You got it! Eating salty food won't irritate your cervix, but harsh chemicals, friction, and infections definitely can. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T16#GNS216_U5_T16_h3)

question: A menopausal patient has vaginal spotting and mild burning. What is the most likely cause of her cervical sensitivity?

options.A: Hyperactive cellular growth in the transformation zone
options.B: Frequent use of harsh chemical douches for hygiene
options.C: Lower estrogen levels causing thinning and drying of mucosal tissue
options.D: Increased production of thick mucus blocking the cervical canal

explanation: Well done! After menopause, lower estrogen makes the tissues thinner, drier, and much easier to irritate. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T16#GNS216_U5_T16_h3)

question: What is a classic sign of cervical irritation that often shows up after sexual intercourse?

options.A: Severe lower back stiffness
options.B: Post-coital bleeding
options.C: Intermittent abdominal swelling
options.D: Sudden loss of bladder control

explanation: Spot on! When the cervix is inflamed and fragile, any physical touch or rubbing during sex can easily trigger light bleeding. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T16#GNS216_U5_T16_h4)

question: Why might some patients with cervical irritation feel absolutely no symptoms at all?

options.A: The inflammatory process can remain mild and localized without triggering pain receptors.
options.B: Hormones in the vagina completely block any physical sensation of swelling.
options.C: The body instantly neutralizes all bacterial toxins before they reach the surface.
options.D: Nerve endings in the cervix are purely motor and never transmit sensory signals.

explanation: Exactly! Mild inflammation often stays quiet without setting off pain signals, which is why regular screening tests are so important for women's health. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T16#GNS216_U5_T16_h4)

question: Which test is primarily used to collect cellular samples for cervical cancer screening?

options.A: Pelvic ultrasound
options.B: Complete blood count
options.C: Pap smear
options.D: Urinalysis strip

explanation: Correct! A Pap smear gently collects cells from the transformation zone to check for any early, unusual changes. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T16#GNS216_U5_T16_h5)

question: A nurse is getting a patient ready for a speculum exam. What is the best way to help her prepare?

options.A: Instructing the patient to hold her breath whenever the speculum is opened
options.B: Explaining the procedure step-by-step and encouraging relaxation to reduce discomfort
options.C: Administering a strong local anesthetic gel directly onto the outer cervix
options.D: Placing the patient flat on her back with legs extended straight out

explanation: Spot on! Good communication and a calm, reassuring approach help ease anxiety and relax pelvic muscles, making the exam much easier. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T16#GNS216_U5_T16_h5)

question: What is the main goal of medical treatment for an infectious cervical irritation?

options.A: Eliminating the underlying pathogen with targeted medications
options.B: Numbing the pelvic nerve endings to eliminate pain sensations
options.C: Permanently removing the cervix to stop future infections
options.D: Increasing local hormone production through oral supplements

explanation: You got it! To fix an infection, we find out what germ is causing it and hit it with the right medication. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T16#GNS216_U5_T16_h6)

question: Why do sexual partners sometimes need treatment too when a patient has an infection?

options.A: To prevent passing the infection back and forth between partners
options.B: To ensure the patient takes all prescribed medication on schedule
options.C: To strengthen the partner's immune system against viral mutations
options.D: To stop the partner from experiencing sudden hormonal imbalances

explanation: Spot on! Many infections don't show symptoms in partners, so treating both prevents the annoying cycle of passing it right back. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T16#GNS216_U5_T16_h6)

question: Which hygiene practice should nurses advise patients to avoid to protect their cervix?

options.A: Using scented vaginal douches and chemical sprays
options.B: Washing the external vulva with plain warm water
options.C: Wearing loose-fitting cotton undergarments daily
options.D: Changing sanitary pads frequently during menstruation

explanation: Correct! Douching and scented products mess with the vagina's natural balance and easily irritate delicate tissues. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T16#GNS216_U5_T16_h7)

question: How do barrier contraceptives help protect against cervical irritation?

options.A: They physically block infectious microorganisms from reaching the cervical mucosa.
options.B: They permanently seal the transformation zone to stop cellular changes.
options.C: They eliminate all normal bacteria living inside the reproductive tract.
options.D: They automatically increase natural estrogen levels in the vaginal canal.

explanation: Well done! Barrier methods like condoms act like a shield, stopping germs from making direct contact with the cervix. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T16#GNS216_U5_T16_h7)

question: What is another common medical name for cervical erosion?

options.A: Cervical carcinoma
options.B: Cervical ectropion
options.C: Cervical dysplasia
options.D: Cervical stenosis

explanation: You will often hear cervical erosion called cervical ectropion in the clinic. It just means the inner cells of the cervix have moved outward a bit. You've got this! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h1)

question: Why can the word 'erosion' be a bit confusing for this condition?

options.A: The condition only affects postmenopausal women
options.B: It always causes complete destruction of the cervix
options.C: The outer cells grow inward rather than outward
options.D: The tissue is not actually worn away or ulcerated

explanation: Even though we call it 'erosion', there is no actual sore or wound on the cervix. It is just a shift in where the normal cells sit. Don't let the scary name trick you! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h1)

question: Which hormone is mainly responsible for pushing those delicate inner cervical cells outward?

options.A: Estrogen
options.B: Thyroxine
options.C: Insulin
options.D: Progesterone

explanation: Estrogen is the key player here! High levels of estrogen stimulate the inner cervical cells to grow and push outward onto the surface. Great job remembering your reproductive hormones. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h2)

question: What type of cells normally cover the outer part (ectocervix) of a healthy cervix?

options.A: Stratified squamous epithelium
options.B: Transitional epithelium
options.C: Simple columnar epithelium
options.D: Pseudostratified ciliated epithelium

explanation: The outer cervix is covered by tough stratified squamous cells. They act like a strong shield against friction and the natural acidity of the vagina. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h2)

question: Which of these everyday life stages is a major trigger for cervical ectropion?

options.A: Hypothyroidism
options.B: Osteoporosis
options.C: Pregnancy
options.D: Menopause

explanation: Pregnancy floods the body with high levels of estrogen, which commonly brings out or worsens cervical ectropion. It's a normal physiological change during this time! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h3)

question: A patient asks why she noticed cervical changes after starting a new oral contraceptive pill. What is the best way to explain it?

options.A: The pill permanently scars the muscular walls of the uterus.
options.B: The pill causes the outer cervical skin to become very dry and crack open.
options.C: The hormone estrogen in the pill causes inner cervical cells to shift outward.
options.D: The pill creates a bacterial infection that eats away at the outer cervix.

explanation: Birth control pills contain estrogen, which signals the inner cervical cells to expand outward. Explaining this simply to your patients helps ease their worries completely! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h3)

question: What is the most common symptom a patient with cervical ectropion might notice?

options.A: Severe pelvic pain
options.B: Postcoital bleeding
options.C: Complete cessation of menses
options.D: Foul-smelling green discharge

explanation: Because those shifted inner cells are quite fragile, minor friction during intercourse can sometimes cause light spotting or bleeding. Good to keep in mind for clinical assessments! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h4)

question: Why do some patients with cervical ectropion report having more vaginal mucus than usual?

options.A: Bacterial vaginosis always accompanies every case of ectropion.
options.B: The vagina creates extra fluid to wash away dead squamous cells.
options.C: The columnar cells exposed on the surface produce large amounts of mucus.
options.D: The uterus is actively expelling early products of conception.

explanation: Inner columnar cells are natural mucus-makers! When they sit out on the surface, they keep doing their job, leading to a bit more discharge than normal. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h4)

question: Which tool do clinicians use to magnify and closely inspect the cervix using a vinegar solution?

options.A: Colposcopy
options.B: Cystoscopy
options.C: Hysteroscopy
options.D: Laparoscopy

explanation: A colposcopy is like a magnifying glass for the cervix, and the vinegar solution helps highlight any areas that need a closer look. You'll likely see this done in the gynecology clinic! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h5)

question: During a routine speculum exam, you notice a red, velvety patch on a patient's cervix. What is your priority action?

options.A: Preparing the patient for emergency surgical removal of the cervix
options.B: Assisting with obtaining a Pap smear and screening tests to rule out dysplasia or infection
options.C: Instructing the patient to avoid all fluid intake for twelve hours
options.D: Administering intravenous antibiotics immediately without testing

explanation: Always prioritize screening! You can't tell what a red patch is just by looking at it, so a Pap smear or swab is necessary to check for infections or abnormal cells. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h5)

question: What is the best nursing approach for a patient with a normal Pap smear and an asymptomatic cervical ectropion?

options.A: Scheduling immediate cryotherapy to freeze the red area off
options.B: Administering a course of strong oral antibiotics
options.C: Advising strict bed rest in the Trendelenburg position
options.D: Providing reassurance and explaining that the condition is often normal

explanation: If the patient feels fine and her Pap smear is clear, no treatment is needed! Your best tool here is kind, reassuring education to let her know her body is doing just fine. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h6)

question: What is a crucial instruction for a patient who just had cryotherapy (freezing) for symptomatic cervical ectropion?

options.A: Increase strenuous physical exercise to speed up pelvic blood flow
options.B: Expect complete absence of vaginal discharge for at least two months
options.C: Avoid sexual intercourse and tampon use for a specified healing period
options.D: Perform vigorous vaginal douching twice daily to clear debris

explanation: Pelvic rest is vital after cryotherapy to give the treated cervical tissue time to heal safely without introducing infection. Excellent clinical advice to remember! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h6)

question: Why is a Pap smear so important when you spot a red patch on the cervix?

options.A: To chemically destroy the extra columnar cells on the surface
options.B: To measure the exact hormonal levels circulating in the bloodstream
options.C: To rule out malignant or pre-cancerous changes that can look similar to benign erosion
options.D: To prove that the patient has an active bacterial infection

explanation: Harmless ectropion can sometimes look very similar to early cellular changes or cancer. A Pap smear helps us be 100% sure the patient is safe. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h7)

question: Which of these conditions is NOT typically confused with a benign cervical ectropion during an exam?

options.A: Uterine fibroids located in the myometrium
options.B: Benign cervical polyps protruding from the os
options.C: Early malignant tumors of the cervix
options.D: Cervicitis caused by sexually transmitted organisms

explanation: Fibroids sit deep inside the muscular wall of the uterus, way past the surface of the cervix, so they won't look like a red patch on the outer cervix. You nailed it! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h7)

question: Which part of the female reproductive organ is affected by cervical cancer?

options.A: The lower part of the uterus
options.B: The external folds of the labia majora
options.C: The muscular walls of the fallopian tubes
options.D: The inner lining of the ovarian cortex

explanation: Great job! Cervical cancer happens right in the cervix, which is the lower, narrow neck of the uterus connecting to the vagina. You've got this! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T18#GNS216_U5_T18_h1)

question: How does cervical cancer usually develop over time?

options.A: It begins slowly as pre-cancerous cellular changes before invading
options.B: It spreads directly from the ovaries within a few days
options.C: It appears suddenly as a widespread systemic blood infection
options.D: It forms from scar tissue after normal childbirth

explanation: Don't worry, it doesn't happen overnight! It starts with quiet, abnormal cell changes that take years to become true cancer. That is why screening is so powerful. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T18#GNS216_U5_T18_h1)

question: What is the common name for the special area where two different cell types of the cervix meet?

options.A: The internal os cavity
options.B: The transformation zone
options.C: The fundal attachment point
options.D: The myometrial border

explanation: Spot on! We call it the transformation zone. This is a very busy area where most cervical cell changes love to start. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T18#GNS216_U5_T18_h2)

question: Why are abnormal cell changes in the transformation zone a big deal if left unchecked?

options.A: The outer layer stops producing normal protective mucus secretions
options.B: Abnormal cells can break through the basement membrane and invade deep tissues
options.C: The glandular cells immediately block all normal menstrual blood flow
options.D: Squamous cells instantly destroy the surrounding pelvic bone structure

explanation: You're doing great! Once those stubborn cells cross the basement membrane line, a simple localized change turns into an invasive cancer. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T18#GNS216_U5_T18_h2)

question: Which viral infection is known as the main cause of cervical cancer?

options.A: Hepatitis B Virus
options.B: Human Papillomavirus
options.C: Human Immunodeficiency Virus
options.D: Herpes Simplex Virus

explanation: Yes! High-risk strains of HPV are strongly linked to almost all cervical cancer cases. Keeping safe is key! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T18#GNS216_U5_T18_h3)

question: Why does cigarette smoking increase a woman's chance of getting cervical cancer?

options.A: Tobacco smoke alters systemic blood pressure in the pelvic organs
options.B: Byproducts in tobacco smoke weaken local immunity and damage cervical cells
options.C: Smoking causes immediate permanent closure of the internal cervical os
options.D: Nicotine directly destroys all protective antibodies inside the uterus

explanation: Think of cigarette smoke as carrying harmful chemicals that settle in cervical mucus, wearing down local defenses and damaging cell DNA. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T18#GNS216_U5_T18_h3)

question: What is often the very first sign a woman might notice with early cervical cancer?

options.A: Abnormal vaginal bleeding
options.B: Complete cessation of urine output
options.C: Severe swelling in both feet
options.D: Sudden loss of scalp hair

explanation: Spot on! Bleeding between periods, after intercourse, or after menopause is a classic red flag that means 'time to see a doctor.' [learn more](GNS216_U5_T18#GNS216_U5_T18_h4)

question: A patient presents to the clinic complaining of bleeding after sexual intercourse and a foul-smelling vaginal discharge. What is the most appropriate initial nursing action?

options.A: Advise her to start taking heavy doses of oral iron supplements immediately
options.B: Instruct her to apply medicated vaginal creams every night for a month
options.C: Reassure her that this is a normal part of aging and send her home
options.D: Perform a detailed health history and facilitate a pelvic examination by the doctor

explanation: Post-coital bleeding requires prompt clinical investigation and visualization of the cervix to rule out malignancy. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T18#GNS216_U5_T18_h4)

question: What simple household solution is applied to the cervix during a Visual Inspection with Acetic Acid (VIA)?

options.A: Vinegar
options.B: Betadine solution
options.C: Hydrogen peroxide
options.D: Normal saline

explanation: Yes, acetic acid is just clinical vinegar! It makes abnormal cells turn a temporary white color so nurses can easily spot them. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T18#GNS216_U5_T18_h5)

question: Why do doctors perform a colposcopy and take a biopsy after a woman gets an abnormal Pap smear result?

options.A: To clean out the entire uterine cavity and prevent future infections
options.B: To examine suspicious areas closely and take a tissue sample for definitive diagnosis
options.C: To measure the exact hormone levels circulating in the pelvic blood vessels
options.D: To instantly cure the viral infection using high-intensity light beams

explanation: Think of a Pap smear as a warning bell, while a colposcopy and biopsy are the detectives that look closer to confirm what is really going on. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T18#GNS216_U5_T18_h5)

question: What treatment involves placing tiny radioactive sources directly inside or close to a cervical tumor?

options.A: Hysterectomy
options.B: Cryotherapy
options.C: Brachytherapy
options.D: Chemotherapy

explanation: You've got it! 'Brachy' means close—so brachytherapy places radiation right next to or inside the tumor to target bad cells while sparing healthy tissue. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T18#GNS216_U5_T18_h6)

question: What main factor helps doctors decide whether to use surgery or radiation for cervical cancer?

options.A: The clinical stage of the cancer and patient health status
options.B: The patient's personal preference for herbal remedies
options.C: The availability of blood donors in the local hospital ward
options.D: The exact blood type of the individual diagnosed

explanation: Exactly! Early stages are often fixed with surgery, while more advanced stages need a mix of radiation and drugs. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T18#GNS216_U5_T18_h6)

question: Why is watching a patient's urine output so important after major pelvic surgery for cervical cancer?

options.A: Surgical dissection near the cervix can temporarily disrupt bladder nerve pathways
options.B: Patients are forbidden from drinking water for days after the operation
options.C: Chemotherapy drugs crystallize instantly inside the urinary bladder
options.D: The kidneys automatically shut down when the uterus is removed

explanation: Because the bladder nerves run very close to the womb, big surgeries can stun them temporarily, meaning the patient might need a catheter for a little while. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T18#GNS216_U5_T18_h7)

question: A patient recovering from a radical hysterectomy notices a clear fluid leaking from her vagina along with tummy discomfort. What should you suspect?

options.A: The natural start of early post-surgical menstruation
options.B: An allergic reaction to standard oral pain medication
options.C: A completely normal sign of rapid wound healing
options.D: A potential urinary tract fistula or surgical complication

explanation: Good catch, nurse! Uncontrolled fluid leaking after pelvic surgery can point to a fistula—an abnormal opening between the bladder and the vagina. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T18#GNS216_U5_T18_h7)

question: Who is the main target group for the preventive HPV vaccine?

options.A: Young adolescent girls before sexual debut
options.B: Infants during their routine immunization schedule
options.C: Elderly women over the age of sixty-five
options.D: Adult men diagnosed with chronic prostatitis

explanation: Spot on! The vaccine works best when given to young girls before they are ever exposed to HPV. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T18#GNS216_U5_T18_h8)

question: Why is Visual Inspection with Acetic Acid (VIA) so helpful in primary healthcare clinics across Nigeria?

options.A: It completely cures any existing viral infection within a few minutes
options.B: It is inexpensive, fast, and does not require a complex laboratory setup
options.C: It replaces the need for any healthcare personnel during the procedure
options.D: It provides a permanent digital image stored in a computer database

explanation: Brilliant! VIA is cheap, quick, and gives instant results right there in the community clinic without needing a fancy lab. Perfect for low-resource settings! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T18#GNS216_U5_T18_h8)

question: Why are women biologically more at risk of getting STIs than men?

options.A: The rapid turnover rate of vaginal epithelial cells
options.B: The large area of delicate mucosal tissue in the female reproductive tract
options.C: Lower natural antibody counts in female sweat
options.D: A higher resting internal body temperature in the pelvis

explanation: The fragile lining inside the female reproductive tract easily forms tiny micro-tears during sex, giving germs an easy way to enter the body. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h1)

question: Why is it tricky that many STIs in women show no symptoms at all?

options.A: The immune system permanently attacks healthy tissues instead of the pathogen
options.B: Infected women unknowingly spread the infection and delay necessary treatment
options.C: Routine diagnostic tests consistently fail to detect silent infections
options.D: Asymptomatic infections immediately progress to systemic organ failure

explanation: When an infection causes no signs or pain, a woman has no reason to visit the clinic, letting the disease grow quietly and pass to others. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h1)

question: What do we call passing an STI from a mother to her baby during childbirth?

options.A: Fomite transfer
options.B: Vertical transmission
options.C: Horizontal transmission
options.D: Systemic inoculation

explanation: Vertical transmission simply means passing an infection from mother to child during pregnancy, labor, or delivery. You've got this! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h2)

question: What happens during an 'ascending infection' in the female reproductive system?

options.A: Pathogens move upward from the vagina and cervix into the uterus and fallopian tubes
options.B: Viruses migrate from skin lesions down to the regional lymph nodes
options.C: Fungi multiply rapidly on the external vulva and travel to the bladder
options.D: Bacteria travel through the bloodstream directly to the heart valves

explanation: An ascending infection is just germs traveling upward—moving past the cervix and into the upper reproductive organs where they can cause serious trouble. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h2)

question: What is the name of the painless sore that shows up during the first stage of syphilis?

options.A: Chancre
options.B: Pustule
options.C: Vesicle
options.D: Gumma

explanation: The classic early sign of syphilis is a firm, round, usually painless sore called a chancre right where the bacteria entered the skin. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h3)

question: A young female patient has Chlamydia. What is the standard medical treatment?

options.A: A series of therapeutic vaccines given over a six-month recovery period
options.B: Strict bed rest and immune-boosting vitamins with no prescription medications
options.C: A course of oral antibiotics for the patient and treatment for her recent sexual partners
options.D: Surgical drainage of infected cervical cysts followed by topical anti-fungals

explanation: Chlamydia is caused by bacteria, so it needs antibiotics! Always remember to treat sexual partners too, otherwise, they'll just pass it right back. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h3)

question: Which viral STI is managed with lifelong antivirals to keep painful blisters under control?

options.A: Herpes Simplex Virus
options.B: Cytomegalovirus
options.C: Human Papillomavirus
options.D: Hepatitis A Virus

explanation: Herpes simplex causes flare-ups of painful blisters. Antivirals don't cure the virus completely, but they help manage and shorten the outbreaks. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h4)

question: Why do high-risk strains of HPV require regular cervical screening even when a woman feels fine?

options.A: High-risk HPV can cause silent cellular changes in the cervix that lead to cancer over time
options.B: Routine screening is the only way to clear the virus completely from nerve tissues
options.C: HPV bacteria become resistant to standard antibiotic therapies if left unchecked
options.D: The virus rapidly destroys red blood cells and causes severe systemic anemia

explanation: High-risk HPV can change cervical cells without causing any pain or warning signs. That's why routine Pap smears are so lifesaving! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h4)

question: What type of germ causes trichomoniasis?

options.A: Bacterium
options.B: Retrovirus
options.C: Protozoan parasite
options.D: Dermatophyte fungus

explanation: Trichomoniasis is caused by a tiny, swimming parasite known as *Trichomonas vaginalis*. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h5)

question: Which symptom helps tell a yeast infection apart from trichomoniasis?

options.A: A painless firm chancre on the external labia
options.B: Frothy, yellow-green discharge with a strong, fishy smell
options.C: Painful, fluid-filled vesicles that rupture into open ulcers
options.D: Thick, white, cottage-cheese-like discharge with no foul odor

explanation: Yeast infections (candidiasis) usually bring thick, white discharge and intense itching, unlike the frothy, foul-smelling discharge of trichomoniasis. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h5)

question: What is the main laboratory test used to detect chlamydia and gonorrhea from a swab or urine sample?

options.A: Nucleic Acid Amplification Tests
options.B: Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay
options.C: Stool occult blood analysis
options.D: Complete blood count with differential

explanation: NAATs are the gold standard! They accurately copy and spot tiny amounts of the germ's genetic material. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h6)

question: A patient looks very anxious while preparing for a pelvic exam for lower belly pain. What should you do first?

options.A: Skip the speculum exam entirely and prescribe broad-spectrum antibiotics without testing
options.B: Insist she lie back immediately to keep the clinic schedule running on time
options.C: Explain each step of the procedure calmly and reassure her about privacy and comfort
options.D: Ask a security guard to stand in the room until the examination is finished

explanation: As a nurse, your warmth and clear explanations help ease patient fears, build trust, and make the clinical exam go much smoother. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h6)

question: Why must sexual partners be treated at the same time when someone has a bacterial STI?

options.A: To ensure the laboratory insurance claim covers the cost of the initial diagnostic workup
options.B: To speed up the metabolic clearance of the antibiotic through the kidneys
options.C: To prevent the patient from becoming immediately reinfected after finishing treatment
options.D: To prevent the development of drug-resistant fungal strains in the community

explanation: Treating partners simultaneously stops the back-and-forth 'ping-pong' spread of the infection between couples. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h7)

question: What key advice should you give a patient being treated for a new sexually transmitted infection?

options.A: Abstain from sexual intercourse until medication is finished and symptoms resolve
options.B: Share remaining prescription pills with friends who report similar symptoms
options.C: Stop taking the prescribed antibiotics as soon as the physical itching stops
options.D: Avoid drinking clean water for forty-eight hours after taking oral medication

explanation: Taking a break from sex during treatment lets the body heal fully and stops the infection from being passed around again. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h7)

question: What major reproductive problem is linked to fallopian tube scarring from untreated pelvic infections?

options.A: Premature menopause
options.B: Hypertrophic cervical polyps
options.C: Endometrial hyperplasia
options.D: Ectopic pregnancy and infertility

explanation: Scars in the fallopian tubes can block eggs from traveling normally, leading either to trouble getting pregnant or dangerous ectopic pregnancies. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h8)

question: How does an untreated lower genital infection turn into Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID)?

options.A: Fungi colonize the bladder wall and obstruct the normal flow of urine
options.B: Bacteria enter the systemic circulation and settle permanently in the heart valves
options.C: Pathogens ascend from the cervix through the uterus into the fallopian tubes and pelvic cavity
options.D: Viruses alter bone marrow production, leading to severe immunological suppression

explanation: PID happens when bacteria travel upward from the vagina and cervix, causing widespread inflammation in the upper reproductive organs. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h8)

question: What is one of the best everyday ways to teach patients to lower their risk of catching STIs?

options.A: Underlining the importance of monthly pelvic ultrasound scans
options.B: Taking daily prophylactic doses of strong broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.C: Avoiding all physical contact with family members in public settings
options.D: Consistent and correct use of barrier methods like condoms

explanation: Barrier methods create a physical block that stops infectious fluids from passing during sex, offering great protection. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h9)

question: Why is it so important for nurses to offer non-judgmental counseling when discussing sexual health?

options.A: It legally waives the hospital from liability during invasive pelvic examinations
options.B: It builds trust, encouraging patients to share accurate health history and seek timely care
options.C: It guarantees that the patient will never contract a viral infection in the future
options.D: It eliminates the need for laboratory diagnostic testing during clinical visits

explanation: When patients feel judged or shamed, they hide their symptoms and avoid clinics. A warm, open approach keeps them safe and cared for! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h9)

question: What are the three main types of germs that cause sexually transmitted infections (STIs)?

options.A: Fungal, protozoal, and cellular toxins
options.B: Nutritional, bacterial, and hormonal elements
options.C: Genetic, environmental, and viral factors
options.D: Bacterial, viral, and parasitic agents

explanation: You'll often see these three! STIs are primarily caused by bacteria, viruses, and parasites. Knowing your enemy helps you educate your patients better. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T3#GNS216_U5_T3_h1)

question: Why do many men unknowingly spread STIs to their partners?

options.A: They only transmit infections during the winter months
options.B: They refuse to take oral medications prescribed by nurses
options.C: They develop immediate immunity that masks active laboratory results
options.D: They frequently harbour asymptomatic infections without realising it

explanation: Many guys walk around feeling totally fine with zero symptoms (asymptomatic), which is why testing is so important even when someone feels healthy! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T3#GNS216_U5_T3_h1)

question: Which bacterial STI is famous for causing a classic, usually painless sore called a chancre in its early stage?

options.A: Chlamydia
options.B: Candidiasis
options.C: Gonorrhoea
options.D: Syphilis

explanation: That's primary syphilis! It loves to throw patients off because the initial sore (chancre) doesn't hurt at all, so people often ignore it. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T3#GNS216_U5_T3_h2)

question: A male patient comes in complaining of a thick, pus-like discharge from his private part. Which infection is the most likely suspect?

options.A: Human papillomavirus
options.B: Gonorrhoea
options.C: Primary syphilis
options.D: Genital herpes

explanation: Spot on! Gonorrhoea in men is classic for that heavy, purulent (pus-like) urethral discharge and burning when peeing. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T3#GNS216_U5_T3_h2)

question: What is the medical term for pain or a burning feeling when passing urine?

options.A: Polyuria
options.B: Hematuria
options.C: Dysuria
options.D: Proteinuria

explanation: Dysuria is a word you'll use all the time in clinicals. 'Dys-' means painful or difficult, and '-uria' refers to urine! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T3#GNS216_U5_T3_h3)

question: A male patient insists he doesn't have an STI because his sores don't hurt. How should you gently correct him?

options.A: Painlessness proves that the infection is restricted to the skin surface only
options.B: Some serious infections like syphilis can cause painless sores in their early stages
options.C: If a lesion does not hurt, the body will eliminate the virus automatically
options.D: Painless sores always indicate a non-infectious skin allergy rather than an STI

explanation: It's a common trap! Remind your patients that a lack of pain does not mean lack of disease—syphilis chancres are notorious for being painless. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T3#GNS216_U5_T3_h3)

question: When taking a sexual history from a patient, what is the best interviewing style to use?

options.A: Asking rapid closed-ended questions to get through the interview quickly
options.B: Expressing personal moral disapproval to encourage future safe behaviour
options.C: Avoiding questions about anal or oral practices to prevent client embarrassment
options.D: Using a neutral, non-judgmental tone and asking open-ended questions

explanation: As nurses, we keep our personal biases out of the room. A warm, open approach makes the patient trust you enough to tell the whole truth. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T3#GNS216_U5_T3_h4)

question: Why is it important for a nurse to ask about oral and anal sexual practices during a check-up?

options.A: Clients expect nurses to document their personal lifestyle choices for insurance
options.B: Urethral swabs are sensitive enough to detect infections in all other body parts
options.C: Infections can transmit across different mucosal sites and require site-specific testing
options.D: Standard blood tests will automatically cover all anatomical exposure sites

explanation: Germs don't just stay in the genitals! If a patient had oral or anal exposure, we need swabs from the throat or rectum to catch the infection accurately. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T3#GNS216_U5_T3_h4)

question: What is a main goal of counseling a patient *before* they take an STI test?

options.A: Administering therapeutic antibiotics before laboratory confirmation returns
options.B: Explaining test procedures and infection window periods to the client
options.C: Providing the client with their final laboratory test results immediately
options.D: Forcing the client to disclose the names of all past sexual partners

explanation: Pre-test counseling helps prep the patient so they know what to expect and understand why timing (the window period) is everything. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T3#GNS216_U5_T3_h5)

question: A patient tests negative for an STI just three days after a risky exposure. What crucial advice must you give them?

options.A: Antibiotics should still be taken immediately to prevent future infections
options.B: No further precautions are necessary because the immune system has cleared it
options.C: The test may be a false negative due to the window period, so a repeat test is needed
options.D: A negative result means the client is permanently immune to this specific pathogen

explanation: Remember the window period! It takes time for the body to build up enough markers for tests to spot them. Testing too early can give a false sense of safety. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T3#GNS216_U5_T3_h5)

question: What is the primary goal of partner notification (contact tracing) when dealing with STIs?

options.A: To break the chain of transmission and prevent reinfection
options.B: To punish individuals who engage in high-risk sexual behaviours
options.C: To collect financial penalties for public health clinic operations
options.D: To establish legal liability for disease outbreaks in the community

explanation: It's all about stopping the cycle! Treating partners ensures they don't keep passing the infection back and forth. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T3#GNS216_U5_T3_h6)

question: Which contact tracing method allows public health staff to reach out to partners privately without revealing the patient's name?

options.A: Direct self-testing
options.B: Client referral
options.C: Provider referral
options.D: Mandatory quarantine

explanation: That's provider referral! The health team steps in to handle the delicate notification confidentially, protecting the original patient's privacy. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T3#GNS216_U5_T3_h6)

question: Why must patients finish every single dose of their prescribed antibiotics for a bacterial STI?

options.A: To build lifelong immunity against all future viral and bacterial strains
options.B: To ensure the laboratory test results turn negative by the next day
options.C: To ensure complete eradication of the pathogen and prevent treatment failure
options.D: To prevent the development of permanent skin discolouration

explanation: Stopping meds early just because symptoms fade leaves the toughest germs alive, leading to drug resistance. Always teach patients to finish their drugs! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T3#GNS216_U5_T3_h7)

question: What advice should you give a patient receiving treatment for a bacterial STI regarding sex?

options.A: Resume intercourse immediately once the burning sensation starts to fade
options.B: Limit intercourse to protected methods without needing partner treatment
options.C: Abstain from sexual activity until he and his partner have finished treatment
options.D: Use oil-based lubricants to prevent transmission while taking oral tablets

explanation: No sex until both partners finish their treatment course! This stops the dreaded 'ping-pong' effect of passing the infection right back to each other. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T3#GNS216_U5_T3_h7)

question: Which vaccines should nurses recommend to help protect patients against viral STIs and related long-term complications?

options.A: Tetanus and diphtheria
options.B: BCG and yellow fever
options.C: HPV and Hepatitis B
options.D: Malaria and typhoid

explanation: Spot on! HPV and Hep B vaccines are powerful shields against major viral infections that can cause serious long-term issues like liver damage or cancers. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T3#GNS216_U5_T3_h8)

question: Which of these is NOT a safe or recommended way to lower your risk of getting an STI?

options.A: Receiving available prophylactic vaccinations against viral pathogens
options.B: Using barrier methods like condoms consistently and correctly
options.C: Relying solely on herbal supplements to block infection transmission
options.D: Undergoing routine periodic STI screenings with new or multiple partners

explanation: Herbal mixtures won't stop an STI! Safe practices mean using condoms, getting vaccinated, and going for regular checks. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T3#GNS216_U5_T3_h8)

question: Why are young women biologically more vulnerable to catching sexually transmitted infections?

options.A: Faster overall blood circulation to the lower abdomen
options.B: Increased acidity of the normal vaginal flora
options.C: A higher resting body temperature in the pelvic region
options.D: The large area of mucous membrane in the reproductive tract

explanation: Think of the delicate lining inside the female reproductive tract—it has a large surface area that makes it easy for bacteria and viruses to settle in. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T4#GNS216_U5_T4_h1)

question: How can social and economic factors increase a woman's risk of getting an infection?

options.A: They frequently limit her ability to negotiate safe sex practices
options.B: They directly alter the chemical balance of cervical mucus
options.C: They prevent the body from producing natural antibodies
options.D: They speed up the reproductive cycle of common pathogens

explanation: In real life, lack of financial independence or social power can make it really difficult for a woman to insist on using protection like condoms. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T4#GNS216_U5_T4_h1)

question: Which common bacterial infection is famous for causing silent damage that can lead to infertility if ignored?

options.A: Candidiasis
options.B: Chlamydia
options.C: Pubic lice
options.D: Bacterial vaginosis

explanation: Chlamydia is often called a 'silent' infection because it sneaks in without symptoms while quietly harming the fallopian tubes. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T4#GNS216_U5_T4_h2)

question: What type of germ causes trichomoniasis?

options.A: A bacterium
options.B: A protozoan
options.C: A fungus
options.D: A prion

explanation: Trichomoniasis is caused by a tiny, single-celled parasite (a protozoan) that loves to cause irritation and unusual discharge. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T4#GNS216_U5_T4_h2)

question: Why do many women wait a long time before seeking help for a reproductive tract infection?

options.A: The infections frequently do not cause noticeable symptoms early on
options.B: Laboratory tests take several weeks to show any positive results
options.C: Antibiotics for these conditions are universally unavailable
options.D: Initial symptoms always present as severe systemic shock

explanation: Since many of these infections start off completely silent, women feel totally fine and have no idea they need to visit a clinic. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T4#GNS216_U5_T4_h3)

question: A patient walks into the clinic with lower tummy pain and unusual discharge. What serious upper-body complication should a nurse watch out for if this is left untreated?

options.A: Pelvic inflammatory disease
options.B: Iron deficiency anemia
options.C: Chronic hypertension
options.D: Type 2 diabetes mellitus

explanation: If a lower infection is ignored, it can travel upwards into the reproductive organs and trigger pelvic inflammatory disease (PID). [learn more](GNS216_U5_T4#GNS216_U5_T4_h3)

question: What is the best and most accurate lab test used to check for chlamydia and gonorrhea?

options.A: Complete blood count with differential
options.B: Nucleic acid amplification test
options.C: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate
options.D: Routine urinalysis dipstick

explanation: Nucleic acid amplification tests (NAATs) are top-tier because they spot the actual genetic material of the bacteria with high accuracy. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T4#GNS216_U5_T4_h4)

question: When is it most important to routinely screen women for reproductive infections?

options.A: Whenever routine malaria testing is conducted
options.B: Only after the patient develops severe chronic pelvic pain
options.C: Strictly upon reaching forty years of age
options.D: During the first prenatal visit and for sexually active young adults

explanation: Early screening catches silent infections early, especially during pregnancy or in young adults before any lasting damage is done. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T4#GNS216_U5_T4_h4)

question: Why is it so important for a nurse to create a private, non-judgmental space during patient counseling?

options.A: It prevents the patient from ever contracting another infection
options.B: It eliminates the need to prescribe any pharmaceutical medications
options.C: It guarantees that the laboratory test results will return faster
options.D: It helps reduce fear of stigma so the patient shares accurate history

explanation: When patients feel safe and unjudged, they are much more likely to open up and tell you the truth about their health and partners. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T4#GNS216_U5_T4_h5)

question: As a nurse explaining a treatment plan, what should you avoid doing?

options.A: Using heavy medical jargon that the patient does not understand
options.B: Ensuring the conversation remains strictly confidential
options.C: Explaining the importance of abstaining from sex during treatment
options.D: Asking the patient about her current sexual partners

explanation: Always keep it simple! Heavy medical grammar just confuses patients. Talk to them in clear, everyday language they can easily grasp. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T4#GNS216_U5_T4_h5)

question: Why doesn't it work to treat only the female patient while completely ignoring her sexual partners?

options.A: It frequently leads to immediate reinfection of the patient
options.B: It stops the patient's immune system from producing antibodies
options.C: It causes the laboratory tests to show false positive results
options.D: It automatically makes the bacteria resistant to all antibiotics

explanation: It's a cycle! If the partner still has the infection, sleeping together again will just pass it right back to her. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T4#GNS216_U5_T4_h6)

question: What does 'expedited partner therapy' mean in plain nursing terms?

options.A: Requiring the partner to undergo major surgery before getting drugs
options.B: Providing medication or prescriptions directly through the patient for her partner
options.C: Admitting the sexual partner into the emergency ward immediately
options.D: Sending a text message alert to all known contacts automatically

explanation: This clever strategy lets you give treatment or prescriptions straight to the patient to take to her partner, especially if he hates visiting clinics. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T4#GNS216_U5_T4_h6)

question: What is the main danger when a patient stops taking her antibiotics halfway just because she feels better?

options.A: Surviving germs can multiply and cause drug resistance
options.B: The laboratory will lose the record of her initial test
options.C: The patient will instantly develop a severe viral illness
options.D: Her body will stop producing any natural red blood cells

explanation: Stopping early kills off the weak germs but leaves the strongest ones alive to bounce back stronger and harder to treat! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T4#GNS216_U5_T4_h7)

question: What advice should you give a patient about sex while she is undergoing treatment for an infection?

options.A: Increase sexual frequency to help flush out the remaining bacteria
options.B: Stop sexual activity only for the first two hours after taking drugs
options.C: Abstain from sexual intercourse until treatment is finished and cure is confirmed
options.D: Continue normal sexual activity as long as condoms are used

explanation: Advise her to pause sexual activity until she finishes her meds and gets the all-clear. This stops reinfection and gives her body time to heal. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T4#GNS216_U5_T4_h7)

question: Which preventive method is still the absolute best for stopping the spread of infections during sex?

options.A: High-dose vitamin supplements
options.B: Daily herbal detox teas
options.C: Barrier methods like condoms
options.D: Frequent douching with water

explanation: Condoms act like a reliable physical shield, stopping infectious fluids from passing between partners. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T4#GNS216_U5_T4_h8)

question: Which of the following is NOT a goal of community health education on infections?

options.A: Promoting routine screening for sexually active adults
options.B: Encouraging women to rely solely on herbal remedies
options.C: Dispelling common myths surrounding disease transmission
options.D: Advocating for correct and consistent condom use

explanation: Herbal mixtures won't cure STIs. Good health education focuses on proven medical steps like screening, safe sex, and busting harmful myths. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T4#GNS216_U5_T4_h8)

question: How are most sexually transmitted infections (STIs) mainly spread?

options.A: Sharing eating utensils or drinking cups
options.B: Unprotected sexual contact with an infected person
options.C: Direct contact with public swimming pool water
options.D: Inhalation of airborne droplets from coughing

explanation: Spot on! STIs are mostly spread through vaginal, anal, or oral sexual contact. You've got this! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h1)

question: Why are some STIs tricky because they don't show any physical signs or symptoms?

options.A: Infected people can spread the disease without knowing they have it
options.B: Laboratory tests cannot detect pathogens if symptoms are absent
options.C: The body builds permanent immunity during the latent phase
options.D: Asymptomatic infections always resolve spontaneously without treatment

explanation: Exactly! When someone has no symptoms, they feel healthy and can unknowingly pass the infection to their partners. Good thinking! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h1)

question: Which of these common STIs is caused by bacteria and can be easily cured with antibiotics?

options.A: Human papillomavirus
options.B: Human immunodeficiency virus
options.C: Chlamydia
options.D: Herpes simplex virus

explanation: Great job! Chlamydia is bacterial, which means standard antibiotics clear it right up. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h2)

question: What is the main difference between bacterial and viral STIs in the body?

options.A: Bacterial infections cause permanent cellular mutations, while viral infections do not
options.B: Viral infections remain in the body long-term, while bacterial infections are usually cured
options.C: Viral infections never respond to any form of pharmaceutical treatment
options.D: Bacterial infections require lifelong maintenance therapy instead of short courses

explanation: Spot on! Bacteria can usually be kicked out with medications, but viruses like HIV or herpes stay in the body for life and need long-term management. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h2)

question: How do barrier methods like condoms actually prevent STIs?

options.A: To permanently neutralize circulating viral loads in the bloodstream
options.B: To increase local mucosal immunity against parasitic invasion
options.C: To block the exchange of infectious bodily fluids during intercourse
options.D: To destroy bacterial cell walls upon contact in the vaginal canal

explanation: You got it! Condoms act as a physical shield so infectious fluids don't pass between partners. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h3)

question: A patient wants a daily pill to prevent getting HIV before any potential exposure. What is this prevention method called?

options.A: Syndromic management protocol
options.B: Contact tracing therapy
options.C: Pre-exposure prophylaxis
options.D: Post-exposure prophylaxis

explanation: Awesome! 'Pre-exposure' simply means taking the medicine before exposure to protect yourself. Keep it up! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h3)

question: The Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine is most famous for helping prevent which major health condition?

options.A: Acquired immunodeficiency syndrome
options.B: Cervical cancer
options.C: Bacterial vaginosis
options.D: Pelvic inflammatory disease

explanation: Correct! The HPV vaccine protects against high-risk strains that can lead to cervical changes and cancer later in life. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h4)

question: Why is it best to give the HPV vaccine before a person becomes sexually active?

options.A: The vaccine changes its chemical formulation based on sexual history
options.B: Adolescent immune systems cannot process the vaccine after sexual debut
options.C: The vaccine provides the highest protection before any potential exposure to the virus
options.D: Insurance policies refuse coverage for the vaccine once a person turns eighteen

explanation: Spot on! Vaccines work best when your immune system meets the pathogen before the actual virus does. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h4)

question: What is the most reliable, go-to test used in labs to check for chlamydia and gonorrhea?

options.A: Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay
options.B: Microscopic wet mount preparation
options.C: Nucleic acid amplification testing
options.D: Complete blood cell count analysis

explanation: That's right! Nucleic acid amplification testing (NAAT) is super accurate at spotting the genetic material of these bacteria. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h5)

question: Why do pregnant women routinely get screened for STIs during early prenatal visits?

options.A: To eliminate common morning sickness symptoms during the first trimester
options.B: To determine the exact biological sex of the unborn infant
options.C: To prevent transmitting infections from the mother to the developing fetus
options.D: To cure congenital genetic abnormalities present at conception

explanation: Exactly! Catching and treating infections early protects the baby from complications during pregnancy and birth. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h5)

question: What important advice should you give a patient who just got antibiotics for a bacterial STI?

options.A: Double the next dose if you forget to take one pill
options.B: Stop taking the pills the moment physical discomfort disappears
options.C: Complete the entire medication course even if symptoms resolve
options.D: Share remaining medication with your partner to save money

explanation: You got it! Even if they feel better in a few days, finishing all the pills ensures the bacteria are fully wiped out. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h6)

question: What is the main goal of antiretroviral therapy (ART) for someone living with HIV?

options.A: Suppressing the viral load and protecting immune function
options.B: Stimulating the immediate production of thick mucosal barriers
options.C: Permanently killing all virus particles within the bone marrow
options.D: Preventing the development of seasonal respiratory allergies

explanation: Spot on! ART keeps the virus levels super low, which keeps the immune system strong and healthy. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h6)

question: Why is tracing sexual partners and notifying them so important after an STI diagnosis?

options.A: It punishes individuals who fail to use proper barrier protection
options.B: It proves whether the patient acquired the infection locally
options.C: It breaks the cycle of reinfection and treats exposed individuals
options.D: It provides statistical data for insurance companies to adjust rates

explanation: Exactly! Partner notification ensures everyone gets tested and treated so they don't keep passing the infection back and forth. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h7)

question: A patient is scared and hesitant to tell their partner about a new STI diagnosis. As a nurse, how should you help?

options.A: Offer support, discuss confidential partner notification options, and explore safe ways to share the news
options.B: Tell the patient that law enforcement will handle the notification process immediately
options.C: Refuse to provide further treatment until the partner arrives at the clinic
options.D: Advise the patient to end the relationship without mentioning the health diagnosis

explanation: Wonderful nursing care! Being empathetic and offering safe, confidential options helps the patient feel supported and understood. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h7)

question: Why is it so vital for a nurse to keep a non-judgmental attitude during sexual health assessments?

options.A: It reduces the financial cost of purchasing barrier methods
options.B: It encourages the patient to share accurate health history and seek care
options.C: It eliminates the need for laboratory diagnostic testing
options.D: It guarantees the patient will never contract another infection

explanation: Spot on! When patients feel safe and respected without shame, they are honest about their health and more likely to get help. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h8)

question: Which of these actions is NOT a good recommendation for nurse-led STI prevention education?

options.A: Demonstrating the correct application of barrier methods
options.B: Discussing the schedule for routine screening and follow-up tests
options.C: Instructing patients on how to use chemical disinfectants vaginally
options.D: Explaining the importance of completing prescribed antibiotic courses

explanation: You nailed it! Douching and harsh chemicals actually harm natural protective barriers and raise the risk of infection. Never recommended! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h8)

question: What is the medical term for inflammation of the external female genitalia?

options.A: Endometritis
options.B: Cervicitis
options.C: Salpingitis
options.D: Vulvitis

explanation: Vulvitis specifically refers to the inflammation of the external female structures making up the vulva. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T6#GNS216_U5_T6_h1)

question: Why do vulvitis and vaginitis often happen together?

options.A: The vaginal canal produces secretions that protect the vulva from damage.
options.B: Both areas share the exact same hormonal receptors.
options.C: Infections always start inside the uterus first.
options.D: The physical closeness of the external and internal tissues allows irritation to spread easily.

explanation: Think of it like neighbors—because the vulva and vagina live right next to each other, an infection or irritation in one can easily reach the other. Great job thinking through clinical anatomy! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T6#GNS216_U5_T6_h1)

question: Which common fungus frequently causes yeast infections on the vulva?

options.A: Neisseria gonorrhoeae
options.B: Trichomonas vaginalis
options.C: Candida albicans
options.D: Escherichia coli

explanation: Candida albicans is a fungus that normally hangs out on our bodies harmlessly, but when conditions are right, it can overgrow and cause that familiar itching and irritation. Keep up the great revision! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T6#GNS216_U5_T6_h2)

question: A patient complains of sudden vulval redness and intense itching after starting a new brand of scented bubble bath. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: A hormone-secreting ovarian tumor
options.B: A chronic autoimmune joint disorder
options.C: An irritant or allergic contact reaction
options.D: A congenital anatomical defect

explanation: Chemicals and fragrances in bubble baths often trigger contact dermatitis on the sensitive skin of the vulva. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T6#GNS216_U5_T6_h2)

question: What is the number one symptom patients with vulval inflammation usually report?

options.A: Intense itching
options.B: Excessive hair growth
options.C: Severe bone pain
options.D: Complete numbness

explanation: Pruritus, which is just the medical word for itching, is almost always the main complaint when a patient has vulvitis. You're building solid clinical instincts! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T6#GNS216_U5_T6_h3)

question: Why do patients with vulvitis often feel a burning sensation when passing urine?

options.A: The urethral opening becomes completely blocked by swelling.
options.B: Urine flows over raw, inflamed skin tissues on the vulva.
options.C: The kidneys produce acidic waste products that burn the bladder.
options.D: Urine mixes directly with digestive enzymes in the pelvis.

explanation: Imagine pouring liquid over a fresh scrape—when urine washes across sensitive, raw, or inflamed vulval skin, it naturally stings. Such a logical clinical connection to remember! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T6#GNS216_U5_T6_h3)

question: Why might a nurse or doctor collect a vulval tissue biopsy during an investigation?

options.A: To flush out trapped bacteria from the urinary bladder
options.B: To test the patency of the fallopian tubes
options.C: To measure the exact hormone levels in the bloodstream
options.D: To check for chronic skin conditions or rule out abnormal cell changes

explanation: A biopsy sounds scary, but it's just a way for the lab to take a closer look at skin cells under a microscope when standard treatments aren't working. You're mastering diagnostic steps! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T6#GNS216_U5_T6_h4)

question: What is the main reason for preparing a wet mount during a pelvic exam?

options.A: To measure the exact daily urine output of the patient
options.B: To identify specific microorganisms like yeast or parasites under a microscope
options.C: To drain excess fluid from swollen labial glands
options.D: To check if the patient is pregnant

explanation: A wet mount lets the clinician quickly mix a discharge sample with a drop of fluid and peek under a microscope to spot the tiny culprits (like yeast or trichomonas) causing the trouble. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T6#GNS216_U5_T6_h4)

question: Which simple nursing care measure helps soothe irritated vulval tissue and keep the area clean?

options.A: Using scented talcum powder daily
options.B: Scrubbing the area with harsh antiseptic soap
options.C: Applying dry heat packs directly to the skin
options.D: Sitz baths with plain warm water

explanation: Warm sitz baths are a nurse's best friend here—they gently clean the area and soothe discomfort without using harsh chemicals that make irritation worse. Beautiful nursing care! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T6#GNS216_U5_T6_h5)

question: What is a major risk if a patient with severe vulvitis keeps scratching the itchy area?

options.A: Sudden systemic high blood pressure
options.B: Permanent loss of bladder control
options.C: Complete closure of the vaginal canal
options.D: Secondary bacterial infection through broken skin
