options.C: Because antenatal care replaces the need for postnatal visits
options.D: Because all pregnant women require emergency surgery

explanation: Think of it like a chain: each stage of safe motherhood builds on the last to keep both mother and baby protected every step of the way! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h1)

question: Which supplement is most important to give before pregnancy to help prevent birth defects?

options.A: Potassium chloride
options.B: Folic acid
options.C: Vitamin C
options.D: Calcium carbonate

explanation: Folic acid is a superstar vitamin! Taking it before and during early pregnancy greatly lowers the risk of neural tube defects like spina bifida. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h2)

question: How does proper birth spacing protect a mother's health?

options.A: It gives the mother's body time to recover nutrients and strength
options.B: It eliminates the need for any antenatal checkups
options.C: It completely prevents the onset of gestational diabetes
options.D: It guarantees that the next baby will be born full-term

explanation: Giving the body a break between pregnancies allows nutrient stores to refill, making future pregnancies much safer for mum. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h2)

question: What is a standard check done during a routine antenatal clinic (ANC) visit?

options.A: Screening for lifelong hereditary blood disorders
options.B: Performing routine pelvic ultrasounds every week
options.C: Checking maternal blood pressure and urine protein
options.D: Measuring daily caloric intake and physical activity

explanation: Spotting changes in blood pressure and checking urine for protein helps us catch early signs of pre-eclampsia. Great nursing practice! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h3)

question: A pregnant woman at 20 weeks ANC gets mosquito nets and iron supplements. What is the main reason for this?

options.A: To determine the exact genetic sex of the baby
options.B: To induce early labor in high-risk situations
options.C: To prevent malaria and treat or prevent anemia
options.D: To stop morning sickness during the first trimester

explanation: Malaria and low blood (anemia) are major risks in pregnancy, so nets and iron are standard lifesavers in our clinics. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h3)

question: What is the main use of a partograph during labor?

options.A: To monitor labor progress and detect prolonged labor early
options.B: To measure the mother's daily nutritional intake
options.C: To calculate the exact financial cost of the hospital stay
options.D: To record the baby's immunization schedule after birth

explanation: The partograph is a midwife's best friend! It gives a clear picture of how labor is going so you can spot trouble early. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h4)

question: Why is putting traditional substances like saliva or dung on a newborn's umbilical cord dangerous?

options.A: It permanently stains the baby's skin around the abdomen
options.B: It prevents the infant from absorbing breast milk
options.C: It causes the umbilical cord to fall off too quickly
options.D: It introduces harmful bacteria that can cause severe infections like tetanus

explanation: The cord stump is a direct highway to the baby's bloodstream. Unclean substances easily bring in fatal germs like tetanus or sepsis. Keep it clean and dry! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h4)

question: Which of these is a leading direct cause of maternal death worldwide?

options.A: Mild joint stiffness
options.B: Postpartum hemorrhage
options.C: Benign skin rashes
options.D: Common seasonal influenza

explanation: Heavy bleeding after delivery (postpartum hemorrhage) is one of the top dangers new mothers face globally. Knowing how to manage it is key for every nurse! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h5)

question: What makes a comprehensive emergency obstetric care (EmONC) center different from a basic one?

options.A: The ability to perform blood transfusions and Caesarean sections
options.B: The presence of pediatricians in the delivery room at all times
options.C: The requirement that mothers stay in the hospital for a full month
options.D: The exclusive use of traditional herbal remedies for pain

explanation: When things get tough, a comprehensive center can handle surgeries like C-sections and give blood transfusions—things basic clinics can't do. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h5)

question: When does the postnatal period officially start?

options.A: Two weeks after the infant is discharged home
options.B: Immediately after the delivery of the placenta
options.C: When the mother first notices breast milk coming in
options.D: At the start of the third trimester of pregnancy

explanation: The postnatal phase kicks off right after the placenta is delivered and runs through the first six weeks of motherhood. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h6)

question: Why do new mothers need close nursing watch right after delivery?

options.A: Because the mother is at high risk for hemorrhage and infection
options.B: Because the newborn baby requires constant intravenous fluids
options.C: Because mothers cannot produce milk during the first week
options.D: Because routine vital signs are no longer necessary after birth

explanation: The body goes through massive changes right after birth, making those early hours prime time for bleeding and infections. Vigilance saves lives! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h6)

question: What is the main focus of post-abortion care (PAC) services?

options.A: Preventing the client from ever becoming pregnant again
options.B: Filing legal reports against the client in every single case
options.C: Requiring mandatory psychiatric admission for all patients
options.D: Treating incomplete abortion and managing life-threatening complications

explanation: PAC is all about emergency medical care: stopping bleeding, clearing the womb safely, and treating dangerous infections. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h7)

question: Why is family planning counseling a key part of post-abortion care?

options.A: To ensure the client conceives again within the next month
options.B: To fulfill a hospital administrative requirement unrelated to health
options.C: To help the client prevent future unintended pregnancies and repeat procedures
options.D: To punish the client for experiencing a pregnancy loss

explanation: Offering contraception right away helps clients protect their health and avoid another unplanned pregnancy down the line. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h7)

question: How do nurse-led community outreach programs help improve maternal health in rural Nigeria?

options.A: By educating families and encouraging them to seek care at health facilities
options.B: By providing free vehicles to every pregnant woman in the village
options.C: By replacing the need for doctors and hospitals in all situations
options.D: By banning traditional birth attendants from practicing entirely

explanation: Outreach bridges the gap! By teaching families to spot danger signs, we help them get to the clinic early when help is most effective. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h8)

question: A rural clinic nurse finds that many women prefer giving birth at home. What is the best first step for the nurse?

options.A: Engage community leaders and educate women on the safety of facility delivery
options.B: Report all pregnant women who plan home births to the local police
options.C: Close the clinic until the women agree to come in voluntarily
options.D: Ignore the practice since home delivery has no real risks

explanation: Working hand-in-hand with village leaders builds trust and helps women see the safety and benefits of delivering at a health facility. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h8)

question: What is the primary goal of safe motherhood initiatives?

options.A: To completely eliminate the need for traditional birth attendants
options.B: To provide free medications for all childhood illnesses
options.C: To increase the birth rate across rural populations
options.D: To ensure healthy pregnancies and safe deliveries for all women

explanation: Safe motherhood initiatives focus specifically on protecting the health and well-being of mothers throughout pregnancy, childbirth, and the postnatal period. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T004#GNS226_U1_T004_h1)

question: Why is maternal mortality still high in many parts of Nigeria?

options.A: Infectious diseases have been completely wiped out
options.B: Pregnant women completely refuse to visit healthcare facilities
options.C: Transport delays, money issues, and a shortage of skilled staff
options.D: There are too many modern hospitals in remote villages

explanation: You've got this! A mix of delayed care-seeking, poor roads and transport, and health system gaps contributes heavily to poor maternal health outcomes in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T004#GNS226_U1_T004_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT one of the traditional pillars of safe motherhood?

options.A: Antenatal care during pregnancy
options.B: Mandatory military service for parents
options.C: Family planning services
options.D: Postnatal care after delivery

explanation: Easy pick! Safe motherhood pillars focus on family planning, antenatal care, clean and safe delivery, and postnatal care—not military service! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T004#GNS226_U1_T004_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of adding family planning to safe motherhood strategies?

options.A: To ensure that families only have male children
options.B: To reduce the workload of nurses in antenatal clinics
options.C: To allow enough time for a mother's body to recover between pregnancies
options.D: To completely stop population growth in developing nations

explanation: Well done! Proper spacing via family planning prevents closely spaced pregnancies, giving the mother's body the vital time it needs to heal and stay strong. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T004#GNS226_U1_T004_h2)

question: What is a major preventive benefit of routine antenatal care (ANC) visits?

options.A: Treating chronic childhood asthma attacks
options.B: Performing immediate emergency cesarean sections
options.C: Providing permanent surgical contraception
options.D: Giving tetanus toxoid vaccines and iron supplements

explanation: Spot on! ANC visits are crucial for delivering preventive care like immunizations and nutritional supplements to protect both mother and baby. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T004#GNS226_U1_T004_h3)

question: A pregnant woman visits the ANC clinic for the first time at 28 weeks. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Check her vital signs, screen for infections, and check the baby's well-being
options.B: Schedule her for an elective sterilization procedure
options.C: Discharge her immediately because she came late
options.D: Tell her not to return until she goes into labor

explanation: Great clinical thinking! No matter when a woman starts ANC, your immediate duty as a nurse is to check her baseline status and screen for any pregnancy risks. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T004#GNS226_U1_T004_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of using a partograph during labor?

options.A: To monitor labor progress and spot any danger early
options.B: To record the birth weight of the baby
options.C: To measure the mother's daily food intake
options.D: To calculate the hospital bill

explanation: You got it! The partograph gives nurses a clear picture of how labor is going, helping you quickly catch prolonged labor or fetal distress. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T004#GNS226_U1_T004_h4)

question: Why is having a skilled birth attendant present during delivery so important?

options.A: They make antenatal visits unnecessary
options.B: They can quickly spot and manage emergencies like heavy bleeding
options.C: They guarantee the baby won't cry at birth
options.D: They prevent the mother from feeling any contractions

explanation: Exactly! Skilled attendants have the training to handle sudden delivery complications and save lives before things get out of hand. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T004#GNS226_U1_T004_h4)

question: What makes a Comprehensive EmONC center different from a Basic EmONC center?

options.A: Giving routine iron tablets to pregnant women
options.B: Giving health talks during antenatal care
options.C: Performing emergency cesarean sections and blood transfusions
options.D: Weighing newborns right after birth

explanation: Correct! Comprehensive emergency obstetric care (CEmONC) includes major surgical procedures like C-sections and blood replacement services. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T004#GNS226_U1_T004_h5)

question: What should a nurse do when a woman in labor develops a complication too severe for a primary health clinic?

options.A: Quickly arrange a safe transfer to a higher-level facility with CEmONC
options.B: Wait until morning to see if she gets better
options.C: Try to perform surgery right there without proper tools
options.D: Tell the family to take her home for local herbs

explanation: Brilliant! Prompt referral saves lives when your clinic lacks the surgery and blood transfusion resources needed for severe emergencies. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T004#GNS226_U1_T004_h5)

question: When does the highest risk for postpartum hemorrhage and maternal death happen?

options.A: During the fourth month after delivery
options.B: Within the first 48 hours after childbirth
options.C: Two weeks before labor starts
options.D: At the final six-week checkup

explanation: That's right! The first 48 hours after birth are the most critical window for watching out for sudden, dangerous bleeding and infections. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T004#GNS226_U1_T004_h6)

question: A new mother complains of a severe headache, blurred vision, and upper tummy pain 3 days after birth. What is your best response as a nurse?

options.A: Discharge her home to rest
options.B: Report these signs immediately as possible postpartum pre-eclampsia
options.C: Tell her to stop breastfeeding until the headache clears
options.D: Reassure her that it is just normal tiredness

explanation: Excellent catch! Headaches, blurred vision, and upper tummy pain after delivery are red flags for late-onset pre-eclampsia that need urgent medical attention. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T004#GNS226_U1_T004_h6)

question: What is the main health benefit of birth spacing for a mother?

options.A: Allows her body enough time to recover its strength and nutrients
options.B: Ensures all her children are the same gender
options.C: Guarantees she will never have morning sickness again
options.D: Eliminates the need for future antenatal care

explanation: Spot on! Proper spacing prevents maternal depletion and gets the mother's body ready for a healthy future pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T004#GNS226_U1_T004_h7)

question: Why is interconception care (care between pregnancies) so important in safe motherhood?

options.A: It improves health and nutrition before the next pregnancy begins
options.B: It only focuses on baby immunizations
options.C: It replaces the need for medical care during pregnancy
options.D: It forces couples to delay having children

explanation: You've got it! Caring for a mother between pregnancies builds up her health, making her stronger and safer before she conceives again. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T004#GNS226_U1_T004_h7)

question: Who are the best people to involve when mobilizing a local community for safer maternal health?

options.A: Factory owners and corporate bosses
options.B: Traditional rulers, religious leaders, and local community groups
options.C: Construction contractors and road engineers
options.D: International sports bodies and foreign embassies

explanation: Exactly! Local leaders have a huge influence on community health choices and are key partners in encouraging hospital deliveries. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T004#GNS226_U1_T004_h8)

question: Why should healthcare workers partner with traditional birth attendants (TBAs) instead of chasing them away?

options.A: To replace trained midwives with TBAs
options.B: To encourage them to refer pregnant women to clinics for skilled care
options.C: To let them manage severe bleeding at home
options.D: To train them to perform major village surgeries

explanation: Well reasoned! Since many rural women trust TBAs, working with them helps bridge the gap and guides mothers safely to professional clinic care. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T004#GNS226_U1_T004_h8)

question: What is the main goal of the Mother-Baby Package in healthcare?

options.A: To focus exclusively on emergency surgical procedures
options.B: To eliminate the need for community health extension workers
options.C: To provide essential health interventions for mothers and newborns together
options.D: To replace routine childhood immunization schedules

explanation: You got this! The Mother-Baby Package bundles care so that both mum and baby get the protection and support they need right from the start. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T005#GNS226_U1_T005_h1)

question: Why do we bundle maternal and neonatal health services together?

options.A: Midwives only work during the first week after delivery
options.B: It is cheaper for hospitals to buy medications in bulk
options.C: Newborns require the exact same medical treatments as adults
options.D: The health and survival of the mother and baby are directly linked

explanation: Spot on! Mum and baby are a team. Treating them together ensures nothing gets missed during these crucial early stages. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T005#GNS226_U1_T005_h1)

question: Which of the following is a major objective of the Mother-Baby Package?

options.A: To reduce maternal, fetal, and newborn mortality rates
options.B: To increase the cost of maternity drugs in local clinics
options.C: To eliminate all traditional birth attendants completely
options.D: To transfer all pregnant women to tertiary teaching hospitals

explanation: Exactly right! Every clinical guideline and care package ultimately aims to keep both mum and baby safe, healthy, and alive. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T005#GNS226_U1_T005_h2)

question: What does 'continuity of care' mean for mothers and children?

options.A: Seeing a different doctor at every single clinic visit
options.B: Stopping medications as soon as the baby is born
options.C: Linking health services seamlessly from pre-pregnancy through childhood
options.D: Keeping a patient admitted in the hospital for the entire nine months

explanation: Great job! Continuity of care means smooth transitions from antenatal care straight through to childhood so no patient falls through the cracks. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T005#GNS226_U1_T005_h2)

question: Why is folic acid given to women before and during early pregnancy?

options.A: To stop excessive bleeding during the third trimester
options.B: To speed up the onset of active labor pains
options.C: To cure maternal high blood pressure permanently
options.D: To prevent neural tube defects in the developing baby

explanation: Correct! Folic acid is a little vitamin with a big job—it protects the baby's brain and spinal cord development in the early weeks. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T005#GNS226_U1_T005_h3)

question: At an antenatal clinic in Nigeria, a pregnant woman receives sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine. What is this for?

options.A: Malaria
options.B: Pregnancy-induced hypertension
options.C: Gestational diabetes
options.D: Neural tube defects

explanation: Well done! In malaria-endemic areas like Nigeria, intermittent preventive treatment (IPTp) with SP is a routine lifesaver for pregnant mums. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T005#GNS226_U1_T005_h3)

question: Why is oxytocin given right after a baby is delivered?

options.A: To stimulate early breastmilk letdown
options.B: To lower the mother's blood pressure
options.C: To speed up the dilation of the cervix
options.D: To prevent postpartum hemorrhage

explanation: Spot on! Oxytocin makes the uterus clamp down firmly, sealing off blood vessels and keeping heavy bleeding at bay. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T005#GNS226_U1_T005_h4)

question: What tool do midwives use during labor to track contractions, dilation, and baby's heart rate on one sheet?

options.A: Temperature chart
options.B: Immunization card
options.C: Partograph
options.D: Admission register

explanation: You got it! The partograph is a nurse's best friend in the labor room for spotting trouble early and keeping track of progress. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T005#GNS226_U1_T005_h4)

question: When should a mother have her very first postnatal checkup after giving birth in a facility?

options.A: Only when the baby falls sick
options.B: When the child is ready for school
options.C: Within 24 hours of birth
options.D: At the end of the sixth week

explanation: Correct! The first 24 hours carry the highest risk for bleeding and newborn issues, so early checks are vital. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T005#GNS226_U1_T005_h5)

question: Which of these is a key nursing check during routine postnatal care?

options.A: Surgically repairing minor perineal tears after 6 weeks
options.B: Administering the BCG vaccine to the mother
options.C: Measuring the child's head circumference daily
options.D: Checking uterine involution and lochia flow

explanation: Well done! Monitoring how the uterus shrinks (involution) and the type of lochia helps you catch postpartum bleeding or infection early. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T005#GNS226_U1_T005_h5)

question: Which vaccine is given to a newborn right at birth to protect against tuberculosis?

options.A: BCG
options.B: Yellow fever
options.C: Measles
options.D: Tetanus toxoid

explanation: Spot on! BCG is one of those precious birth-dose vaccines given before baby leaves the health facility. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T005#GNS226_U1_T005_h6)

question: What is a major benefit of starting breastfeeding within the first hour of life?

options.A: It helps the baby receive nutrient-rich colostrum and stimulates uterine contraction
options.B: It prevents the mother from experiencing postpartum hair loss
options.C: It replaces the need for any future childhood vaccinations
options.D: It completely guarantees that the child will never catch malaria

explanation: You got it! Early breastfeeding gives baby immune-boosting colostrum and helps mum's uterus contract naturally. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T005#GNS226_U1_T005_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard nursing duty under the Mother-Baby Package?

options.A: Educating mothers on exclusive breastfeeding practices
options.B: Conducting routine antenatal assessments and checkups
options.C: Administering childhood immunizations according to the schedule
options.D: Performing elective major surgeries in primary health clinics

explanation: Correct! Major surgeries belong in a surgical theater with a doctor, not at a basic primary health clinic. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T005#GNS226_U1_T005_h7)

question: Why is health education such an important part of maternal and child nursing?

options.A: It empowers mothers to recognize danger signs and seek timely care
options.B: It ensures that mothers do not visit traditional birth attendants
options.C: It reduces the need for nurses to document patient visits
options.D: It replaces the need for medical checkups during pregnancy

explanation: Wonderful! When mums know what warning signs to look out for, they can report back early and save lives. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T005#GNS226_U1_T005_h7)

question: What is a major financial hurdle stopping many Nigerian women from accessing maternity care?

options.A: Free mandatory transport services
options.B: Mandatory hospital savings accounts
options.C: Out-of-pocket payment systems
options.D: Excessive government health insurance coverage

explanation: Spot on! Having to pay cash directly at the clinic for every single drug or test discourages many families from getting care. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T005#GNS226_U1_T005_h8)

question: How does task-shifting help improve healthcare in understaffed rural areas?

options.A: By moving specialist obstetricians to every village clinic in the country
options.B: By transferring pregnant patients to urban centers permanently
options.C: By replacing all nurses with automated computer systems
options.D: By training community health workers to safely deliver certain basic health interventions

explanation: You nailed it! Task-shifting bridges the staff gap by letting trained community workers handle basic, safe tasks when professional nurses aren't enough. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T005#GNS226_U1_T005_h8)

question: What is another common name for prenatal care?

options.A: Neonatal monitoring
options.B: Postpartum care
options.C: Gynecological screening
options.D: Antenatal care

explanation: Prenatal care is widely referred to as antenatal care, representing health services provided during the period of pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h1)

question: Why do we encourage pregnant women to start their clinic visits (antenatal care) early?

options.A: To detect and manage potential complications early
options.B: To determine the exact sex of the baby immediately
options.C: To guarantee a completely pain-free delivery
options.D: To eliminate all normal physiological changes

explanation: Starting clinic visits early helps you spot risks and treat them before they turn into severe problems. You've got this! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h1)

question: How many total antenatal visits does the World Health Organization recommend for a normal, healthy pregnancy?

options.A: At least eight contacts
options.B: Exactly four visits
options.C: Only one per trimester
options.D: Twelve monthly visits

explanation: Global health guidelines recommend a minimum of eight antenatal visits so moms and babies get optimal monitoring and support throughout the journey. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h2)

question: A pregnant woman comes in for her first booking visit at 10 weeks. What is the main purpose of this early visit?

options.A: To administer high-dose oxytocin
options.B: To prepare the mother for immediate labor
options.C: To measure the baby's exact birth weight
options.D: To establish a baseline health assessment

explanation: This first visit lets us record vital signs, medical history, and early lab findings so we know her normal state of health. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h2)

question: What naturally happens to a pregnant woman's blood (plasma) volume during normal gestation?

options.A: It increases significantly
options.B: It remains completely unchanged
options.C: It decreases by half
options.D: It drops to zero temporarily

explanation: Plasma volume expands greatly during pregnancy to supply the placenta and keep up with the body's new demands. Amazing how the body adapts! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h3)

question: Why do pregnant women often complain of mild heartburn and constipation?

options.A: The kidneys stop producing gastric acid
options.B: Hormones slow down gastrointestinal motility
options.C: Dietary fiber is completely absorbed
options.D: Stomach capacity triples in size

explanation: Pregnancy hormones relax smooth muscles, which slows down digestion. This is a very normal cause of everyday heartburn and constipation! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h3)

question: In the common obstetric history acronym TPAL, what does the letter 'P' stand for?

options.A: Pelvic diameter
options.B: Primary contractions
options.C: Preterm births
options.D: Placental position

explanation: In TPAL, P stands for preterm births—deliveries that happen before 37 completed weeks of pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h4)

question: A woman's last menstrual period began on January 1st. Using Naegele's rule, what is her estimated date of delivery (EDD)?

options.A: September 15th
options.B: November 5th
options.C: October 8th
options.D: December 25th

explanation: Easy trick: add 7 days to the first day of the last period, then subtract 3 months. Jan 1st + 7 days = Jan 8th, minus 3 months = October 8th! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h4)

question: Which routine test is done at antenatal clinics to screen for gestational diabetes or kidney issues?

options.A: Liver biopsy for enzyme levels
options.B: Sputum microscopy for bacteria
options.C: Urinalysis for protein and glucose
options.D: Electrocardiogram for heart rhythm

explanation: Testing urine samples at every visit is a quick way to spot early signs of gestational diabetes or high blood pressure in pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h5)

question: Why is checking the Rhesus factor so important during the first antenatal booking visit?

options.A: To prevent common gastrointestinal infections
options.B: To prevent maternal-fetal blood incompatibility reactions
options.C: To determine the mother's daily caloric requirement
options.D: To calculate the exact birth weight of the baby

explanation: Finding Rhesus-negative mothers early lets us give them anti-D injections to keep both mother and baby safe from blood reactions. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h5)

question: What is the main reason we give folic acid supplements to women in early pregnancy?

options.A: To accelerate infant tooth eruption
options.B: To lower maternal blood pressure
options.C: To prevent neural tube defects
options.D: To stop excessive morning sickness

explanation: Folic acid taken before and during early pregnancy helps protect the baby's developing brain and spinal cord. Super important vitamin! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h6)

question: Why are iron supplements routinely given during antenatal care?

options.A: To increase the speed of fetal bone mineralization
options.B: To prevent gestational diabetes mellitus
options.C: To reduce the frequency of Braxton Hicks contractions
options.D: To support the massive expansion of maternal blood volume

explanation: Because a pregnant woman's blood volume increases so much, she needs extra iron to make enough hemoglobin and prevent anemia. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h6)

question: Which of these symptoms is a classic danger sign that could mean a pregnant woman is developing pre-eclampsia?

options.A: Mild swelling of the fingers in the morning
options.B: Occasional lower back pain
options.C: Severe headache and blurred vision
options.D: Increased appetite for sweet foods

explanation: Severe headaches and changes in vision are big red flags for dangerously high blood pressure (pre-eclampsia). Always take this seriously! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h7)

question: A patient at 32 weeks reports she has not felt her baby move all day. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: Mild physiological anemia of pregnancy
options.B: Potential fetal distress or compromise
options.C: Standard weight gain in the third trimester
options.D: Normal resting behavior of a mature fetus

explanation: Whenever a mom says baby's movements have stopped or slowed right down, treat it as an emergency and check the baby right away. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h7)

question: What is the main goal of birth preparedness and complication readiness in pregnancy?

options.A: To eliminate the need for routine antenatal visits
options.B: To choose the exact time and date of labor
options.C: To remove delays in accessing emergency obstetric care
options.D: To guarantee a home delivery without any skilled staff

explanation: Planning ahead for transport and funds helps ensure a woman gets to the hospital fast if an emergency happens. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h8)

question: A nurse is counseling a couple on birth preparedness. Which action is most important for them to plan before the due date?

options.A: Purchasing infant formula for immediate feeding
options.B: Deciding the baby's future career path
options.C: Buying expensive nursery furniture for the baby
options.D: Arranging reliable transportation to the health facility

explanation: Transport is key! Knowing how and when to get to the clinic prevents dangerous delays when labor starts. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h8)

question: What is the standard medical term for the specialized healthcare given to a woman all through her pregnancy?

options.A: Geriatric care
options.B: Postnatal care
options.C: Antenatal care
options.D: Pediatric care

explanation: You got this! Antenatal care (also called prenatal care) is simply the routine health supervision and support we give expectant mothers throughout pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T007#GNS226_U1_T007_h1)

question: Why is building an early, trusting relationship with an expectant mother so important for a nurse?

options.A: It ensures the mother will have a completely pain-free labor
options.B: It encourages the mother to return for subsequent clinic visits
options.C: It completely eliminates all risks of genetic disorders in the fetus
options.D: It replaces the need for laboratory tests during pregnancy

explanation: Spot on! When mothers trust us, they feel safe and are much more likely to keep coming back for their clinic check-ups, keeping both mum and baby safe. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T007#GNS226_U1_T007_h1)

question: Which of these is a vital disease-prevention shot routinely given during pregnancy clinics in Nigeria?

options.A: Insulin pump placement
options.B: Tetanus toxoid vaccination
options.C: Chemotherapy infusion
options.D: Joint replacement surgery

explanation: Well done! Tetanus toxoid is a routine life-saver given during pregnancy to protect both the mother and newborn baby from tetanus. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T007#GNS226_U1_T007_h2)

question: What is the main benefit of sorting pregnant women into low-risk or high-risk groups at the clinic?

options.A: Eliminating the need for routine blood pressure checks
options.B: Determining the exact biological sex of the unborn child
options.C: Targeted management and appropriate referral when needed
options.D: Deciding the exact date the baby will be born

explanation: Exactly! Grouping mothers helps us give extra attention to those who need closer monitoring, and quickly refer complex cases to doctors when necessary. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T007#GNS226_U1_T007_h2)

question: High blood pressure, protein in the urine, and sudden swelling during pregnancy are classic warning signs of:

options.A: Gestational diabetes
options.B: Placenta previa
options.C: Preeclampsia
options.D: Iron deficiency anemia

explanation: Great job! Preeclampsia is a serious pregnancy condition marked by high BP and protein in the urine that requires quick medical attention. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T007#GNS226_U1_T007_h3)

question: A mum at 28 weeks comes to the clinic with swollen face and high blood pressure. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: The fetus is growing at an unusually rapid and healthy rate
options.B: The mother is simply eating too much salt in her daily diet
options.C: This is a completely normal physical change in the third trimester
options.D: These are potential warning signs of preeclampsia requiring prompt evaluation

explanation: You nailed it! Sudden facial swelling plus high BP are red flags for preeclampsia. We always check these out immediately to keep the mum safe. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T007#GNS226_U1_T007_h3)

question: Why is taking folic acid very important in the early months of pregnancy?

options.A: To stop the mother from experiencing morning sickness
options.B: To prevent neural tube defects in the developing fetus
options.C: To ensure the baby is born with a dark hair color
options.D: To lower the mother's blood pressure immediately

explanation: Correct! Folic acid helps the baby's brain and spinal cord form properly in the early weeks, preventing serious birth defects. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T007#GNS226_U1_T007_h4)

question: Why do pregnant women routinely need iron supplements during gestation?

options.A: To harden the bones of the mother's hands and feet
options.B: To increase the amount of amniotic fluid in the womb
options.C: To support the significant increase in maternal blood volume
options.D: To prevent the baby from developing gestational diabetes

explanation: Spot on! A pregnant woman's body makes a lot more blood to support the baby, and iron helps prevent anemia during this heavy workload. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T007#GNS226_U1_T007_h4)

question: In antenatal care, what does BPCR stand for?

options.A: Baby Physical Care and Recovery
options.B: Birth Preparedness and Complication Readiness
options.C: Basic Physiological Childbirth Routine
options.D: Blood Pressure and Cardiac Response

explanation: You've got it! BPCR is all about helping families plan ahead for a normal delivery and know what to do if an emergency pops up. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T007#GNS226_U1_T007_h5)

question: What is the main goal of planning emergency transport and money before labor starts?

options.A: To replace the need for professional skilled attendants at birth
options.B: To guarantee that the mother will have a completely painless delivery
options.C: To eliminate costly delays when unexpected complications strike
options.D: To ensure the baby is born precisely on the expected due date

explanation: Exactly right! Having transport and funds ready ahead of time saves precious minutes and prevents dangerous delays if an emergency happens. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T007#GNS226_U1_T007_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a normal emotional challenge many women face during pregnancy?

options.A: Mood swings driven by profound hormonal shifts
options.B: Heightened anxiety about the upcoming labor process
options.C: Stress regarding financial changes and parenting duties
options.D: Complete emotional numbness and lack of heartbeat awareness

explanation: Well spotted! Mood swings, stress, and anxiety are totally normal with pregnancy hormones, but complete emotional numbness is not a typical response. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T007#GNS226_U1_T007_h6)

question: How does health education during antenatal clinics directly help an expectant mother?

options.A: It removes the need for physical examinations by the doctor
options.B: It guarantees that her baby will sleep through the night
options.C: It builds her confidence and encourages positive health behaviors
options.D: It completely stops her from ever experiencing physical fatigue

explanation: Spot on! Knowledge gives mums confidence, calms their fears, and guides them to take great care of themselves and their growing baby. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T007#GNS226_U1_T007_h6)

question: What is one of the main day-to-day duties of a nurse during antenatal clinic visits?

options.A: Prescribing permanent contraceptive sterilizations
options.B: Performing major surgical deliveries in the outpatient clinic
options.C: Conducting physical assessments and administering immunizations
options.D: Diagnosing rare genetic mutations in the laboratory

explanation: Correct! As a nurse, you'll check vital signs, monitor the baby's growth, and give essential vaccines like tetanus toxoid. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T007#GNS226_U1_T007_h7)

question: Why is it important for nurses to understand local customs when caring for pregnant women in their communities?

options.A: To replace all standard medical textbooks with local folklore
options.B: To avoid performing physical examinations on pregnant women
options.C: To respect local beliefs while gently correcting harmful traditional practices
options.D: To force every patient to adopt Western cultural habits immediately

explanation: You got it! Respecting culture builds trust, making it easier to guide mothers away from unsafe cultural practices with love and patience. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T007#GNS226_U1_T007_h7)

question: What is the main goal of antenatal care (ANC) services for a pregnant mother?

options.A: Determine the exact sex of the baby early on
options.B: Eliminate all physical discomforts during gestation
options.C: Monitor normal pregnancy and detect early complications
options.D: Guarantee a completely pain-free labor experience

explanation: Spotting issues early is everything! ANC is all about watching how the pregnancy progresses so you can catch and manage any little problem before it becomes serious. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h1)

question: Why are nurses so important when pregnant women come in for prenatal services?

options.A: They are legally required to perform all surgical procedures during birth
options.B: They prescribe all medications independently of medical doctors
options.C: They diagnose genetic disorders without needing laboratory equipment
options.D: They serve as the primary contact to build trust and encourage hospital deliveries

explanation: You are often the very first person she talks to! Building that warm, trusting relationship makes her feel safe and much more likely to come back for a safe hospital delivery. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h1)

question: When is the best time for a pregnant woman to come in for her first booking visit?

options.A: Right after active labor begins
options.B: During the first trimester
options.C: During the final postpartum month
options.D: Only at week thirty-six

explanation: Getting her in during the first trimester lets you set a solid health baseline right from the start and catch any early risks. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h2)

question: Why do nurses need to provide individualized care instead of treating every pregnant woman the exact same way?

options.A: It ensures that all pregnant women take the exact same supplements
options.B: Medical doctors refuse to see patients who follow standard routines
options.C: Standard hospital guidelines are illegal to use in public clinics
options.D: Every woman has unique social, cultural, and physiological needs

explanation: No two mothers are alike! Factoring in her background, culture, and unique body helps you give care that truly fits her life. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of doing a thorough initial prenatal booking visit?

options.A: To administer the final dose of the tetanus vaccine
options.B: To perform an emergency delivery for safety
options.C: To establish a complete baseline health and obstetric history
options.D: To finalize the birth certificate before delivery

explanation: Think of the booking visit as your complete roadmap. Gathering all her past and current health details helps you guide her safely through the rest of the pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h3)

question: Why is finding out if a mother is Rhesus-negative during her first visit so crucial?

options.A: It proves the mother has adequate iron levels in her blood
options.B: It guarantees the baby will never develop newborn jaundice
options.C: It allows the nurse to schedule the exact day of delivery
options.D: It helps prevent potential blood incompatibility and isoimmunization

explanation: Catching a Rhesus-negative blood type early lets you plan ahead for special care (like anti-D injections) to keep both current and future babies safe! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h3)

question: Which two quick checks must a nurse do at every single antenatal visit?

options.A: Blood pressure and urine protein testing
options.B: Internal pelvic exam and ultrasound scan
options.C: Chest X-ray and sputum culture
options.D: Blood glucose and stool microscopy

explanation: Always check BP and urine! These simple routine tests are your best tools for catching early warning signs of pre-eclampsia. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h4)

question: What are you trying to find out when you perform Leopold's maneuvers on a pregnant client?

options.A: To check the mother's cardiovascular health status
options.B: To stimulate the uterus into early contraction
options.C: To determine fetal lie, presentation, and engagement
options.D: To measure the exact weight of the placenta

explanation: Leopold's maneuvers are just feeling the bump with your hands to figure out how the baby is curled up and positioned inside as delivery gets closer. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h4)

question: Why do we routinely give iron and folic acid tablets to pregnant women?

options.A: To prevent iron-deficiency anemia and support fetal development
options.B: To completely eliminate morning sickness throughout the pregnancy
options.C: To speed up the onset of labor during the final week
options.D: To ensure the baby is born with a higher birth weight

explanation: A pregnant woman's body needs extra blood volume! Iron prevents anemia, and folate protects the baby's brain and spine development. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h5)

question: A 28-week pregnant client comes in complaining of a pounding headache and sudden blurry vision. What should pop into your head first?

options.A: A simple reaction to eating too much sugar
options.B: Signs of potential pregnancy-induced hypertension
options.C: Normal physiological changes due to increased sleep
options.D: Standard fatigue that requires drinking more coffee

explanation: Headaches and blurry vision combined in pregnancy are classic red flags for pre-eclampsia. Grab that BP cuff right away! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h5)

question: What is the main reason we give intermittent preventive treatment (IPTp) for malaria during pregnancy?

options.A: To boost the mother's daily caloric and protein intake
options.B: To prevent the development of gestational diabetes mellitus
options.C: To cure a chronic respiratory infection in the mother
options.D: To reduce placental malaria parasitemia and associated risks

explanation: In malaria-endemic areas like ours, IPTp stops malaria parasites from hiding out in the placenta where they can harm both mother and baby. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h6)

question: Which medication do nurses rely on to manage severe pre-eclampsia and stop dangerous seizures?

options.A: Oxytocin infusion
options.B: Magnesium sulfate
options.C: Ferric folate syrup
options.D: Amoxicillin capsules

explanation: Magnesium sulfate is your go-to lifesaver drug for preventing and controlling eclamptic fits when blood pressure gets dangerously high. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h6)

question: What is a major part of helping a pregnant client make a practical birth plan?

options.A: Arranging transportation and identifying the place of delivery
options.B: Purchasing expensive imported toys for the nursery
options.C: Choosing the exact college the child will attend later
options.D: Deciding whether the mother will return to work in a week

explanation: A good birth plan solves logistics! Knowing how she will get to the hospital and exactly which health facility she is going to prevents dangerous delays during labor. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h7)

question: Why is it best to start talking about family planning during antenatal care rather than waiting until after the baby is born?

options.A: Postpartum mothers are too tired to understand reproductive health
options.B: Hospitals forbid mothers from discussing birth control after birth
options.C: It is a legal requirement to purchase contraceptives before leaving the hospital
options.D: It gives parents adequate time to make informed choices about birth spacing

explanation: Bringing it up during ANC gives couples plenty of calm time to talk about birth spacing before the rush and exhaustion of newborn care sets in. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h7)

question: Why is the antenatal clinic card given to the pregnant woman to carry around herself?

options.A: Because clinics are not allowed to store paper records on site
options.B: To prove she has paid all her hospital bills in advance
options.C: To serve as a ticket for free meals at the hospital canteen
options.D: So any healthcare worker can review her history during an emergency

explanation: If an emergency happens away from her regular clinic, any nurse or doctor can instantly check her medical history right off her personal card! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h8)

question: What should you do as a nurse at a primary clinic if a patient walks in with a complication you cannot handle?

options.A: Wait until the next scheduled clinic day to ask a senior doctor
options.B: Send the patient home immediately with instructions to rest
options.C: Stabilize the patient, write a referral letter, and contact the receiving facility
options.D: Ignore the complication since primary clinics handle all cases

explanation: Always stabilize first! Then, make sure you write a clear referral note and call ahead so the bigger hospital is ready to take over her care smoothly. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h8)

question: What is the main goal of Emergency Obstetric Care (EmOC)?

options.A: Treating sudden life-threatening pregnancy complications
options.B: Monitoring normal fetal growth during the third trimester
options.C: Providing routine antenatal counseling and vitamins
options.D: Assessing nutritional status prior to conception

explanation: You've got this! EmOC is all about handling sudden, dangerous emergencies during labor, delivery, and after birth to save both mother and baby. Great job! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T009#GNS226_U1_T009_h1)

question: Why can routine antenatal care alone miss some pregnancy dangers?

options.A: Pregnant women rarely attend clinics during their first trimester
options.B: Antenatal clinics refuse to monitor blood pressure during visits
options.C: Many critical emergencies strike unpredictably without prior warning signs
options.D: Complications only develop after healthcare facilities close for the day

explanation: Even if a pregnancy looks completely healthy, sudden issues like heavy bleeding or high blood pressure can pop up out of nowhere. That is why emergency care is so vital! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T009#GNS226_U1_T009_h1)

question: Which type of facility is fully equipped to perform emergency C-sections?

options.A: Basic Emergency Obstetric Care health posts
options.B: Comprehensive Emergency Obstetric Care facilities
options.C: Community pharmacy outreach centers
options.D: Primary maternal health counseling desks

explanation: Well done! Major surgeries like Cesarean sections need a CEmOC facility because they have a proper operating theatre and surgical team ready. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T009#GNS226_U1_T009_h2)

question: What is the main difference between BEmOC and CEmOC facilities?

options.A: BEmOC handles medical management and simple procedures without major surgery
options.B: CEmOC facilities never provide newborn resuscitation services
options.C: CEmOC centers only offer outpatient antenatal consultations
options.D: BEmOC facilities routinely perform elective surgical sterilizations

explanation: Think of BEmOC as handling medications, simple births, and first aid, while CEmOC takes on major surgeries and blood transfusions. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T009#GNS226_U1_T009_h2)

question: What symptom turns pre-eclampsia into full-blown eclampsia?

options.A: Total cessation of fetal heart tones
options.B: A sudden drop in body temperature
options.C: The onset of convulsive seizures
options.D: Severe localized pain in the lower back

explanation: Spot on! Pre-eclampsia has high blood pressure and protein in the urine, but once seizures start, it is classified as eclampsia. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T009#GNS226_U1_T009_h3)

question: A new mother soaks two heavy pads in twenty minutes and feels dizzy. What should you suspect?

options.A: Postpartum hemorrhage
options.B: Normal postpartum lochia rubra
options.C: Delayed uterine subinvolution
options.D: Gestational trophoblastic disease

explanation: Rapid, heavy bleeding combined with dizziness is a classic sign of postpartum hemorrhage. Quick action is key here! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T009#GNS226_U1_T009_h3)

question: How many total signal functions define a fully working CEmOC facility?

options.A: Twelve
options.B: Three
options.C: Nine
options.D: Five

explanation: You got it! They handle the 7 basic signal functions plus 2 comprehensive ones, bringing the total to 9. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T009#GNS226_U1_T009_h4)

question: Why do health teams check 'signal functions' instead of just looking at hospital buildings?

options.A: To verify that actual life-saving treatments are actively being delivered to patients
options.B: To calculate the exact electricity consumption of hospital lighting
options.C: To determine the architectural layout required for nursing stations
options.D: To audit the daily cleaning schedules of delivery rooms

explanation: A nice building isn't enough! Signal functions prove that the staff, drugs, and equipment are actually there to save lives. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T009#GNS226_U1_T009_h4)

question: What is your very first priority when a pregnant patient arrives in an emergency?

options.A: Completing the hospital billing and admission forms
options.B: Obtaining a detailed family medical history
options.C: Weighing the patient on the clinic scale
options.D: Ensuring a patent airway and stable breathing

explanation: Always remember ABCDE! Airway and breathing come before any paperwork or routine questions in an emergency. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T009#GNS226_U1_T009_h5)

question: Which of these is a dangerous mistake during an emergency obstetric triage?

options.A: Notifying the medical doctor immediately upon finding abnormal bleeding
options.B: Placing an unstable patient in a quiet resuscitation bay
options.C: Delaying vital sign assessment to fill out admission paperwork
options.D: Checking maternal blood pressure upon entry

explanation: Never let paperwork delay patient care! In emergencies, checking vital signs and stabilizing the patient comes first. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T009#GNS226_U1_T009_h5)

question: Which medication is standard for stopping seizures in a pregnant woman with eclampsia?

options.A: Sodium bicarbonate
options.B: Magnesium sulfate
options.C: Calcium gluconate
options.D: Diazepam drops

explanation: Magnesium sulfate is the magic word here! It is the go-to drug to control and prevent seizures in eclampsia. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T009#GNS226_U1_T009_h6)

question: A patient has heavy postpartum bleeding and a soft, boggy uterus. What should you do first?

options.A: Prepare the patient for an immediate MRI scan
options.B: Encourage the patient to walk around the ward
options.C: Perform bimanual uterine massage
options.D: Insert a nasogastric tube for decompression

explanation: Massaging the uterus helps the muscle contract tightly, which closes off bleeding blood vessels. Great nursing intervention! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T009#GNS226_U1_T009_h6)

question: Why is it important to call the receiving hospital before transferring an emergency patient?

options.A: It allows the receiving team to prepare blood products and surgical staff in advance
options.B: It ensures that the transferring nurse does not need to accompany the patient
options.C: It eliminates the need for any documentation to travel with the patient
options.D: It guarantees that the patient will not incur any hospital treatment fees

explanation: Calling ahead gives the team time to prep the operating room and blood bank so treatment starts the second the ambulance arrives. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T009#GNS226_U1_T009_h7)

question: What must you ensure before sending an emergency obstetric patient on a long ambulance ride?

options.A: The patient has signed discharge papers against medical advice
options.B: All routine hospital laundry duties have been fully completed
options.C: A family member has paid the complete transport fare in cash
options.D: The patient is stabilized and secure intravenous access is established

explanation: Always make sure your patient is as stable as possible with a working IV line so you can give fluids or meds during transit. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T009#GNS226_U1_T009_h7)

question: Why do nurses monitor urine output closely after a patient suffers severe bleeding?

options.A: To calculate the exact dietary protein intake required
options.B: To measure the effectiveness of routine infant feeding schedules
options.C: To evaluate renal perfusion and detect early kidney injury
options.D: To determine when the patient can be discharged home

explanation: When blood loss causes shock, the kidneys can suffer. Watching urine output helps us catch early signs of kidney trouble! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T009#GNS226_U1_T009_h8)

question: What emotional care is essential for a woman recovering from a scary birth emergency?

options.A: Emotional debriefing and supportive counseling about the traumatic event
options.B: Immediate transfer to a psychiatric institution for sedation
options.C: Complete isolation from family members to ensure physical rest
options.D: Strict avoidance of talking about the childbirth experience

explanation: Birth emergencies can be terrifying. A listening ear and compassionate counseling help mothers heal both inside and out. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T009#GNS226_U1_T009_h8)

question: What is the typical duration of the postpartum period known as the puerperium?

options.A: Three months
options.B: Two weeks
options.C: Six weeks
options.D: One year

explanation: The puerperium generally lasts for about six weeks after childbirth, which is the time required for maternal organs to return close to their pre-pregnant state. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h1)

question: Why is nursing care during the puerperium so important for a new mother?

options.A: It ensures the mother avoids all postpartum sadness
options.B: It prevents sudden complications like hemorrhage and infection
options.C: It eliminates the need for any follow-up doctor visits
options.D: It guarantees the infant will sleep through the night

explanation: You've got this! Regular checks in the postpartum period help catch physical problems early, keeping the new mother safe and healthy during her recovery. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h1)

question: What do we call the process where the uterus shrinks back to its normal, non-pregnant size?

options.A: Involution
options.B: Diastasis
options.C: Atrophy
options.D: Lochia

explanation: Great job! Involution is just the medical term for the uterus quickly returning to its pre-pregnant state through steady contractions. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h2)

question: You feel a patient's uterus (fundus) on her second day after birth and notice it feels soft and is higher than expected. What should you do first?

options.A: Encourage the patient to walk around the ward
options.B: Massage the fundus gently until it becomes firm
options.C: Administer an intravenous fluid bolus
options.D: Document that the uterus is healing normally

explanation: A soft or 'boggy' uterus needs a little help! Massaging it gently makes the muscle fibers tighten up, which stops heavy bleeding. You're doing great. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h2)

question: In the popular BUBBLE-EE postpartum assessment guide, what does the second 'B' stand for?

options.A: Bonding
options.B: Bleeding
options.C: Bladder
options.D: Bowel

explanation: Remember the checklist: Breasts, Uterus, Bowel, Bladder, Lochia, Episiotomy, Extremities, and Emotions. You'll master this assessment in no time! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h3)

question: Why is checking the bladder so important in the first few hours after childbirth?

options.A: Urinary retention always leads to permanent kidney failure
options.B: A full bladder pushes the uterus out of place and causes heavy bleeding
options.C: Bladder fullness is the primary sign of postpartum preeclampsia
options.D: It prevents the lochia from changing from red to white

explanation: Think of it this way: a full bladder takes up space and pushes against the uterus, stopping it from contracting properly. Keeping the bladder empty keeps mom safe from extra bleeding! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h3)

question: Why do nurses apply an ice pack to the perineum right after a vaginal delivery?

options.A: To speed up the return of lochia alba
options.B: To reduce localized swelling and numb pain
options.C: To prevent the uterus from becoming boggy
options.D: To stimulate early bowel movements

explanation: Ice is wonderful here! It narrows the blood vessels, which quickly brings down swelling and helps numb the area so the mother feels more comfortable. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h4)

question: Why do mothers who have given birth before (multiparous women) often feel stronger afterpains than first-time mothers?

options.A: Their perineal wounds are always surgically larger
options.B: They are more sensitive to standard doses of analgesics
options.C: They produce significantly less lochia than primiparous mothers
options.D: Their uterine muscles lose tone and contract intermittently with greater force

explanation: Because her uterus has worked before, it doesn't stay clamped down all at once. Instead, it relaxes and contracts rhythmically, leading to stronger cramps as it gets back into shape. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h4)

question: What direction should you teach a new mother to clean her perineal area?

options.A: In a circular scrubbing motion
options.B: From front to back
options.C: From back to front
options.D: From side to side

explanation: Always front to back! This simple habit stops germs from the anal area from spreading to the healing vaginal and urinary openings. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h5)

question: What is the main reason we tell postpartum mothers to drink plenty of fluids and eat high-fiber foods?

options.A: To stop painful uterine afterpains
options.B: To turn lochia serosa into lochia rubra
options.C: To shrink the size of the bladder
options.D: To prevent postpartum constipation

explanation: Straining after delivery can be very painful, especially with stitches or piles (hemorrhoids). Fluids and fiber keep things soft and easy! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h5)

question: What is the maximum expected duration for normal postpartum blues before they should resolve?

options.A: Forty-eight hours
options.B: One year
options.C: Six months
options.D: Two weeks

explanation: Postpartum blues typically peak around the fourth or fifth day and resolve spontaneously within the first two weeks after delivery. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h6)

question: On day four after delivery, a breastfeeding mother tells you she feels overwhelmed and cries easily when the baby fusses, but she loves holding her baby and sleeps well when the baby sleeps. What is your best response?

options.A: Inform her that she shows classic signs of postpartum psychosis
options.B: Tell her to stop breastfeeding immediately to stabilize her hormones
options.C: Reassure her that these feelings are common postpartum blues and will likely pass soon
options.D: Immediately arrange an emergency psychiatric admission for depression

explanation: Tearfulness and mood swings in the first two weeks are totally normal 'baby blues.' A listening ear and gentle reassurance work wonders here! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h6)

question: Which of these is a classic sign of mastitis in a breastfeeding mother?

options.A: Foul-smelling brownish lochia
options.B: Localized breast redness, pain, and fever
options.C: Complete absence of milk production
options.D: Painless bilateral breast enlargement

explanation: Mastitis means the breast tissue is inflamed or infected. You'll usually spot a painful, red, warm area on the breast along with fever and body aches. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h7)

question: On her third day after delivery, a patient complains that her right calf is painful, swollen, and feels warmer than the left. What is the most important thing you should do?

options.A: Encourage her to walk briskly around the hospital corridor
options.B: Massage the calf firmly to break up any muscle cramps
options.C: Apply an ice pack directly to the painful calf muscle
options.D: Instruct the patient to stay off her feet and notify the physician immediately

explanation: This sounds like a deep vein thrombosis (blood clot). Never massage a suspected clot, as it could break loose and travel to the lungs—always keep the patient resting and call the doctor right away! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h7)

question: What do we call the thick, yellowish first milk produced right after birth?

options.A: Colostrum
options.B: Lochia
options.C: Surfactant
options.D: Meconium

explanation: Colostrum is like liquid gold for the baby! It's packed with antibodies and nutrients to protect the newborn against early infections. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h8)

question: What is one of the biggest benefits of placing a newborn directly on the mother's bare chest (skin-to-skin contact) right after birth?

options.A: It helps stabilize the infant's temperature and blood sugar
options.B: It prevents the mother from experiencing afterpains
options.C: It completely eliminates the risk of newborn jaundice
options.D: It guarantees the infant will latch without any assistance

explanation: Skin-to-skin is magical! The mother's body acts like a natural incubator, helping the baby's breathing, temperature, and blood sugar stay steady. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h8)

question: Why is family planning counseling so important before a mother is discharged from the postpartum ward?

options.A: Ovulation can occur before the first postpartum menstrual period returns
options.B: Sexual intercourse is strictly forbidden for a full year
options.C: Hormonal contraceptives are required to stop lochia flow
options.D: Pregnancy is impossible during the first six months postpartum

explanation: Many women are surprised to learn that an egg can be released (ovulation) before their monthly period ever comes back. Early advice helps them plan safely! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h9)

question: Which report from a postpartum mother at home means she needs to see a doctor urgently?

options.A: Experiencing mild fatigue in the late afternoon
options.B: Having pinkish-brown lochia on day ten
options.C: Soaking through more than one sanitary pad in an hour
options.D: Feeling mild muscle soreness from walking

explanation: Soaking a pad or more every single hour is a major warning sign of late postpartum hemorrhage. She needs immediate medical attention! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h9)

question: What is the nurse's very first priority right after a baby is born?

options.A: To clean all the white cheesy stuff off the skin
options.B: To give the first routine vitamin K injection
options.C: To check if the newborn is vigorous and breathing well
options.D: To check the exact birth weight on a scale

explanation: As soon as a baby arrives, our main check is to see how well they are transitioning and if they need help taking their first breaths. You've got this! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T011#GNS226_U1_T011_h1)

question: Which set of findings means a newborn can safely stay right with mum for skin-to-skin care?

options.A: Full-term baby, thick meconium, weak cry, and floppy
options.B: Post-term baby, bloody fluid, gasping, and stiff posture
options.C: Preterm baby, stained fluid, quiet, and limp limbs
options.D: Full-term baby, clear fluid, crying, and good muscle tone

explanation: A baby born at full term who cries well and has strong muscle tone is doing great! They don't need to be separated from mum. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T011#GNS226_U1_T011_h1)

question: At what exact times do we check the Apgar score for a newborn?

options.A: Every 30 minutes for the first two hours
options.B: At birth, 1 hour, and 6 hours of life
options.C: Right at birth and again at 10 minutes
options.D: At 1 minute and 5 minutes after birth

explanation: Remember the classic rule: Apgar is routinely checked at 1 minute of life, and then again at 5 minutes to track how the baby is adjusting. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T011#GNS226_U1_T011_h2)

question: What is the true purpose of doing an Apgar score in the delivery room?

options.A: To diagnose long-term brain disabilities
options.B: To see how well the baby is adjusting to life outside
options.C: To decide the exact second resuscitation must start
options.D: To predict future intelligence in school

explanation: Resuscitation actually starts before the 1-minute Apgar is even done! The score just helps us see how the baby is responding and adapting over those first few minutes. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T011#GNS226_U1_T011_h2)

question: What is the single most important and effective step when trying to resuscitate a newborn?

options.A: Giving emergency IV drugs
options.B: Ventilating the newborn's lungs with air or oxygen
options.C: Giving a quick fluid drip
options.D: Doing chest compressions

explanation: Most newborn emergencies happen because they aren't breathing. Getting oxygen into their lungs is always our top rescue step! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T011#GNS226_U1_T011_h3)

question: Why is drying a newborn immediately after birth so crucial?

options.A: It washes away skin oils
options.B: It lowers their heart rate to normal
options.C: It stimulates breathing and keeps them warm
options.D: It stops baby jaundice from developing

explanation: Drying wipes away wet fluid so the baby doesn't get chilled from evaporation, and the rubbing action acts as a gentle nudge telling them to breathe! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T011#GNS226_U1_T011_h3)

question: Since newborns cannot shiver when they are cold, how do they mainly generate body heat?

options.A: By burning regular white fat under the skin
options.B: By shaking their arm and leg muscles
options.C: By sweating more on their skin
options.D: By burning special brown fat deposits

explanation: Babies have a special type of fat called 'brown adipose tissue'. Burning this fat creates heat internally without needing to shiver! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T011#GNS226_U1_T011_h4)

question: A nurse places a naked newborn onto a cold metal scale, making the baby lose body heat. What is this specific type of heat loss called?

options.A: Conduction
options.B: Evaporation
options.C: Convection
options.D: Radiation

explanation: Think of Conduction as direct contact. When a baby touches a cooler solid surface directly, heat transfers right out of them. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T011#GNS226_U1_T011_h4)

question: What triggers the baby's circulatory system to close its fetal blood shunts?

options.A: Putting eye ointment in
options.B: Changes in oxygen levels and clamping the cord
options.C: The vernix washing away
options.D: Brown fat kicking in

explanation: When the cord is clamped and the baby takes that first big breath, oxygen levels change in the chest, telling those temporary fetal shunts to close up. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T011#GNS226_U1_T011_h5)

question: Why is lung surfactant so vital for a newborn's breathing?

options.A: It warms up the cold air entering the nose
options.B: It fights off chest infections
options.C: It pumps fluid out of the tiny airways
options.D: It reduces surface tension in the alveoli to keep them open

explanation: Surfactant acts like a slick coating inside the tiny air sacs (alveoli) so they don't stick shut and collapse every time the baby breathes out. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T011#GNS226_U1_T011_h5)

question: What is the main health benefit of early breast milk (colostrum) for a newborn?

options.A: It gives them high dietary fiber
options.B: It stops jaundice from happening
options.C: It acts as a sleeping pill
options.D: It provides heavy antibodies and protein to protect the tummy

explanation: Colostrum is liquid gold! It is packed with protective antibodies (like IgA) that line the baby's gut to fight off early germs. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T011#GNS226_U1_T011_h6)

question: What is the biggest advantage of rooming-in (keeping mum and baby in the same bed space)?

options.A: It helps mum spot feeding cues early and builds milk supply
options.B: It keeps the baby warm using room lamps
options.C: It means nurses don't have to check vitals as often
options.D: It lets the mother sleep all night without waking

explanation: When mum and baby stay together, mum can easily catch those early feeding cues (like rooting), which makes breastfeeding go much smoother. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T011#GNS226_U1_T011_h6)

question: Why do we give a routine injection of Vitamin K to all newborns shortly after birth?

options.A: To boost their appetite for milk
options.B: To prevent dangerous bleeding since their clotting factors are low
options.C: To protect against hepatitis B
options.D: To protect against eye infections from the birth canal

explanation: Babies are born with sterile bellies that haven't built up the gut bacteria needed to make Vitamin K yet, putting them at risk for bleeding until feeding gets going. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T011#GNS226_U1_T011_h7)

question: What specific condition does erythromycin eye ointment prevent in a newborn?

options.A: Congenital cataracts from viral infections
options.B: Dry eyes from forgetting to blink
options.C: Blinding eye infections from maternal sexually transmitted bugs
options.D: Blocked tear ducts from narrow passages

explanation: It's a standard protective step given right after birth to shield the baby's eyes from infections like gonorrhea or chlamydia picked up in the birth canal. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T011#GNS226_U1_T011_h7)

question: What are the normal blood vessels found inside a healthy newborn umbilical cord?

options.A: Two arteries and one vein
options.B: Three arteries and two veins
options.C: Two veins and one artery
options.D: One artery and one vein

explanation: Think 'AVA': Artery, Vein, Artery (two arteries, one vein). Finding this normal trio is a great reassuring sign during assessment! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T011#GNS226_U1_T011_h8)

question: Which of these is NOT normal and actually represents a danger sign in a newborn?

options.A: Passing dark green meconium poop on the first day
options.B: Grunting when breathing and chest sinking in
options.C: Spitting up a tiny bit of milk after feeding
options.D: Sleeping soundly between regular feeds

explanation: Chest retractions and grunting are red flags! They tell us the baby is working way too hard to breathe and needs urgent help. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T011#GNS226_U1_T011_h9)

question: A mother calls because her 2-day-old baby is super sleepy and won't feed at all. What should you suspect as a nurse?

options.A: A mild milk allergy needing a brand change
options.B: Normal newborn behavior that will fix itself
options.C: A serious hidden problem needing urgent medical review
options.D: Just normal tiredness from growing

explanation: Lethargy and refusing to feed are major warning signs in babies. It could point to infection, low blood sugar, or dehydration—always treat it as urgent! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T011#GNS226_U1_T011_h9)

question: What is the safest sleeping position to teach parents to prevent SIDS (Sudden Infant Death Syndrome)?

options.A: On the tummy with the head turned
options.B: Sitting upright in a baby chair
options.C: On the side propped up with pillows
options.D: Flat on the back on a firm, flat mattress

explanation: Always 'Back to Sleep'! Placing babies flat on their back on a firm surface is the golden rule for safe infant sleep. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T011#GNS226_U1_T011_h10)

question: Why is it so important to have a clinic follow-up visit within 48 to 72 hours after leaving the hospital?

options.A: To check weight gain, hydration, and watch for yellow jaundice
options.B: To do the official hearing test
options.C: To give routine childhood vaccines
options.D: To pull out the remaining cord stump

explanation: Those first few days at home can be tricky with feeding. An early check helps us catch weight loss, dehydration, or worsening jaundice early on! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T011#GNS226_U1_T011_h10)

question: Up to how many days after childbirth can a mother's death still be classified as maternal mortality?

options.A: Ninety days
options.B: Forty-two days
options.C: Seven days
options.D: Fourteen days

explanation: You've got this! Officially, maternal death includes any death during pregnancy or within 42 days (6 weeks) after delivery. Keep that timeline in mind! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T012#GNS226_U1_T012_h1)

question: What is the main difference between a direct and an indirect obstetric death?

options.A: Direct deaths occur during labor, while indirect deaths occur in the postpartum period
options.B: Direct deaths are caused by infections, while indirect deaths are caused by bleeding
options.C: Direct deaths happen in the hospital, while indirect deaths happen at home
options.D: Direct deaths are from pregnancy complications, while indirect deaths are from pre-existing diseases worsened by pregnancy

explanation: Spot on! Direct causes come straight from pregnancy or childbirth issues (like bleeding), while indirect causes happen when a pre-existing condition (like heart disease or malaria) gets worse because of the pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T012#GNS226_U1_T012_h1)

question: What does the maternal mortality ratio actually measure?

options.A: Total deaths of women of childbearing age
options.B: Infant deaths per 1,000 live births
options.C: Deaths per 1,000 pregnant women
options.D: Deaths per 100,000 live births

explanation: Think of it this way: the maternal mortality ratio tells us how many mothers we lose for every 100,000 live births. Super important metric in public health! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T012#GNS226_U1_T012_h2)

question: Why is a pregnant woman living in a remote rural Nigerian village at the highest risk for maternal mortality?

options.A: Strict adherence to modern medical guidelines
options.B: A higher biological predisposition to bleeding
options.C: Geographic isolation and limited access to emergency obstetric care
options.D: Overuse of specialized antenatal clinics

explanation: Distance matters! Living far from a clinic means severe delays in getting emergency help when complications arise. This is a huge challenge in rural healthcare. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T012#GNS226_U1_T012_h2)

question: What is the single leading cause of maternal death worldwide?

options.A: Postpartum hemorrhage
options.B: Gestational diabetes
options.C: Malaria
options.D: Eclampsia

explanation: Severe bleeding after childbirth (PPH) is the number one global killer of new mothers. As a nurse, knowing how to spot and manage PPH is a total lifesaver! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T012#GNS226_U1_T012_h3)

question: Which of these is considered a direct cause of maternal death?

options.A: Sickle cell anemia
options.B: Eclampsia
options.C: Severe malaria
options.D: Rheumatic heart disease

explanation: Eclampsia (severe pregnancy-induced high blood pressure leading to seizures) is a direct complication of pregnancy. The others are medical conditions made worse by pregnancy (indirect). [learn more](GNS226_U1_T012#GNS226_U1_T012_h3)

question: In the Three Delays model, what does the 'first delay' stand for?

options.A: Delay in arriving at the hospital due to bad roads
options.B: Delay in receiving treatment from doctors
options.C: Delay in diagnosing the pregnancy
