explanation: As blood floods back from the newly working lungs into the left side of the heart, the pressure pushes the little flap of the foramen ovale shut. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h7)

question: Which temporary foetal structure turns into the ligamentum arteriosum after birth?

options.A: Umbilical vein
options.B: Ductus venosus
options.C: Ductus arteriosus
options.D: Foramen ovale

explanation: Spot on! Once the ductus arteriosus finishes its job and seals up with high oxygen levels, it turns into a sturdy little ligament called the ligamentum arteriosum. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h7)

question: What is it called when the ductus arteriosus fails to close normally after a baby is born?

options.A: Patent ductus arteriosus
options.B: Umbilical cord rupture
options.C: Hepatic duct closure
options.D: Foramen ovale stenosis

explanation: You've got this! 'Patent' simply means open. If that little bypass tube stays open past the newborn period, we call it a patent ductus arteriosus (PDA). [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h8)

question: Which sign is a nurse most likely to notice in a newborn with an open heart shunt like PDA?

options.A: High fever accompanied by generalized body rash
options.B: Extreme weight gain within the first twenty-four hours
options.C: An abnormal heart murmur and breathing difficulty
options.D: Complete inability to pass any meconium stool

explanation: Brilliant! Extra blood swirling through unclosed shunts creates extra sounds we hear as a murmur, and extra fluid can make the baby breathe a bit faster. You're learning real clinical skills! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h8)

question: What is the main job of the foramen ovale in a baby before birth?

options.A: Connect the pulmonary artery directly to the aorta
options.B: Drain waste products directly into the umbilical vein
options.C: Supply oxygenated blood to the developing liver tissue
options.D: Shunt blood from the right atrium to the left atrium

explanation: Great job! Before birth, a baby's lungs aren't being used yet. The foramen ovale acts like a shortcut door between the upper heart chambers, letting oxygen-rich blood skip the resting lungs and head straight out to the body. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T007#GNS226_U2_T007_h1)

question: Why does most of a baby's blood skip the lungs before birth?

options.A: Foetal lung tissue requires very little blood to survive and grow
options.B: The pulmonary arteries are completely blocked by scar tissue
options.C: The lungs are filled with fluid and do not yet oxygenate blood
options.D: Blood pressure in the left ventricle is much higher than the right

explanation: You've got this! Since the baby gets all its oxygen from mum through the placenta, the lungs are resting and filled with fluid. So, the body naturally diverts blood away from them. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T007#GNS226_U2_T007_h1)

question: How does a newborn's very first breath instantly change blood flow in the heart?

options.A: It causes blood to back up into the superior vena cava from the lungs
options.B: It increases pressure in the right atrium to force the ductus open wider
options.C: It lowers pulmonary resistance, encouraging blood to flow into the lungs
options.D: It stops blood from returning to the right side of the heart entirely

explanation: Amazing! When air rushes into the baby's lungs for the first time, the blood vessels inside open right up. This makes it super easy for blood to flow in and pick up oxygen. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T007#GNS226_U2_T007_h2)

question: What physical pressure change forces the foramen ovale to snap shut when a baby is born?

options.A: Direct action of circulating maternal hormones in the blood
options.B: Higher pressure in the left atrium than the right atrium
options.C: Muscular spasms triggered by cold air hitting the skin
options.D: Complete physical scarring of the tissue within seconds

explanation: You're doing great! As blood rushes back from the freshly filled lungs into the left side of the heart, the pressure on the left side goes up, pushing that little flap door firmly shut. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T007#GNS226_U2_T007_h3)

question: A healthy newborn cries hard and briefly gets a little blue around the lips. Why might this happen with the foramen ovale?

options.A: Vigorous crying can raise right-sided heart pressure and reopen the valve temporarily
options.B: The umbilical cord was clamped too tightly, cutting off systemic oxygen
options.C: Crying stops blood flow through the lungs completely for several minutes
options.D: The ductus arteriosus has permanently scarred too early in development

explanation: Don't worry, this is normal! Straining from a big cry can temporarily spike pressure on the right side of the heart, gently pushing that recently closed flap open for just a second. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T007#GNS226_U2_T007_h3)

question: What chemical trigger makes the ductus arteriosus close up after birth?

options.A: High blood oxygen levels
options.B: Elevated carbon dioxide levels
options.C: Low systemic blood pressure
options.D: High levels of maternal estrogen

explanation: Wonderful! The sudden surge of oxygen in the baby's bloodstream acts like a natural signal telling the walls of the ductus arteriosus to tighten up and close. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T007#GNS226_U2_T007_h4)

question: Why do premature babies often have trouble getting their ductus arteriosus to close?

options.A: The umbilical cord was left unclamped for too long after delivery
options.B: Their tissues are more sensitive to prostaglandins and have lower blood oxygen levels
options.C: Their liver produces excessive amounts of bile that block circulation
options.D: Their left atrium has too much pressure compared to the right atrium

explanation: You're learning fast! Preterm babies often have immature lungs (meaning less oxygen) and higher levels of natural chemicals that keep that shortcut vessel open. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T007#GNS226_U2_T007_h4)

question: What do the umbilical arteries do the moment a baby is born?

options.A: They widen to allow increased blood flow to the skin
options.B: They constrict tightly to prevent blood loss
options.C: They turn directly into the ligamentum venosum
options.D: They remain open to drain waste into the bladder

explanation: Brilliant! The walls of these arteries react to temperature changes and fresh oxygen by clamping down hard, acting as the baby's built-in safety lock against bleeding. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T007#GNS226_U2_T007_h5)

question: What is the permanent adult name for the leftover, closed-up ductus venosus inside the liver?

options.A: Medial umbilical ligament
options.B: Ligamentum venosum
options.C: Fossa ovalis
options.D: Ligamentum teres

explanation: You've got it! Once that old fetal bypass inside the liver shuts down for good, it turns into a fibrous little band known as the ligamentum venosum. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T007#GNS226_U2_T007_h5)

question: Which heart chamber grows thicker and more muscular in the weeks after birth because of its new workload?

options.A: Right ventricle
options.B: Right atrium
options.C: Left ventricle
options.D: Left atrium

explanation: Fantastic! Because the left ventricle is now pumping blood through the entire body without the placenta's help, its muscle works harder and naturally grows thicker over time. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T007#GNS226_U2_T007_h6)

question: A healthy full-term baby is a few days old. How does blood flow through its heart now compared to inside the womb?

options.A: Deoxygenated blood travels directly back to the placenta via the cord
options.B: Blood bypasses the pulmonary circuit via the open ductus arteriosus
options.C: All blood from the right side now flows entirely through the lungs
options.D: Oxygenated blood continues to cross directly from right to left atrium

explanation: Spot on! With all the baby shunts closed up, the heart circulation is fully independent: the right side pumps blood through the lungs, and the left side pumps it to the body. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T007#GNS226_U2_T007_h6)

question: What is a major warning sign that a newborn is struggling to make the normal transition to baby circulation?

options.A: High resting body temperature
options.B: Persistent central cyanosis
options.C: Excessive weight gain on day one
options.D: Frequent passing of meconium

explanation: You're doing great! A bluish tint around the baby's core, lips, or tongue tells us that oxygen-poor blood is still somehow bypassing the lungs or mixing where it shouldn't. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T007#GNS226_U2_T007_h7)

question: Why do nurses check oxygen levels (pulse oximetry) on both a newborn's right hand and their feet?

options.A: To confirm that the umbilical cord was clamped in the correct location
options.B: To compare pre-ductal and post-ductal oxygen levels for abnormal shunting
options.C: To measure how fast blood is traveling through the ductus venosus
options.D: To ensure the liver is receiving enough blood through the hepatic portal system

explanation: Brilliant nursing logic! The right hand gets blood before the ductus arteriosus shortcut, while the feet get blood after it. Comparing them helps nurses catch hidden heart issues early. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T007#GNS226_U2_T007_h7)

question: What do we call the tiny finger-like bits of the placenta that dip into the mother's blood to swap nutrients?

options.A: Umbilical rings
options.B: Amniotic folds
options.C: Chorionic villi
options.D: Decidua basalis

explanation: Great job! Chorionic villi are those lovely little finger-like projections that increase the surface area so the baby and mother can easily exchange nutrients and gases. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T008#GNS226_U2_T008_h1)

question: Why is it actually a good thing that the mother's blood and the baby's blood do not mix directly?

options.A: To keep the fetal body temperature lower than the mother's core temperature
options.B: To allow the placenta to produce hormones without interference
options.C: To prevent the mother's high blood pressure from damaging fragile fetal blood vessels
options.D: To stop the fetus from rejecting the mother's blood cells immediately

explanation: Spot on! Mother's blood pressure can be quite high, so keeping the bloodstreams separate protects the baby's tiny, delicate blood vessels from bursting. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T008#GNS226_U2_T008_h1)

question: How do oxygen and carbon dioxide easily move back and forth across the placental membrane?

options.A: Osmotic filtration
options.B: Pinocytosis
options.C: Active transport
options.D: Simple diffusion

explanation: You've got it! Gases just drift naturally across the membrane from high to low concentration using simple diffusion, needing zero energy from the baby. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T008#GNS226_U2_T008_h2)

question: What makes fetal hemoglobin so special compared to an adult's hemoglobin?

options.A: It changes color faster in bright light.
options.B: It carries more white blood cells.
options.C: It is immune to carbon dioxide poisoning.
options.D: It holds onto oxygen much more tightly.

explanation: Brilliant! Fetal hemoglobin grabs oxygen extra tightly so it can successfully steal oxygen away from the mother's blood across the placenta. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T008#GNS226_U2_T008_h2)

question: What is the main food and energy source that fuels a growing fetus?

options.A: Proteins
options.B: Lactic acid
options.C: Fats
options.D: Glucose

explanation: Correct! Glucose crosses the placenta super easily and acts as the primary fuel keeping the baby growing and developing nicely. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T008#GNS226_U2_T008_h3)

question: If a pregnant mum temporarily eats less protein, what does the placenta do to protect the baby?

options.A: The placenta actively pumps amino acids to the fetus, maintaining its supply.
options.B: Amino acids turn into glucose inside the placenta.
options.C: The fetus stops growing entirely until the mother eats more meat.
options.D: Fetal amino acid levels drop immediately to match the mother's level.

explanation: Clever placenta! Even if mum's intake dips, active transport lets the placenta push extra amino acids over to keep the baby well-nourished. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T008#GNS226_U2_T008_h3)

question: Once the fetus produces waste, which organs of the mother ultimately clear and get rid of it?

options.A: Kidneys and liver
options.B: Lungs and skin
options.C: Gastrointestinal tract
options.D: Lymphatic system

explanation: You're right! Once the waste crosses over into the mother's blood, her own kidneys and liver do the heavy lifting to filter it out. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T008#GNS226_U2_T008_h4)

question: Which of these is a major nitrogen waste product that the placenta clears away from the baby?

options.A: Albumin
options.B: Urea
options.C: Calcium
options.D: Glucose

explanation: Spot on! Urea is a normal byproduct of protein breakdown, and the placenta helps shuttle it away so the mother can excrete it. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T008#GNS226_U2_T008_h4)

question: What is the main job of Human Chorionic Gonadotropin (hCG) in early pregnancy?

options.A: To signal the corpus luteum to continue producing progesterone
options.B: To lower the mother's blood pressure during the first trimester
options.C: To prepare the fetal lungs for air breathing
options.D: To stimulate milk production in the maternal mammary glands

explanation: Wonderful! hCG is the famous pregnancy hormone that tells the ovary's corpus luteum to keep pumping out progesterone until the placenta is ready to take over. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T008#GNS226_U2_T008_h5)

question: Which hormone acts like a chill pill for the uterus, keeping its muscles calm and preventing early contractions?

options.A: Prolactin
options.B: Progesterone
options.C: Oxytocin
options.D: Estrogen

explanation: You got it! Progesterone relaxes smooth muscles, keeping the uterus nice and quiet throughout the pregnancy journey. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T008#GNS226_U2_T008_h5)

question: Which antibody is small enough to cross the placenta and give the baby temporary immunity?

options.A: IgE
options.B: IgM
options.C: IgA
options.D: IgG

explanation: Correct! IgG is the champion antibody that crosses the placental barrier to give the newborn a helpful head start against infections. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T008#GNS226_U2_T008_h6)

question: Why doesn't the mother's immune system treat the growing fetus like a foreign invader and attack it?

options.A: The mother's immune system turns off completely during pregnancy.
options.B: The placenta uses special mechanisms to suppress local maternal immune responses.
options.C: Fetal cells disguise themselves as maternal liver cells.
options.D: The fetus has no white blood cells to trigger an immune reaction.

explanation: Fascinating, right? The placenta acts like a peacekeeper, creating a special low-immune zone so the mother's body doesn't reject the baby. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T008#GNS226_U2_T008_h6)

question: What do we call poor baby growth that happens when the placenta fails to send enough food and oxygen?

options.A: Intrauterine growth restriction
options.B: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.C: Placental abruption syndrome
options.D: Fetal erythroblastosis

explanation: You nailed it! Intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR) simply means the baby isn't growing to its full expected weight because the placenta isn't quite coping. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T008#GNS226_U2_T008_h7)

question: A 34-week pregnant mum comes in with painless, bright red vaginal bleeding. What condition should you suspect first?

options.A: Placenta previa
options.B: Placenta accreta
options.C: Chorioamnionitis
options.D: Placental abruption

explanation: Spot on! Classic textbook sign: painless, bright red bleeding late in pregnancy is a major red flag for placenta previa, where the placenta sits low over the cervix. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T008#GNS226_U2_T008_h7)

question: What is the main goal of antenatal care for a pregnant mother?

options.A: To determine the exact sex of the baby early on
options.B: To guarantee a completely pain-free labor and delivery
options.C: To prevent the mother from gaining excess body fat
options.D: To safeguard the health of both mother and fetus

explanation: You got it! Antenatal care is all about keeping both mum and baby safe and healthy all through the pregnancy journey. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T009#GNS226_U2_T009_h1)

question: Why do we love early detection of health issues during antenatal visits?

options.A: It reduces the financial cost of hospital delivery to zero
options.B: It ensures the baby will be born exactly on the due date
options.C: It stops minor issues from developing into severe emergencies
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for any medications later

explanation: Spotting small changes early lets us step in quickly before things get dangerous. Great nursing intuition! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T009#GNS226_U2_T009_h1)

question: Which hormone is mostly responsible for relaxing smooth muscles during pregnancy?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Progesterone
options.D: Prolactin

explanation: Spot on! Progesterone relaxes smooth muscles everywhere in the body, which is why digestion slows down and blood vessels change. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T009#GNS226_U2_T009_h2)

question: A pregnant patient in her second trimester complains of heartburn and mild constipation. What's the most likely culprit?

options.A: Hormone-induced slowing of the gastrointestinal tract
options.B: An infection of the upper digestive lining
options.C: Consuming too much water with her meals
options.D: The physical weight of the placenta pressing on her stomach

explanation: You nailed it. High progesterone levels slow down bowel movements and relax the stomach valve, causing that familiar pregnancy heartburn and constipation. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T009#GNS226_U2_T009_h2)

question: After 36 weeks of pregnancy, how often should an expectant mum come for routine antenatal visits?

options.A: Every week
options.B: Every month
options.C: Only if she feels pain
options.D: Every two weeks

explanation: That's correct! Once she passes 36 weeks, visits change to weekly so we can closely keep an eye on both mum and baby as delivery approaches. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T009#GNS226_U2_T009_h3)

question: What is the main reason midwives and nurses measure fundal height during antenatal checks?

options.A: To estimate gestational age and monitor fetal growth
options.B: To calculate the total amount of amniotic fluid
options.C: To determine the exact birth weight of the baby
options.D: To check the strength of the uterine muscle walls

explanation: Correct! Fundal height in centimeters usually matches the weeks of pregnancy, helping us track if the baby is growing just right. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T009#GNS226_U2_T009_h3)

question: Why is taking folic acid supplements so important in the early stages of pregnancy?

options.A: To increase the mother's blood volume
options.B: To stop maternal morning sickness
options.C: To strengthen the baby's tooth enamel
options.D: To prevent neural tube defects

explanation: Spot on! Folic acid helps form the baby's neural tube early on, protecting the brain and spinal cord from serious issues. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T009#GNS226_U2_T009_h4)

question: Routine iron supplements are given during pregnancy mainly to prevent which condition?

options.A: Pregnancy-induced hypertension
options.B: Iron-deficiency anemia
options.C: Excessive amniotic fluid
options.D: Gestational diabetes mellitus

explanation: You got it! Since blood volume shoots up during pregnancy, extra iron helps make enough hemoglobin to stop anemia. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T009#GNS226_U2_T009_h4)

question: Which vaccine is routinely given during antenatal care to protect the newborn against tetanus?

options.A: BCG vaccine
options.B: Tetanus toxoid
options.C: Hepatitis A vaccine
options.D: Measles vaccine

explanation: Correct! Tetanus toxoid is given to expectant mums to keep the newborn safe from lockjaw (neonatal tetanus) after birth. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T009#GNS226_U2_T009_h5)

question: Which of these lifestyle habits should a nurse strongly advise a pregnant woman to cut out completely?

options.A: Drinking clean water throughout the day
options.B: Engaging in any form of physical exercise
options.C: Eating fresh fruits and green vegetables
options.D: Consuming alcohol and smoking tobacco

explanation: Spot on! Alcohol and tobacco carry nasty toxins that can severely harm the baby's growth and cause birth defects. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T009#GNS226_U2_T009_h5)

question: Which group of symptoms strongly points towards preeclampsia in a pregnant patient?

options.A: Low blood pressure, excessive sleepiness, and hunger
options.B: Frequent urination, mild thirst, and dry skin
options.C: High blood pressure, headache, and visual disturbances
options.D: Lower back pain and increased appetite

explanation: You nailed it! Preeclampsia is marked by high blood pressure paired with stubborn headaches and blurry vision. Always watch out for this! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T009#GNS226_U2_T009_h6)

question: A pregnant patient at 32 weeks says she hasn't felt her baby kick all day. What should you do first as the nurse?

options.A: Advise her to wait until the next scheduled appointment next month
options.B: Arrange for an immediate assessment of fetal heart sounds and movement
options.C: Give her a strong laxative to stimulate digestive activity
options.D: Tell her this is completely normal and send her back home

explanation: Spot on! A quiet baby can mean distress. Always check fetal heartbeats and movements right away when a mum reports this. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T009#GNS226_U2_T009_h6)

question: What is the main goal of birth preparedness and complication readiness?

options.A: To ensure the mother pays all hospital bills in advance
options.B: To completely eliminate any need for hospital visits
options.C: To reduce delays in getting emergency care during childbirth
options.D: To guarantee that the baby is born on a specific weekday

explanation: Correct! Planning ahead with transport and funds stops dangerous delays when things get critical during labor. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T009#GNS226_U2_T009_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a core part of an effective birth preparedness plan?

options.A: Identifying a designated health facility with skilled staff
options.B: Arranging reliable emergency transportation in advance
options.C: Buying expensive decorative clothing for the newborn
options.D: Saving emergency funds for unexpected medical costs

explanation: You got it! Fancy baby clothes are nice, but true emergency readiness focuses on transport, money, and skilled hands to help deliver safely. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T009#GNS226_U2_T009_h7)

question: How would you simply describe a high-risk pregnancy?

options.A: Any gestation that lasts longer than thirty-six weeks
options.B: A pregnancy that automatically ends in a surgical delivery
options.C: Any pregnancy that occurs in a woman older than twenty years
options.D: A pregnancy where the health of the mother or baby is at increased risk

explanation: You've got this! A high-risk pregnancy just means there are extra health factors that need closer watch to keep both mum and baby safe. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T010#GNS226_U2_T010_h1)

question: Why is catching a high-risk pregnancy early so important for us as nurses?

options.A: It guarantees that the baby will be born without any congenital defects
options.B: It completely stops the mother from experiencing any physical discomfort
options.C: It allows the healthcare team to plan timely interventions and prevent complications
options.D: It removes the need for any laboratory tests during the third trimester

explanation: Spotting risks early gives you and the medical team time to step in and manage things smoothly before they become emergency situations. Great nursing instinct! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T010#GNS226_U2_T010_h1)

question: Which of these is a classic example of an obstetric risk factor?

options.A: Chronic kidney disease
options.B: A history of recurrent miscarriages
options.C: Smoking cigarettes daily
options.D: Young maternal age under seventeen

explanation: Obstetric factors are linked right to a woman's past pregnancies and birth history, like previous miscarriages or early deliveries. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T010#GNS226_U2_T010_h2)

question: A pregnant woman who smokes and drinks alcohol falls under which category of risk?

options.A: Genetic factors
options.B: Anatomical factors
options.C: Lifestyle factors
options.D: Obstetric factors

explanation: Behaviors like smoking and alcohol consumption are classified as lifestyle risk factors that can negatively impact fetal development. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T010#GNS226_U2_T010_h2)

question: What is the hallmark warning sign of placenta previa?

options.A: Painless, bright red vaginal bleeding
options.B: Sudden swelling of the face and hands
options.C: High fever and foul-smelling discharge
options.D: Severe sharp pain with a rigid abdomen

explanation: Think of placenta previa as the placenta lying low near the cervix. When it bleeds, it's typically painless and bright red—a classic sign to watch out for on the ward! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T010#GNS226_U2_T010_h3)

question: A pregnant woman at 32 weeks comes in with high blood pressure and sudden swelling in her face and hands. What should you suspect?

options.A: Early onset gestational diabetes
options.B: Normal physiological edema of pregnancy
options.C: Gestational hypertension or preeclampsia
options.D: Placental abruption with internal bleeding

explanation: New high blood pressure plus sudden swelling after 20 weeks is a major red flag for preeclampsia. Always keep a close eye on your patient's BP readings! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T010#GNS226_U2_T010_h3)

question: What does a Non-Stress Test (NST) actually check for?

options.A: Fetal heart rate changes in response to movement
options.B: The maturity of the fetal lungs before delivery
options.C: The exact amount of protein in maternal urine
options.D: Maternal blood pressure fluctuations over time

explanation: An NST looks at how the baby's heart rate reacts when they move around. A healthy baby's heart rate speeds up a bit with movement—simple and non-invasive! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T010#GNS226_U2_T010_h4)

question: Why might doctors order an amniocentesis late in a high-risk pregnancy?

options.A: To treat an active uterine infection
options.B: To measure the exact weight of the growing fetus
options.C: To check if the fetal lungs are mature enough for birth
options.D: To lower the mother's elevated blood pressure

explanation: If there's talk of delivering early, a late amniocentesis checks the fluid to see if the baby's lungs are strong and ready to breathe on their own. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T010#GNS226_U2_T010_h4)

question: Why do doctors often give corticosteroids to a mum facing early labor?

options.A: To accelerate fetal lung maturity and reduce breathing difficulties
options.B: To permanently stop all uterine contractions from happening
options.C: To prevent postpartum hemorrhage after delivery
options.D: To lower the mother's blood glucose levels rapidly

explanation: Steroids give a fantastic boost to the baby's developing lungs, helping them avoid serious breathing trouble if they decide to arrive early. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T010#GNS226_U2_T010_h5)

question: You are caring for a patient with severe preeclampsia. Which symptom needs your immediate attention?

options.A: An oral temperature of thirty-seven degrees Celsius
options.B: A sudden report of a severe headache and blurred vision
options.C: A slight increase in anxiety about the hospital stay
options.D: A mild increase in appetite during the afternoon shift

explanation: Headaches and blurry vision in preeclampsia mean the brain is under pressure and a seizure might be near. Quick action saves lives here! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T010#GNS226_U2_T010_h5)

question: Which of these is a critical warning sign that a pregnant woman must report straight away?

options.A: Occasional mild heartburn
options.B: Decreased fetal movement
options.C: Increased fatigue in the evening
options.D: Mild swelling in the ankles

explanation: Always teach mums to track their baby's kicks! Fewer movements can mean the baby is stressed and needs an immediate check-up. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T010#GNS226_U2_T010_h6)

question: Why is emotional and psychological support so important in high-risk pregnancy care?

options.A: Patients on bed rest have nothing else to do during the day
options.B: Mental health counseling replaces the need for medical check-ups
options.C: Chronic stress and anxiety can negatively affect both maternal and fetal well-being
options.D: It guarantees the mother will have a natural vaginal delivery

explanation: Mind and body are connected! High stress releases hormones that can impact the pregnancy, so a comforting word from you as a nurse goes a long way. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T010#GNS226_U2_T010_h6)

question: What is the main reason we roll a laboring patient onto her side during an emergency?

options.A: To prepare the patient's back for an epidural anesthetic injection
options.B: To relieve pressure on the vena cava and improve blood flow to the fetus
options.C: To completely stop the progression of active labor contractions
options.D: To make it easier to perform a sterile vaginal examination

explanation: Lying flat lets the heavy uterus press on major blood vessels. Turning her to the side opens up blood flow and sends vital oxygen straight to the baby! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T010#GNS226_U2_T010_h7)

question: A high-risk mum in labor suddenly has heavy bleeding and a hard, painful belly. What is your FIRST nursing action?

options.A: Administer an oral pain medication to soothe the uterine cramping
options.B: Stop any infusing oxytocin and turn the patient onto her side
options.C: Encourage the patient to push harder to speed up the delivery
options.D: Wait for the primary doctor to arrive before taking any action

explanation: These signs point to a placental abruption. Stopping contractions (oxytocin) and turning her to protect blood flow are your top life-saving priorities! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T010#GNS226_U2_T010_h7)

question: Around how many weeks of pregnancy do morning sickness and nausea usually start?

options.A: 1 to 3 weeks
options.B: 16 to 18 weeks
options.C: 10 to 12 weeks
options.D: 4 to 6 weeks

explanation: You will often see this early in the first trimester around weeks 4 to 6, right when hormones start shooting up. Great job keeping this in mind for antenatal care! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T011#GNS226_U2_T011_h1)

question: Why does high progesterone during pregnancy tend to cause digestive sluggishness?

options.A: It causes immediate dehydration of the gut lining
options.B: It relaxes gastrointestinal smooth muscle
options.C: It speeds up overall bowel motility
options.D: It increases stomach acid production directly

explanation: Progesterone is a smooth muscle relaxant! It slows down the whole digestive tract to give nutrients more time to absorb, which unfortunately brings on that heavy, nauseous feeling. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T011#GNS226_U2_T011_h1)

question: Which of these is a very common trigger that makes pregnancy nausea worse?

options.A: Drinking cold water
options.B: An empty stomach
options.C: Eating bland crackers
options.D: Sleeping on the left side

explanation: An empty stomach lets blood sugar drop, making nausea spike. That is why mums often feel worst first thing in the morning before eating! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T011#GNS226_U2_T011_h2)

question: A pregnant mum says cooking smells instantly make her want to throw up. What is happening in her body?

options.A: Immediate closure of the pyloric sphincter from heat
options.B: Direct stimulation of the vomiting center by sensory input
options.C: Rapid absorption of airborne food toxins into the bloodstream
options.D: Sudden drop in systemic blood pressure from food aromas

explanation: Strong smells hit sensory nerves that directly trigger the brain's vomiting center. Pregnant senses are super sharp! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T011#GNS226_U2_T011_h2)

question: Why do nurses test for urinary ketones in a pregnant patient with severe vomiting?

options.A: It indicates the body is breaking down fat due to poor intake
options.B: It shows if the kidneys are failing from a bacterial infection
options.C: It rules out gestational diabetes mellitus completely
options.D: It confirms the exact gestational age of the developing fetus

explanation: Ketones mean the body has run out of easy energy and has started burning fat instead because the mum can't keep food down. It's a key sign to watch out for! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T011#GNS226_U2_T011_h3)

question: Which physical sign tells you right away that a patient is getting dehydrated?

options.A: Flushed and warm skin
options.B: Moist, pink mucous membranes
options.C: Dry, cracked mucous membranes
options.D: Bounding peripheral pulses

explanation: Dry mouth and lips are classic, quick red flags that the body is low on water. Always check the mucous membranes during your assessments! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T011#GNS226_U2_T011_h3)

question: What is the main reason we advise pregnant women to eat small, frequent meals?

options.A: To eliminate the need for drinking water entirely
options.B: To prevent the stomach from becoming overly full and distended
options.C: To speed up the transit time of food through the large intestine
options.D: To increase total daily calorie consumption by fifty percent

explanation: Keeping portions small lightens the load on a slow digestive tract, keeping the vomiting reflex quiet. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T011#GNS226_U2_T011_h4)

question: A pregnant patient asks how to manage morning sickness before she even gets out of bed. What is the best tip?

options.A: Brush your teeth thoroughly with strong mint toothpaste first
options.B: Drink a large glass of cold milk immediately upon waking
options.C: Exercise vigorously for ten minutes to boost morning energy
options.D: Keep dry crackers by the bed and eat a few before standing up

explanation: Munching a dry cracker before sitting up lifts blood sugar just enough to calm the stomach before gravity and movement trigger nausea. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T011#GNS226_U2_T011_h4)

question: Which vitamin is most commonly recommended as a first-line supplement for pregnancy nausea?

options.A: Vitamin D
options.B: Vitamin A
options.C: Vitamin C
options.D: Vitamin B6

explanation: Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6) is a safe, go-to supplement prescribed in antenatal clinics to help ease that queasy feeling. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T011#GNS226_U2_T011_h5)

question: What is an important nursing duty when a pregnant patient is given an antiemetic drug?

options.A: Encourage the patient to stop taking all oral fluids
options.B: Advise the patient to double the dose if nausea returns
options.C: Check fetal heart tones every fifteen minutes around the clock
options.D: Monitor the patient for common side effects like drowsiness

explanation: Many antiemetics make patients sleepy. Keeping an eye on safety and advising them about drowsiness is a key nursing role. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T011#GNS226_U2_T011_h5)

question: Which sign separates severe hyperemesis gravidarum from normal morning sickness?

options.A: Weight loss exceeding five percent of body weight
options.B: Mild fatigue during the afternoon hours
options.C: Queasiness that improves by the second trimester
options.D: Occasional dislike for the smell of coffee

explanation: Losing more than 5% of pre-pregnancy body weight tells us it's no longer regular morning sickness—it's hyperemesis and needs medical help! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T011#GNS226_U2_T011_h6)

question: What is the biggest risk of untreated hyperemesis gravidarum for the mother?

options.A: Severe electrolyte imbalance and dehydration
options.B: Chronic high blood pressure disorders
options.C: Sudden development of adult-onset asthma
options.D: Permanent loss of taste and smell

explanation: When nothing stays down, the body quickly loses vital fluids and salts (electrolytes), leading to dangerous dehydration that requires IV fluids. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T011#GNS226_U2_T011_h6)

question: How can a nurse best reassure a patient who has mild pregnancy nausea?

options.A: You must take prescription drugs immediately to protect the fetus.
options.B: Mild nausea and vomiting typically do not harm the developing baby.
options.C: Eating large meals will cure the queasiness within hours.
options.D: The symptoms will disappear completely by the second week.

explanation: Mums worry the baby isn't eating enough. Letting them know that mild early nausea won't hurt their little one brings great peace of mind! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T011#GNS226_U2_T011_h7)

question: What pregnancy hormone is most closely linked to the timing of first-trimester nausea and vomiting?

options.A: Human chorionic gonadotropin
options.B: Follicle stimulating hormone
options.C: Thyroid stimulating hormone
options.D: Luteinizing hormone

explanation: Human chorionic gonadotropin peaks during the first trimester right when nausea and vomiting are usually at their worst. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T012#GNS226_U2_T012_h1)

question: How does elevated progesterone contribute to digestive discomfort during early pregnancy?

options.A: By relaxing smooth muscle and slowing down digestion
options.B: By increasing the production of strong stomach acids
options.C: By causing the liver to produce excess bile salts
options.D: By speeding up the movement of food through the bowels

explanation: Progesterone relaxes smooth muscles all over the body, including the digestive tract, which slows stomach emptying and leads to reflux. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T012#GNS226_U2_T012_h1)

question: What percentage of pre-pregnancy weight loss is typically used to help define hyperemesis gravidarum?

options.A: Exactly 10%
options.B: Greater than 5%
options.C: Less than 1%
options.D: Around 20%

explanation: Losing more than 5 percent of pre-pregnancy body weight due to continuous vomiting points strongly toward hyperemesis gravidarum. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T012#GNS226_U2_T012_h2)

question: A pregnant patient comes to the clinic vomiting ten times a day, unable to keep water down, and showing ketones in her urine. What condition is she most likely experiencing?

options.A: Hyperemesis gravidarum
options.B: Gestational hypertension
options.C: Normal morning sickness
options.D: Eclamptic seizure

explanation: Uncontrolled vomiting with dehydration, inability to retain fluids, and urinary ketones goes far beyond normal morning sickness into hyperemesis gravidarum. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T012#GNS226_U2_T012_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of checking urine ketones in a patient with severe pregnancy vomiting?

options.A: To detect starvation and fat breakdown from lack of food
options.B: To measure the exact amount of daily protein intake
options.C: To confirm the presence of a urinary tract infection
options.D: To check if the kidneys are filtering excess red blood cells

explanation: When the body cannot keep food down, it burns fat for energy, which leaves ketone byproducts in the urine. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T012#GNS226_U2_T012_h3)

question: Why is an obstetric ultrasound often performed when evaluating a patient with severe hyperemesis gravidarum?

options.A: To check for multiple gestation or molar pregnancy
options.B: To see if the liver is enlarged from fluid backup
options.C: To measure the exact thickness of the stomach lining
options.D: To test the baby's hearing and nervous system

explanation: Conditions like twins or a molar pregnancy cause much higher levels of hormones, which can trigger worse vomiting. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T012#GNS226_U2_T012_h3)

question: What is a recommended eating pattern to help reduce nausea during early pregnancy?

options.A: Eating small, frequent meals throughout the day
options.B: Eating three large meals loaded with healthy fats
options.C: Fasting until the afternoon to let the stomach rest
options.D: Drinking a large glass of water right before every meal

explanation: Keeping a little food in the stomach prevents the empty-stomach feeling that often worsens nausea. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T012#GNS226_U2_T012_h4)

question: Why are pregnant women advised to drink fluids between meals rather than during meals?

options.A: To keep stomach acid completely inactive during digestion
options.B: To prevent over-stretching the stomach which can trigger vomiting
options.C: To ensure the body absorbs all the vitamins from the solid food
options.D: To stop the kidneys from working too hard after eating

explanation: Filling the stomach with both food and large amounts of liquid at the same time increases pressure and promotes vomiting. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T012#GNS226_U2_T012_h4)

question: What is the common first-line vitamin supplement used alongside an antihistamine to treat pregnancy nausea?

options.A: Vitamin D3
options.B: Vitamin C
options.C: Vitamin B6
options.D: Vitamin B12

explanation: Pyridoxine, or Vitamin B6, is widely recommended as a safe and effective starting medication for pregnancy nausea. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T012#GNS226_U2_T012_h5)

question: A patient admitted for severe hyperemesis is about to receive IV glucose fluids. Why must she receive thiamine (Vitamin B1) first?

options.A: To help the liver process the incoming sugar more quickly
options.B: To prevent Wernicke's encephalopathy from vitamin deficiency
options.C: To prevent allergic reactions to the plastic IV tubing
options.D: To stop the patient from feeling sleepy during the infusion

explanation: Great catch! Giving sugar to a malnourished patient without thiamine can trigger a serious brain complication called Wernicke's encephalopathy. Always protect the brain first! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T012#GNS226_U2_T012_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common physical complication of severe, prolonged vomiting in pregnancy?

options.A: Electrolyte and acid-base imbalance
options.B: Esophageal tears from forceful retching
options.C: Acute kidney injury from dehydration
options.D: Gestational diabetes mellitus

explanation: Gestational diabetes is related to insulin resistance and glucose metabolism, not directly caused by vomiting. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T012#GNS226_U2_T012_h6)

question: How can severe, untreated hyperemesis gravidarum impact the developing fetus?

options.A: It stops the umbilical cord from growing longer
options.B: It can lead to low birth weight or preterm delivery
options.C: It causes permanent skeletal bone deformities
options.D: It accelerates brain development too rapidly

explanation: When the mother cannot keep food down and loses significant weight, the baby may not get enough nutrients, raising the risk of low birth weight. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T012#GNS226_U2_T012_h6)

question: What symptom should a pregnant woman be taught is a red flag requiring immediate contact with her clinic?

options.A: Inability to keep any fluids down for twenty-four hours
options.B: A slight increase in appetite during the second trimester
options.C: Occasional mild bloating after eating plain toast
options.D: Mild tiredness during the middle of the afternoon

explanation: Not being able to retain any fluids for a full day puts the mother at high risk for dangerous dehydration. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T012#GNS226_U2_T012_h7)

question: Why is regular follow-up care essential for a patient recovering from hyperemesis gravidarum?

options.A: To monitor her weight, hydration, and lab values for stability
options.B: To measure the exact length of the baby using a tape measure
options.C: To make sure she is exercising at the gym twice a week
options.D: To change her prescribed prenatal vitamins every single week

explanation: Frequent checks allow healthcare providers to catch returning dehydration or weight loss early before hospitalization becomes necessary. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T012#GNS226_U2_T012_h7)

question: What is the clinical term for heartburn?

options.A: Pyrosis
options.B: Peristalsis
options.C: Preeclampsia
options.D: Pruritus

explanation: Pyrosis is simply the medical word for that burning feeling in your chest caused by stomach acid splashing up. You've got this! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T013#GNS226_U2_T013_h1)

question: During which stage of pregnancy does heartburn usually act up the most?

options.A: Immediate postpartum
options.B: Third trimester
options.C: Implantation phase
options.D: First trimester

explanation: As the baby grows big and cozy in the third trimester, it pushes right up against the stomach, making acid reflux much more common. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T013#GNS226_U2_T013_h1)

question: Which pregnancy hormone is mainly responsible for relaxing the valve between the stomach and food pipe?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Progesterone
options.C: Prolactin
options.D: Estrogen

explanation: Progesterone relaxes smooth muscles all over the body to make room for baby, which also loosens the sphincter keeping stomach acid down. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T013#GNS226_U2_T013_h2)

question: How does a growing uterus directly cause acid reflux in expectant mothers?

options.A: By pushing the stomach upward and increasing pressure
options.B: By causing the liver to produce more digestive enzymes
options.C: By tightening the muscular walls of the esophagus
options.D: By increasing the total volume of stomach acid produced

explanation: Think of space issues! The growing womb crowds the belly and literally squeezes the stomach upward, pushing contents toward the throat. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T013#GNS226_U2_T013_h2)

question: What common mouth symptom often tags along with pregnancy heartburn?

options.A: A metallic taste from iron deficiency
options.B: Excessive production of sweet saliva
options.C: Numbness of the tongue and gums
options.D: A sour or bitter taste in the mouth

explanation: When acid travels up the esophagus, it reaches the mouth and leaves behind a very unpleasant sour or bitter taste. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T013#GNS226_U2_T013_h3)

question: Which sleeping or resting position is most likely to make heartburn worse for an expectant mother?

options.A: Standing while cooking food
options.B: Lying flat on her back
options.C: Sitting upright in a chair
options.D: Walking slowly after a meal

explanation: Lying flat takes away gravity's help, making it super easy for stomach acid to flow right back up. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T013#GNS226_U2_T013_h3)

question: A pregnant patient reports severe chest pain spreading down her left arm. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Report it immediately for cardiac evaluation
options.B: Suggest she take a strong antacid tablet right away
options.C: Reassure her that this is normal third-trimester heartburn
options.D: Advise her to lie down and drink cold milk

explanation: Chest pain spreading to the arm is a red flag for the heart! Never brush it off as simple heartburn. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T013#GNS226_U2_T013_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a normal sign of simple pregnancy heartburn?

options.A: Worsening discomfort after eating a large meal
options.B: A sour taste at the back of the throat
options.C: A burning feeling behind the breastbone
options.D: Crushing chest pain radiating to the jaw

explanation: Crushing jaw pain points toward heart trouble, not regular acid reflux. Good clinical spotting! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T013#GNS226_U2_T013_h4)

question: A pregnant woman complains of terrible night heartburn. What easy adjustment can the nurse suggest for bedtime?

options.A: Elevate the head of the bed by several inches
options.B: Sleep lying flat on her right side with no pillows
options.C: Sleep flat on her stomach with a pillow under her hips
options.D: Use extra heavy blankets to keep the abdomen warm

explanation: Propping up the head of the bed uses gravity to keep stomach acid where it belongs while she sleeps. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T013#GNS226_U2_T013_h5)

question: Why do we advise pregnant mothers to eat small, frequent meals instead of three massive plates of food?

options.A: To prevent sudden drops in blood sugar during the afternoon
options.B: To speed up the absorption of prenatal vitamins into the bloodstream
options.C: To prevent the stomach from becoming overly full and putting pressure on the sphincter
options.D: To stop the liver from producing excess bile during digestion

explanation: Smaller meals keep tummy pressure low, stopping acid from splashing up into the food pipe. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T013#GNS226_U2_T013_h5)

question: When lifestyle changes don't quite cut it, what type of medication is usually recommended first for pregnancy heartburn?

options.A: Heavy narcotic pain relievers
options.B: Prescription laxatives
options.C: Strong proton pump inhibitors
options.D: Antacids containing calcium or magnesium

explanation: Calcium and magnesium antacids work fast to neutralize acid and have a safe track record during pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T013#GNS226_U2_T013_h6)

question: Why should pregnant women steer clear of sodium bicarbonate for everyday heartburn?

options.A: It causes immediate and permanent closure of the esophagus
options.B: It triggers severe allergic reactions in the fetus
options.C: It completely stops the liver from filtering blood
options.D: It can cause fluid retention and electrolyte imbalances

explanation: Sodium bicarbonate has lots of salt, which can cause dangerous swelling and fluid buildup during pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T013#GNS226_U2_T013_h6)

question: What can happen if severe, constant pregnancy heartburn is left completely untreated?

options.A: Inflammation and damage to the lining of the esophagus
options.B: Permanent hardening of the muscular stomach walls
options.C: Complete blockage of the upper respiratory airway
options.D: Sudden loss of all maternal digestive enzymes

explanation: Constant acid wash irritates and damages the delicate lining of the food pipe over time, leading to inflammation. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T013#GNS226_U2_T013_h7)

question: A pregnant patient says she wants to take a random herbal remedy she saw online for her heartburn. What is the nurse's best reply?

options.A: Advise her to check with her healthcare provider first to ensure safety
options.B: Suggest she stop eating completely until the baby is born
options.C: Encourage her to take a double dose to get fast relief
options.D: Tell her that all natural herbs are completely safe in pregnancy

explanation: Always guide patients to chat with their doctor or midwife before trying unverified remedies during pregnancy. Safety first! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T013#GNS226_U2_T013_h7)

question: What is the most common reason for mild lower abdominal cramping during a normal pregnancy?

options.A: Normal stretching of uterine ligaments
options.B: Severe maternal urinary retention
options.C: Early separation of the placenta
options.D: Complete closure of the cervix

explanation: As the uterus grows, the supporting ligaments stretch and pull, which naturally causes mild discomfort in the lower abdomen. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T014#GNS226_U2_T014_h1)

question: Why should a nurse take every report of cramping in pregnancy seriously?

options.A: Milder aches can sometimes mask or precede serious complications.
options.B: All pregnant women require immediate bed rest for any pain.
options.C: Pain medications are mandatory for any reported discomfort.
options.D: Cramping always indicates an active uterine infection.

explanation: Even though most cramps are completely normal, checking them out helps us make sure we don't miss important warning signs like an ectopic pregnancy or preterm labor. Great nursing instincts! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T014#GNS226_U2_T014_h1)

question: What causes sharp, stabbing round ligament pain on the sides of the abdomen during pregnancy?

options.A: Infection of the urinary bladder lining
options.B: Stretching of the ligaments supporting the growing uterus
options.C: Rapid drop in maternal blood pressure
options.D: Spasms of the intestinal smooth muscle

explanation: Round ligament pain happens when these supporting structures stretch rapidly to accommodate the enlarging uterus. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T014#GNS226_U2_T014_h2)

question: Why do pregnant women often get painful muscle cramps in their legs at night?

options.A: The heavy uterus slows down blood return from the lower limbs.
options.B: Walking too much causes permanent nerve damage in the feet.
options.C: The thyroid gland stops functioning normally during sleep.
options.D: Excess calcium builds up rapidly in the calf muscles.

explanation: The growing uterus puts a bit of pressure on blood vessels in the pelvis, which can slow down circulation and lead to those annoying calf cramps. Staying hydrated helps! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T014#GNS226_U2_T014_h2)

question: Which symptom along with tummy cramps in early pregnancy is a major red flag?

options.A: Mild morning nausea
options.B: Occasional breast tenderness
options.C: Vaginal bleeding
options.D: Increased skin pigmentation

explanation: Bleeding combined with cramps always needs quick medical attention because it can point to a potential miscarriage or ectopic pregnancy. You are learning to spot the crucial signs! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T014#GNS226_U2_T014_h3)

question: A patient at 28 weeks reports sharp, regular tummy pains and a watery vaginal discharge. What should you suspect?

options.A: Typical pregnancy-related constipation
options.B: Normal round ligament stretching
options.C: Preterm labor or rupture of membranes
options.D: Benign nighttime leg cramps

explanation: Regular pain and fluid leakage before full term are signs of preterm labor or water breaking, which needs immediate evaluation. Excellent clinical judgment! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T014#GNS226_U2_T014_h3)

question: Which resting position is best for improving circulation and comfort during pregnancy?

options.A: Sitting upright all night
options.B: Stomach prone position
options.C: Flat on the back
options.D: Left lateral position

explanation: Lying on the left side takes the heavy uterus off major blood vessels, boosting blood flow to the baby and helping mum feel much more comfortable. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T014#GNS226_U2_T014_h4)

question: How do maternity support belts help reduce pregnancy-related discomfort?

options.A: They stop all uterine contractions from happening entirely.
options.B: They increase the amount of amniotic fluid inside the womb.
options.C: They cure underlying urinary tract infections automatically.
options.D: They lift the heavy abdomen to take strain off ligaments and back muscles.

explanation: Support belts distribute the weight of the growing belly more evenly, relieving the pull on the lower back and pelvis. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T014#GNS226_U2_T014_h4)

question: What is a very common and easily fixed cause of muscle spasms during pregnancy?

options.A: High protein intake
options.B: Excess water
options.C: Low fiber intake
options.D: Dehydration

explanation: Not drinking enough water can easily trigger muscle cramps and even make the uterus irritable. Always remind your mums to carry a water bottle! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T014#GNS226_U2_T014_h5)

question: Why are minerals like magnesium and calcium emphasized in the diet of a pregnant woman experiencing muscle cramps?

options.A: They speed up the growth of fetal bones.
options.B: They prevent the placenta from detaching early.
options.C: They completely eliminate all pregnancy nausea.
options.D: They help muscles relax and contract smoothly.

explanation: Electrolytes like calcium and magnesium are essential for normal muscle function and preventing painful spasms. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T014#GNS226_U2_T014_h5)

question: What is the main goal of teaching pregnant women about cramps during antenatal visits?

options.A: Eliminating the need for any further doctor checkups
options.B: Instructing the mother to avoid all physical movement
options.C: Helping the patient tell normal discomforts from warning signs
options.D: Teaching the patient how to perform an ultrasound scan

explanation: Good health education helps mothers feel confident, knowing what is normal while staying alert to red flags. You're thinking like a great community nurse! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T014#GNS226_U2_T014_h6)

question: How should you best care for a pregnant woman who has mild round ligament cramps?

options.A: Prescribing strong pain medications without consulting a doctor
options.B: Telling her to ignore all pain because it is completely imaginary
options.C: Admitting her immediately to the labor ward for IV fluids
options.D: Reassuring her about normal changes and suggesting gentle stretching

explanation: Warm reassurance and simple comfort measures are all that's needed for normal pregnancy aches. Keep up the brilliant work! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T014#GNS226_U2_T014_h6)

question: How many bowel movements per week is typically used to help define constipation in pregnancy?

options.A: More than five bowel movements per week
options.B: One bowel movement every single day
options.C: A bowel movement only after every meal
options.D: Fewer than three bowel movements per week

explanation: You've got this! Constipation is generally marked by going less than three times a week. Knowing this helps you spot early signs in your antenatal patients. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T015#GNS226_U2_T015_h1)

question: When do pregnant women most commonly start experiencing symptoms of constipation?

options.A: Early in the first trimester
options.B: Only during active labor
options.C: Right after delivery occurs
options.D: Exclusively in the final week

explanation: Great job! Hormonal shifts happen right from the start of pregnancy, which is why tummy troubles often pop up early in the first trimester. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T015#GNS226_U2_T015_h1)

question: Which hormone is mainly responsible for relaxing smooth muscles and slowing down digestion in pregnancy?

options.A: Estrogen
options.B: Oxytocin
options.C: Prolactin
options.D: Progesterone

explanation: Spot on! Progesterone is the relaxing hormone that keeps the womb safe, but it also relaxes the bowel muscles, making digestion slower. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T015#GNS226_U2_T015_h2)

question: How does the growing baby and uterus contribute to constipation later in pregnancy?

options.A: By increasing the production of digestive enzymes
options.B: By putting direct mechanical pressure on the bowels
options.C: By completely stopping the production of stomach acid
options.D: By speeding up the movement of food through the colon

explanation: Exactly! As the baby grows, there is less space in the tummy, and the heavy uterus presses right against the intestines, slowing things down. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T015#GNS226_U2_T015_h2)

question: Which common antenatal supplement is well-known for causing hard stools and constipation?

options.A: Iron
options.B: Folic acid
options.C: Vitamin C
options.D: Calcium

explanation: You nailed it! Iron tablets are great for preventing anaemia, but they frequently make stools hard. Always prepare your mums for this side effect! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T015#GNS226_U2_T015_h3)

question: A pregnant mum taking daily iron pills complains of severe constipation. What is the main reason behind this?

options.A: Iron vitamins cause the stomach to shrink in size
options.B: Iron instantly stops the production of all digestive juices
options.C: Excess iron unabsorbed in the gut binds and hardens the stool
options.D: Iron forces the body to expel water through the skin instead

explanation: Well thought out! The iron that the body doesn't absorb interacts inside the gut, turning the waste firmer and harder to pass. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T015#GNS226_U2_T015_h3)

question: What should a nurse focus on when assessing a pregnant patient for constipation?

options.A: The blood pressure reading taken in the right arm
options.B: Exclusively the heartbeat of the developing fetus
options.C: Stool consistency, straining effort, and dietary habits
options.D: Only the exact weight of the patient on the scale

explanation: Spot on! To truly help, we need to ask about how hard the stool is, if she struggles to push, and what she's been eating and drinking. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T015#GNS226_U2_T015_h4)

question: Which symptom do pregnant women often report along with constipation?

options.A: Sudden loss of all body hair
options.B: Constant swelling of the eyelids
options.C: Abdominal bloating and cramping
options.D: Inability to hear high-pitched sounds

explanation: Correct! When gas and waste move slowly through the large bowel, it naturally leads to uncomfortable bloating and mild cramps. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T015#GNS226_U2_T015_h4)

question: What is a frequent, painful problem caused by excessive pushing during bowel movements in pregnancy?

options.A: Gestational diabetes
options.B: Placental abruption
options.C: Preeclampsia
options.D: Hemorrhoids

explanation: You got it! Straining puts heavy pressure on the pelvic veins, which often leads to swollen, painful hemorrhoids (piles). [learn more](GNS226_U2_T015#GNS226_U2_T015_h5)

question: Why can severe, untreated constipation sometimes lead to a fecal impaction?

options.A: The liver stops producing bile needed for digestion
options.B: The stomach acid dissolves the bowel wall entirely
options.C: Stool remains in the colon too long, becoming a dry, hard mass that cannot pass
options.D: Excess water floods the intestines and washes away all waste

explanation: Brilliant! As the colon absorbs water from the sitting waste, the stool packs down so solidly that normal movement can't push it out. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T015#GNS226_U2_T015_h5)

question: What is considered the best first step for managing constipation in pregnant women?

options.A: Strong prescription enemas
options.B: Complete bed rest
options.C: Immediate surgical intervention
options.D: Lifestyle and dietary modifications

explanation: Exactly right! Always start with safe, natural changes like drinking more water, eating fiber, and walking before reaching for medications. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T015#GNS226_U2_T015_h6)

question: A pregnant mum is told to eat more fiber for constipation. What else must she do for that fiber to work properly?

options.A: Stop taking all iron and vitamin pills immediately
options.B: Eliminate all physical exercise from her routine
options.C: Drink plenty of water throughout the day
options.D: Lie flat on her back for two hours after meals

explanation: You're doing great! Fiber needs water to bulk up and soften the stool. Without enough fluids, extra fiber can actually make constipation worse! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T015#GNS226_U2_T015_h6)

question: Which type of laxative is generally safe in pregnancy because it draws water into the stool to soften it?

options.A: Strong chemical purgatives
options.B: Raw castor oil blends
options.C: Stool softeners and bulk-forming laxatives
options.D: High-dose mineral oil enemas

explanation: Spot on! Gentle agents like docusate or psyllium work naturally without irritating the womb, making them safe choices for expectant mums. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T015#GNS226_U2_T015_h7)

question: Why should pregnant women AVOID taking stimulant laxatives unless prescribed by a doctor?

options.A: They stop the kidneys from making urine
options.B: They instantly cause permanent blindness
options.C: They turn breast milk completely green
options.D: They can stimulate the uterus and potentially trigger contractions

explanation: Correct! Stimulant laxatives irritate the bowel walls so strongly that they can sometimes trigger unwanted uterine contractions. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T015#GNS226_U2_T015_h7)

question: What good daily habit should nurses encourage patients to practice regarding bowel movements?

options.A: Waiting until the weekend to try passing stool
options.B: Responding promptly to the natural urge to defecate
options.C: Holding bowel movements until bedtime
options.D: Straining forcefully every morning regardless of urge

explanation: You've got this! Ignoring the call of nature lets the colon suck out more water, making the stool much harder to pass later. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T015#GNS226_U2_T015_h8)

question: When is the best time for a nurse to educate an expectant mum about potential prenatal vitamin side effects?

options.A: At the child's one-year checkup
options.B: Only after a fecal impaction occurs
options.C: Early in the prenatal care schedule
options.D: During the postpartum hospital discharge

explanation: Brilliant! Teaching mums early means they can adjust their diet and water intake before vitamin side effects become a painful problem. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T015#GNS226_U2_T015_h8)

question: What percentage of weight loss from pre-pregnancy weight helps nurses identify hyperemesis gravidarum?

options.A: Loss of exactly 2 percent of body weight
options.B: Loss of more than 5 percent of body weight
options.C: Loss of up to 1 percent of body weight
options.D: Loss of 1 to 3 percent of body weight

explanation: Dropping more than 5% of her original body weight is a key sign that a mom-to-be has moved past normal morning sickness into severe hyperemesis. You've got this! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T016#GNS226_U2_T016_h1)

question: How does hyperemesis gravidarum differ from normal pregnancy morning sickness?

options.A: It only occurs during the final trimester of pregnancy
options.B: It causes severe, unstoppable vomiting leading to dehydration and weight loss
options.C: It has no effect on the overall fluid balance of the body
options.D: It usually resolves completely within the first four weeks

explanation: While normal morning sickness is manageable, hyperemesis involves nonstop vomiting that drains the body's fluids and nutrition. Great job keeping the clinical differences clear! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T016#GNS226_U2_T016_h1)

question: Which hormone is most strongly linked to the severe nausea of early pregnancy?

options.A: Prolactin
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Oxytocin
options.D: Human chorionic gonadotropin

explanation: Rapidly rising levels of human chorionic gonadotropin peak in the first trimester and strongly correlate with intense nausea and vomiting. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T016#GNS226_U2_T016_h2)

question: Which pregnant patient has the highest risk of developing hyperemesis gravidarum?

options.A: A woman in her third trimester experiencing mild heartburn
options.B: A primigravida with low levels of estrogen and progesterone
options.C: A woman carrying twins with a family history of the condition
options.D: An older adult woman with low blood pressure

explanation: Carrying multiples pushes hormone levels sky-high, and family genes play a big role too. Spotting these risk factors makes you a fab nurse! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T016#GNS226_U2_T016_h2)

question: What finding in a pregnant patient's urine points to prolonged vomiting and starvation?

options.A: Ketones
options.B: Red blood cells
options.C: Glucose
options.D: Bilirubin

explanation: When the body can't keep food down, it starts burning its own fat for fuel. This breakdown leaves behind ketones in the urine—a classic sign of prolonged vomiting! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T016#GNS226_U2_T016_h3)

question: A pregnant patient with hyperemesis has low potassium and high blood pH. What is happening?

options.A: Respiratory acidosis
options.B: Metabolic acidosis
options.C: Respiratory alkalosis
options.D: Metabolic alkalosis

explanation: Pumping out stomach acid through continuous vomiting strips the body of hydrogen ions, causing blood pH to rise. That's metabolic alkalosis in action—keep smashing those lab values! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T016#GNS226_U2_T016_h3)

question: Why is a severe lack of vitamin B1 (thiamine) a major worry in hyperemesis?

options.A: It directly causes sudden gestational diabetes in the second trimester
options.B: It triggers immediate placental abruption and severe bleeding
options.C: It can lead to serious neurological issues like Wernicke's encephalopathy
options.D: It stops the production of amniotic fluid completely

explanation: Starvation and vomiting deplete vitamin B1, which can trigger confusion and nerve issues known as Wernicke's encephalopathy. Knowing this helps you protect your patients early! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T016#GNS226_U2_T016_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a common fetal complication linked to untreated hyperemesis?

options.A: Intestinal growth restriction
options.B: Low birth weight
options.C: Congenital heart murmurs
options.D: Preterm birth

explanation: Heart defects happen during early structural development, whereas hyperemesis baby issues are usually about poor nutrition and low birth weight. You're mastering neonatal risks! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T016#GNS226_U2_T016_h4)

question: What is the best daily nursing action to track fluid loss in a hyperemesis patient?

options.A: Checking the patient's blood pressure twice a shift
options.B: Measuring abdominal girth every morning
options.C: Asking the patient how many times she vomited
options.D: Weighing the patient at the same time each day

explanation: Daily weights don't lie! They give you an exact mathematical picture of how much fluid and tissue mass the patient is losing. Simple and super effective. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T016#GNS226_U2_T016_h5)

question: Why might doctors order a thyroid test for a patient with severe hyperemesis?

options.A: It helps check the exact gestational age of the fetus
options.B: Thyroid failure is the primary cause of all pregnancy vomiting
options.C: High levels of hCG can temporarily stimulate the thyroid gland
options.D: Thyroid medication is always used to cure morning sickness

explanation: Because hCG hormone looks a bit like thyroid-stimulating hormone, sky-high pregnancy hormones can trick the thyroid into working overtime. Brilliant clinical insight! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T016#GNS226_U2_T016_h5)

question: What is the primary medical goal when admitting a patient with hyperemesis gravidarum?

options.A: Feeding the patient a heavy high-protein meal right away
options.B: Starting immediate surgical options to empty the uterus
options.C: Discharging the patient with herbal teas and rest
options.D: Correcting fluid and electrolyte imbalances with IV fluids

explanation: Before anything else, we must rehydrate and restore lost electrolytes to keep vital organs safe. You're thinking like a real ward nurse! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T016#GNS226_U2_T016_h6)

question: Why is vitamin B1 added to an admitted pregnant patient's intravenous fluid bag?

options.A: To prevent severe brain disorders like Wernicke's encephalopathy
options.B: To increase the baby's birth weight within twenty-four hours
options.C: To lower the patient's blood pressure back to normal
options.D: To instantly stop the uterus from having early contractions

explanation: Thiamine protects the brain from the nasty effects of prolonged vomiting and malnutrition. Ward protocols made easy! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T016#GNS226_U2_T016_h6)

question: Why is mouth care an essential part of the nursing care plan for hyperemesis?

options.A: Good mouth care cures the underlying hormonal imbalances
options.B: Stomach acid from vomiting damages teeth and leaves a bad taste
options.C: Brushing teeth stops the stomach from contracting
options.D: It prevents the patient from swallowing her own saliva

explanation: Vomiting coats the mouth in harsh stomach acids that eat away at tooth enamel. Regular mouth care keeps her teeth safe and her breath fresh. Spot on! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T016#GNS226_U2_T016_h7)

question: Which nursing action helps reduce nausea triggers in a hospital room?

options.A: Opening the window wide during meal service times
options.B: Playing loud music to distract the patient from her symptoms
options.C: Keeping the room free from strong food odors and bright lights
options.D: Encouraging the patient to eat three large meals daily

explanation: Strong smells and glaring lights can easily set off a vomiting wave in a sensitive pregnant mom. A calm, scent-free room works wonders! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T016#GNS226_U2_T016_h7)

question: Why should a recovering hyperemesis patient avoid drinking lots of fluid during meals?

options.A: It permanently ruins the function of the kidneys
options.B: It stretches the stomach quickly and can trigger vomiting
options.C: It washes away all the digestive enzymes in the mouth
options.D: It causes severe cramping in the lower extremities

explanation: Chugging water alongside food overfills the stomach too fast, which is an express ticket right back to vomiting. Small sips separate from meals are best! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T016#GNS226_U2_T016_h8)

question: What tip should a nurse give a pregnant woman to help prevent severe morning nausea?

options.A: Drink a large glass of orange juice immediately upon waking up
options.B: Skip breakfast entirely until the afternoon hours arrive
options.C: Keep plain crackers near the bed and eat a small amount before getting up
options.D: Exercise vigorously for twenty minutes before eating breakfast

explanation: Nibbling a dry cracker before getting out of bed lifts morning blood sugar and settles an empty stomach. Classic nursing advice that really helps patients! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T016#GNS226_U2_T016_h8)

question: What is the gestational age threshold that defines antepartum haemorrhage?

options.A: From 32 weeks until delivery
options.B: From 24 weeks until delivery
options.C: From 28 weeks until delivery
options.D: From 20 weeks until delivery

explanation: Bleeding from the genital tract from 24 weeks of pregnancy until the baby is born is officially classified as antepartum haemorrhage. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T017#GNS226_U2_T017_h1)

question: Why is bleeding after 24 weeks of pregnancy (antepartum haemorrhage) considered a major medical emergency?

options.A: It prevents the placenta from functioning entirely
options.B: It always indicates immediate preterm labor is starting
options.C: It causes painless uterine contractions that tear tissues
options.D: It rapidly leads to severe fetal and maternal danger

explanation: Sudden blood loss during the second half of pregnancy can quickly cause life-threatening shock for the mother and oxygen deprivation for the baby. Taking it step by step makes it easy! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T017#GNS226_U2_T017_h1)

question: What are the two most common major causes of antepartum haemorrhage?

options.A: Ectopic pregnancy and bloody show
options.B: Placenta praevia and abruptio placentae
options.C: Uterine rupture and cervical polyps
options.D: Vasa praevia and gestational diabetes

explanation: Placenta praevia and abruptio placentae are responsible for the vast majority of heavy bleeding episodes in the late stages of pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T017#GNS226_U2_T017_h2)

question: What happens in the condition known as vasa praevia?

options.A: When the placenta implants directly over the lower uterine segment
options.B: When fetal blood vessels run across or near the internal cervical os
options.C: When the placenta peels away from the uterine wall prematurely
options.D: When severe inflammation of the cervix causes heavy spotting

explanation: Vasa praevia occurs when unprotected fetal blood vessels cross the cervical opening ahead of the baby, putting the fetus at extreme risk if they rupture. You are learning fast! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T017#GNS226_U2_T017_h2)

question: Which clinical feature is most characteristic of placenta praevia?

options.A: Painless bright red vaginal bleeding
options.B: Rigid, board-like abdomen with no bleeding
options.C: Painful dark red vaginal bleeding
options.D: Continuous clear fluid leakage with cramps

explanation: Placenta praevia typically presents with sudden, painless bleeding consisting of bright red blood because the source is close to the vagina. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T017#GNS226_U2_T017_h3)

question: Why must nurses and doctors strictly avoid inserting fingers into the vagina (digital exam) when placenta praevia is suspected?

options.A: It will immediately cause the baby to drop into a breech position
options.B: It introduces severe bacterial infection into the amniotic sac
options.C: It can disrupt the placenta and trigger massive, life-threatening bleeding
options.D: It causes the uterine muscle to contract into painful spasms

explanation: Touching the lower segment through the vagina can tear the low-lying placenta and cause severe hemorrhage. Knowing this safety rule keeps mothers safe! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T017#GNS226_U2_T017_h3)

question: What is the key symptom that helps differentiate abruptio placentae from placenta praevia?

options.A: Complete absence of any bleeding
options.B: Presence of severe abdominal pain
options.C: Bright red color of the blood
options.D: Onset of bleeding before 24 weeks

explanation: Abruptio placentae is characterized by painful bleeding and a rigid uterus, whereas placenta praevia bleeding is typically painless with a soft uterus. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T017#GNS226_U2_T017_h4)

question: What happens in a 'concealed' type of placental abruption?

options.A: The separation occurs entirely at the edge of the placental disk
options.B: Blood accumulates behind the placenta and does not escape outwardly
options.C: Blood flows rapidly through the cervix as bright red fluid
options.D: The placenta detaches silently without any pain or bleeding whatsoever

explanation: In a concealed abruption, blood gets trapped inside the uterus. This means external bleeding looks deceptively small while internal shock can develop quickly. Great job keeping this in mind! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T017#GNS226_U2_T017_h4)

question: Which nursing action is strictly forbidden during the initial assessment of a patient bleeding in late pregnancy?

options.A: Checking the maternal blood pressure
options.B: Palpating the abdominal wall gently
options.C: Performing a digital vaginal examination
options.D: Monitoring the fetal heart rate

explanation: Never do a digital vaginal exam when late pregnancy bleeding is unexplained, because it can provoke severe hemorrhage if placenta praevia is present! Safety first! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T017#GNS226_U2_T017_h5)

question: A pregnant woman at 32 weeks gestation arrives with vaginal bleeding and a rigid, painful abdomen. What is the most appropriate immediate nursing action?

options.A: Prepare the patient for an immediate routine digital cervical exam
options.B: Apply warm compresses to the lower abdomen to relieve muscle cramps
options.C: Encourage the patient to walk around to help stimulate labor progress
options.D: Notify the doctor, check vital signs, and monitor fetal heart tones

explanation: An unstable patient presenting with signs of abruption requires immediate medical notification, vital sign stabilization, and fetal surveillance while avoiding internal exams. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T017#GNS226_U2_T017_h5)

question: What is the primary emergency goal when nursing a patient with severe antepartum haemorrhage?
