options.A: Lack of blood supply causing pituitary gland tissue death
options.B: A severe kidney infection spreading from the uterus
options.C: Permanent nerve damage from regional anaesthesia
options.D: An autoimmune reaction attacking the thyroid gland

explanation: Extreme blood loss drops the body's blood pressure so low that the pituitary gland gets starved of oxygen and blood, leading to tissue death (necrosis) and hormone imbalances later. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T012#GNS226_U4_T012_h7)

question: How does severe postpartum anaemia commonly impact a new mother in the weeks following discharge?

options.A: It causes permanent high blood pressure requiring daily meds
options.B: It boosts her physical energy due to fast red blood cell recycling
options.C: It speeds up the return of her monthly periods within a week
options.D: It causes deep, persistent fatigue that makes newborn care and bonding tough

explanation: Low haemoglobin means less oxygen travels to her tissues, leaving her utterly exhausted. Supporting her nutrition and recovery is a huge part of postpartum nursing care! [learn more](GNS226_U4_T012#GNS226_U4_T012_h7)

question: What is the primary definition of maternal morbidity in nursing practice?

options.A: Any health condition resulting from or worsened by pregnancy and childbirth
options.B: The permanent inability to conceive after experiencing a miscarriage
options.C: Any psychological stress experienced immediately after delivering a baby
options.D: The total number of maternal deaths recorded in a specific community

explanation: Maternal morbidity covers any physical or mental condition that affects a woman because of pregnancy, childbirth, or the postpartum period, short of death itself. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h1)

question: Why do many women in Nigeria end up using unsafe abortion methods?

options.A: Strict laws, social stigma, and poor access to safe care
options.B: Surgical facilities are cheap and everywhere
options.C: People just love traditional herbs more than hospitals
options.D: Primary health workers give very clear instructions

explanation: Fear of judgment, legal barriers, and a lack of friendly youth clinics push vulnerable people toward dangerous procedures. Great insight to keep in mind for clinical practice! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h1)

question: What keeps the uterus bleeding heavily after an incomplete abortion?

options.A: The outer layer of the womb suddenly becomes very thick
options.B: The lower part of the womb closes up immediately
options.C: The uterine muscle fibers fail to contract tightly
options.D: The main blood vessels in the pelvis get blocked completely

explanation: When tissue stays trapped inside, the womb muscles can't squeeze down tightly to shut off the bleeding vessels. Makes total sense when you picture it! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h2)

question: How can an unsterile instrument used during an abortion lead to septic shock?

options.A: By introducing bacteria that multiply and spread into the bloodstream
options.B: By causing an immediate allergic reaction inside the womb
options.C: By cutting off oxygen to the major abdominal organs
options.D: By causing a sudden drop in blood pressure purely from pain

explanation: Unclean tools carry germs straight into the womb, causing a severe infection that can enter the bloodstream and trigger shock. You're mastering the basics of sepsis! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h2)

question: Which of these is an immediate complication you might see right after an unsafe abortion?

options.A: Severe hemorrhage
options.B: Chronic pelvic pain
options.C: Secondary infertility
options.D: Menstrual irregularities

explanation: Massive blood loss happens right away during or right after the procedure, making it a true emergency. Spotting this quickly saves lives! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h3)

question: Which complication is most likely to show up months or years after an untreated septic abortion?

options.A: Acute kidney failure needing dialysis
options.B: Severe allergic shock from local herbs
options.C: A sudden hole in the womb with bowel exposure
options.D: Infertility caused by blocked fallopian tubes

explanation: Scar tissue from past infections can permanently block the fallopian tubes, making it hard to get pregnant later. Brilliant nursing knowledge! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h3)

question: Why would a doctor order a pelvic ultrasound for a patient with a suspected incomplete abortion?

options.A: To check the patient's blood group and crossmatch
options.B: To measure hormone levels in the kidneys
options.C: To check for leftover pregnancy tissue in the uterus
options.D: To count the exact white blood cells in the body

explanation: An ultrasound lets the team peek inside the womb to confirm if any pregnancy tissue is still trapped. Super helpful diagnostic tool! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h4)

question: Why is blood typing and crossmatching ordered right away for a patient with heavy post-abortion bleeding?

options.A: To check for chronic viral infections
options.B: To figure out how many weeks pregnant she was
options.C: To have matching blood ready for an emergency transfusion
options.D: To find out if she is allergic to IV fluids

explanation: Heavy bleeding drops blood volume fast, so having matched blood on standby is a lifesaver. You're thinking like a true nurse! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h4)

question: Why is a urinary catheter put in place during emergency care for severe abortion complications?

options.A: To flush the bladder with antiseptics to kill germs
options.B: To keep the patient from moving around the ward
options.C: To monitor hourly urine output and check kidney function
options.D: To collect a clean urine sample for a routine pregnancy test

explanation: Watching urine output closely tells us if the kidneys are getting enough blood flow while recovering from shock. Excellent clinical tracking! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h5)

question: What is your main nursing duty when giving drugs to stop excessive bleeding after an abortion?

options.A: Encourage her to drink large amounts of oral rehydration fluids
options.B: Watch for the womb to contract and bleeding to slow down
options.C: Check her skin for rashes every five minutes
options.D: Keep the patient flat with her legs raised high

explanation: These drugs work by making the womb muscle squeeze tight, closing off those bleeding vessels. You're doing great with your medication checks! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h5)

question: How soon can a woman get pregnant again after having an abortion?

options.A: Only after her normal monthly period returns
options.B: After waiting at least six months
options.C: As early as two weeks
options.D: Not until a full year has passed

explanation: Ovulation can bounce back super fast after an abortion, so family planning counseling before discharge is a must. Keep this in mind for patient education! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h6)

question: A patient recovering from an unsafe abortion looks quiet and won't speak to her family. What should you do first?

options.A: Call hospital security to watch for self-harm
options.B: Leave her alone in the ward until she asks for help
options.C: Demand an explanation of why she tried an illegal procedure
options.D: Sit quietly with her, listen with compassion, and promise privacy

explanation: Creating a safe, non-judgmental space builds trust and helps her share her emotional burden. Your empathy is your greatest nursing tool! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h6)

question: What is the best way for community health nurses to help stop unsafe abortions?

options.A: Reporting patients who come in with abortion complications
options.B: Increasing police patrols around illegal clinics
options.C: Promoting education and easy access to family planning
options.D: Banning the sale of common pain relievers

explanation: Stopping unintended pregnancies before they happen through education and contraception is the absolute best way to beat unsafe abortion. Well reasoned! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a good role for nurses in preventing abortion-related health issues?

options.A: Educating local communities on modern family planning
options.B: Advocating for better access to safe reproductive care
options.C: Providing friendly contraceptive counseling in clinics
options.D: Punishing patients who admit to trying self-induced methods

explanation: Nurses never judge or punish patients. Our care must always be professional, kind, and focused on healing. You're going to be an amazing nurse! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h7)

question: What makes an abortion procedure classified as "unsafe"?

options.A: An elective termination performed using modern pharmaceutical drugs
options.B: Any pregnancy loss occurring naturally during the first trimester
options.C: A legal surgical procedure performed by a certified gynecologist
options.D: A termination done without proper medical training or in unsterile settings

explanation: You've got this! An unsafe abortion simply means it was carried out by untrained hands or in dirty places, which puts the patient at a huge risk for severe complications. Spotting this definition helps you protect your patients early! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T002#GNS226_U5_T002_h1)

question: Why do many women end up turning to dangerous, clandestine abortion methods?

options.A: A personal preference for traditional herbal treatments over hospitals
options.B: Mandatory government programs requiring family planning compliance
options.C: Restrictive laws, social stigma, and poor access to contraception
options.D: Abundant availability of safe surgical clinics in rural areas

explanation: It's all about barriers! When society judges harshly and legal or financial access to safe care is blocked, desperate situations drive people toward risky alternatives. Understanding this helps us practice with empathy, not judgment. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T002#GNS226_U5_T002_h1)

question: What is the most common and immediate cause of death after an unsafe abortion?

options.A: Hemorrhage
options.B: Uterine cancer
options.C: Renal failure
options.D: Gestational diabetes

explanation: Heavy, uncontrolled bleeding is the number one emergency here. When tissues are torn or left behind in unsterile procedures, severe bleeding can turn fatal very quickly if we don't act fast. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T002#GNS226_U5_T002_h2)

question: A patient comes in after a clandestine abortion with a high fever, smelly vaginal discharge, and lower tummy pain. What is the most likely problem?

options.A: Normal postpartum involution
options.B: Pelvic inflammatory sepsis
options.C: Uncomplicated uterine atony
options.D: Primary ovarian hyperstimulation

explanation: Fever plus foul-smelling discharge is a red flag for infection. Unsterile instruments easily introduce bacteria right into the uterus, leading quickly to pelvic sepsis. Great clinical spotting! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T002#GNS226_U5_T002_h2)

question: Why do nurses need to keep a close eye out when caring for women with sudden tummy pain in the emergency ward?

options.A: Patients may hide a history of unsafe abortion due to fear or legal stigma
options.B: Abortion complications never present with abnormal vaginal bleeding
options.C: Routine screening policies forbid nurses from asking about sexual history
options.D: Standard diagnostic tests cannot detect early stages of pregnancy

explanation: Fear of judgment or legal trouble often makes patients keep quiet about what really happened. As nurses, our compassionate detective work helps us uncover the truth and save lives! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T002#GNS226_U5_T002_h3)

question: Which physical sign strongly points toward a uterine perforation or pelvic peritonitis?

options.A: Painless bilateral swelling of the lower extremities
options.B: Generalized skin rash and localized itching
options.C: Elevated blood pressure and clear breath sounds
options.D: A rigid and tender abdomen with rebound tenderness

explanation: When the lining of the belly (peritoneum) gets irritated or infected, the abdominal muscles lock up tight ('rigidity'), and pressing and letting go hurts sharply ('rebound tenderness'). A classic exam and ward clue! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T002#GNS226_U5_T002_h3)

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should do for a patient going into shock from severe post-abortion bleeding?

options.A: Perform a detailed psychosocial history regarding the pregnancy
options.B: Send the patient immediately for diagnostic pelvic ultrasound
options.C: Administer oral rehydration salts and counsel on contraception
options.D: Insert large-bore intravenous lines for fluid resuscitation

explanation: ABC comes first—and in bleeding shock, getting IV lines open fast to pump fluids and restore blood volume is an absolute lifesaver! You've got this. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T002#GNS226_U5_T002_h4)

question: Aside from giving fluids, what type of medication is routinely given right away if an infected (septic) abortion is suspected?

options.A: Long-acting oral hypoglycemic agents
options.B: Broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics
options.C: Topical corticosteroid ointments
options.D: Inhaled short-acting beta-agonists

explanation: Infection spreads fast! Starting broad-spectrum IV antibiotics early stops bacteria in their tracks and prevents the patient from sliding into full septic shock. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T002#GNS226_U5_T002_h4)

question: What are the main parts of Post-Abortion Care (PAC)?

options.A: Surgical sterilization, blood donation drives, and psychiatric isolation
options.B: Emergency treatment, family planning counseling, and reproductive health linkages
options.C: Mandatory legal reporting, punitive counseling, and moral interrogation
options.D: Routine hysterectomy, genetic testing, and long-term foster care referral

explanation: PAC is a complete care package: treat the immediate danger, talk about family planning so it doesn't happen again, and connect them to healthy support networks. Brilliant concept to master! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T002#GNS226_U5_T002_h5)

question: What is the main goal of "value clarification" workshops for nursing staff?

options.A: To train nurses on advanced surgical procedures like abdominal hysterectomy
options.B: To enforce strict legal penalties against patients who induce abortions
options.C: To help nurses set aside personal biases to provide non-judgmental care
options.D: To update hospital billing policies for emergency obstetric services

explanation: We all have personal beliefs, but value clarification helps us check our biases at the door so we can treat every single patient with professional, loving kindness. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T002#GNS226_U5_T002_h5)

question: How does making modern contraception easy for everyone to get help lower maternal death rates?

options.A: By shortening the normal physiological gestation period for women
options.B: By completely eliminating the need for emergency obstetric departments
options.C: By preventing all forms of sexually transmitted bacterial infections
options.D: By reducing the incidence of unintended pregnancies and unsafe abortions

explanation: Prevention is key! When people can easily access contraception, unplanned pregnancies drop, which means fewer people resort to dangerous, life-threatening unsafe abortions. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T002#GNS226_U5_T002_h6)

question: Which healthcare approach works best when teaching young people about reproductive health?

options.A: Mandatory public announcements broadcast only in corporate workplaces
options.B: Strict punitive laws targeting teenagers seeking health information
options.C: Youth-friendly clinics offering confidential counseling and contraceptives
options.D: Excluding adolescents from family planning discussions until marriage

explanation: Young people want privacy and a welcoming environment without fear of being scolded. Youth-friendly clinics build trust so teens actually feel safe seeking help! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T002#GNS226_U5_T002_h6)

question: How does the World Health Organization define an unsafe abortion?

options.A: A termination done by unskilled persons or in unsterile environments
options.B: A surgical procedure performed strictly in a teaching hospital
options.C: Any termination of pregnancy requested by a minor
options.D: Any pregnancy loss occurring naturally before the twentieth week

explanation: You've got this! An unsafe abortion simply means a procedure done without proper medical skills, sterile tools, or safe standards. Always look out for the setting and who is performing it. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T003#GNS226_U5_T003_h1)

question: Why do many young women in Nigeria turn to secret, unsafe abortion methods?

options.A: Advise from community health extension workers
options.B: Preference for traditional herbal preparations over modern medicine
options.C: Fear of social stigma and strict legal or religious restrictions
options.D: Lack of awareness that government hospitals offer free services

explanation: Societal pressure, shame, and strict laws often push frightened individuals away from safe hospitals and into risky, hidden places. A supportive nurse makes all the difference! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T003#GNS226_U5_T003_h1)

question: In Nigeria, under what single main condition is an abortion legally allowed?

options.A: If fetal abnormalities are detected early
options.B: When requested by the parents of a minor
options.C: To save the life of the pregnant woman
options.D: If the pregnancy resulted from financial hardship

explanation: Good to know for your exams and practice: Nigerian law is very strict and only permits abortion if it is done to preserve the mother's physical life. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T003#GNS226_U5_T003_h2)

question: How does Nigeria's strict legal stance on abortion end up hurting maternal health?

options.A: It forces procedures underground, leading to dangerous and secretive practices
options.B: It eliminates the need for contraceptives in rural communities
options.C: It guarantees that all women receive free post-abortion medications
options.D: It encourages traditional birth attendants to learn modern surgery

explanation: Making laws strict doesn't stop abortions; it just drives them underground where unsterile tools and secret methods cause severe complications. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T003#GNS226_U5_T003_h2)

question: What is a major root cause of unwanted pregnancies that lead to unsafe abortions?

options.A: Universal access to emergency birth control pills
options.B: Unmet needs and lack of access to modern contraceptives
options.C: Mandatory sex education classes in all primary schools
options.D: Excessive availability of free family planning clinics

explanation: When people cannot get or afford reliable birth control, unplanned pregnancies happen more often. Patient education is our best tool here! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T003#GNS226_U5_T003_h3)

question: A university student hides her pregnancy out of fear of expulsion and shame. What factor does this highlight?

options.A: A recognized legal indication for safe abortion
options.B: The direct physical effect of herbal toxins
options.C: Peer pressure and social stigma
options.D: Direct medical complication of hypertension

explanation: Fear of judgment and losing her education often pushes a student toward risky, secret procedures. Empathy from nurses is crucial! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T003#GNS226_U5_T003_h3)

question: Which complication happens most directly when sharp metal objects are pushed into the uterus?

options.A: Chronic hypertension and peripheral edema
options.B: Uterine perforation and severe hemorrhage
options.C: Allergic rhinitis and skin rashes
options.D: Renal stone formation and bladder spasms

explanation: Unskilled hands using sharp instruments can easily pierce the muscular wall of the uterus, causing heavy internal bleeding. That's a major medical emergency! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T003#GNS226_U5_T003_h4)

question: Why is washing out the vagina with harsh chemicals like bleach extremely dangerous?

options.A: It immediately halts all hormonal activity in the pituitary gland
options.B: It permanently prevents future urinary tract infections
options.C: It reliably evacuates the entire uterine contents within minutes
options.D: It causes severe chemical burns, tissue necrosis, and systemic toxicity

explanation: Caustic substances destroy delicate vaginal and cervical tissue right on contact and can enter the bloodstream, causing whole-body poisoning. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T003#GNS226_U5_T003_h4)

question: Which group of symptoms strongly points to a pelvic infection (sepsis) after an unsafe abortion?

options.A: Painless vaginal bleeding and elevated blood pressure
options.B: High fever, foul-smelling discharge, and lower abdominal pain
options.C: Frequent urination, clear discharge, and normal temperature
options.D: Severe headache, blurred vision, and dry skin

explanation: Think of infection signs: fever, bad-smelling discharge, and tummy pain are classic red flags that unsterile instruments or tissue were left behind. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T003#GNS226_U5_T003_h5)

question: A young woman comes to the clinic with a rigid, painful abdomen and shoulder pain after visiting an unlicensed place. What is the most likely issue?

options.A: Normal physiological postpartum recovery
options.B: Uterine perforation with peritonitis
options.C: Acute urinary tract infection
options.D: Uncomplicated incomplete abortion

explanation: A board-like, rigid tummy and shoulder pain mean internal bleeding is irritating the lining of the abdomen (peritoneum). This needs urgent surgical care! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T003#GNS226_U5_T003_h5)

question: What is the absolute first thing a nurse must do when a patient arrives with complications from an unsafe abortion?

options.A: Stabilizing airway, breathing, and circulation
options.B: Filling out legal police reports immediately
options.C: Conducting a detailed religious counseling session
options.D: Interrogating the patient about who performed the procedure

explanation: ABC comes first in every emergency! Saving the patient's life and treating shock always takes priority over asking questions. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T003#GNS226_U5_T003_h6)

question: Why is it so important for a nurse to communicate without judgment when assessing these patients?

options.A: It prevents the hospital from paying for laboratory investigations
options.B: It encourages the patient to truthfully share what methods were used, aiding proper treatment
options.C: It guarantees the patient will never experience physical pain
options.D: It is required by criminal law enforcement agencies in all Nigerian states

explanation: When patients feel judged, they hide details like chemical use or instrument trauma. A warm, welcoming attitude saves lives! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T003#GNS226_U5_T003_h6)

question: What is the preferred modern method for clearing the uterus safely during post-abortion care?

options.A: Vaginal douching with hot water
options.B: Manual Vacuum Aspiration (MVA)
options.C: High-dose oxytocin infusion alone
options.D: Radical abdominal hysterectomy

explanation: MVA is gentle, quick, and much safer for the uterine wall than old-fashioned sharp scraping (curettage). It's a wonderful modern standard! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T003#GNS226_U5_T003_h7)

question: Why must broad-spectrum antibiotics be given right away to a patient with a septic incomplete abortion?

options.A: To directly stimulate uterine contractions and expel retained tissue
options.B: To control and prevent the spread of ascending bacterial infection and septic shock
options.C: To replace lost blood volume and increase hemoglobin levels
options.D: To lower systemic blood pressure and reduce anxiety

explanation: Unsterile procedures let bacteria into the uterus, which can quickly spread into the blood and cause deadly septic shock. Quick antibiotics are life-savers! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T003#GNS226_U5_T003_h7)

question: How soon can a woman start ovulating and get pregnant again after an abortion?

options.A: Only after six months of complete amenorrhea
options.B: After her third normal menstrual cycle
options.C: Not until she reaches menopause
options.D: As early as two weeks post-abortion

explanation: Fertility bounces back super fast! That is why family planning counseling before discharge is a vital part of nursing care. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T003#GNS226_U5_T003_h8)

question: What is the main goal of giving birth control counseling during Post-Abortion Care (PAC)?

options.A: To prevent repeat unintended pregnancies and subsequent unsafe abortions
options.B: To enforce government population control quotas in rural areas
options.C: To punish the patient for engaging in premarital sex
options.D: To permanently sterilize high-risk young women

explanation: PAC counseling is all about empowering women with choices so they can protect their health and avoid future unplanned pregnancies. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T003#GNS226_U5_T003_h8)

question: How can community health nurses help lower the number of unsafe abortions?

options.A: By dispelling contraceptive myths and promoting youth-friendly reproductive health services
options.B: By teaching women how to safely use herbal concoctions at home
options.C: By arresting individuals who perform illegal abortions in local villages
options.D: By distributing heavy surgical instruments to traditional birth attendants

explanation: Education and open access to family planning stop unwanted pregnancies before they happen—that is the most powerful prevention! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T003#GNS226_U5_T003_h9)

question: A community health nurse notices many teens in her local area know nothing about birth control. What is her best first step?

options.A: Report all teenagers to the local police division for investigation
options.B: Establish an educational youth-friendly reproductive health club at the local center
options.C: Wait until patients present with complications before offering advice
options.D: Ban all public discussions regarding sexual health in schools

explanation: Creating safe, welcoming spaces gives adolescents the accurate facts they need to protect their health and futures. Great nursing initiative! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T003#GNS226_U5_T003_h9)

question: What makes an abortion procedure classified as "unsafe"?

options.A: Any pregnancy loss occurring naturally during the first trimester
options.B: A legal termination performed in a fully equipped hospital
options.C: A procedure done by unskilled persons or in poor medical environments
options.D: Any abortion that requires the use of surgical instruments

explanation: You've got this! An abortion is unsafe if it's carried out by people without proper training or in places that lack basic medical standards. Keeping patients safe means knowing the difference. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T004#GNS226_U5_T004_h1)

question: Where do most unsafe abortions and related complications happen around the world?

options.A: In nations where abortion is completely legal on request
options.B: In urban centers with universal healthcare access
options.C: In low- and middle-income countries with restrictive laws
options.D: In countries with high ratios of trained obstetricians

explanation: Spot on! Strict laws paired with weak healthcare systems in developing regions create a high burden of unsafe procedures. Understanding this helps us advocate for better maternal care. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T004#GNS226_U5_T004_h1)

question: What is a major result of having very strict, restrictive abortion laws in a country?

options.A: A higher rate of natural spontaneous miscarriages
options.B: An increase in clandestine and dangerous abortion procedures
options.C: Better access to modern family planning services
options.D: A complete elimination of unwanted pregnancies

explanation: Great thinking! Banning procedures doesn't stop them from happening; it just pushes women to seek out hidden, risky methods in secret. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T004#GNS226_U5_T004_h2)

question: How does social stigma make the problem of unsafe abortions even worse?

options.A: It forces women to hide their condition and delay seeking safe help
options.B: It prevents healthcare workers from learning basic nursing skills
options.C: It causes severe hormonal imbalances that mimic pregnancy complications
options.D: It directly reduces the availability of surgical equipment in hospitals

explanation: Spot on. Fear of judgment and shame makes patients wait too long or use dangerous home remedies instead of coming to us for safe care. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T004#GNS226_U5_T004_h2)

question: What is one of the most immediate, life-threatening dangers after an unsafe abortion?

options.A: Severe hemorrhage
options.B: Gestational diabetes
options.C: Permanent hypertension
options.D: Chronic hair loss

explanation: You nailed it! Heavy bleeding from incomplete tissue removal or trauma is a leading cause of emergency admissions and death after unsafe procedures. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T004#GNS226_U5_T004_h3)

question: Why does using unsterile instruments during an abortion often lead to severe sepsis?

options.A: The cervix permanently closes and traps natural bodily fluids
options.B: Bacteria are introduced directly into the sterile uterine cavity
options.C: Incomplete emptying of the uterus causes immediate kidney failure
options.D: The body reacts to the metal by producing toxic white blood cells

explanation: Exactly! Unclean tools carry harmful germs straight into the pelvis, which quickly turns into a dangerous, widespread infection. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T004#GNS226_U5_T004_h3)

question: As a nurse, what is your very first priority when a patient arrives with post-abortion complications?

options.A: Conducting a detailed interview about contraception history
options.B: Reporting the incident immediately to law enforcement
options.C: Asking about her religious and cultural beliefs
options.D: Evaluating airway, breathing, and circulation

explanation: Safety first! Emergency nursing always starts with the ABCs to stabilize vital signs and catch shock or heavy bleeding early. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T004#GNS226_U5_T004_h4)

question: A patient arrives pale, dizzy, and bleeding heavily after an unsafe abortion. What action should you take right away?

options.A: Perform a complete pelvic exam without checking vital signs
options.B: Start a large-bore intravenous line for fluid resuscitation
options.C: Ask the patient to write down a detailed confession of the act
options.D: Wait for the attending physician to arrive before acting

explanation: You got this! When someone is bleeding heavily, getting IV access fast is crucial to restore fluids, boost blood volume, and prevent shock. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T004#GNS226_U5_T004_h4)

question: What are the core parts of comprehensive Post-Abortion Care (PAC)?

options.A: Antibiotic therapy alone without any further clinical follow-up
options.B: Criminal investigation, legal counseling, and mandatory detention
options.C: Surgical sterilization, blood transfusions, and long-term isolation
options.D: Emergency treatment, family planning, and reproductive health linkages

explanation: Wonderful! PAC is a complete package that covers acute medical treatment, birth control counseling, and connection to wider health resources. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T004#GNS226_U5_T004_h5)

question: Why is family planning counseling considered such an important part of Post-Abortion Care?

options.A: It cures underlying pelvic inflammatory disease without antibiotics
options.B: It stops all immediate bleeding from uterine perforation
options.C: It helps women prevent another unwanted pregnancy in the near future
options.D: It is required by law to permanently sterilize every female patient

explanation: Spot on! Fertility returns very quickly after an abortion, so giving timely contraceptive advice helps prevent repeat unsafe procedures. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T004#GNS226_U5_T004_h5)

question: What attitude should you as a nurse always maintain when caring for patients with post-abortion complications?

options.A: Skeptical, inquisitive, and publicly critical
options.B: Empathetic, confidential, and free from moral judgment
options.C: Strict, punitive, and emotionally detached
options.D: Indifferent, passive, and task-oriented only

explanation: You're doing great. Being non-judgmental and keeping things strictly confidential builds trust, ensuring vulnerable patients feel safe enough to get lifesaving help. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T004#GNS226_U5_T004_h6)

question: How can nurses actively help prevent unsafe abortions out in the community?

options.A: By educating the public on modern contraception and reproductive health
options.B: By banning the sale of harmful chemicals in local markets
options.C: By arresting individuals who perform illegal medical procedures
options.D: By strictly refusing to treat patients who attempted self-induction

explanation: Exactly right! Community education prevents unintended pregnancies in the first place, reducing the need for dangerous, hidden procedures. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T004#GNS226_U5_T004_h6)

question: Up to how many weeks of pregnancy is an abortion generally defined to occur?

options.A: Under 20 to 22 weeks of gestation
options.B: Any time after 40 weeks of gestation
options.C: At exactly 28 weeks of gestation
options.D: Between 32 and 36 weeks of gestation

explanation: We define an abortion as the end of a pregnancy before the baby can survive outside the womb, which is generally under 20 to 22 weeks. You've got this! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T005#GNS226_U5_T005_h1)

question: What is the main difference between a spontaneous abortion and an induced abortion?

options.A: Induced abortions happen completely by accident
options.B: Induced abortions are always caused by chromosomal defects
options.C: Spontaneous abortions only occur during the third trimester
options.D: Spontaneous abortions happen naturally without outside intervention

explanation: A spontaneous abortion (miscarriage) happens on its own due to natural factors, while an induced abortion is brought on by intentional medical or surgical steps. Simple and clear! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T005#GNS226_U5_T005_h1)

question: Which type of early pregnancy loss features vaginal bleeding while the cervix remains firmly closed?

options.A: Threatened abortion
options.B: Inevitable abortion
options.C: Complete abortion
options.D: Incomplete abortion

explanation: In a threatened abortion, there's some bleeding, but because the cervix is still closed, there's still a strong chance the pregnancy can continue safely. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T005#GNS226_U5_T005_h2)

question: A patient has heavy bleeding, bad cramps, an open cervix, and reports that some tissue has passed but parts are still inside. What is this called?

options.A: Threatened abortion
options.B: Missed abortion
options.C: Incomplete abortion
options.D: Septic abortion

explanation: When some tissue comes out but part of it stays trapped inside with an open cervix, we call it an incomplete abortion. Great clinical spotting! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T005#GNS226_U5_T005_h2)

question: Why would a doctor perform a therapeutic abortion?

options.A: Fulfilling an elective personal request without medical reason
options.B: Preventing multiple births during fertility treatments
options.C: Ending a pregnancy due to financial convenience alone
options.D: Protecting maternal health or addressing severe fetal anomalies

explanation: Therapeutic abortions are done to save the mother's life or health, or when the baby has very severe issues that mean it cannot survive. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T005#GNS226_U5_T005_h3)

question: What is the biggest danger that causes high complications in unsafe abortions?

options.A: Early detection of pregnancy in a regulated hospital setting
options.B: The use of untrained providers and unsterile conditions
options.C: Regular monitoring by professional obstetric nurses
options.D: The prescription of standard medical abortion pills by doctors

explanation: Unsafe abortions often involve dirty tools and untrained people, which sadly leads to heavy infections and severe bleeding. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T005#GNS226_U5_T005_h3)

question: A patient with possible incomplete abortion has a fast heart rate (120 bpm) and low blood pressure (90/60 mmHg). What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Monitor for signs of hemorrhage and hypovolemic shock
options.B: Document the findings in the chart and wait until morning
options.C: Prepare the patient for a routine dietary consultation
options.D: Discharge the patient home with mild pain relievers

explanation: A fast pulse and low BP in a bleeding patient are major warning signs of heavy blood loss. Catching shock early saves lives! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T005#GNS226_U5_T005_h4)

question: Why do nurses need to check pads and tissues passed by a patient having a miscarriage?

options.A: To calculate the exact weight of the pregnant woman
options.B: To determine if all products of conception have left the uterus
options.C: To prevent the patient from experiencing abdominal pain
options.D: To prove that an induced abortion was performed legally

explanation: Checking the tissue helps us know if everything came out cleanly or if pieces are still trapped inside needing medical help. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T005#GNS226_U5_T005_h4)

question: What injection must be given to an Rh-negative mother after a miscarriage to protect her future pregnancies?

options.A: Oxytocin injection
options.B: Broad-spectrum antibiotic
options.C: Iron supplement syrup
options.D: RhoGAM (Rh immunoglobulin)

explanation: RhoGAM stops an Rh-negative mother's body from forming antibodies that could attack the blood of future babies. Brilliant nursing knowledge to keep in mind! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T005#GNS226_U5_T005_h5)

question: Why is emotional support such a big part of nursing care after an abortion or miscarriage?

options.A: Emotional counseling completely eliminates the risk of physical infection
options.B: Patients often experience complex grief, anxiety, and psychological distress
options.C: Psychological support replaces the need for vital sign monitoring
options.D: Hormonal changes only affect physical health and never mental well-being

explanation: Losing a pregnancy hurts deeply on the inside. Being a warm, listening nurse is just as important as checking physical vitals! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T005#GNS226_U5_T005_h5)

question: What is the main goal of post-abortion care (PAC)?

options.A: To reduce maternal illness and death from abortion complications
options.B: To provide permanent sterilization to all female patients
options.C: To investigate the legal circumstances of a pregnancy loss
options.D: To promote mandatory reporting of all spontaneous miscarriages

explanation: Great job! PAC is all about saving lives and treating any physical or emotional issues after a pregnancy loss so the patient can recover safely. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T006#GNS226_U5_T006_h1)

question: Why is post-abortion care viewed as a complete package rather than just a single medical procedure?

options.A: It must involve legal teams alongside medical doctors in every case
options.B: It requires multiple surgical operations over a span of several months
options.C: It combines emergency treatment, counseling, contraception, and health linkages
options.D: It is only performed in specialized tertiary teaching hospitals

explanation: Spot on! PAC covers more than just the immediate physical cleanup—it looks at the whole person by offering counseling, family planning, and follow-up support. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T006#GNS226_U5_T006_h1)

question: How many core elements make up the standard post-abortion care framework?

options.A: Ten
options.B: Three
options.C: Seven
options.D: Five

explanation: You got it! The standard PAC framework is built on five key elements that guide clinical care and community support. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T006#GNS226_U5_T006_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT one of the five core elements of post-abortion care?

options.A: Mandatory criminal investigation
options.B: Treatment of abortion complications
options.C: Contraceptive and family planning services
options.D: Post-abortion counseling

explanation: Correct! PAC is strictly about health, safety, and support—not punitive legal investigations. Our job as nurses is medical care. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T006#GNS226_U5_T006_h2)

question: What is the preferred method for first-trimester uterine evacuation in post-abortion care?

options.A: High-dose oral oxytocin alone
options.B: Manual vacuum aspiration
options.C: Sharp metallic curettage without anesthesia
options.D: Major open abdominal surgery

explanation: Well done! Manual vacuum aspiration (MVA) is widely preferred because it is safe, highly effective, and much gentler than older methods. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T006#GNS226_U5_T006_h3)

question: A patient comes in with an incomplete abortion showing fever, lower belly pain, and foul-smelling discharge. What should you do first as the nurse?

options.A: Send the patient home with instructions to return next week
options.B: Administer high-dose fertility drugs to stimulate ovulation
options.C: Prepare for broad-spectrum antibiotics and report signs of infection
options.D: Withhold all fluids to prevent vomiting during the assessment

explanation: Spot on! Fever and foul discharge are classic warning signs of a septic abortion. Immediate antibiotics and medical stabilization are lifesavers here. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T006#GNS226_U5_T006_h3)

question: Why are active listening and a non-judgmental attitude so important during post-abortion counseling?

options.A: It prevents patients from ever experiencing normal grief
options.B: It replaces the need for any physical medical treatments
options.C: It helps patients process diverse emotional reactions safely
options.D: It guarantees that the patient will choose permanent sterilization

explanation: You got it! Everyone reacts differently emotionally, and offering a safe, open space lets patients express themselves without fear of being judged. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T006#GNS226_U5_T006_h4)

question: What is a common emotional response a patient might experience after an abortion?

options.A: An immediate desire to write a public memoir about the event
options.B: Complete emotional numbness that lasts for an entire lifetime
options.C: A wide range of feelings including relief, grief, or anxiety
options.D: Permanent clinical detachment from all family members

explanation: Exactly! Feelings after pregnancy loss are deeply personal and can span anywhere from sadness and anxiety to relief. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T006#GNS226_U5_T006_h4)

question: How soon can a person start ovulating again after experiencing an abortion?

options.A: As early as two weeks
options.B: Only after a full year passes
options.C: Never, fertility is permanently lost
options.D: After exactly six months

explanation: Correct! Fertility can return surprisingly fast—sometimes in just two weeks—which is why talking about contraception early is so crucial. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T006#GNS226_U5_T006_h5)

question: When is the best time to discuss family planning options with a patient receiving post-abortion care?

options.A: Before the patient is discharged from the clinical setting
options.B: Only after the patient experiences a second unplanned pregnancy
options.C: Refer them to a distant pharmacy without discussing options
options.D: Wait until six months have passed to avoid overwhelming them

explanation: Spot on! Bringing up family planning before discharge ensures the patient is protected against a quick repeat pregnancy while they are still connected to care. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T006#GNS226_U5_T006_h5)

question: Why are community referrals and health linkages important in post-abortion care?

options.A: They replace the need for emergency treatment during complications
options.B: They ensure that the patient never has to visit a hospital again
options.C: They support long-term wellness and prevent future reproductive health issues
options.D: They are only used to track legal infractions in the community

explanation: Well done! Community linkages connect patients to ongoing check-ups, STI care, and other vital primary health resources. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T006#GNS226_U5_T006_h6)

question: Which group of people often acts as a bridge between local communities and clinical PAC facilities?

options.A: Hospital maintenance staff
options.B: International tax auditors
options.C: Community health workers
options.D: Forensic investigators

explanation: Correct! Community health workers play a wonderful role in guiding patients to local support networks and follow-up care. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T006#GNS226_U5_T006_h6)

question: How does social stigma directly affect patients who need post-abortion care?

options.A: It guarantees faster recovery times inside the emergency ward
options.B: It encourages patients to attend more routine health checkups
options.C: It delays patients from seeking timely and life-saving medical attention
options.D: It improves the emotional rapport between nurses and patients

explanation: Spot on! Fear of being judged or mistreated often forces patients to hide their symptoms, delaying the urgent care they need. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T006#GNS226_U5_T006_h7)

question: What is a core professional duty of a nurse caring for a PAC patient?

options.A: Providing unbiased, confidential, and compassionate medical care
options.B: Reporting the patient to local law enforcement authorities
options.C: Sharing clinical details publicly to educate the community
options.D: Refusing treatment if personal beliefs conflict with the diagnosis

explanation: You nailed it! As nurses, we are ethically bound to treat every patient with dignity, total confidentiality, and professional kindness. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T006#GNS226_U5_T006_h7)

question: What is the main goal of post-abortion care (PAC) counselling?

options.A: To punish clients who break hospital rules
options.B: To force clients to speak with law enforcement
options.C: To support clients physically and emotionally
options.D: To convince clients to change their religious beliefs

explanation: PAC counselling is all about giving compassionate physical and emotional support to help your client heal safely. As a nurse, creating a safe space makes all the difference! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h1)

question: Why is a non-judgmental approach so important when caring for a post-abortion client?

options.A: Clients often face stigma, fear, and guilt
options.B: It lowers the cost of medical supplies
options.C: It is required by the hospital billing department
options.D: It shortens the length of hospital stays

explanation: Many clients carry heavy emotional burdens like fear and societal stigma. A welcoming, open-hearted nurse helps build the trust they need to heal. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h1)

question: What does 'values clarification' help a nurse examine?

options.A: Hospital equipment inventory
options.B: Monthly salary deductions
options.C: Personal beliefs and biases
options.D: Public transport schedules

explanation: Values clarification is a great self-check tool. It allows us as nurses to look at our own inner biases so our personal opinions never get in the way of great patient care. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h2)

question: How should you handle your personal moral beliefs when caring for a post-abortion client?

options.A: Refuse to provide any medication or comfort
options.B: Put personal views aside to deliver respectful care
options.C: Report the client to religious leaders
options.D: Argue with the client about their life choices

explanation: Professional nursing ethics mean we always put our patient's health and dignity first, delivering unbiased, compassionate care no matter our personal background. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h2)

question: What is a key physical sign you must check for during an initial post-abortion assessment?

options.A: Yellowing of the fingernails
options.B: Increased hair growth
options.C: Excessive vaginal bleeding
options.D: Swelling in the lower legs

explanation: Checking for heavy or excessive bleeding is a vital first step to catch potential hemorrhage early and keep your patient safe. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h3)

question: A client is quiet, avoids eye contact, and trembles slightly during your assessment. What might this suggest?

options.A: The client is ready for immediate hospital discharge
options.B: The client is hiding a contagious respiratory infection
options.C: The client may be experiencing significant emotional distress
options.D: The client has a normal blood pressure reading

explanation: Withdrawn behavior and physical trembling are classic signs of anxiety, fear, or emotional shock. A gentle touch and supportive counselling go a long way here! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h3)

question: Which symptom is a major danger sign that requires immediate medical help after an abortion?

options.A: Feeling slightly tired in the afternoon
options.B: Light spotting that stops after three days
options.C: Mild cramping for twenty minutes in the morning
options.D: Soaking through two heavy pads per hour for two hours

explanation: Heavy bleeding soaking multiple pads in a short time is a red flag for hemorrhage. Always act fast and notify the doctor on duty! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h4)

question: A client asks when it is safe to have sexual intercourse again after an abortion. What is the best advice?

options.A: Wait exactly one full year before trying again
options.B: Resume only during the weekend
options.C: Resume immediately if there is no headache
options.D: Wait until bleeding stops completely and the cervix closes

explanation: Advise 'pelvic rest' until bleeding stops and the cervix closes. This simple rule prevents bacteria from entering and drastically cuts down the risk of infection. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h4)

question: How soon can a person's fertility return after an abortion procedure?

options.A: After exactly six months
options.B: Not for at least two years
options.C: As early as two weeks
options.D: Only after menopause begins

explanation: Surprise! Ovulation can bounce back in as little as two weeks. That's why talking about family planning early is so crucial before she leaves the clinic. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h5)

question: Why is client-centered contraceptive counselling so important during post-abortion care?

options.A: It forces the client to use surgical sterilization
options.B: It helps the client freely choose a method that fits her life
options.C: It reduces the amount of paperwork for the clinic
options.D: It guarantees that the client will never need healthcare again

explanation: Client-centered care respects autonomy. We help her pick a method that matches her personal lifestyle and goals without pressure or judgment. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h5)

question: What are some common emotional reactions a client might experience after an abortion?

options.A: Uncontrollable happiness and laughter
options.B: Complete physical paralysis
options.C: Relief, sadness, or guilt
options.D: Total loss of memory

explanation: Emotions are complex and vary widely. A client might feel relief, sorrow, or a mixture of many things—and all of these responses can be completely normal. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h6)

question: When should you refer a post-abortion client to a mental health specialist?

options.A: When the client shows signs of severe depression or suicidal thoughts
options.B: Whenever the client has a mild headache
options.C: Every single time a client asks for a prescription for pain medicine
options.D: Only when the client refuses to take iron tablets

explanation: While basic emotional support is part of everyday nursing, deep psychological distress, severe depression, or self-harm threats need expert psychiatric help. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of community referral pathways in post-abortion care?

options.A: To keep clients inside the hospital for months
options.B: To connect clients with extended support and specialized services
options.C: To force clients to change their home addresses
options.D: To increase the cost of local pharmacy drugs

explanation: Referrals link clients to outside resources like support groups and community counsellors so they continue to get holistic care even after leaving the ward. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a goal of a strong healthcare referral network?

options.A: Isolating the client from all family and friends
options.B: Ensuring continuity of medical follow-up
options.C: Providing access to professional social workers
options.D: Connecting the client with community support groups

explanation: Good referral networks are designed to build a strong safety net and reduce isolation, never to cut a client off from the people who love and support them. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h7)

question: What is the maximum gestational age used to define an abortion?

options.A: Before 20 weeks of gestation
options.B: Before 37 weeks of gestation
options.C: Before 28 weeks of gestation
options.D: Before 12 weeks of gestation

explanation: An abortion is classified as the loss of a pregnancy before 20 weeks of gestation, or when the baby weighs less than 500 grams. You've got this! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T008#GNS226_U5_T008_h1)

question: A patient has vaginal bleeding, mild lower tummy cramps, but her cervix is still tightly closed. What kind of abortion is this?

options.A: Incomplete abortion
options.B: Threatened abortion
options.C: Inevitable abortion
options.D: Complete abortion

explanation: When bleeding and cramps happen but the cervix stays closed, it's called a threatened abortion because the pregnancy might still continue safely. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T008#GNS226_U5_T008_h1)

question: Which test is best for checking if any pregnancy tissue is left inside the uterus?

options.A: Urinalysis dipstick
options.B: Endometrial biopsy
options.C: Abdominal X-ray
options.D: Pelvic ultrasound

explanation: A pelvic ultrasound gives a clear picture of the inside of the uterus so we can easily tell if it's completely empty or if tissue remains. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T008#GNS226_U5_T008_h2)

question: Why do we check the Rhesus blood group for a patient having an incomplete abortion?

options.A: To calculate her exact gestational age
options.B: To check for severe iron deficiency anemia
options.C: To find out if she has a bacterial infection
options.D: To see if she needs anti-D immunoglobulin

explanation: If a mother is Rhesus-negative, giving anti-D immunoglobulin protects her future pregnancies from blood-type mismatch issues. Great clinical thinking! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T008#GNS226_U5_T008_h2)

question: What is the first life-saving goal when treating a patient with heavy bleeding from an abortion?

options.A: Discharging the patient home with pain relief
options.B: Restoring circulating blood volume and perfusion
options.C: Conducting a detailed psychosocial interview
options.D: Scheduling routine laboratory blood tests

explanation: When there is heavy bleeding, stopping shock and getting fluids back into circulation is always the number one emergency priority. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T008#GNS226_U5_T008_h3)

question: Why is a urinary catheter put in place when treating a patient in severe shock from bleeding?

options.A: To stop the patient from moving around in bed
options.B: To empty the bladder before a surgical procedure
options.C: To collect a clean-catch urine culture specimen
options.D: To monitor hourly urine output to check kidney function

explanation: Urine output is a fantastic mirror for how well the kidneys and vital organs are receiving blood during resuscitation. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T008#GNS226_U5_T008_h3)

question: Which medication is used in medical abortion to cause strong uterine contractions?

options.A: Magnesium sulfate
options.B: Ergometrine
options.C: Misoprostol
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: Misoprostol helps the uterus contract and safely push out any remaining tissue. You'll see this drug used a lot in ward practice! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T008#GNS226_U5_T008_h4)

question: What does mifepristone do when used in a medical abortion?

options.A: Blocks progesterone to soften the cervix and break down the lining
options.B: Stops sudden bacterial growth inside the womb
options.C: Lowers blood pressure during heavy bleeding
options.D: Provides immediate pain relief from cramps

explanation: Mifepristone prepares the ground by blocking progesterone, making the follow-up medication (misoprostol) work smoothly. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T008#GNS226_U5_T008_h4)

question: What is the preferred gentle way to clear the uterus in an early pregnancy loss up to 14 weeks?

options.A: Diagnostic laparoscopy
options.B: Manual Vacuum Aspiration
options.C: Cesarean section delivery
options.D: Total abdominal hysterectomy

explanation: Manual Vacuum Aspiration (MVA) is safe, quick, and very effective for early evacuation with fewer complications. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T008#GNS226_U5_T008_h5)

question: What important task must a nurse do right after a surgical uterine evacuation?

options.A: Perform a pelvic exam without gloves
options.B: Discharge the patient home right away
options.C: Administer general anesthesia
options.D: Inspect the removed tissue to confirm everything came out

explanation: Always check the evacuated tissue! It guarantees no tissue was left behind, keeping the patient safe from infection. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T008#GNS226_U5_T008_h5)

question: How soon can a woman start ovulating again after having an abortion?

options.A: After six months
options.B: After three menstrual cycles
options.C: Within two weeks
options.D: After one year

explanation: Fertility can bounce back as early as two weeks! That's why family planning counseling before discharge is super important. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T008#GNS226_U5_T008_h6)

question: Why is Post-Abortion Care (PAC) considered a complete, all-round care model?

options.A: It involves police reports for every single case
options.B: It delays discharge until lab results are ready
options.C: It combines emergency treatment, family planning, and emotional support
options.D: It focuses only on theatre surgeries

explanation: PAC looks at the whole patient—healing her body, supporting her emotions, and helping her plan for the future. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T008#GNS226_U5_T008_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a direct complication of an unsafe or incomplete abortion?

options.A: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.B: Intrauterine adhesions
options.C: Severe pelvic infection
options.D: Heavy hemorrhage

explanation: Gestational diabetes is linked to metabolic changes during an ongoing pregnancy, whereas bleeding, infection, and adhesions follow abortion complications. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T008#GNS226_U5_T008_h7)

question: A patient returns three days after an abortion with fever, lower tummy pain, and a bad-smelling discharge. What does this point to?

options.A: Complete abortion
options.B: Normal recovery phase
options.C: Ectopic pregnancy
options.D: Septic abortion

explanation: Fever, pain, and foul discharge are classic warning signs of a septic abortion needing quick antibiotics. You'll spot these clinical cues easily in the ward! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T008#GNS226_U5_T008_h7)

question: Under Nigerian law, when is an abortion legally allowed?

options.A: To save the life of the pregnant woman
options.B: When the pregnancy is a result of rape
options.C: When there is severe financial hardship
options.D: Whenever the woman requests it

explanation: Nigerian law permits termination only when it is strictly necessary to save the mother's life. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T008#GNS226_U5_T008_h8)

question: What is your main duty as a nurse when a patient comes in with complications from an illegal abortion?

options.A: Report her to security before starting any fluids
options.B: Lecture her on the morality of her actions
options.C: Provide immediate, non-judgmental life-saving emergency care
options.D: Refuse treatment until the police arrive

explanation: As a professional nurse, saving a life always comes first. We treat every patient with care, empathy, and zero judgment. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T008#GNS226_U5_T008_h8)

question: What is the key difference between a spontaneous abortion and an induced abortion?

options.A: Spontaneous abortions happen naturally, while induced abortions are deliberately brought about.
options.B: Induced abortions occur due to chromosomal issues, while spontaneous abortions involve trauma.
options.C: Induced abortions only occur in the first trimester, while spontaneous abortions occur later.
options.D: Spontaneous abortions always require surgery, while induced abortions use only medication.

explanation: You've got this! A spontaneous abortion is a natural loss of pregnancy (often called a miscarriage), whereas an induced abortion is deliberately done using medical or surgical methods. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T009#GNS226_U5_T009_h1)

question: When do immediate complications of an abortion typically show up?

options.A: Between one and two weeks after the event
options.B: During the procedure or within the first 24 hours
options.C: Only after a subsequent pregnancy begins
options.D: Several months to years later

explanation: Think of 'immediate' as happening right away! These complications usually show up while the procedure is going on or within the first 24 hours. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T009#GNS226_U5_T009_h1)

question: What is the most frequent cause of heavy bleeding after an abortion?

options.A: Severe high blood pressure
options.B: An allergic reaction to antibiotics
options.C: Retained products of conception
options.D: A sudden drop in body temperature

explanation: When tiny bits of tissue are left behind in the uterus, the muscle cannot clamp down tight to stop the bleeding. Always suspect retained tissue when heavy bleeding happens! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T009#GNS226_U5_T009_h2)

question: A patient after an abortion has a weak, fast pulse, low blood pressure, and cold skin. What condition is she likely developing?

options.A: Uterine perforation
options.B: Hypovolemic shock
options.C: Postpartum depression
options.D: Pelvic inflammatory disease

explanation: Spotting these vital signs is a core nursing skill! A fast pulse, low BP, and cold skin tell us the body is running low on fluid volume due to heavy bleeding—classic hypovolemic shock. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T009#GNS226_U5_T009_h2)

question: What happens during a uterine perforation?

options.A: An instrument punctures the wall of the uterus.
options.B: The uterine muscle permanently stops contracting.
options.C: Blood clots block the fallopian tubes completely.
options.D: The cervix fails to dilate during surgery.

explanation: Simply put, 'perforation' means a hole. It occurs when a surgical instrument accidentally pokes through the muscular wall of the uterus. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T009#GNS226_U5_T009_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT a sign that a uterine perforation might have happened?

options.A: Sudden relief from all abdominal cramping
options.B: Tenderness across the lower abdomen
options.C: Severe and worsening lower abdominal pain
options.D: Signs of internal bleeding and low blood pressure

explanation: A perforated uterus causes worsening pain and tenderness—not sudden relief! Always watch out for sharp abdominal pain after instrumentation. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T009#GNS226_U5_T009_h3)

question: What is endometritis?

options.A: A blood clot inside the deep veins of the leg
options.B: A complete tear in the muscular wall of the bladder
options.C: An allergic reaction to surgical anesthesia
options.D: An infection of the inner lining of the uterus

explanation: Look at the root words: 'endometrio' refers to the inner lining of the uterus, and '-itis' means inflammation or infection. You've got this! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T009#GNS226_U5_T009_h4)

question: Why does leftover tissue inside the uterus sharply increase the risk of infection?

options.A: It lowers the body temperature below normal levels.
options.B: It stops the liver from producing infection-fighting proteins.
options.C: It provides an ideal environment for bacteria to multiply.
options.D: It directly inactivates all circulating white blood cells.

explanation: Bacteria love stagnant, dead tissue mixed with blood! Leftover tissue creates a cozy breeding ground where bacteria can easily multiply and cause infection. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T009#GNS226_U5_T009_h4)

question: What is Asherman's syndrome?

options.A: A chronic bacterial infection of the fallopian tubes
options.B: The formation of scar tissue inside the uterine cavity
options.C: The complete inability of the cervix to ever dilate
options.D: Permanent high blood pressure following heavy bleeding

explanation: Asherman's syndrome happens when scar tissue (adhesions) forms inside the uterus, which can sometimes interfere with future periods or fertility. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T009#GNS226_U5_T009_h5)

question: How can a prior traumatic abortion affect a woman's future pregnancies?

options.A: It permanently prevents the placenta from attaching anywhere in the body.
options.B: It guarantees that all future babies will develop chromosomal disorders.
options.C: It can cause cervical incompetence, increasing the risk of premature birth.
options.D: It stops the mother's body from producing breast milk later.

explanation: If the cervix is injured or stretched too forcefully during a procedure, its muscles may become weak. This weakness (cervical incompetence) makes it harder for the cervix to stay closed during a later pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T009#GNS226_U5_T009_h5)

question: What is the main reason for doing a pelvic ultrasound when post-abortion complications are suspected?

options.A: To determine the patient's exact psychological state
options.B: To check for retained products of conception or free fluid
options.C: To test for specific bacterial strains causing infection
options.D: To measure the patient's exact blood clotting time

explanation: An ultrasound gives doctors a clear 'window' inside to check if any pregnancy tissue was left behind or if fluid leaked where it shouldn't. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T009#GNS226_U5_T009_h6)

question: A patient reports soaking three large sanitary pads in less than an hour after an abortion. What should you as a nurse do first?

options.A: Discharge the patient home with instructions to return in one week.
options.B: Advise the patient to take a hot bath and rest in bed.
options.C: Report the heavy bleeding to the clinician and assess vital signs.
options.D: Tell the patient this is a completely normal post-procedure finding.

explanation: Soaking more than two pads an hour is a red flag for hemorrhage! Your immediate nursing priority is to check her vital signs and notify the doctor right away. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T009#GNS226_U5_T009_h6)

question: What is the primary power source for creating a vacuum during an MVA procedure?

options.A: A wall-mounted hospital vacuum pipeline
options.B: A foot-pumped mechanical pressure valve
options.C: A manually operated hand-held syringe
options.D: A heavy-duty electric suction machine

explanation: An MVA relies entirely on a hand-held syringe that the operator pulls to generate a vacuum, eliminating the need for electricity. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h1)

question: Up to what gestational age is MVA typically performed in the first trimester?

options.A: 28 to 30 weeks
options.B: 12 to 14 weeks
options.C: 4 to 6 weeks
options.D: 20 to 22 weeks

explanation: MVA is designed and validated as a safe and effective procedure for early pregnancy loss and termination up to 12 to 14 weeks of gestation. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT an indication for manual vacuum aspiration?

options.A: Endometrial biopsy for abnormal uterine bleeding
options.B: Management of a full-term normal vaginal delivery
options.C: First-trimester elective termination of pregnancy
options.D: Incomplete miscarriage with retained tissue

explanation: MVA is restricted to first-trimester uterine evacuation and diagnostic sampling, not full-term deliveries. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h2)

question: Why is active pelvic inflammatory disease considered a strong contraindication for immediate MVA?

options.A: It stops the vacuum syringe from creating negative pressure
options.B: It turns the remaining tissue into hard calcified masses
options.C: It makes the uterine muscle completely resistant to dilation
options.D: It can spread infection upward into the pelvic cavity

explanation: Entering an infected uterus with surgical instruments risks pushing bacteria further into the upper reproductive tract, worsening sepsis or pelvic infection. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h2)

question: What is the function of the flexible plastic canulas used in an MVA kit?

options.A: To seal the outside opening of the vagina during suction
options.B: To travel through the cervix and vacuum out uterine tissue
options.C: To measure the exact internal temperature of the uterus
options.D: To pump local anesthetic pain medicine into the cervix

explanation: Canulas are the sterile tubes inserted past the cervix into the uterus to channel the suctioned tissue into the syringe. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h3)

question: What must the nurse check or do immediately before pulling back the syringe plunger to create a vacuum?

options.A: Boil the entire plastic syringe in hot water
options.B: Attach a heavy electrical cord to the back handle
options.C: Ensure the vacuum valves or buttons are closed
options.D: Fill the cylinder completely with sterile water

explanation: If the valves are left open while pulling the plunger, air simply enters the syringe from the outside and no vacuum is created. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h3)

question: Why is it important for a patient to empty her bladder right before an MVA procedure?

options.A: To stop the kidneys from producing urine for the next several hours
options.B: To prevent accidental urine contamination of the surgical field
options.C: To test kidney function before giving any local anesthetic drugs
options.D: To make the pelvic exam and uterine positioning easier and less painful

explanation: A full bladder displaces the uterus, makes bimanual palpation difficult, and increases patient discomfort during speculum and instrument insertion. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h4)

question: A patient scheduled for MVA is visibly shaking and expresses fear of severe pain. What is the most appropriate initial nursing action?

options.A: Sit close, explain the steps calmly, and offer emotional reassurance
options.B: Cancel the procedure immediately and reschedule for another day
options.C: Tell her that pain is minor and she should try to stay strong
options.D: Administer a strong general anesthetic drug without a doctor's order

explanation: Anxious patients benefit greatly from calm explanations, validation of their feelings, and reassurance, which helps reduce physical tension and perceived pain. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h4)

question: What clinical sign typically tells the clinician that the uterine cavity is successfully emptied during MVA?

options.A: The syringe plunger automatically pushes itself back
options.B: The patient falls into a deep sleep
options.C: Fluid turns completely clear without any blood bubbles
options.D: Bright red foam appears and a gritty feeling is sensed

explanation: When tissue is cleared, the canula comes into contact with the empty uterine wall, producing a characteristic gritty sound or feel along with red foam in the tubing. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h5)

question: What is the purpose of performing a bimanual examination right before an MVA starts?

options.A: To determine the exact size and position of the uterus
options.B: To scrape away loose tissue without needing a canula
options.C: To check if the patient's bladder is completely empty
options.D: To measure the patient's blood pressure and pulse rate

explanation: Knowing whether the uterus is tilted forward or backward helps the clinician guide instruments smoothly and prevents accidental perforation. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h5)

question: How often should vital signs be monitored immediately after an MVA procedure during the first hour?

options.A: Only if the patient complains of dizziness
options.B: Every hour on the hour
options.C: Every 5 minutes
options.D: Every 15 minutes

explanation: Frequent checks every 15 minutes during the first hour help catch early signs of hemorrhage or vasovagal shock. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h6)

question: Which instruction should a nurse give a patient regarding pelvic rest after an MVA?

options.A: Avoid eating solid food for at least 48 hours post-procedure
options.B: Keep taking vaginal douches daily to clean out old blood
options.C: Exercise strenuously starting the very next morning
options.D: Avoid sexual intercourse and tampons for about two weeks

explanation: To prevent bacteria from entering the healing cervix and causing an infection, patients are advised against putting anything in the vagina for two weeks. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h6)

question: What is the primary cause of a vasovagal reaction during cervical manipulation or MVA?

options.A: An acute drop in the patient's body temperature
options.B: Complete blockage of the airway by mucus
options.C: Sudden stimulation of nerves around the cervix
options.D: A severe allergic reaction to the plastic syringe

explanation: Stretching or manipulating the cervix triggers nerve responses that can lower the heart rate and blood pressure, causing fainting or dizziness. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h7)

question: A patient recovering from an MVA suddenly complains of dizziness, looks pale, and her pulse drops. What is the nurse's best immediate action?

options.A: Elevate the patient's legs and monitor vital signs
options.B: Take her to the operating room for an emergency laparotomy
options.C: Administer a strong dose of oral antibiotics
options.D: Tell her to stand up and walk around to improve circulation

explanation: Elevating the legs helps blood return to the brain during a vasovagal episode, quickly relieving dizziness and fainting symptoms. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h7)

question: What is the very first step required for MVA instruments immediately after a procedure is finished?

options.A: Placing them into a decontamination solution
options.B: Wrapping them tightly in sterile cloth drapes
options.C: Storing them directly in a warm drying cabinet
options.D: Scrubbing them with dry steel wool pads

explanation: Decontaminating instruments right after use inactivates infectious agents and prevents blood from drying on the plastic surfaces. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h8)

question: Why is it important to inspect MVA plastic syringes and canulas closely before sterilization?

options.A: To ensure the plastic has changed color indicating expiration
options.B: To check for cracks, scratches, or wear that could harbor bacteria
options.C: To verify the manufacturing country and brand name
options.D: To measure how much weight the plastic can hold under pressure

explanation: Damaged or cracked plastic instruments cannot maintain a proper vacuum and can trap microorganisms, leading to infection risks. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h8)

question: What is the main job of mifepristone during a medical abortion?

options.A: Stimulating strong uterine contractions
options.B: Inducing systemic maternal hypertension
options.C: Blocking progesterone receptors to detach the sac
options.D: Paralyzing the musculature of the cervix

explanation: You've got this! Mifepristone blocks progesterone, the hormone needed to maintain pregnancy. This causes the uterine lining to soften and detaches the sac, preparing the way for the next step. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T011#GNS226_U5_T011_h1)

question: Why is misoprostol taken after mifepristone instead of taking it first?

options.A: It softens the cervix before the mifepristone is absorbed.
options.B: It triggers contractions to expel tissue loosened by the first drug.
options.C: It prevents heavy bleeding from starting too early.
options.D: It neutralizes the extreme toxicity of the first drug.

explanation: Great thinking! Mifepristone loosens the pregnancy tissue first, so when misoprostol comes in to cause uterine contractions, it can easily push the tissue out. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T011#GNS226_U5_T011_h1)

question: Up to how many weeks of pregnancy can a standard medical abortion safely be done?

options.A: Up to 20 to 22 weeks
options.B: Anytime during the first trimester only
options.C: Up to 10 to 11 weeks
options.D: Strictly within the first 4 weeks

explanation: Spot on! Medical abortion is most effective and safest when used within the first 10 to 11 weeks of pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T011#GNS226_U5_T011_h2)

question: A patient requesting a medical abortion is found to have an IUD in place. What needs to happen first?

options.A: The patient must be switched immediately to a surgical procedure.
options.B: The medications can be given safely around the IUD.
options.C: The IUD must be removed before starting the medications.
options.D: Progesterone supplements should be given to offset the IUD.

explanation: Well done! Any existing intrauterine device (IUD) needs to be removed before starting the regimen to lower the risk of severe infection and make sure the medication works properly. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T011#GNS226_U5_T011_h2)

question: Which test is crucial before giving medical abortion drugs to rule out a dangerous condition where the pregnancy implants outside the uterus?

options.A: An electrocardiogram
options.B: An ultrasound to check for ectopic pregnancy
options.C: A routine chest X-ray
options.D: A complete metabolic panel

explanation: You nailed it! An ultrasound is essential to confirm the pregnancy is inside the uterus, ruling out a risky ectopic pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T011#GNS226_U5_T011_h3)

question: Why is it so important to counsel patients on what to expect physically before they take abortion medications at home?

options.A: It reduces the financial cost of the hospital visit.
options.B: It legally waives the clinic from malpractice claims.
