question: Why do modern clinical guidelines prefer Manual Vacuum Aspiration (MVA) over traditional sharp metal curettage?

options.A: MVA is associated with less pain, lower complication rates, and quicker recovery
options.B: Sharp curettage instruments are too expensive for most developing nations
options.C: MVA completely eliminates the need for any pre-procedure pain medication
options.D: Sharp curettage requires general anesthesia in an operating theatre every time

explanation: You nailed it! MVA is gentler on the uterine lining and poses lower risks of perforation compared to sharp metal curettage. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T021#GNS226_U5_T021_h3)

question: Why is early contraceptive counseling crucial immediately following abortion treatment?

options.A: Because hormonal contraceptives immediately cure any underlying uterine infections
options.B: Because ovulation can return as early as two weeks after an abortion
options.C: Because federal law mandates contraceptive use before hospital discharge
options.D: Because patients lose their fertility permanently if they wait one month

explanation: That's right! A woman can get pregnant again very quickly, even before her first normal period returns, making immediate counseling essential. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T021#GNS226_U5_T021_h4)

question: A client requests an IUD right after receiving treatment for an incomplete abortion. What is the best clinical action?

options.A: Prescribe oral contraceptive pills instead because IUDs are never safe post-abortion
options.B: Schedule major abdominal surgery to insert the device under general anesthesia
options.C: Refuse the request and insist she returns after three normal menstrual cycles
options.D: Provide the IUD immediately on the same day if no severe infection is present

explanation: Good job! Many modern methods, including IUDs and implants, can be safely started on the very same day as PAC treatment. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T021#GNS226_U5_T021_h4)

question: What is the main goal of adding psychosocial support to post-abortion care?

options.A: To diagnose underlying psychiatric disorders through formal testing
options.B: To help patients process emotional distress, fear, and stigma
options.C: To convince patients to testify against unsafe abortion providers
options.D: To provide legal representation for women facing criminal charges

explanation: Spot on! Psychosocial support offers a safe, compassionate space to address the emotional trauma or guilt associated with pregnancy loss. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T021#GNS226_U5_T021_h5)

question: How does maintaining strict confidentiality during post-abortion counseling help the patient?

options.A: It builds trust and encourages women to seek timely care without fear of judgment
options.B: It guarantees that the patient will never experience another unplanned pregnancy
options.C: It prevents the hospital administration from billing the patient for services
options.D: It replaces the need for physical medical interventions during an emergency

explanation: Exactly! Because of heavy social stigma, clients fear being judged. Absolute privacy helps them feel safe and cared for. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T021#GNS226_U5_T021_h5)

question: What is a major benefit of involving community health workers in post-abortion care programs?

options.A: They manufacture affordable modern contraceptives locally
options.B: They replace doctors and nurses in urban teaching hospitals
options.C: They help educate the public and guide women to facilities early
options.D: They perform surgical manual vacuum aspirations in rural homes

explanation: You got it! Community workers are vital links who spot danger signs early and direct women to get proper medical help. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T021#GNS226_U5_T021_h6)

question: Why do some women delay seeking medical care for incomplete abortions in local communities?

options.A: Automatic recovery without intervention in nearly all septic cases
options.B: Lack of interest in recovering from physical weakness or bleeding
options.C: Strict government regulations that ban women from leaving their homes
options.D: Fear of social stigma, legal repercussions, and judgment from healthcare workers

explanation: True. Fear of harsh treatment by hospital staff or society stops many women from seeking timely care. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T021#GNS226_U5_T021_h6)

question: What training tool is commonly used to help healthcare providers address personal biases toward abortion patients?

options.A: Mandatory pharmaceutical sales and marketing courses
options.B: Value clarification and attitude transformation workshops
options.C: Strict legal prosecution guidelines for nursing students
options.D: Advanced surgical training in abdominal hysterectomy

explanation: Well done! These workshops help staff examine their own beliefs and separate personal bias from their duty to save lives. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T021#GNS226_U5_T021_h7)

question: How does provider bias negatively affect women seeking post-abortion care?

options.A: It automatically lowers the cost of prescription antibiotics and painkillers
options.B: It causes delays in treatment, poor quality care, and discourages women from seeking help
options.C: It improves the speed at which emergency surgical instruments are sterilized
options.D: It guarantees that the patient receives specialized psychological therapy

explanation: Spot on. When health workers show judgmental attitudes, patients hide information or avoid health facilities, making things worse. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T021#GNS226_U5_T021_h7)

question: What is the main purpose of monitoring and evaluation in post-abortion care programs?

options.A: To restrict patient access to modern contraceptive methods
options.B: To eliminate the need for clinical supervision in rural clinics
options.C: To track service quality, identify gaps, and guide continuous improvement
options.D: To punish nurses who make minor documentation errors in patient charts

explanation: You're doing great! Monitoring collects essential data so managers can improve care delivery and patient safety. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T021#GNS226_U5_T021_h8)

question: A clinic audit reveals low uptake of post-abortion contraception among discharged PAC patients. What is the best quality improvement response for the nursing team?

options.A: Discharge patients immediately without discussing family planning options
options.B: Stop offering all abortion complication treatments until rates improve
options.C: Blame patients for failing to request birth control during their emergency
options.D: Review and strengthen same-day contraceptive counseling and supply availability

explanation: Brilliant! Spotting this gap lets the team fix counseling issues and make sure supplies are ready before discharge. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T021#GNS226_U5_T021_h8)

question: What do we call the everyday living conditions, money, and environments that shape a person's health and life choices?

options.A: Social determinants of health
options.B: Biological risk factors
options.C: Physiological markers
options.D: Genetic predispositions

explanation: Spot on! Social determinants are the external things like money, community, and housing that deeply influence our health decisions every day. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T022#GNS226_U5_T022_h1)

question: Why should nurses care about a patient's social background when talking about reproductive health?

options.A: It ensures the patient will always follow medical advice
options.B: It allows nurses to change national laws regarding healthcare
options.C: It replaces the need for a physical medical examination
options.D: It helps nurses see the real-world barriers affecting patient choices

explanation: You got it! Understanding social factors helps you see the real struggles a patient faces in getting care, making you a more empathetic nurse. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T022#GNS226_U5_T022_h1)

question: What is a major reason why people with very little money sometimes end up with unsafe abortion practices?

options.A: Excessive availability of trained doctors
options.B: Lack of interest in personal health matters
options.C: Abundance of free clinics in rural communities
options.D: Inability to afford safe and legal medical services

explanation: Exactly. When safe care costs too much, financial desperation pushes people toward dangerous alternatives. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T022#GNS226_U5_T022_h2)

question: A patient facing severe financial hardship asks you about family planning. What is her money constraint most likely to affect?

options.A: Her natural immunity against common infections
options.B: Her ability to consistently buy and use modern contraceptives
options.C: Her biological response to hormonal medications
options.D: Her genetic predisposition to chronic illnesses

explanation: That's right! Money worries directly affect purchasing power, making it tough to afford steady supplies of birth control. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T022#GNS226_U5_T022_h2)

question: Why do many women hide complications from an unsafe abortion in communities where it is heavily looked down upon?

options.A: Instructions given routinely by hospital doctors
options.B: Desire to test their own physical endurance
options.C: Fear of public judgment, disgrace, and legal trouble
options.D: Lack of pain receptors in the reproductive organs

explanation: Spot on. Stigma creates a scary wall of silence, making patients hide emergencies out of fear of being shamed or punished. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T022#GNS226_U5_T022_h3)

question: How do strict cultural and religious beliefs usually impact a young woman facing an unintended pregnancy?

options.A: They eliminate the need for any form of healthcare
options.B: They automatically provide financial support for single mothers
options.C: They increase the social pressure to carry the pregnancy to term
options.D: They encourage open dialogue between family members

explanation: Correct! Society's strict expectations can make a woman feel like she has zero room to choose otherwise. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T022#GNS226_U5_T022_h3)

question: What does having low reproductive health literacy mean for a young woman?

options.A: She has advanced training in nursing and pharmacology
options.B: She lacks basic understanding of contraception and her own anatomy
options.C: She is immune to common reproductive tract infections
options.D: She can easily navigate complex hospital billing systems

explanation: Great job! Health literacy is just knowing how your body works and how to protect it. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T022#GNS226_U5_T022_h4)

question: Why does a lack of basic education often lead to higher rates of unintended pregnancies?

options.A: It guarantees employment in high-stress urban environments
options.B: It increases the biological fertility rate of every woman
options.C: It physically alters the organs of the reproductive system
options.D: It limits access to accurate information on how to prevent conception

explanation: Exactly! Without proper education, people are left relying on myths instead of solid facts about family planning. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T022#GNS226_U5_T022_h4)

question: Under Nigerian law, when is an abortion legally allowed?

options.A: Whenever requested by the male partner or husband
options.B: Only when necessary to save the life of the pregnant woman
options.C: In all cases involving financial hardship or unemployment
options.D: Whenever the woman decides she is not ready for a child

explanation: Spot on. Nigerian law is quite strict and generally permits termination only if the mother's life is in direct danger. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T022#GNS226_U5_T022_h5)

question: What is a common result of having very restrictive abortion laws in developing countries?

options.A: Better funding and equipment for public maternity hospitals
options.B: Improved cooperation between traditional healers and doctors
options.C: The complete eradication of unintended pregnancies in society
options.D: An increase in dangerous, clandestine procedures performed by unqualified people

explanation: Correct. Making a procedure illegal doesn't stop it; it just drives desperate patients into secret, unsafe places. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T022#GNS226_U5_T022_h5)

question: How do unequal gender roles in a relationship usually affect a woman's reproductive choices?

options.A: She may lack the authority to decide on contraceptive use or family size
options.B: She automatically gains complete control over household finances
options.C: Extended family members lose all interest in her personal life
options.D: Her partner is legally required to consult her on all medical matters

explanation: You got it! In male-dominated settings, women often struggle to make independent choices about birth control. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T022#GNS226_U5_T022_h6)

question: A pregnant patient is abandoned by her partner and threatened with rejection by her family. What is she most at risk for?

options.A: Complete physical immunity to pregnancy-related complications
options.B: Severe psychological distress and seeking unsafe abortion options
options.C: Immediate promotion to a leadership position at her workplace
options.D: Instant access to free government housing and welfare

explanation: Spot on. Total isolation without support can push scared patients to take terrible risks. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T022#GNS226_U5_T022_h6)

question: Which of these is a major barrier to healthcare access in rural Nigerian communities?

options.A: Severe shortage of health facilities and poor road networks
options.B: Instant availability of advanced surgical equipment
options.C: Too many well-trained medical doctors per capita
options.D: Excessive number of specialized tertiary hospitals

explanation: Correct! Bad roads and faraway clinics make getting to a hospital a massive challenge for rural villagers. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T022#GNS226_U5_T022_h7)

question: Why do complication rates from unsafe abortions tend to be higher in villages than in cities?

options.A: Delays in reaching qualified medical help worsen emergency outcomes
options.B: Rural women have better access to sterile surgical instruments
options.C: Traditional healers in villages always use modern antibiotics
options.D: Rural clinics are strictly reserved for reproductive emergencies

explanation: You nailed it. Long travel times mean infections and bleeding go unchecked for too long before reaching a nurse. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T022#GNS226_U5_T022_h7)

question: What is your main duty as a nurse when treating a patient with complications from an unsafe abortion?

options.A: Report the patient to local law enforcement authorities immediately
options.B: Provide immediate, professional, and non-judgmental medical care
options.C: Scold the patient to ensure she never repeats the procedure
options.D: Refuse treatment until a police officer investigates the case

explanation: Wonderful! As a nurse, saving lives and offering compassionate, unbiased care always comes first. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T022#GNS226_U5_T022_h8)

question: Why is it dangerous for a nurse to show judgment or anger toward a patient with abortion complications?

options.A: It legally terminates the nurse's professional employment contract
options.B: It discourages the patient from speaking honestly about what substances were used
options.C: It permanently cures the underlying infection causing the sepsis
options.D: It forces the hospital to close down its emergency department

explanation: Spot on! When patients are afraid of being judged, they hide vital secrets, making it much harder for you to save their lives. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T022#GNS226_U5_T022_h8)

question: Under Nigerian law, what is the main legal ground that allows for a safe and lawful termination of pregnancy?

options.A: When the pregnancy results from consensual sex
options.B: Upon the request of both parents
options.C: To save the life of the pregnant woman
options.D: In cases of severe economic hardship

explanation: You've got this! Nigerian law is very strict, allowing pregnancy termination only when it is necessary to preserve the mother's life. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T023#GNS226_U5_T023_h1)

question: Why do many women in Nigeria still resort to unsafe abortions despite strict laws?

options.A: Abortion being completely free in government hospitals
options.B: Desire to experience traditional surgical practices
options.C: Lack of access to safe services and modern contraceptives
options.D: Legal encouragement from local community leaders

explanation: Spot on! When family planning services and safe care are hard to reach, vulnerable women sadly turn to dangerous alternatives. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T023#GNS226_U5_T023_h1)

question: What is the key sign that an abortion procedure is unsafe?

options.A: Done using standard medical pills prescribed by a doctor
options.B: Conducted inside a registered tertiary hospital facility
options.C: Performed strictly within the first four weeks of gestation
options.D: Performed by untrained persons or in unhygienic environments

explanation: Correct! Unsafe procedures usually happen in dirty places or are done by people without proper medical training. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T023#GNS226_U5_T023_h2)

question: Which of these is a dangerous method often seen in back-alley or clandestine terminations?

options.A: Receiving intravenous fluids at a primary health centre
options.B: Taking oral contraceptive pills prescribed by a pharmacist
options.C: Undergoing ultrasound scanning in a private clinic
options.D: Inserting sharp sticks or knitting needles into the uterus

explanation: Well done. Using crude objects like sticks is extremely dangerous and can easily cause severe bleeding and organ damage. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T023#GNS226_U5_T023_h2)

question: As a nurse, what is your very first priority when a patient arrives with complications from an abortion?

options.A: Filing a formal police report immediately
options.B: Evaluating vital signs for shock and stability
options.C: Asking about her religious and marital status
options.D: Conducting a detailed financial background check

explanation: Safety first! Always check vital signs and stabilize the patient first to prevent life-threatening shock or heavy bleeding. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T023#GNS226_U5_T023_h3)

question: A patient whispers to you in panic that she used a dangerous herbal mix to try and stop her pregnancy. How should you respond?

options.A: Maintain confidentiality, offer reassurance, and assess her physical condition
options.B: Ignore the statement and focus entirely on routine vital sign recording
options.C: Scold her for breaking the law and refuse to treat her until she confesses
options.D: Call security to have her detained for attempting an illegal abortion

explanation: You're building great clinical judgment! Being non-judgmental and keeping patient trust is vital to saving her life in an emergency. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T023#GNS226_U5_T023_h3)

question: Which two drugs are most commonly used together for a medical abortion?

options.A: Oxytocin and ergometrine
options.B: Ampicillin and metronidazole
options.C: Paracetamol and ibuprofen
options.D: Mifepristone and misoprostol

explanation: Great job! Mifepristone pauses the pregnancy, and misoprostol helps the uterus contract and empty safely. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T023#GNS226_U5_T023_h4)

question: Why do doctors often prefer Manual Vacuum Aspiration (MVA) over sharp metal instruments for early pregnancy care?

options.A: It permanently prevents future pregnancies without hormones
options.B: It eliminates the need for any pre-procedure counseling
options.C: It requires general anesthesia in a major operating theatre
options.D: It carries a lower risk of uterine perforation and trauma

explanation: Exactly! MVA uses gentle suction and soft tubes, which is much safer for the delicate walls of the uterus. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T023#GNS226_U5_T023_h4)

question: What are the classic signs that a patient has developed a post-abortion pelvic infection?

options.A: Foul-smelling vaginal discharge and fever
options.B: Clear, watery discharge lasting several days
options.C: Sudden painless swelling of the lower limbs
options.D: High blood pressure and severe throbbing headache

explanation: Spot on! Bad-smelling discharge and fever are major warning signs that bacteria have entered the uterus. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T023#GNS226_U5_T023_h5)

question: A patient post-abortion complains of sudden, sharp belly pain, and her abdomen feels very hard and stiff. What complication should come to mind?

options.A: Post-procedure anxiety
options.B: Mild urinary tract infection
options.C: Normal uterine cramping
options.D: Uterine perforation

explanation: You've got it! A rigid, painful belly is a red flag that the uterine wall may have been accidentally punctured. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T023#GNS226_U5_T023_h5)

question: Why is it so important to talk about family planning before discharging a post-abortion care patient?

options.A: Contraceptives cure existing pelvic infections
options.B: Hospital policy mandates permanent sterilization
options.C: It prevents the onset of menopausal symptoms
options.D: Fertility can return very quickly after a termination

explanation: Brilliant! Ovulation can start as early as two weeks after an abortion, so counseling helps prevent unplanned repeat pregnancies. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T023#GNS226_U5_T023_h6)

question: What does truly comprehensive Post-Abortion Care (PAC) involve beyond treating medical emergencies?

options.A: Restricting her fluid intake to monitor kidney output
options.B: Providing emotional support and linking her to family planning services
options.C: Reporting her to local law enforcement authorities
options.D: Discharging the patient immediately without speaking to her

explanation: Spot on! PAC isn't just about patching up physical injuries; it's caring for her mental well-being and future reproductive health too. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T023#GNS226_U5_T023_h6)

question: What is the best way for a nurse to handle common myths and rumors about modern birth control?

options.A: Telling clients to rely solely on traditional calendar methods
options.B: Agreeing that contraceptives cause permanent internal damage
options.C: Providing accurate, evidence-based education tailored to the client
options.D: Withholding information about long-acting reversible methods

explanation: Great nursing insight! Patient education clears up fear and empowers clients to make healthy choices. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T023#GNS226_U5_T023_h7)

question: A young patient is worried that getting a contraceptive implant will make her permanently barren. How should you reassure her?

options.A: Confirm her fear and advise her to avoid all modern methods
options.B: Suggest she use ineffective traditional herbs instead
options.C: Ignore her concern and insert the device without discussion
options.D: Explain that fertility returns quickly once the implant is removed

explanation: You nailed it! Explaining that these methods are fully reversible helps calm her fears and builds strong trust. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T023#GNS226_U5_T023_h7)

question: What is the main goal of post-abortion care (PAC)?

options.A: To investigate the legal cause of pregnancy termination
options.B: To treat complications from spontaneous or induced abortions
options.C: To perform mandatory psychological evaluations
options.D: To provide routine family planning counseling only

explanation: PAC is all about emergency medical support! It focuses on treating physical issues like heavy bleeding or infections so the patient can recover safely. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T024#GNS226_U5_T024_h1)

question: Why is a warm, professional attitude especially important when caring for post-abortion patients?

options.A: It speeds up the physical healing of uterine tissues
options.B: Nigerian law mandates specific bedside manners for maternity staff
options.C: Hospital management requires strict adherence to uniform dress codes
options.D: Patients are often vulnerable and fear judgment from healthcare staff

explanation: Because of societal stigma, these patients are often scared of being judged. A welcoming attitude helps them feel safe enough to get the help they need. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T024#GNS226_U5_T024_h1)

question: What is a major danger of the social stigma surrounding abortion in healthcare?

options.A: Clients may delay seeking life-saving medical care out of fear
options.B: Hospital pharmacies automatically run out of emergency drugs
options.C: Infection rates drop because patients use home remedies first
options.D: Doctors are legally required to discharge patients within hours

explanation: Fear of harsh words or mistreatment often makes women wait too long to come to the hospital, which sadly makes their physical complications much worse. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T024#GNS226_U5_T024_h2)

question: How might personal or religious stigma poorly show up in a nurse during PAC care?

options.A: Prescribing higher doses of antibiotics to punish the patient
options.B: Mandating public community service for every PAC client
options.C: Displaying coldness, disapproval, or open hostility toward the client
options.D: Refusing to document the patient's vital signs on the chart

explanation: Sometimes nurses let personal beliefs slip out through cold sighs, dirty looks, or harsh remarks, which really hurts a vulnerable patient. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T024#GNS226_U5_T024_h2)

question: What does 'unconditional acceptance' mean when practicing non-judgmental nursing?

options.A: Treating the patient as a human in need of help without moralizing
options.B: Allowing family members to perform nursing duties at the bedside
options.C: Waiving all hospital bills for emergency surgical procedures
options.D: Agreeing with every personal life choice the patient has ever made

explanation: It means leaving your personal opinions at the door. Your only job is to care for the sick human being sitting in front of you. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T024#GNS226_U5_T024_h3)

question: A nurse sighs loudly and makes a rude comment while cleaning up a PAC patient. Which nursing rule was broken?

options.A: Objective, non-judgmental communication
options.B: Aseptic surgical technique
options.C: Accurate medication dosage calculation
options.D: Emergency triage prioritization

explanation: Making disapproving remarks or sighs shames the patient and completely breaks the rule of giving non-judgmental, professional care. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T024#GNS226_U5_T024_h3)

question: What is the legal status of treating medical complications from an abortion in Nigeria?

options.A: It is strictly forbidden unless authorized by a high court judge
options.B: It is a legal and medically necessary life-saving intervention
options.C: It is classified as an elective cosmetic procedure
options.D: It is only permitted in federal tertiary teaching hospitals

explanation: Saving a patient's life by treating emergency complications is always legal and always the top priority in healthcare. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T024#GNS226_U5_T024_h4)

question: Why might a nurse mistakenly refuse or delay PAC care due to legal fears?

options.A: Absence of any regulatory guidelines from the Nursing Council
options.B: Confusion between performing an abortion and treating its emergency complications
options.C: Strict hospital policies requiring police clearance for all emergency admissions
options.D: Lack of basic nursing equipment in rural health clinics

explanation: Some providers get scared, mistakenly thinking that treating post-abortion complications makes them an accomplice to an illegal act. Remember: treating complications is saving a life! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T024#GNS226_U5_T024_h4)

question: What is the best way to protect a PAC patient's privacy in a busy ward?

options.A: Transferring the client to an administrative office
options.B: Asking family members to step outside during visiting hours only
options.C: Placing a warning sign on the door of the main ward
options.D: Drawing bedside curtains and speaking in low, quiet tones

explanation: Simple steps like pulling the curtains tight and keeping your voice down stop nosey neighbors from hearing private health details. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T024#GNS226_U5_T024_h5)

question: Why is keeping PAC patient information strictly confidential so important?

options.A: A breach of information can lead to severe social stigma or harm
options.B: The Nursing Council requires permanent archiving of all case notes
options.C: It prevents insurance companies from raising premium rates
options.D: Hospital accreditation depends entirely on zero medical errors

explanation: Because abortion carries heavy social stigma around us, a leaked secret can ruin relationships, jobs, or even put a patient's safety at risk. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T024#GNS226_U5_T024_h5)

question: Which type of questioning helps an anxious PAC patient share their story comfortably?

options.A: Closed yes-or-no prompts
options.B: Open-ended questions
options.C: Leading legal inquiries
options.D: Rapid fire interrogation

explanation: Asking questions like 'How have you been feeling since yesterday?' lets patients talk in their own words without feeling cornered. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T024#GNS226_U5_T024_h6)

question: Which body language shows a supportive and comforting style to a nervous patient?

options.A: Standing over the bed to show clinical dominance
options.B: Staring intently at the medical chart while the patient speaks
options.C: Crossing arms firmly across the chest to establish authority
options.D: Maintaining a calm tone and open, welcoming body language

explanation: A gentle voice and open posture tell the patient 'I am here for you, and you are safe with me.' [learn more](GNS226_U5_T024#GNS226_U5_T024_h6)

question: What is the term for emotional exhaustion and numbness that nurses feel after dealing with too much trauma?

options.A: Compassion fatigue
options.B: Post-surgical shock
options.C: Florence Nightingale syndrome
options.D: Professional burnout syndrome

explanation: Compassion fatigue happens when seeing heavy, stressful cases day after day drains your emotional tank. It is totally normal to feel this way, which is why self-care matters! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T024#GNS226_U5_T024_h7)

question: How can a nurse best handle personal biases when caring for a stigmatized patient?

options.A: Reading legal textbooks to punish patients who break social norms
options.B: Asking another nurse to handle all female reproductive health cases
options.C: Practicing active self-reflection and discussing feelings with supportive peers
options.D: Suppressing all emotions until the end of the calendar year

explanation: Talking things through with supportive colleagues and checking your own mindset helps you catch hidden biases before they affect your patient care. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T024#GNS226_U5_T024_h7)

question: Besides physical treatment, what else is an essential part of holistic post-abortion care?

options.A: Mandatory reporting of the client to local religious leaders
options.B: Empathetic emotional support and contraceptive counseling
options.C: Permanent hospital admission for psychological observation
options.D: Informing the client's family members about the medical history

explanation: Good nursing looks at the whole person! Along with healing the body, we offer kind emotional support and teach them about family planning for the future. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T024#GNS226_U5_T024_h8)

question: A PAC patient is stable and ready to go home. What is the best next step for the nurse?

options.A: Provide compassionate contraceptive counseling and discharge instructions
options.B: Withhold discharge until a family elder arrives to sign papers
options.C: Scold the patient so she does not experience complications again
options.D: Prescribe heavy sedatives to prevent emotional processing

explanation: Before they leave, always give clear discharge notes and friendly, non-judgmental advice on how to prevent another unplanned pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T024#GNS226_U5_T024_h8)

question: What is the main goal of post-abortion care (PAC) in the ward?

options.A: To investigate the legal circumstances surrounding the pregnancy
options.B: To conduct routine cervical cancer screening procedures
options.C: To provide permanent family planning counseling for all women
options.D: To treat incomplete or unsafe abortions and manage complications

explanation: PAC is an emergency service to help women safely recover from incomplete or unsafe abortions. You've got this! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T025#GNS226_U5_T025_h1)

question: Why is being kind and compassionate so important when caring for a PAC patient?

options.A: It prevents the physical pain caused by uterine contractions
options.B: It shortens the standard hospital stay to less than two hours
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for any antibiotic therapy
options.D: It reduces anxiety and encourages honest disclosure of medical history

explanation: When patients feel safe and free from judgment, they are much more likely to share true details that help us care for them better. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T025#GNS226_U5_T025_h1)

question: Which ethical rule reminds nurses to make sure their actions cause no extra harm to a vulnerable patient?

options.A: Non-maleficence
options.B: Veracity
options.C: Autonomy
options.D: Justice

explanation: Non-maleficence simply means 'do no harm'. As nurses, protecting our patients from extra injury or distress is our core duty. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T025#GNS226_U5_T025_h2)

question: A nurse quietly grumbles about a patient's abortion while making her bed. Which important standard of care is the nurse breaking?

options.A: The legal requirement for mandatory police reporting
options.B: Strict adherence to hospital administrative policies
options.C: Unconditional positive regard and non-maleficence
options.D: The principle of client autonomy over surgical choices

explanation: Showing judgment or disapproval hurts patients emotionally. We are here to support and heal, not to judge! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T025#GNS226_U5_T025_h2)

question: What is a common sign that a PAC patient might be struggling emotionally?

options.A: Asking excessive questions about discharge medications
options.B: Demanding an immediate discharge from the hospital
options.C: Avoiding eye contact and withdrawing from conversation
options.D: Laughing loudly with visiting family members

explanation: When someone is overwhelmed or anxious, they often pull back, stay quiet, and avoid looking you in the eye. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T025#GNS226_U5_T025_h3)

question: Why do social and religious pressures in many Nigerian communities often make emotional recovery harder for a PAC patient?

options.A: They force clients to hide their experiences and suffer in silence
options.B: They require mandatory public announcements of medical records
options.C: They prohibit nurses from administering physical pain relief
options.D: They mandate automatic psychiatric admission for every patient

explanation: Heavy stigma creates fear of being blamed, making many women bottle up their trauma instead of seeking help. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T025#GNS226_U5_T025_h3)

question: What is the best reason to use open-ended questions when talking with a PAC patient?

options.A: They shorten the overall time required for the nursing interview
options.B: They prevent the client from crying during the conversation
options.C: They legally protect the hospital from malpractice lawsuits
options.D: They invite the client to share more detailed information in her own words

explanation: Open-ended questions (like 'How are you feeling today?') let patients express themselves freely instead of just saying yes or no. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T025#GNS226_U5_T025_h4)

question: A nurse sits at the patient's eye level, listens softly, and repeats back key points the patient shared. What is the nurse showing?

options.A: Passive observation and clinical delegation
options.B: Routine administrative record keeping
options.C: Aggressive interrogation and data gathering
options.D: Active listening and therapeutic communication

explanation: These simple bedside actions make a patient feel truly heard, respected, and safe with you. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T025#GNS226_U5_T025_h4)

question: Why is keeping patient information strictly confidential especially vital in post-abortion care?

options.A: It prevents the need for any documentation in the official hospital chart
options.B: Clients fear societal stigma, gossip, and exposure of their medical history
options.C: It is only necessary if the client is a minor under eighteen years old
options.D: Hospital management requires all records to be burned after discharge

explanation: Because abortion carries harsh social judgments in many places, patients need to trust us completely to keep their business private. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T025#GNS226_U5_T025_h5)

question: Which nursing action helps build instant trust with a newly admitted PAC patient?

options.A: Reviewing the client's chart at the nursing station before entering
options.B: Asking the client to sign financial clearance forms immediately
options.C: Instructing visitors to leave the ward before nursing assessment begins
options.D: Explaining every clinical procedure clearly before touching the client

explanation: Telling her what you are about to do shows deep respect for her body and eases the fear of feeling helpless in the hospital. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T025#GNS226_U5_T025_h5)

question: What is a vital legal and clinical truth Nigerian nurses must know about post-abortion care?

options.A: Treating complications from an abortion is a legal, life-saving medical service
options.B: Nurses are legally required to report every PAC client to the police
options.C: Only medical doctors are legally permitted to provide post-abortion counseling
options.D: Emergency post-abortion treatment is prohibited by the national health act

explanation: Even with strict abortion laws, giving emergency medical care to save a woman from an incomplete or septic abortion is completely legal and necessary. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T025#GNS226_U5_T025_h6)

question: How should a nurse handle personal religious beliefs when faced with an emergency PAC case?

options.A: By prioritizing the immediate life-saving care and treating the client without judgment
options.B: By transferring the patient to another facility without stabilization
options.C: By lecturing the client on morality before administering intravenous fluids
options.D: By refusing to touch the patient until a religious leader speaks with her

explanation: In an emergency, saving a patient's life and providing compassionate nursing care always comes before personal opinions. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T025#GNS226_U5_T025_h6)

question: Which of these is a quiet sign that a nurse might be showing bias against a PAC patient?

options.A: Providing written educational pamphlets on nutrition
options.B: Unnecessarily delaying care or withholding proper pain relief
options.C: Checking vital signs every fifteen minutes as ordered
options.D: Offering a clean hospital gown and warm blanket

explanation: Sometimes bias shows up as poor treatment—like making a patient wait too long or skipping proper pain meds because of personal judgment. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T025#GNS226_U5_T025_h7)

question: Why is regular self-reflection important for nurses working in post-abortion care?

options.A: It guarantees promotion to senior nursing administrative positions
options.B: It replaces the need for formal clinical pharmacology training
options.C: It helps nurses recognize their personal biases and prevent them from affecting care
options.D: It ensures the nurse never experiences physical fatigue on duty

explanation: Checking in with our own feelings helps us separate personal beliefs from professional duty, keeping our care fair and respectful. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T025#GNS226_U5_T025_h7)

question: What must you always check before involving a partner or family member in a PAC patient's care plan?

options.A: The explicit consent and permission of the client
options.B: Mandatory attendance at a community health seminar
options.C: A written approval letter from the hospital administrator
options.D: Proof of legal marriage verified by hospital registration

explanation: The patient's privacy is paramount. You can never bring family or partners into her care without her clear go-ahead. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T025#GNS226_U5_T025_h8)

question: A patient says she does not want her partner to visit because she is scared of his reaction. What should you do?

options.A: Insist that family presence is mandatory for hospital discharge clearance
options.B: Call the partner immediately to inform him of her hospital admission
options.C: Respect her wishes, maintain confidentiality, and protect her from visitors
options.D: Ask the hospital security team to convince the client to change her mind

explanation: As a nurse, your primary loyalty is to protect your patient's safety and honor her personal boundaries. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T025#GNS226_U5_T025_h8)

question: How soon can a woman's fertility return after an abortion or pregnancy loss?

options.A: As early as two weeks
options.B: Only after regular menses resume for a full year
options.C: Fertility does not return until age forty
options.D: After exactly six months

explanation: Ovulation can bounce back very quickly, meaning a woman can get pregnant again even before her next period starts. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T025#GNS226_U5_T025_h9)

question: What is the right approach when counseling a PAC patient on family planning and contraception?

options.A: Withholding contraceptive information to encourage abstinence
options.B: Ensuring the advice is non-coercive and respects her personal choices
options.C: Choosing the most expensive birth control method for her automatically
options.D: Insisting that she accepts permanent sterilization before leaving

explanation: Contraceptive counseling should empower her with choices, never force or pressure her into a method she doesn't want. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T025#GNS226_U5_T025_h9)

question: What makes an abortion officially classified as 'unsafe' by global health standards?

options.A: Any pregnancy loss occurring naturally during the first trimester
options.B: A procedure done by unskilled persons or in poor environments
options.C: A termination done without proper surgical instruments
options.D: A medical termination performed past the first trimester

explanation: An unsafe abortion happens when the procedure is carried out by people without proper training, in dirty or poorly equipped places, or both. Knowing this helps us understand why access to safe care is so vital! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h1)

question: Why do many young women and teenagers in Nigeria end up turning to unsafe abortion methods?

options.A: Preference for traditional herbal remedies over modern medicine
options.B: Easy availability of safe surgical clinics in rural areas
options.C: Lack of financial resources and reproductive health access
options.D: Strict enforcement of mandatory hospital reporting laws

explanation: Poverty, fear of social stigma, and struggling to find safe, legal services often push vulnerable girls into dangerous alternatives. As nurses, keeping our clinics open and welcoming is key to changing this. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h1)

question: In most parts of Nigeria, under what single major condition is an abortion legally permitted?

options.A: When both parents agree in writing before the first trimester
options.B: When the woman is below the age of consent
options.C: When the pregnancy results from an act of sexual assault
options.D: When the procedure is strictly necessary to save the woman's life

explanation: Nigerian law is quite strict, usually only allowing an abortion if the continuation of the pregnancy directly threatens the mother's life. It's an important legal boundary every nurse practicing here should know. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h2)

question: How does the strict criminalization of abortion in Nigeria directly affect patient health outcomes?

options.A: It encourages traditional healers to adopt modern sterile surgical techniques
options.B: It guarantees that all post-abortion patients receive free government care
options.C: It forces patients to seek secretive care, leading to dangerous treatment delays
options.D: It completely eliminates the practice of illegal pregnancy terminations

explanation: Because of fear of arrest, women often hide what they've done and only come to the hospital when complications become life-threatening. Compassionate, confidential nursing care can help break down this fear! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h2)

question: Which immediate complication happens when an instrument accidentally punctures the muscular wall of the uterus during a procedure?

options.A: Secondary amenorrhea
options.B: Cervical incompetence
options.C: Gestational trophoblastic disease
options.D: Uterine perforation

explanation: Uterine perforation occurs when sharp instruments or foreign objects poke a hole right through the wall of the uterus. It's a surgical emergency you'll want to watch out for during recovery! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h3)

question: A patient arrives at the emergency ward with a high fever, foul-smelling vaginal discharge, and tummy pain after a clandestine abortion. What is your top nursing priority?

options.A: Immediate scheduling for cosmetic scar revision
options.B: Documenting the identity of the illegal practitioner
options.C: Counseling on future contraceptive methods
options.D: Systemic sepsis and infection management

explanation: Fever and foul discharge are classic red flags for a severe infection or sepsis. Stabilizing the patient and starting broad-spectrum antibiotics comes before anything else! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h3)

question: What is a very common long-term problem for women who survive an untreated pelvic infection after an unsafe abortion?

options.A: Premature menopause
options.B: Chronic hypertension
options.C: Gestational diabetes
options.D: Secondary infertility

explanation: Severe pelvic infections can leave behind scar tissue that blocks the fallopian tubes, making it very difficult for the woman to get pregnant in the future. Early infection treatment is a lifesaver for fertility! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h4)

question: A patient who previously had a secretive abortion now struggles with recurrent miscarriages in her second trimester. What underlying issue should you suspect?

options.A: Primary ovarian failure due to hormonal imbalances
options.B: Chronic renal failure from past chemical toxicity
options.C: Acquired uterine fibroids from retained tissue
options.D: Cervical incompetence from past traumatic dilation

explanation: If the cervix was forced open too aggressively during a past procedure, the tissues can become weak, causing it to open prematurely in later pregnancies. You'll learn to spot this history during antenatal booking! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h4)

question: What factor makes the emotional and mental distress much worse for patients recovering from an unsafe abortion in Nigeria?

options.A: Social stigma and fear of legal consequences
options.B: Excessive availability of professional counselors
options.C: Mandatory psychological screening in government hospitals
options.D: Immediate support from community religious leaders

explanation: Fear of being arrested, judged, or rejected by loved ones forces many women to hide their pain and suffer all alone. As nurses, being a safe, listening ear makes all the difference. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h5)

question: Why is it so important for nurses to check in on a patient's mental health during post-abortion care?

options.A: Patients with mental distress are legally barred from receiving contraceptives
options.B: Psychological symptoms interfere directly with the absorption of oral antibiotics
options.C: Hospital insurance policies refuse to pay claims without a mental health diagnosis
options.D: Physical healing alone does not address hidden trauma, anxiety, and depression

explanation: Treating the physical body is only half the job. The secrecy and stress surrounding unsafe abortions leave deep emotional wounds that also need healing and gentle support. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h5)

question: When a patient is suspected of having an unsafe abortion, what should be the primary goal of your first nursing assessment?

options.A: Identifying life-threatening complications and vital sign instability
options.B: Reporting the patient's family members to hospital authorities
options.C: Collecting evidence for police investigation and legal prosecution
options.D: Determining the exact herbal concoction ingested by the patient

explanation: In an emergency, airway, breathing, circulation, and watching for heavy bleeding or sepsis always come first. A nurse's duty is to save the patient's life, not play detective! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h6)

question: Why must you always maintain a non-judgmental and confidential attitude when taking a patient's history?

options.A: To prevent the patient from requesting discharge against medical advice
options.B: To comply with international nursing board regulations on patient billing
options.C: To encourage honest disclosure of the abortion method and ensure prompt treatment
options.D: To help the hospital avoid paying malpractice insurance premiums

explanation: If patients think you will judge or report them, they will lie or hide what happened—and that can cost them their lives. Trust and confidentiality save lives in the ward! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h6)

question: What are the three core components of the standard Post-Abortion Care (PAC) model?

options.A: Surgical sterilization, mandatory psychiatric evaluation, and legal reporting
options.B: Emergency treatment, family planning counseling, and reproductive health linkage
options.C: Antenatal booking, nutritional rehabilitation, and infant immunization
options.D: Blood transfusion, long-term hospitalization, and vocational training

explanation: PAC is a complete package: treat the immediate emergency, talk about family planning so it doesn't happen again, and connect the patient to ongoing health care. You'll see this model everywhere in public health! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h7)

question: A patient with an incomplete abortion has stable vital signs and no signs of severe infection. Which procedure is best for clearing her uterus?

options.A: Immediate total abdominal hysterectomy
options.B: Exploratory laparotomy with bowel resection
options.C: Intravenous broad-spectrum chemotherapy
options.D: Manual vacuum aspiration (MVA)

explanation: Manual vacuum aspiration (MVA) is a quick, safe, and gentle method to clear out the remaining tissue in uncomplicated cases without needing heavy surgery. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h7)

question: What is the most effective way for nurses to help prevent unsafe abortions in the community?

options.A: Providing accessible family planning education and modern contraception
options.B: Reporting all suspected cases of premarital sex to local community elders
options.C: Enforcing strict hospital visitation limits for young unmarried females
options.D: Promoting traditional herbal remedies as safe alternatives for fertility control

explanation: The best cure is prevention! When young people have easy access to modern family planning and accurate education, the rate of unintended pregnancies—and unsafe abortions—drops dramatically. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h8)

question: What is the main purpose of setting up youth-friendly reproductive health clinics in local communities?

options.A: To offer young people a safe, non-judgmental space to access contraception and information
options.B: To track and penalize adolescents who engage in early sexual activity
options.C: To distribute free surgical instruments for home use
options.D: To provide mandatory pregnancy testing for all high school graduates

explanation: Youth-friendly clinics take away the fear of judgment and stigma, making it easy for teenagers to ask questions and get reliable health guidance early on. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h8)

question: Why did people in early history practice family planning?

options.A: To increase the speed of urban industrial growth
options.B: To comply with modern hospital guidelines
options.C: To eliminate the need for traditional birth attendants
options.D: To manage family size and resource allocation

explanation: Even long ago, communities needed to make sure they had enough food and resources for everyone, so they practiced family planning to manage family size. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T001#GNS226_U6_T001_h1)

question: How does spacing children properly help a mother's health?

options.A: It guarantees an easier delivery without any pain management
options.B: It lowers the risks of pregnancy complications and maternal death
options.C: It speeds up the physical aging process of reproductive organs
options.D: It permanently eliminates all future risks of chronic illness

explanation: Giving the body enough time to recover between pregnancies helps prevent severe exhaustion and bleeding, keeping mums safe and healthy! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T001#GNS226_U6_T001_h1)

question: What did ancient Egyptians mix into vaginal pastes to block sperm?

options.A: Purified petroleum jelly
options.B: Boiled palm oil extracts
options.C: Liquid synthetic hormones
options.D: Crocodile dung and honey

explanation: History is wild! Ancient Egyptian records show they used sticky mixes like honey and crocodile dung as early barriers to block sperm. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T001#GNS226_U6_T001_h2)

question: What was the main problem with most ancient birth control methods?

options.A: They were too expensive for ordinary citizens to purchase
options.B: They were frequently toxic, unreliable, or completely ineffective
options.C: They required advanced surgical equipment available only to royalty
options.D: They relied on electronic monitoring of the menstrual cycle

explanation: Ancient remedies relied a lot on guesswork and folk traditions, which often meant they didn't work well and could even be unsafe. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T001#GNS226_U6_T001_h2)

question: Who opened the first birth control clinic in the United States in 1916?

options.A: Florence Nightingale
options.B: Clara Barton
options.C: Mary Seacole
options.D: Margaret Sanger

explanation: Margaret Sanger was a key pioneer who fought legal battles to open the first birth control clinic. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T001#GNS226_U6_T001_h3)

question: Why did early birth control activists get into trouble with the law?

options.A: Laws classified reproductive health information as obscene and illegal
options.B: Governments wanted to encourage higher infant mortality rates
options.C: Medical boards wanted to protect traditional herbal remedies
options.D: Pharmacists feared losing money on prescription medications

explanation: Back then, strict laws (like the Comstock Act in the US) banned sharing reproductive health info, even sending it through the mail! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T001#GNS226_U6_T001_h3)

question: In which decade was the oral contraceptive pill approved and introduced?

options.A: The 1960s
options.B: The 1930s
options.C: The 1910s
options.D: The 1980s

explanation: The 1960s was a huge decade for reproductive health because that's when the birth control pill finally became widely available. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T001#GNS226_U6_T001_h4)

question: Which big medical breakthrough gave women independent control over their fertility without needing barrier devices?

options.A: Traditional withdrawal methods
options.B: Herbal vaginal douches
options.C: Acacia and honey pastes
options.D: The oral contraceptive pill

explanation: The pill was a game-changer! It let women manage their fertility discreetly and on their own terms using a daily medication. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T001#GNS226_U6_T001_h4)

question: How did Nigerian mothers traditionally space their children before modern contraceptives arrived?

options.A: Daily ingestion of synthetic hormone pills
options.B: Intrauterine copper device insertion
options.C: Surgical tubal ligation procedures
options.D: Prolonged breastfeeding and postpartum abstinence

explanation: Traditional Nigerian societies used natural, reliable spacing methods like extended breastfeeding and resting from sex after childbirth. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T001#GNS226_U6_T001_h5)

question: Why were some people initially hesitant about modern family planning programs in Nigeria?

options.A: A total lack of trained nurses in every region of the country
options.B: Strict government bans on building hospitals and clinics
options.C: Cultural norms, religious beliefs, and mistrust of population policies
options.D: The complete absence of traditional birth spacing methods

explanation: Because these programs were newly introduced, many communities viewed them with suspicion, worrying about foreign population control motives. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T001#GNS226_U6_T001_h5)

question: How have many religious views on family planning changed over time?

options.A: Moving toward an emphasis on responsible parenthood and maternal health
options.B: Eliminating the discussion of reproductive health in communities
options.C: Banning all forms of medical care for pregnant women
options.D: Mandating artificial contraception for all married couples

explanation: Many religious groups now embrace family planning when it's used to protect the mother's health and care responsibly for children. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T001#GNS226_U6_T001_h6)

question: A patient is worried about using modern contraceptives because of her religion. As a nurse, what is the best way to respond?

options.A: Provide respectful, non-judgmental counseling that acknowledges her values
options.B: Report her concerns to the hospital administration immediately
options.C: Tell her that her religious beliefs are outdated and incorrect
options.D: Refuse to discuss any options other than surgical sterilization

explanation: Always meet patients where they are! Good nurses respect personal values and give compassionate, supportive guidance without judgment. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T001#GNS226_U6_T001_h6)

question: What is a major focus of modern family planning nursing?

options.A: Eliminating all forms of natural birth spacing methods
options.B: Providing equitable, community-based reproductive health education and care
options.C: Enforcing strict population limits on every family
options.D: Restricting contraceptive access exclusively to urban hospitals

explanation: Modern nursing is all about community outreach—making sure everyone can easily get reproductive health education and services. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T001#GNS226_U6_T001_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT something a modern family planning nurse should do?

options.A: Reaching out to adolescents with friendly reproductive education
options.B: Promoting personalized contraceptive choices for patients
options.C: Forcing universal sterilization on rural communities
options.D: Expanding access to long-acting reversible contraceptives

explanation: Forced procedures go totally against human rights and good nursing. Care should always be voluntary and centered on what the patient wants! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T001#GNS226_U6_T001_h7)

question: What is the primary maternal health benefit of properly spacing pregnancies?

options.A: Permanently stopping all future menstrual cycles
options.B: Eliminating the need for any antenatal care visits
options.C: Giving the mother's body time to recover physically
options.D: Ensuring the mother gives birth only to male children

explanation: Proper spacing allows a woman's body to restore vital nutrients like iron and heal from the physical stress of a previous pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T002#GNS226_U6_T002_h1)

question: A woman who gets pregnant less than six months after her previous delivery is at higher risk for which complication?

options.A: Development of type 1 diabetes
options.B: Permanent loss of vision
options.C: Severe postpartum hemorrhage
options.D: Early onset menopause

explanation: Closely spaced pregnancies strain the uterine muscles, increasing the likelihood of poor uterine contraction and heavy bleeding after birth. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T002#GNS226_U6_T002_h1)

question: How does family planning directly improve infant survival rates?

options.A: By eliminating childhood vaccinations completely
options.B: By replacing breast milk with specialized formula from birth
options.C: By guaranteeing that every child is born via cesarean section
options.D: By reducing the rate of premature births and low birth weight

explanation: Adequate birth spacing gives the uterus optimal conditions, resulting in healthier birth weights and fewer premature deliveries. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T002#GNS226_U6_T002_h2)

question: A mother visits the clinic with a four-month-old baby and asks about getting pregnant again immediately. What is your best nursing response regarding child health?

options.A: Tell her that child health has no connection to how close pregnancies are
options.B: Advise waiting at least two years to protect the health of both the baby and future children
options.C: Encourage immediate conception so the children can grow up as close friends
options.D: Suggest she stop breastfeeding immediately to prepare for the next pregnancy

explanation: Waiting helps ensure the current infant receives prolonged breastfeeding and reduces risks like malnutrition and infections. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T002#GNS226_U6_T002_h2)

question: Why do smaller, planned families often experience better economic stability?

options.A: Resources are not stretched too thin, allowing for better savings and education
options.B: Parents in small families are legally banned from spending money on leisure
options.C: Household utility bills automatically decrease by half
options.D: Governments automatically pay a monthly salary to small families

explanation: Fewer dependents reduce immediate daily expenses, giving parents room to invest in long-term goals like schooling and business ventures. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T002#GNS226_U6_T002_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical socioeconomic benefit of family planning for a household?

options.A: Increased ability to afford nutritious food and clothing
options.B: Higher likelihood of children completing their education
options.C: Reduced spending on emergency medical care for sick infants
options.D: Guaranteed employment for all children upon reaching adulthood

explanation: Family planning improves financial management and education access, but it does not automatically guarantee employment for children later in life. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T002#GNS226_U6_T002_h3)

question: What is a major consequence when young girls experience unplanned early pregnancies?

options.A: They receive free healthcare for the rest of their lives
options.B: They gain immediate leadership roles in politics
options.C: They automatically achieve financial independence
options.D: They are frequently forced to drop out of school

explanation: Unplanned early pregnancy is a leading cause of school dropout among young girls, restricting their future employment opportunities. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T002#GNS226_U6_T002_h4)

question: How does family planning directly promote gender equality?

options.A: By making biological differences between men and women disappear
options.B: By giving women control over their reproductive lives so they can pursue education and work
options.C: By ensuring that only women make decisions regarding community finances
options.D: By legally prohibiting men from participating in healthcare discussions

explanation: Fertility control frees women from the cycle of constant childrearing, enabling them to pursue personal and professional goals on equal footing. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T002#GNS226_U6_T002_h4)

question: What happens when a country experiences rapid population growth without adequate family planning?

options.A: Hospitals experience a permanent surplus of medical supplies
options.B: Public infrastructure like schools and hospitals becomes overwhelmed
options.C: Educational standards automatically rise across all regions
options.D: The national economy instantly becomes the richest in the world

explanation: Uncontrolled population growth outpaces the government's ability to build and maintain essential public services and facilities. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T002#GNS226_U6_T002_h5)

question: Lower national fertility rates are most directly associated with which public health outcome?

options.A: Guaranteed longevity past one hundred years of age
options.B: The elimination of chronic non-communicable illnesses
options.C: Complete eradication of all infectious diseases
options.D: Reduced maternal and child mortality burdens

explanation: Fewer high-risk pregnancies translate to fewer maternal and infant deaths, easing the strain on public health systems. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T002#GNS226_U6_T002_h5)

question: What is the first step a nurse should take when counseling a client on family planning?

options.A: Choose a contraceptive method for the client without asking questions
options.B: Lecture the client on the economic dangers of large families
options.C: Refer the client immediately to a surgeon for sterilization
options.D: Assess the client's medical history and reproductive goals

explanation: Safe and effective counseling must begin with understanding the individual client's health background and personal preferences. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T002#GNS226_U6_T002_h6)

question: A client expresses fear that a contraceptive injection will cause permanent infertility based on rumors heard in the market. How should the nurse respond?

options.A: Provide accurate, gentle education and explain how the method temporarily works
options.B: Agree with the rumor to prevent any future arguments
options.C: Refuse to provide any family planning services to this client
options.D: Scold the client for listening to uneducated people in the community

explanation: Nurses must address fears and correct misconceptions with patience and clear scientific facts rather than judgment. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T002#GNS226_U6_T002_h6)

question: Why is family planning so important for mothers' health in Nigeria?

options.A: It helps reduce maternal mortality by allowing proper pregnancy spacing.
options.B: It removes the need for routine antenatal care visits.
options.C: It completely eliminates the risk of chronic illnesses.
options.D: It guarantees financial stability for large households.

explanation: Spot on! Giving the body enough time to recover between pregnancies protects the mother's health and greatly lowers the risk of complications during childbirth. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T003#GNS226_U6_T003_h1)

question: How does child health directly improve when a family uses effective family planning methods?

options.A: The need for childhood immunizations is drastically reduced.
options.B: Children automatically develop stronger natural immunity to all infections.
options.C: Infants are born with a higher average birth weight without exception.
options.D: Resources can be better shared to prevent malnutrition and infant illness.

explanation: You got it! When births are well-spaced, parents can better invest time, money, and nutrition into each child, keeping them healthier and well-nourished. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T003#GNS226_U6_T003_h1)

question: Why do large family sizes still hold a lot of cultural importance in many Nigerian communities?

options.A: Government policies mandate a minimum number of children per household.
options.B: Modern contraceptives are completely unavailable in rural areas.
options.C: They are viewed as a symbol of wealth and ancestral continuity.
options.D: Traditional healers require large families for spiritual protection.

explanation: Exactly! In many traditional settings, having a large family is celebrated as a sign of prosperity, strength, and keeping the family lineage alive. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T003#GNS226_U6_T003_h2)

question: In some Nigerian households, men make most of the major decisions. How does this affect family planning?

options.A: Maternal mortality rates instantly drop to zero in rural regions.
options.B: Couples automatically adopt natural methods without needing education.
options.C: Health clinics stop stocking hormonal contraceptive injections.
options.D: Women often cannot access modern contraceptives without partner approval.

explanation: Spot on. Because men often lead household decisions, women who want to use family planning may face hurdles or fear disapproval if their partners aren't included in the conversation. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T003#GNS226_U6_T003_h2)

question: Which family planning method gives you dual protection against both pregnancy and sexually transmitted infections (STIs)?

options.A: Subdermal implants
options.B: Oral contraceptive pills
options.C: Intrauterine devices
options.D: Condoms

explanation: That's right! Barrier methods like male and female condoms block both sperm and infections, making them the only modern contraceptives that offer dual protection. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T003#GNS226_U6_T003_h3)

question: A client comes to the clinic asking for a reversible method that lasts for several years without her needing to remember it daily. Which option fits best?

options.A: Periodic calendar rhythm tracking with her partner
options.B: Combined oral contraceptive pills taken every morning
options.C: An intrauterine device inserted into the uterine cavity
options.D: Male withdrawal practice during intercourse

explanation: Great choice! Intrauterine devices (IUDs) are long-acting and give continuous protection for years without needing daily action from the client. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T003#GNS226_U6_T003_h3)

question: What does 'informed choice' truly mean in family planning counseling?

options.A: Clients must select the method with the highest efficacy rate.
options.B: Clients make voluntary decisions based on complete and accurate information.
options.C: Clients must follow the cultural preferences of their local community.
options.D: Nurses have the final authority to choose the method for the client.

explanation: Spot on! Informed choice means the client gets clear, unbiased facts so they can freely pick the method that works best for them without any pressure. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T003#GNS226_U6_T003_h4)

question: Why must a nurse take a detailed medical history before a client starts hormonal contraceptives?

options.A: To find out how many children the client's extended family prefers
options.B: To determine the exact date of the client's future menopause
options.C: To check for underlying conditions that might make certain hormones unsafe
options.D: To calculate the precise financial cost of the clinic visit

explanation: You're right! Conditions like a history of blood clots can make certain hormones unsafe, so checking health history first keeps the client safe. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T003#GNS226_U6_T003_h4)

question: What is a major reason why clients sometimes stop using modern contraceptives early?

options.A: Sudden nationwide shortages of barrier supplies
options.B: Automatic expiration of contraceptive efficacy after one month
options.C: Anxiety and fear regarding normal physiological side effects
options.D: Mandatory government limits on the duration of use

explanation: Spot on! Many clients stop using a method when they notice minor changes like spotting simply because nobody warned them it's a normal body reaction. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T003#GNS226_U6_T003_h5)

question: How should you respond as a nurse if a client worries that injectable contraceptives will make her permanently barren?

options.A: Provide empathetic education explaining that fertility returns after discontinuation.
options.B: Dismiss the concern as an unimportant superstition unworthy of discussion.
options.C: Advise the client to switch immediately to permanent surgical sterilization.
options.D: Confirm that temporary infertility is a permanent risk of modern drugs.

explanation: Well done! Patient, warm counseling helps clear up myths by calmly explaining that normal fertility returns once the injection wears off. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T003#GNS226_U6_T003_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier to getting contraceptives in Nigeria?

options.A: Geographic distance to the nearest healthcare center
options.B: Stockouts of essential commodities at health facilities
options.C: Judgmental attitudes from healthcare workers
options.D: Universal availability of free home-delivery services

explanation: Correct! Free home delivery is not a standard reality across Nigeria. Instead, long distances, running out of supplies, and unfriendly attitudes are the real challenges clients face. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T003#GNS226_U6_T003_h6)

question: What is the main goal of task-shifting policies in Nigerian family planning programs?

options.A: To restrict contraceptive distribution only to senior medical doctors
options.B: To eliminate the need for any documentation during client visits
options.C: To allow lower-level health workers to provide certain contraceptive services
options.D: To transfer all maternal care responsibilities exclusively to private hospitals

explanation: Spot on! Task-shifting helps bridge the gap by training community health workers and nurses to safely provide methods like injectables where doctors are few. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T003#GNS226_U6_T003_h6)

question: What is one of the primary clinical duties of a nurse in a family planning clinic?

options.A: Enforcing mandatory family size limits on couples
options.B: Manufacturing pharmaceutical hormone supplies for national distribution
options.C: Assessing clients and administering chosen contraceptive methods
options.D: Conducting major abdominal surgeries for all clients

explanation: You got it! Nurses play a key role by counseling clients, doing health assessments, and giving out chosen methods right there at the primary healthcare level. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T003#GNS226_U6_T003_h7)

question: Why is community outreach by nurses and midwives so vital for family planning programs?

options.A: It helps engage local leaders and dismantle cultural stigma against modern methods.
options.B: It allows health workers to bypass government health policies entirely.
options.C: It ensures that nurses can collect financial levies from local households.
options.D: It replaces the need for clinical examinations inside health facilities.

explanation: Spot on! Going out into the community builds trust, involves local leaders, and helps clear up cultural or religious worries right at the grassroots level. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T003#GNS226_U6_T003_h7)

question: Which country in West Africa has the highest total population?

options.A: Cameroon
options.B: Ghana
options.C: Nigeria
options.D: Senegal

explanation: Spot on! Nigeria is the most populous nation in Africa and drives a lot of the demographic growth in our region. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T004#GNS226_U6_T004_h1)

question: Why do nursing students learn about population birth trends?

options.A: To calculate national financial budgets for the government
options.B: To accurately predict community maternal and child healthcare needs
options.C: To determine international trade policies for medical goods
options.D: To replace the work of civil registrars and census officers

explanation: You got it! Knowing birth rates helps you anticipate how many mothers and babies will need care in your facility. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T004#GNS226_U6_T004_h1)

question: What does 'Total Fertility Rate' (TFR) actually measure?

options.A: The percentage of women using modern family planning methods
options.B: The average number of children a woman has during her reproductive years
options.C: The average age of mothers when giving birth to their first child
options.D: The total number of children born in a single hospital annually

explanation: Exactly! TFR estimates the average number of children a woman is expected to have throughout her childbearing years. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T004#GNS226_U6_T004_h2)

question: What is a major result of a country having a high birth rate over many years?

options.A: A heavy economic dependency ratio with many young citizens
options.B: A rapid increase in the average age of the working population
options.C: An immediate shortage of geriatric care facilities
options.D: A permanent surplus of maternal hospital beds nationwide

explanation: Correct! High birth rates create a young population, meaning fewer working adults have to support many children. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T004#GNS226_U6_T004_h2)

question: Why do many rural families traditionally view having many children as a great benefit?

options.A: The government pays monthly stipends for large households
options.B: Children provide farm labor and security in old age
options.C: Larger households receive free agricultural land allotments
options.D: School fees are fully subsidized for families with five children

explanation: Spot on! In farming communities, children help out on the farm and support their parents as they grow older. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T004#GNS226_U6_T004_h3)

question: How does wanting a male child (son preference) affect family sizes in some communities?

options.A: It drives couples to keep trying for a boy, increasing total births
options.B: It has no statistical influence on community birth patterns
options.C: It automatically lowers the median age of marriage for women
options.D: It encourages families to stop childbearing after the first daughter

explanation: You're right! When families really want a baby boy, they often keep having children past their original goal until a son arrives. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T004#GNS226_U6_T004_h3)

question: In Nigeria, which setting usually records the lowest fertility rates?

options.A: Rural farming villages
options.B: Remote agrarian settlements
options.C: Urban centers
options.D: Nomadic pastoral communities

explanation: Correct! City dwellers often have smaller family sizes due to higher living costs and better access to school and family planning. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T004#GNS226_U6_T004_h4)

question: How does keeping girls in school longer usually affect their age at marriage?

options.A: It forces marriage at an earlier age
options.B: It has no effect on marriage timing
options.C: It prevents women from ever marrying
options.D: It delays marriage to a later age

explanation: Exactly! Education keeps young women in school, which naturally pushes their age of first marriage higher. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T004#GNS226_U6_T004_h5)
