explanation: You get years of steady protection, but if the client ever wants to get pregnant later, you just take it out and her natural fertility bounces right back! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h1)

question: How does a copper IUD mainly prevent pregnancy?

options.A: By releasing high doses of estrogen to stop ovulation
options.B: By swelling the cervix shut so sperm cannot enter
options.C: By physically blocking the Fallopian tubes with wire
options.D: By releasing copper ions that stun and damage sperm cells

explanation: The copper creates an environment that sperm really hate. It damages them and stops them from ever reaching the egg! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h2)

question: How does a hormonal IUD prevent pregnancy?

options.A: By thickening the cervical mucus to block sperm from entering
options.B: By making the vagina super acidic to destroy sperm on contact
options.C: By tricking the ovaries into releasing multiple eggs
options.D: By creating physical pressure that crushes any fertilized egg

explanation: The tiny bit of hormone released thickens the mucus at the cervix like a strong security guard—sperm just can't swim through it! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h2)

question: How long can the common Copper T 380A IUD stay in place?

options.A: For the rest of the woman's life
options.B: Exactly 1 to 2 years
options.C: A maximum of 6 months
options.D: Up to 10 to 12 years

explanation: The Copper T 380A is a real champion for long-term family planning—it's approved to stay in safely for up to a decade! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h3)

question: A client complains of heavy, painful periods and wants an IUD. Which type should you recommend to help with the heavy bleeding?

options.A: A hormonal IUD that releases levonorgestrel
options.B: A standard copper-bearing T 380A device
options.C: Any IUD, because all types stop bleeding completely
options.D: A plain plastic loop with no hormones or metal

explanation: Hormonal IUDs are great because they lighten the uterine lining over time, which usually means much lighter, less painful periods for the client. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h3)

question: Which of these is a strict 'no-go' (absolute contraindication) for putting in an IUD?

options.A: Mild iron deficiency anemia
options.B: Having had a past cesarean section
options.C: A history of high blood pressure
options.D: Confirmed or suspected pregnancy

explanation: Never place an IUD if a woman is already pregnant! It can cause serious complications, severe infection, or miscarriage. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h4)

question: Why must you perform a bimanual pelvic exam before putting in an IUD?

options.A: To confirm the client is definitely not ovulating
options.B: To stretch the cervix open without using instruments
options.C: To check the weight of the client's ovaries
options.D: To check the size and position of the uterus

explanation: Feeling the uterus first helps you know its exact angle and size so you can insert the device safely without accidentally poking through the uterine wall. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h4)

question: Which sterile instrument is used to gently hold and steady the cervix during an IUD procedure?

options.A: Sims speculum
options.B: Sponge forceps
options.C: Uterine sound
options.D: Tenaculum

explanation: The tenaculum gently holds the cervix steady and straightens out the angle of the uterus so you can pass the IUD smoothly. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h5)

question: What is the main reason for using a uterine sound before IUD insertion?

options.A: To numb the inside of the uterus against cramps
options.B: To measure how deep and in which direction the uterus goes
options.C: To clean out blood and mucus from the canal
options.D: To widen the vagina so the speculum opens wider

explanation: Sounding gives you an exact measurement of the uterine depth, making sure you don't push the IUD in too far and cause a perforation. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h5)

question: What important advice should you give a client about her IUD strings?

options.A: Come to the clinic weekly for string trimming
options.B: Pull gently on the strings every morning to check if it's tight
options.C: Cut the strings shorter with scissors if they curl up
options.D: Check for the strings inside the vagina after every monthly period

explanation: Teach clients to do a quick finger check for their strings after their period to make sure the IUD is still sitting snugly in place. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h6)

question: A client who just got a copper IUD a month ago complains of slightly heavier periods and mild cramps. What is your best response as her nurse?

options.A: Tell her she has a dangerous infection that needs surgery
options.B: Schedule emergency surgery to close her cervix
options.C: Tell her to take it out herself at home right away
options.D: Reassure her that this is normal at first and discuss pain relief

explanation: Copper IUDs often cause heavier periods and mild cramping during the first few weeks or months. Reassure your patient—it usually settles down! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h6)

question: When is the risk of getting pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) highest after an IUD insertion?

options.A: Only if the client gets pregnant with the IUD
options.B: During the first 20 days after insertion
options.C: There is never any risk of infection
options.D: After the IUD has been in place for five years

explanation: Because tiny amounts of bacteria can accidentally enter the uterus during the procedure, the infection risk is highest right after insertion, during the first few weeks. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h7)

question: A client comes back to the clinic three weeks after getting an IUD with severe lower belly pain, fever, and strange vaginal discharge. What should you suspect first?

options.A: The IUD completely falling out on its own
options.B: Simple iron deficiency anemia
options.C: A normal adjustment period to the device
options.D: Pelvic inflammatory disease

explanation: Fever, foul discharge, and severe lower abdominal pain are classic red flags for an ascending uterine infection like PID. Act fast and evaluate her! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h7)

question: How do barrier methods of contraception primarily prevent pregnancy?

options.A: By stopping the ovaries from releasing eggs
options.B: By altering the lining of the uterus
options.C: By thickening the natural cervical mucus
options.D: By physically blocking sperm from meeting the egg

explanation: Spot on! Barrier methods act like a physical shield that keeps sperm from traveling up to meet the egg. You've got this! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T016#GNS226_U6_T016_h1)

question: Why do barrier contraceptives usually have fewer medical restrictions than hormonal birth control pills?

options.A: They require a doctor to insert them every time
options.B: They do not change the body's hormone balance
options.C: They destroy all bacteria present in the vagina
options.D: They are completely 100 percent effective always

explanation: Exactly! Because barriers don't add synthetic hormones to the body, patients can avoid those systemic side effects. Great job! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T016#GNS226_U6_T016_h1)

question: When a female condom is inserted properly, where does its closed end sit?

options.A: Over the cervix
options.B: Around the base of the bladder
options.C: Against the labia majora
options.D: Inside the fallopian tube

explanation: You got it! The closed end goes deep inside to rest right over the cervix, much like a diaphragm does. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T016#GNS226_U6_T016_h2)

question: What are the three main ways a contraceptive sponge works?

options.A: Killing eggs, balancing pH, and stretching the vagina
options.B: Trapping sperm, releasing spermicide, and absorbing semen
options.C: Numbing the area, increasing moisture, and stopping cycles
options.D: Dilating the cervix, heating the tissue, and easing flow

explanation: Well done! The sponge is a multitasker: it blocks the canal, releases spermicide, and soaks up fluid. Learning is fun when it clicks! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T016#GNS226_U6_T016_h2)

question: What is the most common active chemical found in modern spermicides?

options.A: Chlorhexidine
options.B: Hydrogen peroxide
options.C: Nonoxynol-9
options.D: Sodium hypochlorite

explanation: Correct! Nonoxynol-9 is the trusty chemical agent added to gels and foams to target and destroy sperm cell membranes. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T016#GNS226_U6_T016_h3)

question: Why can frequent use of high-strength spermicide sometimes increase the risk of infections?

options.A: It permanently paralyzes the immune cells in the bloodstream
options.B: It neutralizes all normal vaginal flora leaving the body dry
options.C: It can cause tiny cuts in vaginal tissue that let viruses enter
options.D: It reacts with air to create toxic gases inside the pelvis

explanation: That's right! Chemical irritation from overuse can break down natural tissue defenses, making it easier for infections to slip in. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T016#GNS226_U6_T016_h3)

question: In family planning, what do we mean by 'typical use' of a birth control method?

options.A: How effectively the method works during everyday, real-life use
options.B: The percentage of people who choose the method on their first visit
options.C: How well the method works when applied correctly every single time
options.D: The laboratory score assigned by the manufacturing pharmaceutical company

explanation: Spot on! 'Typical use' accounts for real life—meaning human errors, busy schedules, or slip-ups that happen outside a lab. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T016#GNS226_U6_T016_h4)

question: Why is there usually a noticeable difference between 'perfect use' and 'typical use' success rates for barrier methods?

options.A: People sometimes make mistakes or forget to use them consistently
options.B: Hormonal changes in the user alter how the physical device functions
options.C: The materials degrade instantly the moment the package is opened
options.D: Manufacturers intentionally print lower numbers to avoid lawsuits

explanation: Exactly! Humans aren't robots. Real-life inconsistencies and minor user errors are why typical use rates differ from lab perfection. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T016#GNS226_U6_T016_h4)

question: Which barrier method gives the most reliable protection against sexually transmitted infections (STIs)?

options.A: Contraceptive sponges
options.B: Cervical caps
options.C: Diaphragms
options.D: Condoms

explanation: You got it! Condoms create a physical shield over the genitalia, blocking both infectious fluids and skin contact. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T016#GNS226_U6_T016_h5)

question: Why don't diaphragms and cervical caps protect very well against skin-to-skin STIs like HPV?

options.A: They leave the vaginal walls and external skin exposed
options.B: They allow semen to leak freely around the sides of the device
options.C: They dissolve too quickly when exposed to bodily fluids
options.D: They absorb viral particles and push them directly into the uterus

explanation: Correct! Because they only cover the cervix, surrounding skin and vaginal walls are still exposed to touch-based viruses. Great clinical insight! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T016#GNS226_U6_T016_h5)

question: Which of these life changes means a female client needs to be refitted for a new diaphragm?

options.A: Changing her brand of body soap
options.B: Starting a daily multi-vitamin
options.C: A minor seasonal head cold
options.D: Significant weight change

explanation: Spot on! Major shifts in weight alter pelvic anatomy, meaning she'll need a new size for a proper, secure seal. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T016#GNS226_U6_T016_h6)

question: A patient tells you she uses petroleum jelly as a lubricant with her latex condoms. What should be your immediate nursing advice?

options.A: Confirm that petroleum jelly is the ideal choice for extra slip
options.B: Warn her that oil-based lubricants weaken latex and can cause breakage
options.C: Advise her to microwave the jelly first to make it safe for use
options.D: Suggest she switch to oil-based spermicide creams instead

explanation: Brilliant! Oil-based products break down latex rubber super fast, leading to tears. Water-based lube is always the safe choice here! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T016#GNS226_U6_T016_h6)

question: What materials are modern contraceptive diaphragms usually made of?

options.A: Silicone or latex
options.B: Rigid hard plastic
options.C: Absorbable collagen
options.D: Woven cotton mesh

explanation: Modern diaphragms use soft, flexible silicone or latex so they can comfortably bend and fit inside the vagina. You've got this! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T017#GNS226_U6_T017_h1)

question: Why do women need to use chemical spermicide along with a diaphragm?

options.A: To lubricate the device for easy insertion
options.B: To immobilize and kill sperm that pass the barrier
options.C: To permanently alter the pH of the cervix
options.D: To prevent the growth of yeast infections

explanation: While the physical cup blocks most sperm, spermicide acts as a backup to kill any little swimmers that might slip past the edges! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T017#GNS226_U6_T017_h1)

question: Which type of diaphragm bends easily in half along a central hinge to make putting it in easier?

options.A: Flat spring
options.B: Coil spring
options.C: Rigid ring
options.D: Arcing spring

explanation: An arcing spring diaphragm folds right in half like a taco, which helps guide it smoothly into place over the cervix. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T017#GNS226_U6_T017_h2)

question: What is a big perk of the newer, single-size silicone diaphragms?

options.A: They can be left in place inside the vagina for up to a week
options.B: They do not require an internal pelvic exam for professional sizing
options.C: They completely eliminate the need to use spermicide creams
options.D: They provide full protection against all sexually transmitted infections

explanation: Universal single-size diaphragms are a lifesaver because one standard size fits most women, saving them from a traditional fitting exam. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T017#GNS226_U6_T017_h2)

question: During a traditional diaphragm fitting, what two points does the nurse measure between?

options.A: Clitoris to the perineal body
options.B: Posterior fornix to the pubic bone
options.C: Cervical os to the vaginal introitus
options.D: Uterine fundus to the pelvic inlet

explanation: To get the right size, clinicians measure from the back of the vagina (posterior fornix) to the back of the pubic bone. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T017#GNS226_U6_T017_h3)

question: A patient comes back to the clinic after losing 15 kg. What should you do as her nurse?

options.A: Instruct the client to continue using her current diaphragm device
options.B: Perform a repeat pelvic measurement for a new diaphragm size
options.C: Advise the client to stop using spermicide during intercourse
options.D: Recommend switching immediately to an oral contraceptive pill

explanation: Major weight changes shift body fat and pelvic tone, meaning she will likely need a new size for a snug, safe fit. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T017#GNS226_U6_T017_h3)

question: When putting in a diaphragm correctly, where should the front edge be tucked?

options.A: Against the anterior vaginal wall
options.B: Behind the pubic bone
options.C: Directly over the labia majora
options.D: Inside the uterine cavity

explanation: The front rim needs to hook securely behind the pubic bone so it stays locked tightly over the cervix. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T017#GNS226_U6_T017_h4)

question: Why should a user hold their diaphragm up to the light before using it?

options.A: To check for small tears or holes that would let sperm pass through
options.B: To ensure the correct color coding for the specific menstrual cycle
options.C: To activate the chemical properties of the embedded spermicide
options.D: To warm up the silicone material for more comfortable insertion

explanation: A quick visual check against the light helps catch tiny punctures before they lead to an unplanned pregnancy. Simple and smart! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T017#GNS226_U6_T017_h4)

question: At least how long must a diaphragm stay in after sex?

options.A: Twenty-four hours
options.B: One hour
options.C: Six hours
options.D: Twelve hours

explanation: Leaving it in for at least 6 hours gives the spermicide enough time to completely immobilize and destroy all viable sperm. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T017#GNS226_U6_T017_h5)

question: What should a client do if she has sex again just four hours after putting in her diaphragm?

options.A: Apply more spermicide into the vagina without removing the diaphragm
options.B: Remove the diaphragm immediately and use an emergency oral contraceptive
options.C: Leave everything alone because the original spermicide is still active
options.D: Take the diaphragm out, wash it, and reinsert it with fresh spermicide

explanation: For repeat intercourse, she should just push more spermicide straight into the vagina without taking the device out. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T017#GNS226_U6_T017_h5)

question: Which type of lubricant can damage and weaken a latex diaphragm?

options.A: Water-soluble jelly
options.B: Natural saliva
options.C: Spermicidal creams
options.D: Oil-based lubricants

explanation: Oils and petroleum jelly break down latex rubber super fast, creating weak spots and tears. Always stick to water-based lubes! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T017#GNS226_U6_T017_h6)

question: How should a washed diaphragm be stored after it dries?

options.A: In its designated storage case away from heat and sunlight
options.B: Wrapped tightly in a plastic bag inside the kitchen freezer
options.C: At the bottom of a handbag without any protective covering
options.D: Hanging openly on a bathroom wall hook exposed to light

explanation: Keeping it in its cool, dark storage case protects the material from heat and sunlight, helping it last a long time. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T017#GNS226_U6_T017_h6)

question: Leaving a diaphragm in for way too long can put a patient at risk for which rare, serious condition?

options.A: Toxic Shock Syndrome
options.B: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease
options.C: Ectopic pregnancy
options.D: Cervical dysplasia

explanation: Keeping barrier methods in past the 24-hour mark lets bacteria multiply rapidly, raising the risk of Toxic Shock Syndrome. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T017#GNS226_U6_T017_h7)

question: Why do some women who use diaphragms experience more frequent urinary tract infections (UTIs)?

options.A: The spermicide alters the normal bacterial balance inside the urinary bladder
options.B: The device prevents regular urination while it is worn during the day
options.C: The silicone material absorbs urine and introduces bacteria into the kidneys
options.D: The rim of the device can press against the urethra and block complete bladder emptying

explanation: The diaphragm rim can put slight pressure on the urethra, making it harder to empty the bladder completely and causing UTIs. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T017#GNS226_U6_T017_h7)

question: Which material is most commonly used to make everyday condoms?

options.A: Cotton
options.B: Silicone
options.C: Leather
options.D: Latex

explanation: You got this! Latex is the go-to material for modern condoms because it is strong, stretchy, and reliable at blocking sperm and infections. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h1)

question: Why do nurses love recommending condoms as a first-line protection tool?

options.A: They alter the body's natural hormone levels
options.B: They require a doctor's prescription
options.C: They protect against both pregnancy and infections
options.D: They offer permanent sterilization

explanation: Spot on! Condoms give you dual protection—they stop unwanted pregnancy and keep sexually transmitted infections away at the same time. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h1)

question: Which type of condom material fails to block tiny viral infections like HIV effectively?

options.A: Natural membrane
options.B: Polyisoprene
options.C: Latex
options.D: Polyurethane

explanation: Great job thinking this through. Natural membrane (lambskin) condoms have tiny pores that let small viruses slip right through, even though they block sperm. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h2)

question: How does a female condom stay securely in place inside the vagina?

options.A: A flexible inner ring at the closed end
options.B: Suction created by an external pump
options.C: Sutures placed by a healthcare provider
options.D: An adhesive strip on the outside

explanation: You nailed it! The inner ring at the closed end helps the user push and anchor the pouch securely inside. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h2)

question: What is the main way condoms stop pregnancy from happening?

options.A: By thickening cervical mucus permanently
options.B: By stopping ovulation in the ovaries
options.C: By trapping semen to keep sperm out of the uterus
options.D: By killing sperm cells inside the testes

explanation: Exactly right! Condoms act as a physical shield that catches semen so the sperm cannot swim up into the reproductive tract. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h3)

question: How do condoms stop sexually transmitted infections from spreading between partners?

options.A: Antibiotics coated on the inside of the sheath
options.B: Chemical destruction of bacteria by latex proteins
options.C: A physical barrier blocking contact with infectious fluids
options.D: Immune system stimulation from the lubricant

explanation: Spot on! The material creates a solid wall so infectious fluids never touch or enter mucous membranes. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h3)

question: Why should you pinch the tip of a male condom before rolling it on?

options.A: To stop the penis from losing its erection
options.B: To activate the spermicidal lubricant
options.C: To leave space for semen and prevent bursting
options.D: To warm up the latex material

explanation: You got it! Pinching the tip pushes out trapped air and leaves a little room to catch the semen so the condom doesn't tear. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h4)

question: When should a client take off a male condom after ejaculation?

options.A: Wait until the next morning to take it off
options.B: Take it off only after the erection has completely gone down
options.C: Flush it down the toilet right away
options.D: Remove it immediately while holding the base of the penis

explanation: Well done! Pulling out while still a bit erect and holding the base stops the condom from slipping and spilling semen. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h4)

question: Why is it a big no-no to use petroleum jelly or body lotion with a latex condom?

options.A: Petroleum products freeze the latex and crack it
options.B: Oils trap bacteria inside the vaginal canal
options.C: Oil-based products break down and weaken latex
options.D: Lotions make the condom slide off too easily

explanation: Correct! Oils make latex dissolve and tear easily, completely ruining its protective power. Always stick to water-based lubricants! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h5)

question: A client says they wore a condom inside out, flipped it, and kept going. What is your best nursing advice?

options.A: Suggest washing the condom with soap and reusing it
options.B: Recommend taking emergency contraception immediately
options.C: Tell them the method is completely safe
options.D: Advise discarding it because pre-seminal fluid may be on the outside

explanation: Good clinical thinking! Flipping it exposes the inside part—which might already have pre-ejaculatory fluid—to the partner, raising infection and pregnancy risks. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h5)

question: What is one major perk of condoms over hormonal birth control pills?

options.A: Condoms require no action at the time of intercourse
options.B: Condoms cause permanent changes in fertility
options.C: Condoms have a much higher real-world perfection rate
options.D: Condoms offer protection against sexually transmitted infections

explanation: You got it! While pills are great for preventing pregnancy, only barrier methods like condoms protect against STIs too. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h6)

question: Why is the 'typical use' failure rate for condoms higher than the 'perfect use' rate?

options.A: Incompatible blood types between partners
options.B: User errors like inconsistent use or breakage
options.C: Manufacturing defects in the factory
options.D: Natural expiration of latex while in the box

explanation: Spot on! In the real world, mistakes happen—like not wearing it every time or putting it on late—which lowers effectiveness compared to lab tests. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h6)

question: What is the best way for a nurse to teach a client how to use a condom properly?

options.A: Ask them to watch a video without asking questions
options.B: Demonstrate the technique using a model and let the client practice
options.C: Hand them a printed pamphlet to read at home
options.D: Explain the chemical composition of latex in detail

explanation: You're right! Showing them on a model and having them try it builds real confidence and ensures they get the steps right. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h7)

question: A teenage client is super shy and hesitant to talk about sexual health. What should you do first as their nurse?

options.A: Create a safe, confidential, and non-judgmental environment
options.B: Call the client's parents into the room immediately
options.C: Skip the sexual health assessment entirely
options.D: Scold the client for being immature about health matters

explanation: Brilliant nursing instinct! Trust and a warm, welcoming vibe help nervous clients relax and open up to care. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of bilateral tubal ligation?

options.A: Permanent female contraception
options.B: Treatment for severe pelvic infections
options.C: Prevention of ovarian hormone production
options.D: Regulation of irregular menstrual cycles

explanation: Tubal ligation is specifically designed as a permanent surgical method to prevent pregnancy by blocking the fallopian tubes. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T019#GNS226_U6_T019_h1)

question: Why does a patient continue to experience monthly menstrual periods after getting her tubes tied?

options.A: The ovaries and uterus remain completely functional.
options.B: The uterine lining regenerates independently of the tubes.
options.C: Fallopian tubes still produce blood flow monthly.
options.D: Synthetic hormones are provided through daily medications.

explanation: The procedure only blocks the path of the egg and sperm; it does not touch the ovaries or the uterus, so hormone production and regular menstruation continue as normal. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T019#GNS226_U6_T019_h1)

question: In which specific part of the fallopian tube does fertilization normally occur?

options.A: Cervix
options.B: Isthmus
options.C: Ampulla
options.D: Fimbriae

explanation: The ampulla is the wider, middle section of the fallopian tube where the sperm typically meets and fertilizes the released egg. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T019#GNS226_U6_T019_h2)

question: What is the primary function of the fimbriae at the end of the fallopian tubes?

options.A: To catch and guide the released egg into the tube
options.B: To propel sperm upward toward the uterine cavity
options.C: To produce the hormones estrogen and progesterone
options.D: To provide structural support to the lower abdomen

explanation: The fimbriae are finger-like projections that sweep over the ovary surface during ovulation to catch the newly released egg and draw it inside. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T019#GNS226_U6_T019_h2)

question: Why is thorough pre-operative counseling especially critical for tubal ligation?

options.A: Patients must practice alternative birth control for six months after.
options.B: Insurance companies require psychiatric clearance before approval.
options.C: Surgeries on the reproductive system always cause permanent hormone loss.
options.D: The procedure is intended to be permanent and difficult to reverse.

explanation: Because reversal surgery is costly, complex, and has low success rates, patients must be completely certain they are finished having children before proceeding. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T019#GNS226_U6_T019_h3)

question: A 22-year-old client requests a tubal ligation immediately after delivering her first baby, stating she is stressed. What is the most appropriate nursing response?

options.A: Tell her that her husband must sign the consent form before any discussion can continue.
options.B: Discuss her feelings and explore other temporary birth control options while she settles into motherhood.
options.C: Immediately schedule the procedure so it can be performed before hospital discharge.
options.D: Refuse to assist with the paperwork because young mothers are not allowed to choose this surgery.

explanation: High stress during the postpartum period is a common time for impulsive requests, so nurses should provide supportive counseling and present reversible options first. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T019#GNS226_U6_T019_h3)

question: What surgical instrument is typically used during a standard laparoscopy for tubal ligation?

options.A: A lighted camera scope and small grasping tools
options.B: A large open abdominal retractor and surgical saw
options.C: A long uterine curette inserted through the vagina
options.D: An ultrasound probe placed directly on the ovaries

explanation: Laparoscopy relies on a small camera inserted via a tiny umbilical incision to guide specialized instruments that seal or block the tubes. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T019#GNS226_U6_T019_h4)

question: Why is a mini-laparotomy often performed immediately after a vaginal delivery?

options.A: The postpartum uterus is still enlarged, placing the tubes close to the abdominal wall.
options.B: Hormonal changes during birth make the patient immune to surgical site infections.
options.C: Regional anesthesia used for labor completely paralyzes the fallopian tubes.
options.D: Postpartum bleeding prevents the need for any internal stitching of tissues.

explanation: Shortly after birth, the anatomical position of the reproductive organs allows for a very small incision to easily access and tie the tubes. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T019#GNS226_U6_T019_h4)

question: A patient who had a laparoscopic tubal ligation two hours ago complains of sharp pain in her right shoulder. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Reassure her that trapped carbon dioxide gas causes this and encourage walking.
options.B: Administer a strong narcotic pain killer and restrict her to strict bed rest.
options.C: Notify the surgeon immediately because internal bleeding has reached her chest.
options.D: Apply an ice pack directly over her right shoulder joint to reduce inflammation.

explanation: Referred shoulder pain is very common after laparoscopy because residual abdominal gas irritates the diaphragm, and walking helps the body absorb it faster. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T019#GNS226_U6_T019_h5)

question: Which nursing check is most critical immediately after a patient returns from a tubal ligation procedure?

options.A: Assessing the client's ability to conceive within one month
options.B: Testing the patient for signs of future fertility recovery
options.C: Measuring exact daily caloric intake and urinary output
options.D: Monitoring vital signs and assessing the abdominal incision site

explanation: Immediate post-operative care centers on recovery from anesthesia, stable vital signs, and watching for bleeding or complications at the surgical site. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T019#GNS226_U6_T019_h5)

question: What makes an ectopic pregnancy a major concern for a woman who has had a tubal ligation?

options.A: Sperm can easily bypass the surgical blockages and dissolve the uterine lining.
options.B: If pregnancy occurs, the blocked tube increases the chance the egg implants outside the uterus.
options.C: Hormonal imbalances caused by the surgery force eggs to grow in the abdominal wall.
options.D: The scar tissue prevents the ovaries from releasing any hormones at all.

explanation: While overall pregnancy rates after tubal ligation are very low, any pregnancy that does happen carries a much higher risk of being ectopic, which is a medical emergency. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T019#GNS226_U6_T019_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common complication associated with tubal ligation surgery?

options.A: Permanent cessation of the menstrual cycle
options.B: Accidental injury to surrounding pelvic organs
options.C: Infection at the surgical incision site
options.D: Post-operative bleeding or hematoma formation

explanation: Tubal ligation does not stop menstrual periods because the ovaries remain untouched and continue to function normally. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T019#GNS226_U6_T019_h6)

question: Why should a nurse emphasize that tubal ligation is permanent even though microsurgical reversals exist?

options.A: Reversal operations always cause permanent damage to the ovaries and uterus.
options.B: The human fallopian tubes instantly dissolve once they are surgically cut.
options.C: Reversal surgery is expensive, complex, and has uncertain success rates.
options.D: Hospitals legally forbid patients from ever attempting to reverse the procedure.

explanation: Reversing a tubal ligation requires delicate microsurgery that is not always successful, making it unwise for patients to rely on it as a backup plan. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T019#GNS226_U6_T019_h7)

question: What is a major disadvantage of bilateral tubal ligation compared to barrier methods like condoms?

options.A: It requires daily motivation and adherence from the client.
options.B: It immediately causes early menopause and hot flashes.
options.C: It has a very high failure rate within the first year.
options.D: It offers no protection against sexually transmitted infections.

explanation: While highly effective at preventing pregnancy, tubal ligation does not shield against sexually transmitted infections, unlike barrier methods. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T019#GNS226_U6_T019_h7)

question: During a vasectomy, which main tube is cut or blocked to stop sperm from leaving?

options.A: The vas deferens
options.B: The seminal vesicles
options.C: The seminiferous tubules
options.D: The epididymis

explanation: You got this! The vas deferens is the muscular tube that carries sperm from the testes, making it the exact target for this procedure. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T020#GNS226_U6_T020_h1)

question: How does a vasectomy change a man's semen volume after surgery?

options.A: It becomes completely clear and watery
options.B: It stays almost exactly the same
options.C: It drops to zero immediately
options.D: It increases to make up for lost sperm

explanation: Spot on! Sperm only make up a tiny fraction of semen, so blocking their path doesn't noticeably change the amount of fluid. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T020#GNS226_U6_T020_h1)

question: What is the most important thing a nurse must make clear during pre-vasectomy counseling?

options.A: Sperm analysis is optional after the first month
options.B: The procedure is intended to be permanent
options.C: General anesthesia will be used in the operating room
options.D: Sexual performance will improve after surgery

explanation: Great job! Patients need to know that a vasectomy is meant to be permanent because reversing it is difficult and costly. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T020#GNS226_U6_T020_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT part of a standard nursing check before a vasectomy?

options.A: Scheduling a mandatory prostate biopsy
options.B: Checking for active local skin infections
options.C: Screening for permanent reproductive intent
options.D: Evaluating bleeding history and anticoagulant use

explanation: That's right! A prostate biopsy checks for cancer and has nothing to do with routine preparation for a vasectomy. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T020#GNS226_U6_T020_h2)

question: What is the big plus of choosing a no-scalpel vasectomy over the older method?

options.A: It can be performed without any local anesthetic
options.B: It causes less bleeding and requires no skin stitches
options.C: It guarantees immediate sterility without a semen test
options.D: It makes surgical reversal much easier later on

explanation: Brilliant! The no-scalpel technique uses a tiny puncture instead of a cutting blade, which means less bleeding and a quicker recovery. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T020#GNS226_U6_T020_h3)

question: Why do surgeons often tie and heat-seal the tubes during a vasectomy?

options.A: To prevent the cut ends from spontaneously reconnecting
options.B: To completely numb the scrotal sac for pain relief
options.C: To speed up the healing of the outer scrotal skin
options.D: To destroy any remaining sperm inside the testicles

explanation: Spot on! Using two methods like tying and sealing ensures the tubes don't accidentally grow back together. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T020#GNS226_U6_T020_h3)

question: A client had a vasectomy yesterday and asks when he can go back to heavy lifting at work. What do you tell him?

options.A: Wait until your semen analysis proves you are sterile in three months
options.B: You can return to lifting heavy items immediately if you wear a support
options.C: Heavy lifting is fine as long as you take pain medication
options.D: Wait at least a week and check with your doctor first

explanation: Correct! Strenuous work should wait for about a week to avoid bleeding or swelling in the scrotum. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T020#GNS226_U6_T020_h4)

question: What simple home care helps most with scrotal swelling on the first day after surgery?

options.A: Massaging the scrotum gently to drain excess fluid
options.B: Applying an ice pack wrapped in a cloth intermittently
options.C: Taking a long soak in a warm bathtub twice a day
options.D: Applying a firm heating pad directly to the skin

explanation: You got it! Cold packs help narrow blood vessels, keeping early swelling and bruising under control. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T020#GNS226_U6_T020_h4)

question: Which sign strongly points to an infection after a vasectomy?

options.A: Temporary discomfort when wearing loose underwear
options.B: A small, painless pea-sized lump near the cut end
options.C: Mild bruising and a dull pulling ache in the groin
options.D: Fever and pus draining from the scrotal incision

explanation: Brilliant! Fever and pus are classic warning signs of a bacterial infection that needs quick medical attention. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T020#GNS226_U6_T020_h5)

question: What actually is a scrotal hematoma after a vasectomy?

options.A: An infection of the epididymis caused by trapped bacteria
options.B: A collection of blood pooling inside the scrotal tissues
options.C: Scar tissue blocking the normal flow of seminal fluid
options.D: A harmless collection of fluid inside the testicle sac

explanation: Spot on! A hematoma happens when a tiny blood vessel keeps leaking after surgery, leading to swelling and pain. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T020#GNS226_U6_T020_h5)

question: Why can a man still cause a pregnancy right after getting a vasectomy?

options.A: Seminal fluid still requires three months to regenerate its chemistry
options.B: The body continues to produce live sperm inside the vas deferens tubes
options.C: Sperm already stored above the surgical cut remain active for weeks
options.D: The surgical incisions take several weeks to close completely

explanation: You nailed it! There is still a leftover supply of sperm stored further up that needs to be cleared out through ejaculation. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T020#GNS226_U6_T020_h6)

question: A client 4 weeks post-vasectomy asks if he can stop using condoms since he feels great. What is your best advice?

options.A: You can stop condoms now since four weeks is enough healing time
options.B: Continue using birth control until your semen analysis confirms zero sperm
options.C: Wait for one more week and then you can safely discard condoms
options.D: Stop using condoms only if you haven't experienced any swelling

explanation: Correct! Always remind clients to keep using backup contraception until a lab test officially confirms the semen is sperm-free. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T020#GNS226_U6_T020_h6)

question: What is the main job of emergency contraception?

options.A: To terminate an established pregnancy safely
options.B: To serve as a regular daily family planning method
options.C: To prevent pregnancy after unprotected intercourse
options.D: To protect against sexually transmitted infections

explanation: Think of emergency contraception as your backup plan after a contraceptive slip-up or unprotected sex. It is not meant for daily family planning and doesn't work if a pregnancy has already started. You've got this! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h1)

question: Why do nurses need to explain that emergency contraceptives are not abortifacients?

options.A: To show that they can also cure sexually transmitted infections
options.B: To prove that the drugs are 100 percent effective every time
options.C: To encourage patients to use them instead of regular condoms
options.D: To clear up cultural and moral misconceptions about how the drugs work

explanation: A lot of people mix up emergency pills with abortion pills. As a nurse, clarifying how it actually works helps calm unnecessary fears and clears up social myths. Brilliant work! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h1)

question: What is the single most important factor for emergency contraception to work successfully?

options.A: The time of day the client ate their last meal
options.B: The age and weight of the client receiving the pill
options.C: The brand name of the emergency contraceptive drug
options.D: The timing of administration after unprotected sex

explanation: Time is everything with emergency contraception! The sooner you take it after unprotected sex, the better it works. Don't leave it too late! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h2)

question: A client comes to the clinic saying her partner's condom tore three hours ago. What advice should you give?

options.A: Avoid emergency contraception because it only works after 72 hours
options.B: Wait exactly 48 hours before taking any action to let natural cycles adjust
options.C: Come back next week for a pregnancy test before doing anything
options.D: Take the emergency contraceptive as soon as possible for the highest effectiveness

explanation: When accidents happen like a torn condom, acting fast is key. Taking the pill right away gives the client the highest chance of preventing a pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h2)

question: How do standard hormonal emergency contraceptive pills stop a pregnancy from happening?

options.A: By destroying a fertilized egg that is already implanted
options.B: By permanently stopping the normal production of estrogen
options.C: By thickening the bladder lining to trap excess hormones
options.D: By delaying or preventing the release of an egg from the ovary

explanation: Hormonal emergency pills simply hit the pause button on ovulation. If no egg is released, the sperm has nothing to fertilize. Simple and clever! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h3)

question: Why won't hormonal emergency pills work if a woman has already ovulated?

options.A: Because the hormone dose is too low to stay in the stomach
options.B: Because the egg has already been released and is available for fertilization
options.C: Because ovulation automatically neutralizes all chemical drugs
options.D: Because the uterine lining instantly sheds upon ovulation

explanation: Remember, these pills work by delaying ovulation. If the egg has already been released, the pill is too late to stop it from meeting a sperm. Makes total sense, right? [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h3)

question: Within what window of time should standard levonorgestrel emergency pills be taken for the best result?

options.A: Within 14 days of unprotected intercourse
options.B: At any time during the entire monthly cycle
options.C: Exactly 24 hours after the next menstrual period
options.D: Within 72 hours of unprotected intercourse

explanation: Levonorgestrel (like the popular Postinor-2) works best when taken within 72 hours (3 days) after unprotected sex. Keep this rule of thumb handy! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h4)

question: How does ulipristal acetate compare to levonorgestrel in terms of its time window?

options.A: Ulipristal must be taken within the first 12 hours only
options.B: Ulipristal is only used for regular daily birth control
options.C: Ulipristal can remain effective for up to 120 hours after intercourse
options.D: Ulipristal requires surgical insertion by a trained doctor

explanation: Ulipristal gives a bit more breathing room, staying effective for up to 120 hours (5 days) after unprotected sex. You're mastering pharmacology step by step! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h4)

question: What makes the copper IUD special compared to emergency contraceptive pills?

options.A: It is only effective if taken within the first two hours
options.B: It must be swallowed as a tablet with a full glass of water
options.C: It provides ongoing long-term birth control after emergency use
options.D: It permanently stops a woman from ever having children

explanation: The copper IUD is a double-whammy: it works as emergency contraception right now, and it can stay in place to prevent pregnancy for years. Super convenient! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h5)

question: How soon after unprotected sex must a copper IUD be inserted to act as emergency contraception?

options.A: Up to 30 days after the event
options.B: Up to 14 days (two full weeks)
options.C: Up to 5 days (120 hours)
options.D: Within 24 hours without exception

explanation: A copper IUD can be put in place up to 5 days (120 hours) after unprotected sex and still successfully prevent pregnancy. You're doing great! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h5)

question: Why is asking about the last menstrual period crucial during an emergency contraception assessment?

options.A: To check if the patient is already pregnant from a previous cycle
options.B: To calculate the exact date of birth for the current month
options.C: To determine how much weight the patient has recently gained
options.D: To verify if the patient has regular sleeping habits

explanation: Always check the last menstrual period first! Emergency contraception won't help if the client is already pregnant from an earlier cycle. Great clinical thinking! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h6)

question: What attitude should you always show when counseling a client who needs emergency contraception?

options.A: Skeptical and demanding proof
options.B: Non-judgmental and confidential
options.C: Public and sharing with family
options.D: Strictly moralizing and formal

explanation: As nurses, our job is to provide a safe, private, and judgment-free space so clients feel comfortable seeking help without fear of stigma. Excellent nursing values! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h6)

question: What common side effects should you warn a client about after taking hormonal emergency contraception?

options.A: Temporary nausea, headache, or irregular spotting
options.B: Sudden swelling of the lower limbs
options.C: Complete cessation of all future menstrual cycles
options.D: Permanent loss of vision in both eyes

explanation: A sudden rush of hormones can make clients feel a bit nauseous, tired, or give them a mild headache. Reassure them that this is totally normal and temporary! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h7)

question: A client vomits twenty minutes after taking her emergency contraceptive pill. What should you do?

options.A: Ignore the vomiting because it has no effect on the medication
options.B: Consult the provider to see if a repeat dose is needed
options.C: Give her a high dose of intravenous antibiotics immediately
options.D: Tell her the pill failed and she must schedule surgery

explanation: If she vomits shortly after taking the pill (within two hours), her body might not have absorbed the medicine. Always check with the clinician if she needs another dose! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h7)

question: Which of these statements about emergency contraception pills is FALSE?

options.A: They are most effective when taken soon after intercourse
options.B: They work by delaying the release of an egg from the ovary
options.C: They cause permanent and irreversible infertility in women
options.D: They do not protect against sexually transmitted infections

explanation: Emergency pills do NOT make a woman barren! Their hormonal effect is short-term and has zero effect on future fertility. Busting myths like a pro! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h8)

question: A young student in Nigeria worries that taking Postinor-2 will make her barren. How should you respond?

options.A: Prescribe a strong surgical procedure to clear her reproductive system
options.B: Scold her for engaging in premarital sex and refuse to give her the medication
options.C: Gently educate her with facts, explaining that the drug does not cause permanent infertility
options.D: Agree with her fears and advise her never to use any form of family planning

explanation: Market myths can be scary! Gently talking clients through the facts builds trust and ensures they get safe, accurate reproductive healthcare. You're going to be an amazing nurse! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h8)

question: What is the primary goal of family planning counselling?

options.A: Ensuring every client chooses modern barrier methods
options.B: Reducing the overall birth rate in rural communities
options.C: Convincing every client to use permanent surgical methods
options.D: Helping clients make free and informed reproductive choices

explanation: Counselling empowers clients to make voluntary decisions about their own families rather than forcing a specific choice upon them. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h1)

question: What is a likely result of poor family planning counselling?

options.A: Higher rates of natural family planning use
options.B: Better adherence to daily pill schedules
options.C: Early discontinuation of the contraceptive method
options.D: Increased long-term loyalty to clinic staff

explanation: When clients do not fully understand what to expect or how to use their method, they tend to stop using it quickly. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h1)

question: What does the principle of autonomy mean in family planning?

options.A: Clinics must provide free medications to every community member
options.B: Husbands must approve all medical treatments before they begin
options.C: Clients have the right to make their own choices without coercion
options.D: Nurses must choose the safest contraceptive for young clients

explanation: Autonomy protects the client's right to self-determination in their personal reproductive healthcare decisions. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h2)

question: Why is strict confidentiality vital during family planning sessions?

options.A: It builds trust and encourages clients to seek needed care safely
options.B: It guarantees that the government will fund the clinic supplies
options.C: It prevents hospital administrators from auditing patient records
options.D: It stops family members from asking about the client's health

explanation: Clients need assurance that their private reproductive health details will not be shared openly in the community. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h2)

question: What does the letter 'T' stand for in the GATHER counselling model?

options.A: Trust
options.B: Test
options.C: Tell
options.D: Touch

explanation: In GATHER, 'Tell' refers to sharing relevant and balanced information about available contraceptive methods with the client. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h3)

question: A nurse is finishing a counselling session by booking a follow-up date and inviting the client back if problems arise. Which GATHER step is this?

options.A: Help
options.B: Return
options.C: Ask
options.D: Explain

explanation: The 'Return' step focuses on planning for future visits, follow-up care, and open-door re-evaluations. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h3)

question: Why are open-ended questions preferred during reproductive health counselling?

options.A: They shorten the time needed to complete patient registration
options.B: They encourage clients to share their thoughts and concerns fully
options.C: They ensure the nurse makes all the final medical decisions
options.D: They prevent clients from asking complicated medical questions

explanation: Open-ended questions allow clients to express their true feelings and personal stories rather than giving a simple one-word answer. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h4)

question: Which of the following is an example of an open-ended question?

options.A: Are you finished having children with your husband?
options.B: Do you want to use pills or injections today?
options.C: What worries you most about using family planning methods?
options.D: Have you ever experienced high blood pressure before?

explanation: This question cannot be answered with a simple yes or no, prompting the client to elaborate on their specific fears. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h4)

question: What standardized tool do nurses use to check if a contraceptive method is safe for a specific medical condition?

options.A: Apgar scoring system
options.B: GATHER counselling framework
options.C: Partograph monitoring chart
options.D: Medical Eligibility Criteria

explanation: The WHO Medical Eligibility Criteria guide providers on the safety of various contraceptives for clients with specific health conditions. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h5)

question: A client with severe high blood pressure requests a combined oral contraceptive pill. What is the most appropriate nursing action based on safety guidelines?

options.A: Dispense the pills immediately to respect her personal autonomy and choice
options.B: Double the normal starting dose to make sure the pills work effectively
options.C: Tell her to stop checking her blood pressure while taking the hormonal medication
options.D: Suggest an alternative safe method because combined pills pose high cardiovascular risks here

explanation: Combined oral contraceptives can worsen hypertension and increase stroke risks, making them medically restricted for this client. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h5)

question: How should a nurse present different contraceptive choices to a client?

options.A: By strongly recommending the most expensive brand in the clinic
options.B: Objectively, sharing both benefits and drawbacks of each method
options.C: By focusing only on permanent surgical options for parity
options.D: By hiding common side effects so the client does not get scared

explanation: Balanced presentation ensures the client makes a truly informed decision based on complete facts. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h6)

question: Which of the following is classified as a long-acting reversible contraceptive?

options.A: Combined oral contraceptive pill
options.B: Spermicidal vaginal foam
options.C: Subdermal contraceptive implant
options.D: Male latex condom

explanation: Implants provide continuous protection for several years while remaining fully reversible upon removal. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h6)

question: What is the best way to handle a client who expresses fear that an injectable contraceptive causes permanent barrenness?

options.A: Refuse to provide any family planning services to uneducated clients
options.B: Laugh at the misconception so they realize how silly it sounds
options.C: Tell them they must accept whatever side effects happen without complaining
options.D: Listen patiently, validate their worry, and provide factual reassurance

explanation: Respectful dialogue and clear facts help dispel deep-seated cultural myths without shaming the client. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a recommended nursing approach when correcting common contraceptive myths?

options.A: Validating the client's underlying concerns
options.B: Insulting the client for believing rumors
options.C: Providing clear and accurate health facts
options.D: Explaining normal physiological side effects

explanation: Insulting clients creates a hostile environment and drives them away from formal healthcare facilities. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h7)

question: Why is spousal communication often encouraged in Nigerian family planning counselling?

options.A: Partner support helps improve long-term contraceptive adherence
options.B: Nigerian law prohibits women from buying drugs independently
options.C: Men are the only ones who experience contraceptive side effects
options.D: Husbands must legally sign all medical forms in public hospitals

explanation: When partners understand and support the chosen method, the client faces less household conflict and continues use more successfully. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h8)

question: What common barrier often affects contraceptive uptake in resource-constrained Nigerian communities?

options.A: Universal preference for large families exceeding ten children
options.B: Financial constraints and out-of-pocket supply costs
options.C: An absolute lack of any modern contraceptive methods globally
options.D: Laws that ban nurses from discussing birth control openly

explanation: Poverty and high out-of-pocket costs make access difficult, making knowledge of subsidized options vital for nurses. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h8)

question: What is the primary goal of decision making in family planning?

options.A: Choosing pregnancy timing, spacing, and number of children
options.B: Ensuring every family has at least four children
options.C: Eliminating all future pregnancies for every household
options.D: Reducing overall healthcare spending in rural clinics

explanation: Family planning helps individuals and couples decide if, when, and how often to have children to protect their health and well-being. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h1)

question: Why should a nurse view reproductive choices as part of a broader life plan?

options.A: Because personal goals, health, and finances deeply affect family size choices
options.B: Because government policies require strict tracking of household income
options.C: So that medical treatments can be delayed until retirement age
options.D: To ensure the nurse can dictate the exact number of children a client has

explanation: Reproductive decisions do not happen in a vacuum; they are shaped by an individual's financial situation, overall health status, and future life aspirations. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h1)

question: Which factor strongly influences a client's choice regarding contraceptive use?

options.A: The exact color of hospital waiting rooms
options.B: Cultural norms and religious beliefs
options.C: The brand of soap used in the clinic
options.D: Standard parking availability at the health center

explanation: Cultural expectations and religious traditions often guide what contraceptive methods are acceptable to a client and their family. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h2)

question: A client refuses a specific birth control method due to local community rumors. What is the best nursing approach?

options.A: Refuse to provide any further healthcare services to the client
options.B: Listen respectfully and provide accurate education to clear up the rumors
options.C: Dismiss the client's worries as silly and push the method anyway
options.D: Tell the client that community opinions should never matter

explanation: Respectful listening combined with gentle, accurate education helps address fears rooted in social stigma and community misconceptions. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h2)

question: What is a common risk for a woman who uses a secret contraceptive method in a controlling relationship?

options.A: Mandatory enrollment in nursing leadership classes
options.B: Automatic promotion to a higher socioeconomic status
options.C: Instantaneous and permanent relief from all headaches
options.D: Experiencing partner violence or abandonment if found out

explanation: Using birth control without a partner's knowledge in environments with strict gender imbalances can provoke severe domestic conflict and safety risks. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h3)

question: Why is encouraging joint spousal counseling important in family planning?

options.A: It helps couples share responsibility and align their family goals
options.B: It allows the nurse to charge higher fees for the visit
options.C: It ensures that only the male partner makes the final choice
options.D: It prevents the couple from ever visiting the clinic again

explanation: Joint counseling promotes healthy communication, reducing secrets and helping partners make decisions together for their shared future. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h3)

question: What does informed consent require before a client receives a contraceptive method?

options.A: Proof of employment and stable monthly income
options.B: A written letter of approval from a community chief
options.C: Complete agreement from the client's extended family
options.D: Full understanding of benefits, risks, and correct usage

explanation: Informed consent means the client knows what to expect, including how the method works and its potential side effects, before they choose it. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h4)

question: Which action by a nurse violates a client's right to voluntary family planning?

options.A: Explaining how barrier methods prevent sexually transmitted infections
options.B: Asking the client about their future plans for having children
options.C: Strongly pressuring a client to accept a method the nurse prefers
options.D: Providing pamphlets written in the local language of the client

explanation: Coercion and pushing personal preferences onto clients violate the core ethical principle of patient autonomy and voluntary choice. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h4)

question: What does the letter 'B' stand for in the popular BRAIDED counseling mnemonic?

options.A: Billing
options.B: Bandage
options.C: Bedrest
options.D: Benefits

explanation: In contraceptive counseling, the BRAIDED framework reminds nurses to discuss benefits, risks, alternatives, and other key details with the client. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h5)

question: A client with severe hypertension asks for oral contraceptive pills. What should the nurse do during the assessment?

options.A: Identify hypertension as a contraindication and discuss safer alternative methods
options.B: Prescribe the pills immediately because blood pressure does not matter
options.C: Refuse to check the client's blood pressure during the visit
options.D: Tell the client that birth control pills cure high blood pressure

explanation: Estrogen-containing pills can worsen high blood pressure and increase stroke risk, so nurses must screen for medical conditions and offer safer choices like progestin-only options. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h5)

question: Which of the following is a common misconception about modern contraceptives?

options.A: They cause permanent infertility after stopping use
options.B: They require daily surgical procedures to remain active
options.C: They always cure infectious diseases instantly
options.D: They make hair grow faster all over the body

explanation: A widespread myth is that using birth control makes a woman permanently unable to have children later, which nurses must actively correct. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h6)

question: Why do judgmental attitudes from healthcare workers act as a barrier to family planning?

options.A: Clients will demand more expensive medications than needed
options.B: Clients will avoid seeking care out of fear of being shamed or scolded
options.C: The clinic electricity will shut down due to negative energy
options.D: Staff members will forget how to write medical prescriptions

explanation: When providers judge clients for their choices, age, or marital status, patients stop coming to the clinic, leading to unmet health needs. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h6)

question: Which ethical principle gives a client the right to make their own healthcare choices?

options.A: Negligence
options.B: Maleficence
options.C: Paternalism
options.D: Autonomy

explanation: Autonomy is the ethical principle that respects an individual's right to self-determination and personal decision making without outside control. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h7)

question: What is a nurse's legal and ethical duty regarding a client's family planning records?

options.A: Post the details on community bulletin boards for public awareness
options.B: Maintain strict confidentiality and protect records from unauthorized viewers
options.C: Share the client's medical history openly with any curious neighbors
options.D: Hand over all clinical notes to the client's extended family members

explanation: Confidentiality protects the client's privacy, ensuring their health information is only shared with authorized medical personnel involved in their direct care. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h7)

question: Why do we ask family planning clients to come back for follow-up visits?

options.A: To administer routine childhood immunizations
options.B: To conduct major diagnostic surgical procedures
options.C: To permanently discharge the client from care
options.D: To check on the client and offer ongoing support

explanation: Follow-up visits are all about seeing how the client is doing and giving them continuous support with their chosen contraceptive method. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h1)

question: What usually happens if a family planning client never returns for follow-up checks?

options.A: They will experience guaranteed protection from sexually transmitted infections
options.B: They will automatically switch to a permanent surgical method
options.C: They may stop using their method incorrectly or face unmanaged side effects
options.D: They are required by law to pay a large financial penalty

explanation: Without our guidance during follow-ups, clients often struggle with side effects or make mistakes using their contraception, which makes them give up on it. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h1)

question: When is the best time for a first follow-up visit after putting in an IUD (Intrauterine Device)?

options.A: After six months
options.B: After exactly five years
options.C: After twenty-four hours
options.D: After four to six weeks

explanation: Seeing the client at 4 to 6 weeks lets you check the IUD strings and make sure the device hasn't slipped out. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h2)

question: Why do different birth control methods have different follow-up timetables?

options.A: Because each method carries unique risks, mechanisms, and rates of early side effects
options.B: Because government policy dictates a uniform schedule for all medications
options.C: Because clinics only open on specific days of the week for pills
options.D: Because client preferences change every single week

explanation: Every contraceptive works differently and brings its own early side effects, so our follow-up schedule has to match those critical adjustment windows. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h2)

question: In family planning care, what does 'compliance' mean?

options.A: Whether the clinic follows national healthcare budgeting guidelines
options.B: Whether the partner agrees with the choice of contraceptive
options.C: Whether the manufacturer tests the product for chemical safety
options.D: Whether the client follows the precise instructions for using the method

explanation: Compliance simply means how well and accurately a client sticks to the correct usage guidelines for their birth control. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h3)

question: A client says she still takes her birth control pill every day, but admits she forgets it at least three times a week. How would you describe this?

options.A: Good continuation and perfect compliance
options.B: Good continuation but poor compliance
options.C: Poor continuation and no compliance
options.D: Poor continuation but perfect compliance

explanation: She is keeping up with the habit of taking her pills (continuation), but missing doses means she isn't following the schedule properly (poor compliance). [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h3)

question: What is the most common reason clients stop using their birth control method?

options.A: Forgetting clinic locations
options.B: Traveling out of the country
options.C: Experiencing side effects
options.D: Changing religious beliefs

explanation: When clients face physical or emotional side effects that they don't know how to handle, they usually stop using the method. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h4)

question: If a client reports mild, normal side effects from her contraceptive, which action is NOT helpful?

options.A: Dismissing their concerns as imaginary
options.B: Providing reassurance and timeline expectations
options.C: Validating their physical experience
options.D: Explaining simple ways to manage the symptoms

explanation: Never brush off a client's feelings! Listening, validating, and supporting them builds trust and helps them stick to their care. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h4)

question: Why do nurses need to check for new health changes during follow-up visits?

options.A: Because new health conditions can make a current contraceptive method unsafe
options.B: Because government taxes change based on client medical history
options.C: Because clinic software requires updated home addresses every month
options.D: Because blood pressure readings remain identical throughout a person's life

explanation: New medical issues like high blood pressure can pop up, turning a birth control method that used to be safe into a health risk. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h5)

question: A client on combined oral contraceptive pills reports getting severe migraine headaches with visual changes (auras) lately. What should you do first?

options.A: Schedule her next routine appointment for five years later
options.B: Recognize this as a safety risk and discuss changing her contraceptive method
options.C: Praise her for keeping her follow-up appointment on time
options.D: Recommend she continue the pills without any changes

explanation: Migraines with aura plus estrogen-based pills can sharply increase stroke risk. We need to switch her to a non-estrogen method right away! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h5)

question: When a client wants to switch to a different birth control method during a follow-up visit, what is your main job as a nurse?

options.A: Charge an extra administrative fee for changing the care plan
options.B: Refuse service until a senior medical officer approves the change
options.C: Force the client to continue the original method for at least one more year
options.D: Ensure there is no gap in contraceptive coverage to prevent unintended pregnancy

explanation: When changing methods, timing is everything. We must make sure there is no unprotected gap where an unintended pregnancy could happen. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h6)

question: A client complains that taking a daily pill is too hard with her busy work schedule. What is a great recommendation to discuss?

options.A: Double the daily pill dose to make up for missed days
options.B: Scold the client for being irresponsible with her medication
options.C: Stop using all forms of contraception immediately
options.D: Discuss long-acting reversible options like implants or injectables

explanation: If daily pills are a struggle, methods like injectables or implants take away the stress of daily remembering while offering great protection. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h6)

question: What is the main benefit of writing accurate notes during family planning follow-ups?

options.A: Ensuring safe continuity of care when different providers see the client
options.B: Advertising new clinic services to the community
options.C: Providing a colorful drawing book for pediatric visitors
options.D: Reducing the physical weight of clinic filing cabinets

explanation: Clear notes mean that if another nurse or doctor sees the client next time, they can easily pick up right where you left off. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h7)

question: Which of these details is least important to write down in a standard family planning follow-up note?

options.A: Blood pressure and vital health changes
options.B: Current contraceptive method and compliance
options.C: The brand of pen used by the nurse to write the chart
options.D: Side effects discussed and counseling provided

explanation: We only care about clinical facts! The brand of pen has nothing to do with patient health or safe care continuity. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h7)

question: In clinic practice, what do we call a family planning client who misses their scheduled visit or refill date?

options.A: A client who misses a scheduled clinic visit or contraceptive refill
options.B: A woman who refuses to discuss contraception with a nurse
options.C: A client who chooses to switch contraceptive methods
options.D: A patient who permanently stops all healthcare interactions

explanation: A defaulter is simply someone who misses their expected return date for supplies or check-ins. Spotting this early lets us reach out and support them! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T025#GNS226_U6_T025_h1)

question: Why is it unhelpful to just write off a family planning defaulter as simply 'uncooperative'?

options.A: It guarantees the patient will never return to the facility
options.B: It breaks hospital regulations regarding patient confidentiality
options.C: It automatically makes the client pregnant within a week
options.D: It ignores practical barriers and personal reasons driving the missed appointment

explanation: People miss appointments for real reasons—like side effects, transport costs, or busy schedules. Looking past the label helps us solve the actual problem together. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T025#GNS226_U6_T025_h1)

question: What is a very common physical reason why clients stop using their family planning method?

options.A: Gaining the ability to read medical textbooks
options.B: Complete recovery from all chronic illnesses
options.C: Experiencing troublesome side effects like irregular bleeding
options.D: Developing an allergy to clinic waiting room chairs

explanation: Unmanaged side effects are a primary reason clients stop their method. A quick counseling chat about what to expect can make all the difference! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T025#GNS226_U6_T025_h2)

question: How might a partner's attitude cause a client to stop coming for family planning?

options.A: Disapproval or secret opposition can force the client to stop using services quietly
options.B: Supportive partners always pay the clinic staff to cancel appointments
options.C: Involved partners automatically double the efficacy of oral pills
options.D: Partner involvement has no impact on clinic attendance

explanation: Fear of conflict at home can lead clients to quietly drop out. As nurses, creating a safe, confidential space helps us support them through these challenges. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T025#GNS226_U6_T025_h2)

question: Which tools do clinics primarily use to track when a family planning client is due back?

options.A: Daily weather monitoring charts
options.B: Appointment registers and individual client cards
options.C: Pharmacy inventory bills for unrelated drugs
options.D: National television broadcast schedules

explanation: Client cards and clinic registers are our best friends for keeping track of return dates so no one slips through the cracks. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T025#GNS226_U6_T025_h3)

question: A client using an injectable contraceptive is seven days past her due date. What is the best next step for the clinic?

options.A: Assume she has moved abroad and close her record
options.B: Wait two full years before checking on her status
options.C: Discard her client card immediately to save storage space
options.D: Flag her file as a defaulter and initiate tracking procedures

explanation: Once the grace period passes, flagging the file triggers our tracking steps so we can check in before her contraceptive protection completely lapses. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T025#GNS226_U6_T025_h3)

question: Why is scolding or shouting at a returning defaulter a risky practice for a nurse?

options.A: It discourages the client from ever seeking care at that facility again
options.B: It violates international trade agreements
options.C: It instantly invalidates the chemical composition of oral pills
options.D: It causes immediate physical injury to the client's skin

explanation: Nobody wants to walk back into a place where they'll be judged. A welcoming attitude keeps our clinic doors open to those who need us most. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T025#GNS226_U6_T025_h4)

question: What is the best way to greet a client who has missed several family planning appointments?

options.A: Ignore the missed visits and pretend they came on time
options.B: Welcome them warmly and ask gently what made it hard to return
options.C: Report them to the local authorities for breaking rules
options.D: Demand an immediate written apology for wasting clinic time

explanation: Starting with warmth and empathy builds trust, making the client comfortable enough to share the real obstacles they faced. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T025#GNS226_U6_T025_h4)

question: What important clinical step must a nurse take before starting a returning defaulter on a new hormonal contraceptive?

options.A: Require the client to pay a fine for defaulting
options.B: Wait for laboratory tests that take three weeks
options.C: Carefully rule out existing pregnancy
options.D: Consult the national ministry of health directly

explanation: Safety first! Always rule out pregnancy before dispensing or administering new hormonal methods to protect both client and baby. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T025#GNS226_U6_T025_h5)

question: A client stopped taking her oral contraceptive pills because she kept forgetting daily doses. What is a great alternative to suggest?

options.A: Switching to a long-acting method like an implant or injection
options.B: Stopping all contraception permanently without alternatives
